entry.title: EMASAM: a Computationally Efficient Sharpness-Aware Minimization via EMA-Guided Perturbations

author.name: Tanapat Ratchatorn, Masayuki Tanaka

entry.summary: EMASAM removes the extra gradient computation of sharpness-aware minimization by defining the perturbation direction from the discrepancy between current weights and their exponential moving average rather than from a fresh loss gradient. This aims to retain SAM generalization benefits at roughly single-pass cost.

entry.title: PureTD: Reinforcement Learning for Backgammon Money Games with No Evaluation-time Search

author.name: Alexander L. Strehl

entry.summary: Revisits TD-Gammon for backgammon money games with no search at evaluation time, learning both checker play and doubling-cube decisions from scratch through self-play with minimal hand-coded logic and no expert features. The resulting search-free model is reported to be faster and substantially stronger than open-source engines using one-ply lookahead.

entry.title: Does 1/2-Tsallis-INF Also Work Well for Best-Arm Identification?

author.name: Jingxin Zhan, Yuze Han, Zhihua Zhang

entry.summary: Asks whether the canonical best-of-both-worlds bandit algorithm half-Tsallis-INF, designed for regret minimization, can also identify the best arm without extra exploration, analyzing the failure probability that the empirical best arm from importance-weighted loss estimates is wrong. The study connects regret minimization and best-arm identification objectives within one algorithm.

entry.title: Cross-Entropy Risk Estimation for Language Models: Inconsistency Must Be Dense, and the Holdout Method Is No Exception

author.name: Hanti Lin

entry.summary: Argues that held-out per-token cross-entropy risk, the quantity that scaling laws are fitted to, cannot be consistently estimated, because finite-risk and infinite-risk states of the world are topologically intertwined and no sample reveals the relevant tail property of the model distribution. Concludes that even holdout estimation offers no escape.

entry.title: Unifying Graph Neural Networks Through a Common Layer Equation

author.name: Sai Karthik Navuluru, Siddhartha Shankar Das, Bo Ni, Hongjie Chen, Yu Wang, Baris Coskunuzer, Nesreen K. Ahmed, Franck Dernoncourt, Mahantesh Halappanavar, Tyler Derr, Ryan A. Rossi, Lakshman Tamil

entry.summary: Proposes a single layer equation with seven components (propagation bank, message maps, fusion operator, ego map, update map, and so on) that expresses message passing, attention, spectral, global, relational, higher-order, and geometric GNNs in one notation. The key factorization separates where information moves from what moves.

entry.title: Q-based Variational Inverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ondrej Bajgar, Peter Tisnikar, Alessandro Abate, Konstantinos Gatsis, Maike Osborne

entry.summary: QVIRL is a Bayesian inverse reinforcement learning method that recovers a posterior over reward functions by primarily learning a variational distribution over optimal Q-values, combining scalability with uncertainty quantification. Motivated by safety-critical preference inference and active learning where point-estimate rewards are insufficient.

entry.title: MINT: A Universal Zero-Shot Predictor for Transaction Data

author.name: Parameswaran Kamalaruban, Viktor Drobnyi, Maeve Madigan, Julia Rozanova, David Sutton, Stuart Burrell

entry.summary: Presents a foundation-model approach for zero-shot prediction over sequential financial transaction data, aiming to support new downstream banking tasks without task-specific heads or costly text serialization. It targets fraud, credit risk, and personalization use cases from a single universal predictor.

entry.title: A Four-Axis Trustworthiness Benchmark for LLM-as-Judge in Principle-Based Regulation

author.name: Dipankar Sarkar

entry.summary: Releases a benchmark of financial-promotion scenarios mapped to UK regulatory principles and argues that LLM judges applied to principle-based regulation must be evaluated on accuracy, paraphrase robustness, adversarial robustness, and calibration together. It also introduces a calibrated, auditable assessment method.

entry.title: AeroGround: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Aerial-Ground Collaborative Reasoning

author.name: Shenghong Yi, Lin Zhang, Muzian Li, Jiakang Yuan, Haoyu Zhang, Peng Ye, Jiayuan Fan, Huafeng Qin, Tao Chen

entry.summary: A benchmark for vision-language reasoning that requires jointly using aerial drone views and ground-level views of the same scene, built from about 29,000 simulated multimodal observation groups with 2,250 curated questions. It targets rescue and infrastructure inspection scenarios that existing UAV benchmarks ignore.

entry.title: HOIMask: Towards Generative Masked Modeling for Human Object Interaction Generation

author.name: Yihong Ji, Jinsong Zhang, He Hu, Hongbo Xu

entry.summary: The first generative masked-modeling framework for human-object interaction motion, encoding motion and contact signals into discrete 2D token maps rather than 1D sequences and generating in discrete space. It aims to avoid the artifact accumulation of iterative diffusion denoising for interaction sequences.

entry.title: CrossView: Can Vision-Language Models Reason Across Cameras?

author.name: Sahil Shah, S P Sharan, Harsh Goel, Manvik Pasula, Adithya Hebbalae, Minkyu Choi, Sandeep P. Chinchali

entry.summary: CrossView is a benchmark for whether vision-language models can reason across multiple simultaneous camera views, covering context that grows with view count, occlusions visible from only some cameras, view selection and evidence integration. The authors argue multi-camera reasoning is qualitatively different from single-camera video understanding and show current models struggle.

entry.title: SCORE: Shape-Conforming Regions for Flight in Enclosed, Degraded Environments

author.name: Eric Minwoo Kim, Jong-Kook Kim

entry.summary: SCORE defines a conformal prediction nonconformity score directly on a signed distance field so the calibrated obstacle keep-out region can be non-convex and hug real geometry. This avoids the bulges of convex safety margins that block narrow passages in caves and collapsed structures as perception degrades.

entry.title: SparkVLA: Stop-Aware Hierarchical VLA with Adaptive Action Chunking for Long-Horizon Manipulation

author.name: Xunyao Lei, Renjun Wu, Tianlin Huo, Xuesong Li

entry.summary: SparkVLA reframes two coupled decisions in hierarchical vision-language-action systems, when to end a subtask and how much of an action chunk to execute, as a single ranking problem over a unified candidate set including a stop option. This resolves an interdependence that prior architectures handle with separate, isolated modules.

entry.title: Arm-Aware Guided Dexterous Grasp Generation with Arm-Agnostic Grasp Models

author.name: Yongyi Jia, Yongpeng Jiang, Kangchen Lv, Yi Ren, Mingrui Yu, Xiang Li

entry.summary: Provides a way to make pretrained arm-agnostic dexterous grasp generators respect arm constraints such as collision avoidance, workspace limits, and consecutive grasping, using guidance rather than rejection sampling or arm-specific retraining. This preserves generalization across robots and environments while improving sample efficiency.

entry.title: ViHaTeleop: A Low-Cost, Lightweight Visual-Haptic Teleoperation System for Dexterous Manipulation Learning

author.name: Fucai Zhu, Yanhou Lai, Paul Maestre, Koichi Hashimoto

entry.summary: ViHaTeleop is a 0.7 kg, roughly 550-dollar teleoperation rig combining SLAM wrist tracking, camera-based hand tracking, and per-finger vibrotactile feedback, deployed on a Franka arm with a LEAP hand and a tactile fingertip sensor. A nine-participant study across six contact-critical tasks compares demonstration quality with and without haptics.

entry.title: Deep adaptive design with an evidential bias criterion

author.name: David Chen, Michael Evans, Xinwei Li, Prateek Bansal, David J. Nott

entry.summary: Argues that expected information gain, the dominant utility in Bayesian optimal experimental design, rewards strong evidence for the truth on average but does not penalize designs likely to produce evidence for falsehoods, and proposes an evidential bias criterion instead. The criterion is integrated into amortized deep adaptive design for sequential experiments.

entry.title: Toward Safe LLM Agents: A Survey of Specification, Verification, and Enforcement

author.name: Pierre Dantas, Lucas Cordeiro, Ehsan Nowroozi, Tihanyi Norbert

entry.summary: A PRISMA systematic review of 38 studies from 2022 to 2026 on specifying, verifying, and enforcing safety properties for LLM agent plans. It identifies the natural-language-to-formal specification bottleneck as the dominant obstacle, with low reported translation accuracy, and maps gaps across the three layers.

entry.title: CEDAR-GRPO: Process-Aware Reinforcement Learning for General Abductive Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Moein Salimi, Danial Parnian, Shaygan Adim, Amirmohammad Ebrahiminasab, Nima Alighardashi, Parsa Gholami, Sahand Akramipour, Mahdi Jafari Siavoshani, Mohammad Hossein Rohban

entry.summary: CEDAR-GRPO adds process-aware rewards for evidence coverage and evidence-to-explanation directionality on top of final-answer correctness, aiming to make abductive reasoning a transferable capability rather than a benchmark-specific skill. Four open-weight models are post-trained on a domain-neutral abduction mixture and tested for transfer beyond the training benchmark family.

entry.title: Admission Without Answers: Label-Free Certification and Experience Learning for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling

author.name: Junbo Jacob Lian, Huiling Chen, Hanzhang Qin, Chung-Piaw Teo

entry.summary: AdmitOR decides whether an LLM-generated optimization model should be admitted into an agent's reusable skill store without access to ground-truth answers, by running candidates from multiple model families and solver stacks on resampled instances and checking agreement across value-function traces. On a 300-problem label-blind stream, admitting anything executable poisoned roughly a quarter of admissions, while single-instance agreement was also unreliable.

entry.title: Solvable Sokoban Without a Solver via Diffusion

author.name: Sina Baghal

entry.summary: Trains a transformer-based discrete diffusion model purely to fill in masked Sokoban tiles, with no solver, reward or solvability labels, and finds 77 percent of generated puzzles are solvable, with most failures fixable by removing one wall. Suggests a globally search-heavy, PSPACE-complete property can emerge from a purely local reconstruction objective.

entry.title: Gated Against One Model, Open to the Next: Option-Only Solvability in Legal Multiple-Choice Benchmarks

author.name: Volodymyr Ovcharov

entry.summary: Tests how much of a large Ukrainian judicial exam benchmark can be solved from answer options alone, finding that a mid-tier assistant model scores well above chance without seeing the question and that a concentrated subset is solvable blind across all option orderings. The authors rule out simple memorization of legislation and release a gated subset.

entry.title: LENS: In-Context Search via Latent Evidence Exploration over Dynamic Raw Documents

author.name: Xingjun Wang, Gongsheng Li, Qi Fan, Yunlin Mao, Luyan Su, Yingda Chen

entry.summary: LENS formulates question answering over changing raw document collections as budgeted evidence localization in a latent evidence space, maintaining a query-conditioned belief over candidate spans instead of building embeddings or persistent indexes. The index-free design avoids stale preprocessing and premature commitment to a chunk granularity.

entry.title: HalluTracer: Hallucination Detection via Depth-Averaging Truth Signals

author.name: Zhihao Guo, Zonghan Wu, Huan Huo, DaYong Ye, Junwei Zhang, Weiran Yao, Zhiwei Liu, Qingsong Wen, Yilei Shao

entry.summary: HalluTracer detects hallucinations by reading truthfulness signals from every layer of the forward pass before the first answer token is emitted, rather than probing a single layer or component. A geometric analysis shows per-layer signals are weakly correlated, so depth averaging suppresses noise and improves detection.

entry.title: Counting Documents Is Not Counting Text: Unit Bias in Web-PDF Corpus Statistics

author.name: Luca Foppiano

entry.summary: Analyzing a 7.9M-document, 32.6B-token web PDF corpus, this paper shows that per-document rates badly misrepresent per-token reality: about 3 percent of text-bearing documents hold half the tokens, long documents dominate text volume, and Common Crawl truncation affected 23 percent of documents but 63 percent of the text. Widely used extraction libraries recover only a small fraction of the truncated text.

entry.title: Towards Risk-free AI Agent Deployment

author.name: Yintong Huo, Rangeet Pan, Abhik Roychoudhury

entry.summary: This position paper argues that safe deployment of LLM agents must be grounded in trajectories, the recorded sequence of reasoning steps, tool calls, and observations, because many security, compliance, and functional failures are visible only there. It lays out a research agenda for agent testing and debugging, including the oracle problem, non-determinism, and trajectory analysis.

entry.title: Disentangling Homophily and Rarity: Explaining Failure in Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Preben M. Ness, Fariz Ikhwantri, Dusica Marijan

entry.summary: Disentangles whether heterophilic nodes are hard for graph neural networks because they are heterophilic or merely because they are rare, evaluating six GNNs on five datasets of varying homophily. The finding that homophilic nodes remain easier even when rare undercuts the subgroup-generalization framing while also nuancing standard claims about neighborhood aggregation failure.

entry.title: Conditional Evaluation of Language Models with Cheap Auxiliary Signals

author.name: Zhi Zhang, Lingfeng Lyu, Yue Kang, Doudou Zhou

entry.summary: LACE is a semi-supervised estimator for conditional (rather than aggregate) LLM evaluation that uses cheap biased signals such as judge scores and confidence features as control variates, with local centering ensuring the augmentation cannot bias the estimand. It reduces the number of gold labels needed to profile where models succeed and fail.

entry.title: Density-Reweighted Entropic Optimal Transport: Decoupling Geometry from Sampling Density

author.name: Keyi Li, Yuval Kluger, Boris Landa

entry.summary: Identifies a failure mode where entropic optimal transport matches points across datasets by relative sampling density rather than geometric proximity, then introduces a reweighting that tunes how much density influences the transport plan. Aimed at dataset alignment tasks in scientific data analysis such as single-cell integration.

entry.title: Not All Tokens Are Equal: Inflation-Aware Routing for Agentic LLM Systems

author.name: Heming Fu, Shan Lin, Qianqian Xie, Guojun Xiong

entry.summary: Defines token inflation as the ratio of true agentic workflow cost to a single-call cost, arising from retries, and shows that routers relying on per-token price can underestimate real cost by more than twofold on hard tasks. InflationAgent measures inflation across model tiers and task types, reporting up to fourfold inflation for a 7B model on multi-hop QA, and uses this in a four-stage router with chain-of-thought branching.

entry.title: Benchmarking Frontier Text-to-Image Models on Image-Description Prompts

author.name: Sajjad Abdoli, Ghassan Al-Sumaidaee, Ahmed Rashad

entry.summary: Evaluates four production text-to-image systems on 48 deliberately hard compositional prompts involving exact object counts, attribute binding, legible embedded text, and spatial constraints, graded with an automated rubric authored by a frontier reasoning model. It argues average-case reporting hides large gaps between systems.

entry.title: Robust structure from motion for aerial-ground images via detector-free feature matching and multi-view track refinement

author.name: San Jiang, Hui Wang, Xing Zhang, Zhongwen Hu, Zhijun Wang, Ruisheng Wang, Wanshou Jiang, Qingquan Li

entry.summary: A structure-from-motion pipeline for combined aerial and ground imagery that uses a rotation-robust detector-free matcher with directional state-space scanning and multi-view track refinement. It targets the extreme viewpoint, scale, and rotation differences that break conventional matching in urban 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: Gaussian-JEPA: Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for 3D Gaussian Splats

author.name: Bin Ren, Qi Ma, Yue Li, Zongyan Han, Yidi Li, Yuqian Fu, Rao Muhammad Anwer, Theo Gevers, Fahad Shahbaz Khan, Salman Khan

entry.summary: Gaussian-JEPA applies joint-embedding predictive learning to 3D Gaussian Splatting assets, predicting latent representations of held-out Gaussian token blocks from visible context rather than reconstructing masked attributes in input space. This avoids tying supervision to a single sampled primitive realization and removes the need for an input-space decoder.

entry.title: Towards Real-Time and Adaptable LiDAR Scene Completion

author.name: Azhar Hussian, Martin Vossiek, Vasileios Belagiannis

entry.summary: RapidLiDAR reframes LiDAR scene completion by learning the initialization step itself rather than relying on fixed noise perturbation or iterative denoising from Gaussian noise. The goal is real-time completion that adapts across sensor configurations without manual noise recalibration, which matters for deployable autonomous driving perception.

entry.title: Binarized High-Efficiency RAW Video Restoration and Beyond

author.name: Tianyu Zhu, Ying Fu, Hesong Li, Gengchen Zhang, Xin Yuan, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: BinRVR binarizes a RAW video restoration network, cutting computation and parameters by about 96 percent while losing only around 4 percent in quality. It introduces a module for joint spatial-temporal information interaction to fix the weak temporal modeling and activation distribution issues of binary networks.

entry.title: SpotlessGS: Relightable 3D Gaussian Splatting under Dynamic Illumination for Robotic Perception

author.name: Liang Hong, Jiaxin Wei, Simon Schaefer, Stefan Leutenegger, Jaehyung Jung

entry.summary: SpotlessGS extends dark-scene Gaussian splatting so robots with onboard lights can build relightable 3D reconstructions without calibrating light parameters, jointly optimizing lighting inside the splatting framework. A spherical-harmonic low-frequency illumination model captures spatially varying ambient and residual light.

entry.title: ForceU-VLA: A Force-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model for Embodied Ultrasound Scanning

author.name: Xingzheng Wu, Cheng Zhang, Guihao Yan, Xifeng Hu, Zhi Liu, Qing Cai

entry.summary: ForceU-VLA is a vision-language-action model for autonomous ultrasound scanning that tightly couples force sensing with ultrasound image feedback and adds awareness of the scanning stage. The aim is to capture dynamic probe-tissue interaction so acquisition quality improves.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Online Mapping for 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM

author.name: Thai Luu, Quan Tran, Hieu Phan, Tuan Dang

entry.summary: This work replaces offline-derived initialization and density-control heuristics in 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM with geometry-aware online alternatives suited to strict per-keyframe optimization budgets. The argument is that where limited iterations are spent determines map quality during incremental growth.

entry.title: HP2-SLAM: Adaptive Hybrid ICP for Robust and Efficient LiDAR SLAM

author.name: Nam Tran, Thu Tran, Hieu Phan, Thai Luu, Toan Nguyen, William J. Beksi, Tuan Dang

entry.summary: HP2-SLAM is a lightweight LiDAR SLAM system built around a planarity-aware adaptive hybrid iterative closest point formulation with neighborhood-size adaptation. It aims to keep geometry-based methods robust in planar or repetitive scenes without the training cost and generalization limits of learned approaches.

entry.title: ScenarioCharacterization: A Modular Toolkit for Characterizing Safety across Trajectory Datasets

author.name: Ingrid Navarro, Yutong Duan, Jonathan Francis, Jean Oh

entry.summary: Open-source, dataset-agnostic toolkit that profiles driving scenarios in trajectory datasets through a three-layer pipeline of dataset adapters, feature and criticality characterizers, and analysis tools, with schema-validated interfaces so new datasets plug in easily. Aimed at standardizing safety characterization across autonomous driving benchmarks.

entry.title: Unified Condition-Action Modeling for Accurate One-Step Action Generation

author.name: Xinyu Zhou, Zikun Cai, Kuangji Zuo, Gen Li, Boyu Ma, Yanshuo Lu, Yutong Song, Mingqi Yuan, Jiayu Chen, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: UCA-Flow places observation conditions and action trajectories in a shared token space so they co-evolve during generation, rather than treating conditions as side inputs to a diffusion or flow policy. The result is a compact model achieving one-step action generation with reported gains in both speed and accuracy.

entry.title: Planner-Conditioned Diffusion for Coordinated Multi-Agent Exploration

author.name: Marcus Yu Siong Teo, Jeric Lew, Tanishq Duhan, Guillaume Sartoretti

entry.summary: PCDP trains a diffusion planner for multi-robot graph-based exploration on demonstrations from several different planner styles, with a planner-style conditioning variable that allows behavior to be steered at inference time. It targets the narrow behavioral distribution of prior diffusion exploration planners.

entry.title: Weird Re-Tokenization, Symmetries and Compression: Research Agenda

author.name: Xenomirant

entry.summary: Opens a research agenda on tokenization from an alignment perspective, noting that language models handle and even produce nonstandard tokenizations they never saw during training, and framing this as an understudied safety-relevant behavior. The authors plan a sequence of posts synthesizing literature and reporting their own experiments on retokenization, symmetries, and compression.

entry.title: Seeing beyond BMI: Estimating cardiometabolic risk with smartphone imagery

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google research blog post on estimating cardiometabolic risk from smartphone imagery, going beyond BMI as a crude proxy. Only the category label is present in the provided excerpt, so technical details such as model, cohort, and validation cannot be assessed here.

entry.title: Position: AI Lock-In Is in Progress, and We Must Be Prepared

author.name: Jaeho Kim, Seokhyun Lee, Jieun Lee, Changhee Lee

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that AI safety research under-attends to AI lock-in: the risk that heavy reliance on AI systems deskills humans, erodes independent capability, and creates systemic fragility if those systems fail or are compromised. It maps the phenomenon at individual, organizational, and societal levels and proposes research directions.

entry.title: OGX: An Open-Source, Vendor-Neutral Generative AI Application Server

author.name: Francisco Javier Arceo, S\'ebastien Han, Matthew Farrellee, Charlie Doern, Yuan Tang, Derek Higgins, Varsha Prasad Narsing, Gordon Sim, Sumanth Kamenani, Ben Browning, Raghotham Murthy

entry.summary: OGX is an open-source, vendor-neutral generative AI application server that implements the API surfaces of major frontier labs, including a Responses-style agentic orchestration API plus Anthropic and Google message interfaces, with pluggable inference, vector-store, and safety backends. The goal is to let agentic applications switch models and infrastructure without code changes.

entry.title: When Do LLMs Apply the Wrong Law? Diagnosing LLM Failures in Temporal Legal Reasoning

author.name: Yiqian Huang, Shuyuan Zheng, Qianying Liu, Shaowen Peng, Yuntao Kong, Kotaro Funakoshi, Chuan Xiao, Manabu Okumura, Yang Cao

entry.summary: Builds a benchmark for temporal applicable-law determination, testing whether models select the version of a statute in force when the relevant facts occurred. LLMs show a strong recency bias toward the newest enacted law that does not stem from failing to understand that laws have temporal scope, and the paper diagnoses the underlying failure modes.

entry.title: Synchronized Logit Steering: Real-world Steganography

author.name: Andrew Rufail, Aadi Dash, Onir Narahari, Ethan Mui, Mahi Gajare, Prakhar Tiwari, Shrija Makapothula, Nick Cui

entry.summary: Synchronized Logit Steering is a steganographic scheme that removes the usual requirement that sender and receiver share an identical prompt, by deriving a proxy prompt from the generated output itself so both parties can reconstruct the same logit distribution. Payload bits are encoded as token ranks in high-entropy regions, making the method workable in pipelines with retrieval augmentation or hidden system prompts.

entry.title: What the Reranker Sees: Multi-Aspect Page Annotation for Long-Document Multimodal Question Answering

author.name: Guanchen Wu, Jiayuan Ding, Subhabrata Mukherjee, Carl Yang

entry.summary: Trident tackles long-document multimodal question answering by converting each candidate page into an LLM-readable semantic record with visual captions and structural annotations, so the reranker can see table, chart, and layout evidence rather than raw text snippets. The authors show that on long-document benchmarks the bottleneck is reranker-side evidence selection rather than retrieval recall.

entry.title: LLMs Can Predict Failure Risk, But Struggle to Predict Which Collaboration Protocol Pays Off: Cost-Aware Protocol Routing Across Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Chih-Hsuan Yang, Jingyan Jiang, Cheng-Hau Yang, Vikram Vasudevan, Huihuo Zheng, Venkatram Vishwanath, Rajeev Thakur

entry.summary: Holds the solver fixed and runs every problem under four collaboration protocols, from direct solving to self-correction, planner-executor-reviewer, and multi-agent deliberation, over thousands of competition math problems plus science benchmarks. Trained and frozen LLM routers can predict failure risk but struggle to predict which protocol will actually repay its extra cost, and conservative policies under-escalate.

entry.title: Trust Is Not Enough: Influence Calibration for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Agentic RL

author.name: Qizhen Lan, Xi Xiao, Xiangchen Guan, Mengchen Fan, Moule Lin, Jung Im Choi, Lijing Zhu

entry.summary: Argues that on-policy self-distillation for agents allocates token-level supervision by teacher trust, which does not indicate whether emphasizing a token actually helps the RL objective. The proposed influence calibration measures the first-order response of each token importance-weighted surrogate contribution to a teacher-directed perturbation and converts it into a bounded, batch-adaptive weight.

entry.title: S2-MoE: Enabling Efficient Self-Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts on Edge Devices

author.name: Haochen Huang, Shengxuan Qiu, Meng Li

entry.summary: S2-MoE is a self-speculative decoding framework for mixture-of-experts models on memory-constrained edge devices, using routing-aware adaptive speculative expansion, reuse-aware expert gating, and shared draft and target context. It is implemented in a widely used local inference runtime.

entry.title: SCOPE: Score-Isolated Agentic Optimization for Video World Models

author.name: Yuhua Jiang, Jiaming Wang, Qingbin Liu, Feifei Gao

entry.summary: SCOPE provides auditable inference-time adaptation of frozen video world models by representing prompts, samplers, verifiers, and selectors as typed state that may only be updated through bounded changes justified by development-set evidence, then freezing the policy before held-out evaluation. It reports a meaningful improvement over the frozen base on a physics understanding benchmark.

entry.title: ReForge: Keeping ABR Algorithms Never Finished with Verified Large Language Model Edits

author.name: Zhiqiang He, Zhi Liu

entry.summary: ReForge uses an LLM in a loop to continually redesign adaptive bitrate streaming heuristics, proposing one small edit per round while formally checking that each change does not regress previously served network scenarios. It frames algorithm design as never finished, adapting in minutes as new deployment conditions appear.

entry.title: Understanding Cognition-Induced Risks in Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Guanchu Wang, Qinuo Li, Mengnan Du, Xia Hu, Bowen Zhou

entry.summary: A conceptual risk taxonomy for agentic systems organized by cognitive scope, moving from physical to social to self-referential cognition, and mapping each level to threats against human agency, autonomy and control. It closes with proposed mitigation and controllability strategies.

entry.title: Toward AI-Friendly Cartography: Understanding How Color Design Influences Foundation Model Spatial Reasoning on Sequential Choropleth Maps

author.name: Yonghe Sun, Zhenjia Liu, Hua Liao, Wenjia Xu, Nai Yang, Weihua Dong, Zhiwei Wei

entry.summary: Builds a controlled benchmark of thousands of sequential choropleth maps and tens of thousands of questions to test how hue, color ordering and lightness contrast affect multimodal foundation model spatial reasoning, evaluating 21 models. Hue choice matters little, but breaking sequential color ordering sharply degrades comparison and ranking accuracy.

entry.title: Trajectory-Level Automatic Curriculum Learning for Legged Locomotion on Unstructured Terrain

author.name: Rocky Liu, Tengyu Liu, Baoxiong Jia, Fangwei Zhong, Xinyi Tong, Hongzhao Xie, Siyuan Huang

entry.summary: This work proposes trajectory-level automatic curriculum learning for legged locomotion, generating training tasks directly from unstructured terrain maps instead of heuristically parameterized terrain families. A learned evaluator estimates per-trajectory difficulty relative to the current policy, so the curriculum adapts rather than following a fixed ordering. The goal is better generalization on terrain that has no natural difficulty axis.

entry.title: Competing at Every Price Point with Agentic Evolution over a Menu of LLMs

author.name: Andrew Borthwick

entry.summary: RoboPhD is an evolutionary meta-agent that, given a priced menu of nine LLM endpoints, a task description, and a per-problem cost target, evolves complete agent programs to beat competitor accuracy at each price point using training pools of at most one hundred examples. The framing is economic: Pareto-dominating rivals across the whole cost-accuracy curve. It shows cost-aware program search can substitute for larger models.

entry.title: What Does Context Compression Cost an Agent? Interaction Costs Unrevealed by Task-Completion Metrics

author.name: Shuyu Liu

entry.summary: This study argues task-completion metrics hide the true cost of context compression, and introduces a runtime protocol measuring how often an agent must reacquire state that compression discarded. Across three models and two task regimes with a fixed 24-turn horizon, retrieval tool calls rose in all six model-regime combinations even when completion rates looked unchanged. It suggests compression evaluations should report interaction cost alongside success.

entry.title: FabriMAE I Trust Myself? Self-Evaluating VLA Action Generation with Markov Attention Entropy

author.name: Aniri, Chen Yilin, Jinhe Bi, Junfei Guo, Donglai Ran, Xu Bian, Zengjie Jin, Yujun Wang, Yijun Tian, Volker Tresp, Fei Shen, Tat-Seng Chua, Yunpu Ma

entry.summary: The paper observes that internal visual-modality attention entropy separates successful from failed episodes consistently across architecturally different vision-language-action models, and uses this shared internal signal to let policies self-evaluate action reliability without expert labels. It argues a common latent action-generation abstraction underlies heterogeneous VLA designs. This enables label-free failure detection in robot policies.

entry.title: GRIP: Grounded Reasoning via Information-Restricted Premises

author.name: Lirui Teng

entry.summary: GRIP tackles query dominance in retrieval-augmented generation, where a high-capacity encoder lets the query overwhelm retrieved evidence, by imposing capacity asymmetry: full access to the query but a severe stochastic bottleneck on evidence so it only carries residual information. Reported results include large reductions in a query-latent mutual information diagnostic alongside accuracy gains on reasoning benchmarks. The information-theoretic framing is the notable part.

entry.title: When Agents Coordinate: Measuring Coordination in Multi-Agent AI Coding

author.name: Giuseppe Destefanis, Tomaso Aste

entry.summary: This study instruments 1,902 multi-agent coding runs as temporal networks in which agents and files are nodes and messages, reads, and writes are timestamped cost-weighted edges, then examines how coordination changes with team size, structure, and file policy. It measures the internal coordination that task-success-and-cost evaluations ignore. The instrument itself is the contribution.

entry.title: DeMTS: Denoising Trajectories as Multivariate Time Series for Hallucination Detection in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xin Zhang, Yili Wang, Yue Tan, Xin He, Yanyu Qian, Yixin Liu, Yi Chang, Shirui Pan, Xin Wang

entry.summary: DeMTS detects hallucinations in diffusion language models by treating the full two-dimensional denoising trajectory over tokens and steps as a multivariate time series, rather than compressing it along one axis as prior methods do. This preserves patterns such as inconsistent convergence and cross-token fault propagation. It is one of the first hallucination detectors tailored to the diffusion text generation paradigm.

entry.title: Valid Per-Field Selective Risk Control for Document Extraction: Three Failure Modes, a Validity Ladder, and When Conditioning Pays

author.name: Bhaskar Gurram

entry.summary: The paper shows that naive per-field accept-or-review procedures for document extraction silently violate their selective risk guarantee, diagnosing three causes on nearly 14,000 extracted fields from receipts processed by an existing model: document-level clustering inflating variance, leakage from refitting scores, and a degenerate tie-mass score that collapses the threshold grid. It then organizes fixes as a validity ladder with a guarantee stated per tier. This is a rigorous treatment of trust contracts in extraction pipelines.

entry.title: PolyComp: A Polycube-based Benchmark for Compositional 3D Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Models

author.name: Siddharth Patel

entry.summary: PolyComp is a procedurally generated benchmark of 120 polycube assembly problems, each presented in three formats, that requires recognizing which pair of 3D components combine into a target solid. Frontier systems including GPT-5.6 Sol at maximum effort reach only about 50 percent accuracy against a 25 percent guessing baseline, with Claude Fable 5 lower, exposing a persistent compositional spatial reasoning gap.

entry.title: SpIn-ViT: Designing a Sparsity-Induced Vision Transformer That Is Mechanistically Interpretable

author.name: Philip H. Lee, Parth Padalkar

entry.summary: SpIn-ViT jointly trains a vision transformer with a modified sparse autoencoder end-to-end so that sparse features are aligned with the classification objective, rather than fitting an SAE post-hoc to frozen representations. The learned neurons localize semantically coherent image regions while keeping competitive accuracy.

entry.title: GaussMemory: Task-Driven 3D Gaussian Scene Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zhiqiang Hu, Shouren Huang, Masatoshi Ishikawa

entry.summary: GaussMemory turns 3D Gaussian scene memory into an active, task-driven module that learns which objects to track precisely, how aggressively to update them, and what to discard, instead of applying fixed hand-crafted storage rules. It targets long-horizon robotic manipulation where persistent spatial memory determines success.

entry.title: SysEvolve: An AI-native, safe, autonomous adversarial attack-defense co-evolutionary system

author.name: Yuhan Meng, Shaofei Li, Jionghao Huang, Jiandong Jin, Puyi Wang, Hanlin Jiang, Anis Yusof, Peng Jiang, Zhenkai Liang, Yao Guo, Ding Li

entry.summary: SysEvolve argues that cybersecurity's attacker-defender asymmetry persists because evolution has stalled on both sides, and proposes a co-evolutionary system in which attack and defense LLM agents safely drive each other's improvement through repeated adversarial confrontation. It comprises a cyber-range environment component plus paired offensive and defensive agent frameworks.

entry.title: Scale-Consistent Posterior Dynamics for Diffusion Inverse Problems

author.name: Zhaoqiang Liu, Tongyao Pang, Ruibing Wang, Yang Zheng

entry.summary: Develops a principled posterior sampling scheme for diffusion inverse problems by starting from a one-parameter family of posterior SDEs that share marginals, then deriving tractable likelihood proxies in rescaled clean-image coordinates organized by log-SNR. The result is a noise-conditioned covariance path whose targets converge to the clean posterior with attention to transport consistency, not just endpoint matching.

entry.title: Spectral Saliency for Machine Unlearning

author.name: Cedar Site Bai, Amber Yijia Zheng, Raymond A. Yeh, Brian Bullins

entry.summary: Borrows the spectral normalization idea behind the Muon optimizer to design a machine unlearning method that thresholds weak singular components and updates only directions with confident forget signal. The paper adds theoretical analysis alongside the algorithm.

entry.title: Do Assessment Instruments Measure the Same Thing for Humans and LLMs? A Latent Structure Analysis

author.name: Alona Strugatski, Licol Zeinfeld, Giora Alexandron

entry.summary: Applies psychometric latent-structure analysis to ask whether human-designed assessments measure the same underlying constructs when administered to language models. The finding that the latent structure differs undermines the common practice of interpreting model exam scores as evidence of human-like abilities.

entry.title: Beyond Visual CoT: Internalized Visual Thinking for Proactive Video Reasoning

author.name: Xiaoyu Zhu, Xinke Deng, Suresh Taddewadikar, Arnab Kumar Mondal, Zhongyu Jiang, Ian Fasel, Joerg Liebelt

entry.summary: Argues that generating intermediate images for visual chain-of-thought is too slow for proactive video reasoning, and instead trains models to predict latent representations of future frames alongside text during post-training on unlabeled video. At inference the model reasons directly in text while retaining the benefits of learned visual foresight.

entry.title: CAPO: Constraint-Aware Prompt Optimization for LLM Agents

author.name: Victor Ye Dong, Reid Pryzant, Yi Liu, Jian Jiao

entry.summary: Frames system-prompt engineering for tool-using agents as constrained optimization and proposes a primal-dual method that combines pooled rewrites with adaptive constraint weighting to satisfy operational requirements like tool discipline, brevity, and policy compliance. It targets practitioners who cannot assemble supervised data for post-training.

entry.title: Understanding and Stabilizing Deep Q-Learning via Controlled Bootstrapping and Regulated Value Dynamics

author.name: Bozhou Chen, Yongyi Wang, Hanyu Liu, Xionghui Yang, Wenxin Li

entry.summary: This paper offers a unified diagnosis of deep Q-learning instability across three levels: operator bias in Bellman bootstrapping, sensitivity of greedy action selection to regression noise, and parameter-dynamics imbalance under high replay ratios. It identifies a reward-triggered self-reinforcing failure mode and proposes controlled bootstrapping with regulated value dynamics to stabilize training.

entry.title: OceanDepths: A Global Dataset of Paired Subsurface and Surface Ocean Observations

author.name: Simon Donike, Ruben Cartuyvels, Antonino Ian Ferola, Elisa Carli, Diego Fernandez Prieto, Marie-Helene Rio

entry.summary: OceanDepths pairs satellite-derived surface fields such as sea surface temperature and salinity with co-located in situ depth profiles in a regridded, globally distributed, AI-ready format. It targets the absence of standardized observation-based datasets linking ocean surface signals to subsurface structure at mesoscale-relevant resolution.

entry.title: NebulaVLA: A Dual-Frequency Vision-Language-Action Model With Guide Action for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Cong Zhao, Shuai Tian, Xu Zhang, Baocheng Ni, Xinguo Song, Xueying Sun, Shu Jiang, Shouchang Yang, Bo Tang, Jin Deng, Ge Zhu, YongCheng Wang, Jin Xu, Ri Yang

entry.summary: NebulaVLA is an asynchronous dual-frequency vision-language-action architecture that runs high-level semantic reasoning and low-level action control at different rates, adds a unified language-grounded action vocabulary for cross-embodiment transfer, and enforces kinematic continuity through mask-based smoothness constraints. It reports an average manipulation success rate of about 85 percent, outperforming synchronous baselines.

entry.title: When Do Explanations Help In-Context Learning? A Comparative Study of Natural Language Explanation Types and Faithfulness

author.name: Mahdi Dhaini, Adam Dejl, Juraj Vladika, Volkan \"Ozer, Barbara Plank, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: This comparative study evaluates how the source of natural language explanations (human-written, self-generated, or from an external LLM) and their selection (random versus faithfulness-filtered) affect downstream in-context learning across six benchmarks and four instruction-tuned models. It reports that adding explanations to few-shot prompts helps unevenly, particularly on classification-style tasks.

entry.title: Randomly initialized autoencoders: fixed points and edge-of-chaos

author.name: Leonid Berlyand, Roman Sarapin, Yitzchak Shmalo, Victor Slavin, Sasha Sodin

entry.summary: Analyzes randomly initialized autoencoders through the existence, stability, and basins of attraction of their fixed points, connecting contractivity properties to the edge-of-chaos regime that separates ordered from chaotic signal propagation. The paper places autoencoder behavior at initialization within established deep network mean-field theory.

entry.title: Discrete Diffusion Language Models Are Training-Free Multi-Label Classifiers

author.name: Pawan Kumar

entry.summary: Shows that masked discrete diffusion language models can serve as training-free multi-label text classifiers by asking a short yes/no question per label and comparing answer-token probabilities at a single masked position. The paper also documents a severe slot-position asymmetry when all labels appear in one prompt, motivating per-label scoring to equalize syntactic position.

entry.title: Decision-Driven Regularization: A Blended Model for Learning and Optimization

author.name: Gar Goei Loke, Qinshen Tang, Yangge Xiao, Xun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes decision-driven regularization for contextual optimization, a bi-objective blend that controls prediction accuracy alongside decision quality after observing that purely integrated learning-and-optimization can overfit and underperform simple separate estimate-then-optimize pipelines. Applications span delivery, retail, portfolio, and inventory decisions.

entry.title: Earth Observation Foundation Models for Terrestrial Ecohydrology: From Representation Learning to Process Inference

author.name: Yi Yu, Jian Peng, Yucheng Lin, Trevor F. Keenan, Thomas F. A. Bishop

entry.summary: A synthesis assessing when Earth observation foundation models actually support interpretable process inference in terrestrial ecohydrology, developing an observation-to-inference hierarchy and identifying mismatches between what these models provide and what coupled water, energy, and carbon modeling requires under uncertain reference data, scale mismatch, and temporal dependence. It sets out evaluation requirements rather than proposing a new model.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Nonparametric Change-Point Detection via Low-Rank Degree-Three Density Projection

author.name: Guoqing Zhang, Zhaixin Chen

entry.summary: Develops a nonparametric high-dimensional change-point detection method that retains all degree-at-most-three density coefficients via a symmetric order-three Legendre feature tensor, giving an exact isometric encoding of the degree-three density projection without estimating densities directly. This detects distributional shifts in skewness and asymmetric interactions that mean and covariance monitoring miss.

entry.title: In Defense of OCTA: The Reconstruction-Utility Gap in OCT-to-OCTA Synthesis

author.name: Michael Chertok, Alon Tiosano, Orly Gal-Or, Lior Kramarski, Einav Baharav Shlezinger, Irit Bahar, Lior Wolf

entry.summary: Shows that OCT-to-OCTA image synthesis methods with excellent pixel-level reconstruction scores fail on the clinical measurements OCTA is actually acquired for: a frozen real-data segmenter loses far more accuracy on fine capillaries than on large vessels. Introduces a reconstruction-utility gap framing for evaluating medical image synthesis.

entry.title: SubZero+: Efficient Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning via Large Learning Rates

author.name: Ziming Yu, Shuyao Xiao, Xingyu Zhao, Sike Wang, Pan Zhou, Peiyu Zang, Xiangda Yan, Yongjie Yang, Jia Li

entry.summary: SubZero+ improves zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning stability with multi-query gradient estimation inside layer-specific low-rank subspaces, a subspace Adam variant, and a sign correction ensuring properly distributed random projections. The aim is backprop-free adaptation that tolerates larger learning rates.

entry.title: Beat the Counter First: A Baseline for Temporal-Graph Anomaly Detectors

author.name: Omair Shafi Ahmed, Zohair Shafi

entry.summary: Proposes SimpleCount, a parameter-free reference that picks a single scalar count- or recency-derived feature per dataset, and shows it matches or beats sophisticated streaming graph anomaly detectors on several public datasets. Argues that architectural complexity in this area has not been justified empirically.

entry.title: DeepOHeat-v2: Self-Improving Operator Learning for Fast and Trustworthy Thermal Optimization in 3D-IC Design

author.name: Xinling Yu, Yixing Li, Ziyue Liu, Xin Ai, Zhiyu Zeng, Hai Li, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: DeepOHeat-v2 extends physics-trained operator surrogates for 3D-IC thermal simulation to high-contrast multi-die stacks, replacing the ill-defined continuous physics loss at material interfaces with a discretized loss and addressing severe ill-conditioning that defeats first-order optimizers. Enables fast, label-free thermal optimization in chip design.

entry.title: A Privacy Study of Sparse Collaborative Inference

author.name: Maximilian Andreas Hoefler, Karsten Mueller, Wojciech Samek

entry.summary: Tests the common claim that sparsifying transmitted activations improves privacy in split edge-server inference by separately reconstructing inputs from the retained values and from the sparsity pattern (positions) alone. Finds that the position mask itself leaks substantial input information, undermining sparsity-as-privacy arguments.

entry.title: SCALE: State-Calibrated Latent Embeddings for JEPA Planning in the Right Geometry

author.name: Jiaming Hu, Yan Zheng, Tian Wang

entry.summary: Analyzes why joint-embedding world models plan differently depending on whether the latent space is inherited from a pretrained encoder (DINO-WM) or learned end-to-end with anti-collapse regularization, showing that Euclidean planning costs are dominated by high-variance principal directions. SCALE calibrates latent embeddings so that planning happens in a geometry aligned with task-relevant state.

entry.title: Training Leaves Traces: Centered Residual Signatures for Language Model Lineage Verification

author.name: Aman Singh Thakur, Rayan Khoury

entry.summary: Studies data-free white-box lineage verification, asking whether weights alone reveal shared ancestry between two compatible checkpoints, and shows that the identity-aligned component induced by residual training must be removed before comparison. The resulting centered residual signature score separates fine-tuned, LoRA-merged, pruned, and quantized descendants from independent and distilled models with perfect AUROC on residual-MLP and GPT-2 benchmarks.

entry.title: RecurrentGPT: Expressive Depth through Recurrent Modulation in Transformers

author.name: Amr Hegazy, Amr Alanwar, Mostafa Elhoushi

entry.summary: RecurrentGPT is a recurrent-depth transformer where fixed prelude and coda blocks bracket a single shared core iterated multiple times, with a lightweight gated update inspired by gated recurrent networks conditioned on the hidden state, the prelude output, and resampled noise. The aim is to recover the representational diversity that naive layer sharing destroys while keeping the memory savings of weight tying.

entry.title: The Distributional View of Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Gordei Verbii, Juho Lee

entry.summary: Reframes token-level knowledge distillation as matching distributions rather than comparing them pointwise, representing the teacher by a family of multi-temperature views along its logit annealing path and training the student against a geometry-aware aggregate under an embedding-based ground cost. Explores mixtures, log-linear pooling, entropic Wasserstein barycenters, and a debiased Sinkhorn flagship, with a collapse theorem characterizing when the design degenerates.

entry.title: The Null Token Knows: Reducing Message-Free Hallucination in ASR and NMT

author.name: Kirill Borodin, Vasiliy Kudryavtsev, Ivan Viakhirev

entry.summary: Studies whether the reserved end-of-generation or null token in speech recognizers and translation models already encodes an abstention signal that could suppress fluent output when the input contains no message. Finds a usable signal exists in models such as Whisper but that standard decoding ignores it, and that aggressive null-token boosting deletes legitimate speech.

entry.title: Architecture-Dependent Causal Transfer of Activation States Across Large Language Models

author.name: Fernando Cardenas Piepereit

entry.summary: Tests whether internal activation states can be transferred between architecturally different LLMs through a learned projection, evaluating representational similarity, cross-model retrieval, and end-to-end causal effects from activation injection during generation. Uses four small open-weight models and finds alignment above a random-initialization baseline, with transfer success depending strongly on architecture.

entry.title: Bootstrapping Niche Multilingual Code Translation via Reinforcement Learning with Execution-Based Verifiable Supervision

author.name: Kouki Yuki, Jie Zeng, Kyoko Ogawa, Ryunosuke Ikeda, Yohei Kobashi, Takeshi Kojima, Ikuya Yamada, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: Bootstraps many-to-many code translation for less common programming languages by expanding verifiable Python seeds into an execution-validated multilingual pool, labeling model-generated translations by execution outcome, and training a reward model for preference-based reinforcement learning. Addresses the scarcity of parallel supervision that otherwise yields plausible but non-executable translations.

entry.title: How Much Do Legal RAG Systems Still Hallucinate?

author.name: Souvick Das, Sallam Abualhaija, Domenico Bianculli

entry.summary: Conducts a fine-grained audit of hallucination in eight legal retrieval-augmented generation systems across GDPR text in English and a French national civil code, scoring at both claim and answer level. Hallucination rates range from under ten percent for the best systems to much higher elsewhere, with validation on 142 expert-authored questions.

entry.title: You Only Pass Once: Answering and Abstaining Together in a Single Forward Pass of a Frozen Language Model

author.name: Ziyang Luo, Zhongyao Chu, Xinjie He, Youting Wang, Xukui Qin, Runxiong Wu, Yan-Syuan Chen

entry.summary: Combines two activation-space interventions on a frozen LLM: a steering probe that improves reasoning by writing to the residual stream, and a direction that reads the stream to decide when to abstain. The paper shows the two interfere when run together and proposes a way to answer and abstain in a single forward pass.

entry.title: Xemo-Talker: Unlock Emotions Explicitly for Audio-Driven Talking Portrait Synthesis

author.name: Chaolong Yang, Yinuo Guo, Kai Yao, Yuyao Yan, Jie Sun, Guangliang Cheng, Shibin Wu, Bin Dong, Kaizhu Huang

entry.summary: An audio-driven talking-head system that gains finer emotion control by concentrating explicit emotion supervision on lower-variance components of the motion space, leaving principal components to handle articulation and pose. This resolves part of the usual tradeoff between lip sync accuracy and expressive control.

entry.title: Do Visual Grounding Decoders Need Feed-Forward Networks? A Controlled Study over Frozen Vision-Language Features

author.name: Tarun Tomar

entry.summary: A controlled ablation asking whether feed-forward layers are needed in visual grounding decoders built on frozen vision-language features, comparing attention-only, attention-plus-FFN, and deeper attention-only variants. Attention-only decoders match or nearly match while cutting trainable parameters by 44 percent and latency by 10 percent.

entry.title: Scalable Black-Box Model Attribution for Images

author.name: Asaf Livne, Amir Jevnisek, Shai Avidan

entry.summary: RPA shows that attributing an image to the generative model that produced it can be done in the strict black-box setting with a small CNN on raw patches, reaching around 98 percent on a 25-class benchmark and 93 percent on a 27-class one. It is data-efficient, robust to compression, blur and resizing, and its cost does not grow with the number of candidate models.

entry.title: Beyond Uncertainty: Generalizable Failure Monitoring for Surgical Segmentation under Acquisition Degradation

author.name: Hieu D. Pham, Dang P. M. Cao, Thanh Trung Huynh

entry.summary: TCSR-Monitor is a post-hoc failure monitor for surgical segmentation that supplements confidence with shape, temporal consistency, and image-quality cues, so it can catch confidently wrong masks under image degradation. It wraps a frozen model, needs no internals or ground truth at deployment, and is validated with a leave-one-corruption-out protocol.

entry.title: SingDance: Compositional Zero-Shot Singing-and-Dancing Video Generation with Role-Aware Audio Conditioning

author.name: Tao Feng, Xu Li, Xiangyang Luo, Ming Wen, Huadai Liu, Chen Zhang, Wei Xue

entry.summary: SingDance is a video diffusion framework for generating singing-and-dancing videos where the visible subject must both move to the music and articulate the vocals, treating the subject as either the vocal source or a listener. Role-aware conditioning and hard-compact routing select task-relevant pathways for this combined setting.

entry.title: Detachable Wire Drive : Reconfigurable Robot Architecture with Shared Actuators

author.name: Takahiro Hattori, Kento Kawaharazuka, Kei Okada

entry.summary: The Detachable Wire Drive lets a reconfigurable robot share heavy, expensive actuators across morphologies by physically splitting and reconnecting wire drive paths through a Wire Detach Unit. The authors demonstrate a rigid 2-DOF arm, a continuum arm, and additional configurations from a common actuator base.

entry.title: Co-design of Neural and Muscle Network based on Embodied Perceptron Representation

author.name: Siyuan Tao, Yoichi Masuda, Hiroyuki Nabae, Masato Ishikawa

entry.summary: Introduces the Embodied Perceptron, a framework that treats a robot's physical body as a computational layer analogous to a neural network layer, enabling joint theoretical optimization of morphology and controller. It aims to replace expert intuition in body design with a systematic co-design method.

entry.title: Position: Evaluations of AI Moral Reasoning Still Miss Half of the Picture

author.name: Aidan Kierans, Ritam Dutt, Kaley Rittichier, Shiri Dori-Hacohen, Avijit Ghosh

entry.summary: Argues that evaluations of LLM moral competence overwhelmingly test whether outputs match human values while neglecting whether models can identify and apply context-sensitive moral norms. The authors trace this imbalance to reliance on descriptive ethics frameworks and call for benchmarks grounded in normative ethics.

entry.title: Do LLM Agents Negotiate Rationally? A Mechanism-Design Framework for Verifiable Multi-Agent Interaction over A2A/MCP

author.name: Wael Albayaydh, Rui Zhao

entry.summary: Encodes classical negotiation mechanisms such as alternating-offers bargaining and Vickrey-Clarke-Groves auctions as constraints over agent-to-agent message schemas, adds a runtime verification and repair layer, and benchmarks whether LLM agents negotiate rationally. The point is that current agent protocols standardize transport and discovery but guarantee nothing about strategic correctness.

entry.title: From Errors to Proofs: Minimal-Core-Guided Repair for Neuro-Symbolic Constraint Solving

author.name: Dipankar Sarkar

entry.summary: Improves LLM translation of natural-language constraint problems into formal specifications by returning a minimal unsatisfiable core when the generated program is unsatisfiable, instead of a raw solver error message. The core pinpoints the exact conflicting constraints, giving a leakage-free repair signal that also covers programs that run but encode the wrong problem.

entry.title: Gathered, Not Admitted: How Attention Brings a Latent Variable into Verbalizable Form

author.name: Parsa Mazaheri

entry.summary: Investigates what causes a latent quantity inside a language model to become reportable, testing the intuitive idea that a gate admits representations into a global workspace. Using Jacobian-based lenses on open-weight models with five task arms sharing identical context, the authors find no gate where the workspace account predicts one, but do find that task demand for flexible reuse raises a concept visibility.

entry.title: SkillCommit: Evolving Agent Skills through Behaviorally Validated Scope Expansion

author.name: Yu He, Weikai Yang

entry.summary: SkillCommit builds a hierarchical, growing skill library for LLM agents by first storing each experience as an instance-specific patch and only abstracting skills once several share validated behavior. This avoids merging superficially similar but behaviorally incompatible strategies, a known failure of similarity-based experience consolidation.

entry.title: EcoVLA: Energy-Efficient Device-Edge Co-Inference for Vision-Language-Action Models under Real-Time Constraints

author.name: Ao Zhou, Bo Dai, Le Yu, Xingyu Liu, Zeyu Hao, Lingkun Long, Chunming Hu, Jianlei Yang

entry.summary: EcoVLA splits vision-language-action model inference between robot hardware and an edge server to jointly meet real-time control deadlines and energy budgets, adapting to fluctuating network and system conditions. It targets the gap between on-device compute limits and unpredictable offloading latency.

entry.title: Large Models for Small Devices: Recent Advances and Empirical Analysis of Edge AI Deployment

author.name: Subhransu Das, Jiaming Cheng, Arnav Kumar, Sadia Afrose, Mingzhe Han, Michael Silagy, Shreya Palande, Brijesh Soni, Rajiv Ramnath

entry.summary: Surveys recent edge-deployment results for compressed models and then empirically deploys compact language and vision models on GPU, CPU and Raspberry Pi for question answering and segmentation. Finds no single compression technique dominates, with quantization and structured pruning trading places depending on the task.

entry.title: HyMem: Hierarchical Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents via Information Isolation

author.name: XinQi Wang, Jinwei Xiao, Sijia Cui, Hongming Zhang, Yanna Wang, Qingyang Zhang, Bo Xu

entry.summary: HyMem organizes a long-horizon agent's context into distinct functional layers so that high-level plans are isolated from verbose execution traces and intermediate tool outputs, rather than compressing one flat context. The goal is to prevent planning information from being drowned out as interactions accumulate.

entry.title: RLCascadeRouter: Quality-Estimator-Free Cascade Routing via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shihong Huang, Shengjie Wang, Hong Ma, Zhou Xu

entry.summary: Learns cascade routing policies with reinforcement learning directly on routing decisions, avoiding the usual predict-then-optimize pipeline where a quality estimator's prediction error does not align with routing loss. The router decides after each observed response whether to stop or escalate to another model.

entry.title: Augmenting Text to Increase Translation Difficulty

author.name: William Kalikman, \v{S}imon Sukup, Michal Te\v{s}nar, Vil\'em Zouhar

entry.summary: Proposes adversarially rewriting translation benchmark sentences to be harder, using gradients from a differentiable difficulty estimator combined with a fluency objective and beam search over candidate token substitutions. Offers a prompting-free alternative to LLM-based or human benchmark construction as machine translation saturates existing test sets.

entry.title: Navigation-Informed Embeddings: Dense-Retriever Adaptation from Agent Search Traces

author.name: Shrey Shah, Levent Ozgur

entry.summary: Turns the byproduct traces of agentic retrieval, namely queries, retrieved documents and stopping points, into training signal for adapting a deployed dense retriever without new relevance labels or LLM judgments. The stopping document becomes a soft positive and path documents provide ordinal hard comparisons, improving recall on an independent target benchmark.

entry.title: Defake-o3: From Speculative Rationales to Verifiable Evidence for Explainable AIGI Detection

author.name: Bowen Deng, Jiahui Zhan, Yikun Ji, Haozhen Yan, Jianfu Zhang

entry.summary: Defake-o3 detects AI-generated images while producing visually verifiable evidence, combining interactive zoom-in visual search with an evidence verifier that penalizes speculative or hallucinated artifact claims. The aim is to move multimodal detectors from plausible-sounding rationales toward auditable localized evidence.

entry.title: Contrastive Energy Fields for Inference-Time Procedure Planning in Instructional Videos

author.name: Mohamed Afham, Christoph Reich, Oliver Hahn, Daniel Cremers, Stefan Roth

entry.summary: CEFITO learns an action-conditioned representation space and casts procedure planning in instructional videos as a task-constrained optimization at inference time using contrastive energy fields, instead of directly regressing action sequences with feed-forward or diffusion models. This lets the planner reject actions that are implausible for the task rather than treating all actions as viable.

entry.title: Graph Machine Learning: An Opportunity for Power Systems

author.name: Martin Sadric, Sebastian P\"utz, Christian Nauck, Veit Hagenmeyer, Frank Hellmann, Dirk Witthaut, Benjamin Sch\"afer

entry.summary: This survey reviews nearly 800 papers at the intersection of graph machine learning and power systems, spanning forecasting, state estimation, optimization, and control, and argues that grid topology makes graph inductive biases a natural fit where physics-based solvers are too slow for real-time operation. It maps opportunities and open challenges for grid applications.

entry.title: Matched Outcomes, Divergent Gaze: How Foveated MLLMs Search Compared to Humans

author.name: Mohamed Amine Kerkouri, Marouane Tliba, Aladine Chetouani, Ulas Bagci, Alessandro Bruno

entry.summary: The authors drive three general-purpose multimodal LLMs fixation by fixation through human-matched foveated views on a goal-directed search benchmark and compare outcomes with human eye-movement scanpaths. Models match or exceed humans on target-presence decisions and acquisition efficiency, yet their gaze trajectories diverge from human scanpaths, dissociating outcome from process.

entry.title: Listen, Reason, and Segment: Aligning LALMs with Editorial Judgment for Media Chapterization

author.name: Tony Alex, Wish Suharitdamrong, Sara Atito, Armin Mustafa, Muhammad Awais, Philip J. B. Jackson, Jiankang Deng, Ismail Elezi

entry.summary: AudioChaps is a post-training framework that aligns large audio language models with editorial judgment for segmenting long audio into thematically coherent chapters, a task where boundaries reflect subjective creator decisions rather than acoustic events. It targets a commercially relevant media workflow gap that standardized audio benchmarks do not expose.

entry.title: Learning to Unlearn: Machine Unlearning via Learning the Unlearning Behaviors

author.name: Hang Zhang, Kaifeng Zhang, Yixiao Ma, Weijie Xu, Ye Zhu, Kai Ming Ting

entry.summary: Instead of designing an increasingly intricate unlearning function, this paper learns to imitate unlearning behavior, treating the mapping toward a retrained model as something a model can learn, so that removal does not require expensive bespoke procedures on massive training sets. The goal is to approximate retrained-model behavior at lower computational cost.

entry.title: GoalEvolve: From Handcrafted Algorithm Priors to Goal-Driven Evolution of Physical Design Algorithms

author.name: Haixu Liu, Lei Zhou, Yuhao Ren, Yumao Wu, Zhiang Wang

entry.summary: GoalEvolve makes LLM-driven evolution of chip physical design algorithms accountable to end-of-flow quality of results rather than stage-local objectives, converting unmet multi-objective targets into normalized gaps, identifying the dominant bottleneck, and using stage-resolved checkpoint evidence to direct the next iteration. This addresses cases where stage-local gains vanish or hurt downstream stages.

entry.title: LUNG-KGMM: Knowledge-Guided Multimodal Learning for Lung Cancer Incidence Prediction

author.name: Chunlei Yang, Shuyan Li, Zhong Cao

entry.summary: LUNG-KGMM predicts one-to-six-year incident lung cancer by combining longitudinal electronic health records, radiology reports, chest radiograph features, and guideline-derived knowledge graphs, with a leakage-sanitized report pipeline and a horizon-masked cumulative training objective for censored follow-up. The design targets both modality heterogeneity and label leakage risks.

entry.title: Spectral Rank Certification for Foundation Model Adapters

author.name: Mohammed Ahnouch, Lotfi Elaachak

entry.summary: Develops a finite-sample statistical framework for inferring the effective rank of public foundation-model LoRA adapters, distinguishing nominal rank as a design choice from calibrated spectral evidence. It derives an exact chi-square divergence for a rank-one Gaussian reference experiment, a computable Le Cam bound at realistic layer sizes, remainder bounds for truncation, and connects to the rectangular BBP transition.

entry.title: FAST-DeepONet: Factor-Augmented Branch Representations for High-Dimensional PDE Inputs in the Small-Sample Regime

author.name: Jiyong Kwon, Bongseok Kim, Guang Lin

entry.summary: FAST-DeepONet stabilizes deep operator networks when PDE inputs are sampled at thousands of highly correlated sensors but few operator samples exist, combining a fixed spectral branch path with a regularized projection of the orthogonal residual under row-normalized directional penalties. On Navier-Stokes flow it holds error near 0.04 as branch dimension grows from 129 to 8193, where a plain DeepONet degrades from 0.0394 to 0.1556.

entry.title: Second-Moment Memory in Coordinatewise Adam

author.name: Jeonseong Kim

entry.summary: Shows theoretically that the long memory in Adam's second-moment denominator can itself slow progress, deriving an order-M2 to the minus one half bound on expected positive normalized updates and converting it into an average-stationarity lower bound on a smooth convex problem. Suggests long second-moment memory hurts even with well-behaved gradient noise.

entry.title: When Tool-Backed Skill Retrieval Fails: Source-Style Collapse in Executable Capability Retrieval

author.name: Yiqi Liu, Joseph James, Yang Wang, Chenghao Xiao, Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: Documents source-style collapse, where a tool-retrieval model fine-tuned on one slice of the ToolRet benchmark fails badly on another slice of the same benchmark even with higher lexical overlap with the gold tools. Shows simple query-side TF-IDF fingerprints predict where the fine-tuned retriever will fail better than semantic or length proxies.

entry.title: DeltaLog: Deferred Materialization of Recurrent States for Linear Attention Decoding

author.name: Junqing Lin, Jingwei Sun, Guangzhong Sun

entry.summary: DeltaLog reduces the memory-traffic cost of decoding in linear-attention models by keeping the recurrent state as a dense base plus a bounded log of compact recent updates, so most decode steps append small factors instead of writing back the full state. The scheme is semantics-preserving and targets models with large states and many heads.

entry.title: Provenance, Not Behaviour: A Serialisation Artifact in Edge-IIoTset and a Leakage-Free Benchmark for Precision-Agriculture Intrusion Detection

author.name: Mostafa M. Galal

entry.summary: Shows that near-perfect published results on the widely used Edge-IIoTset intrusion detection benchmark largely reflect a serialization artifact rather than network behavior: the dataset's own recommended one-hot preprocessing exposes categorical columns whose placeholder spelling, the string zero in the normal branch versus zero point zero in the attack branch, separates classes with perfect accuracy. The authors then offer a leakage-free benchmark for precision-agriculture intrusion detection.

entry.title: Asymmetric Discourse Homogenization and Shared Language Technology: Evidence from Reddit

author.name: Fengming Liu

entry.summary: Analyzes six million Reddit comments from cross-partisan forums to show an ideologically asymmetric interruption of political discourse diversification starting around late 2022, affecting conservative users. Permutation testing over thousands of candidate dates finds no sharp break at the ChatGPT launch, suggesting gradual rather than discrete change.

entry.title: Spatial Attention Noise Masking for Causally Sufficient Interpretability

author.name: Benjamin Formby, Kuang-Ching Wang, D Hudson Smith

entry.summary: Proposes a vision interpretability method that actively masks the input image with learned spatial attention noise before classification, so that explanations are causally sufficient rather than merely correlational. It contrasts with post hoc saliency methods that cannot make strong causal claims.

entry.title: SA-GEM: Scale-Adaptive and Geospatial Evidence-Modulated Token Pruning for Efficient Remote Sensing Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kexin Ma, Jing Xiao, Bowen Xing, Liang Liao, Chia-Wen Lin

entry.summary: A plug-in token pruning framework for remote sensing vision-language models that adapts token granularity to task scale and modulates importance using geospatial evidence cues, targeting the quadratic growth of visual tokens with resolution. It addresses the dilution of sparse but critical evidence in very high-resolution imagery.

entry.title: Perspective-Invariant Attack with Enhanced Transferability of Adversarial Examples

author.name: Kaisheng Liang, Yiming Cao, Bin Xiao

entry.summary: Improves black-box transferability of adversarial examples by adding global perspective transformations, sampling image-corner vertices with multiple degrees of freedom to simulate viewpoint changes during attack generation. Prior input-transformation attacks used only local operations like shuffling and resizing.

entry.title: Boundary-Aligned Contribution Routing for Robust Optical--SAR Object Detection

author.name: Haifa Zhang, Yijing Wang, Haoyu Wang, Zheng Li, Zhiqiang Zuo

entry.summary: Learns task-conditioned routing that regulates how much each of optical and SAR modalities contributes before cross-modal fusion, using only detection supervision. The motivation is that misaligned or mismatched modalities can be conditionally harmful and cause negative cross-modal transfer.

entry.title: FMReward: Aligning and Evaluating Audio-Driven 3D Facial Animation with Human Preferences

author.name: Sijing Wu, Yunhao Li, Zhilin Gao, Huiyu Duan, Yucheng Zhu, Guangtao Zhai, Patrick Le Callet

entry.summary: Introduces FMPair, described as the first human preference dataset for audio-driven 3D facial animation, and trains a perceptual reward model that is used both to evaluate and to fine-tune animation systems. It moves the field away from ground-truth reconstruction error toward preference-aligned optimization.

entry.title: WorldRover: A Scalable Synthetic Video Data Engine for World Exploration with Rich Annotations

author.name: Xiaojie Xu, Zhengyuan Lin, Runyi Li, Yihao Liu, Kaipeng Zhang, Yongtao Ge

entry.summary: WorldRover is an Unreal Engine data engine producing long-range exploration videos of artist-built environments with paired camera trajectories, dense geometry, temporal correspondence and control signals on the same frames. It targets training and evaluating generative or reconstructive world models where real capture cannot supply all these annotations.

entry.title: StreamOPD: A Post-Training Recipe with Spatio-Temporal Cue Gating for Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Keming Wu, Baoyi Wang, Kaichen Zhang, Xiang An, Zuhao Yang, Sudong Wang, Haowei Zhu, Tingxuan Huang, Hongcheng Gao, Bin Wang

entry.summary: StreamOPD is a post-training recipe for streaming video understanding that fixes a memory-free recent-window protocol and shows a training-free sliding window already matches systems with elaborate inference-time memory and retrieval. It combines verifiable streaming data with thinking-mode on-policy distillation, arguing that reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards fits the low-latency streaming regime poorly.

entry.title: Interactive Whole Slide Images for RL-based Tumour Segmentation

author.name: Mohamad Mohamad, Francesco Ponzio, Maxime Gassier, Nicolas Pote, Xavier Descombes

entry.summary: This work formulates gigapixel whole-slide tumour segmentation as a reinforcement learning navigation problem, where a PPO-trained agent moves, zooms, and selects tumour regions in a multi-resolution slide environment. It combines local views with a global thumbnail in an actor-critic architecture instead of exhaustively scoring all patches.

entry.title: OccamView: Object-Conditioned View Selection for Frame-Budgeted Active 3D Gaussian Reconstruction

author.name: Hongbo Gao, Wei Zhang, Zeyu Ni, Dihao Zhu, Ruifeng Li, Yunke Wang, Chang Xu

entry.summary: OccamView selects next-best views for active 3D Gaussian reconstruction under tight frame budgets by conditioning on objects, maintaining an online object memory rather than treating object-occluded regions as generic unexplored space. This prevents budget-limited planners from covering the scene broadly while leaving objects half-reconstructed.

entry.title: Reliable Piezoresistive Strain Sensing Through Physical Limits and Uncertainty Monitoring

author.name: Carmen Ballester, V\'ictor Mu\~noz, Dorin Copaci, Dolores Blanco

entry.summary: This paper argues that probabilistic regressors for soft piezoresistive strain sensors can look confident while operating outside their calibrated range or while internally failing, so confidence alone is not trustworthiness. It pairs a physics-informed probabilistic inverse model with explicit admissibility limits and uncertainty monitoring for control loops.

entry.title: RAPAC-DP: Response-Aligned Pending-Action Compensation for Diffusion Policies under Delayed Execution

author.name: Tao Wang, Wei Wang, Jianhui Wang, Qi Wang, Weidi Huang, Bing Xu

entry.summary: RAPAC-DP compensates for network and compute delays when diffusion or flow-based imitation policies run on remote servers, by conditioning a lightweight adapter on the actions already queued for execution. Training uses delay-conditioned samples synthesized from delay-free demonstrations, and disabling the adapter exactly recovers the base policy.

entry.title: Bounded Agents: Delegation Security for Multi-Agent AI Systems

author.name: Xabier Muruaga

entry.summary: Argues that agent security is fundamentally an authorization architecture problem and introduces an agentic principal chain that tracks delegated authority across principals and sub-agents, evaluating each request against accumulated context rather than in isolation. This bounds harm from prompt injection by limiting what authority an agent can exercise or pass on.

entry.title: GraniKV: Asymmetric Granularity KV-Cache Paging for Multi-Agent Systems with Long Shared Prefix

author.name: Jinhyun Jeon, Sungjoo Yoo

entry.summary: Observes that multi-agent LLM workloads have two opposite KV-cache needs, a long shared prefix wanting contiguity and per-request suffixes wanting fine-grained allocation, and proposes asymmetric paging with separate hot and cold pools plus a per-step backend dispatcher. It is presented as the first asymmetric-granularity KV cache in a production paged serving engine.

entry.title: PL-Guard: Probabilistic Logic Reasoning for LLM Guardrails

author.name: Satchit Chatterji, Shihan Wang, Giovanni Sileno, Erman Acar

entry.summary: Separates the two jobs that safety classifiers usually conflate by having a local model ground policy-relevant predicates from a prompt-response pair, then reasoning over those facts with probabilistic logic rules. The neurosymbolic split is intended to reduce both unsafe compliance and over-refusal while making policies auditable and editable.

entry.title: Robo-Dopamine 2.0: History-Conditioned and OOD-Aware Process Reward Modeling for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yijie Xu, Haopeng Jin, Run Zhou, Shengbang Liu, Sixiang Chen, Hongyang Cheng, Sicheng Hu, Peterson Co, Jinwen Luo, Huajie Tan, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a process reward model for reinforcement-learning refinement of robot manipulation policies that conditions on execution history and explicitly handles out-of-distribution states, using pairwise comparisons rather than static before-and-after snapshots. This aims to distinguish harmless variations from genuine task failures during off-trajectory execution.

entry.title: TinyCast: Probabilistic Zero-Shot Forecasting with Computed Periodicity

author.name: Armin Steinhauser

entry.summary: Introduces an attention-free zero-shot time series forecaster with roughly 147 thousand parameters that computes dominant periods with a zero-parameter spectral detector, folds the context on phase, and decodes quantiles autoregressively. It claims to define the size-versus-probabilistic-accuracy frontier on a public forecasting leaderboard among entries declaring no test leakage.

entry.title: Routing Divergence Is Not Evidence of Behavioral Influence in Same-Weight MoE Self-Distillation

author.name: Cedric Caruzzo, Donggeun Yoo, Tae Soo Kim
