entry.summary: arXiv:2608.14568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems become deeply integrated into critical global infrastructure, the urgency for robust governance frameworks has ...

entry.title: Decentralized Federated Learning for Heterogeneous Multi-Task Semantic Communication

author.name: Lin Yin, Tiejun Lv, Weicai Li, Xi Yu, Xiaoyu He

entry.summary: Proposes a personalized decentralized federated learning scheme for multi-task semantic communication networks, using policy-driven multi-path routing to split task-specific from shared features and a task-affinity-calibrated consensus matrix to limit negative transfer. Aims to prevent overconsensus bias in heterogeneous wireless deployments.

entry.title: A Network-driven Framework for Public Event Forecasting via Dynamic Interaction Network Evolution

author.name: Jie Wei, Yue Liu, Xiaochuan Tang, Biao Cai, Xiangtao Li, Yanmei Hu

entry.summary: Represents public events as dynamic interaction networks among participants and forecasts event evolution by predicting participant growth from network-science structural metrics fed into deep sequence models. Targets proactive risk management and resource allocation.

entry.title: Who Leads Now? Token-Level Modality Arbitration for Chart-to-Code Generation

author.name: Qinghao Fu, Yarong Wang, Shunlei Ning, Yilin Wang, Shunwen Bai, Xinda Wang, Jiaotuan Wang, Yinan Nie, Wei Zhou

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.15510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chart-to-code generation requires a model to read the fine-grained visual details of a chart and write executable code that reproduces it. Existing cha...

entry.title: MUPA$^{2}$E: Multimodal Unified Perception with Asymmetric Attention for Emotion Assessment

author.name: Stefanos Gkikas, Eric Nichols, Christian Arzate Cruz, Randy Gomez

entry.summary: MUPA2E processes facial video and EEG through one shared asymmetric-attention backbone rather than separate modality-specific encoders, using axis-folded frame tokens and either raw or spatially projected EEG. Evaluated on a subject-independent emotion recognition protocol comparing unimodal and fused settings. The contribution is architectural unification for neuro-behavioral fusion.

entry.title: Beyond Asking: A Pipeline for Personalized Game Generation that Reads Players from Behavior

author.name: Yifan Lu, Xiaopeng Yuan, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: The paper builds a pipeline that infers player ability and style from raw gameplay behavior to drive personalized game generation, and confronts the validation gap by constructing a synthetic player population with known latent traits. This avoids the circularity of validating behavior-based inference against self-report questionnaires. It contributes both a method and a verification protocol.

entry.title: HaReCAP: Habitual-action Grounding for Recursive Large Language Model Agents

author.name: Shen Liu, Zhenguo Xu, Shaopu Wang, Yike Gao, Chunlei Wang

entry.summary: HaReCAP extends recursive planning agents by caching habitual actions so that leaf-level subgoals do not require a fresh model call for grounding, targeting what the authors call last-mile grounding redundancy. This cuts accumulated LLM calls and tokens during long-horizon embodied execution. It is a low-intrusion efficiency add-on to an existing recursive planner.

entry.title: Cost Scales with Change, Not Corpus Size: Incrementally Maintaining an Evolving Semantic Substrate

author.name: Yusuke Takahashi, Kyle Wild, Asako Uraki

entry.summary: The paper argues that compiling corpus meaning once at ingest into a compact queryable semantic substrate is viable because maintenance cost scales with the amount of change, not with corpus size, contrary to fears about rebuilding truncated matrix decompositions or re-embedding after model swaps. It supports this with incremental update experiments. The alternative is re-deriving meaning at every query as agentic retrieval systems do.

entry.title: LAVA: Logic-Aware Validation and Augmentation Framework for Large-Scale Financial Document Auditing

author.name: Ruoqi Shu, Xuhui Wang, Isaac Wang, Yanming Mai, Bo Wan

entry.summary: LAVA is a modular multimodal pipeline for enterprise financial document validation combining document-rule retrieval, layout-preserving extraction, metadata enrichment, and auditable symbolic or arithmetic verification. It targets payroll auditing, tax compliance, and loan underwriting where reproducibility and accuracy requirements are strict. The backbone-agnostic design supports production deployment.

entry.title: Intelligent Base Station Deployment in Urban Wireless Networks: A Geographic Data-Informed Digital Twin Approach

author.name: Zhenyu Tao, Yuxuan Li, Wei Xu, Yongming Huang, Xiaohu You

entry.summary: This framework couples a geographic-data-informed wireless digital twin with deep reinforcement learning to optimize macro base station placement without on-site measurements, real user trajectories, or exhaustive ray tracing. The twin supplies sample-free propagation and user distribution estimates from open map data. It lowers the data barrier for pre-deployment network planning.

entry.title: Extend the Safety Horizon for Intelligent Transportation Systems through Semantic-Aware Cooperative Perception

author.name: Chun-Yeow Yeoh, Chee Keong Tan, Joanne Mun-Yee Lim, Heng-Siong Lim

entry.summary: The proposed hierarchical multi-scale semantic-aware cooperative perception scheme reduces vehicle-to-everything bandwidth demand while preserving intermediate-fusion accuracy, addressing the risk that dense urban traffic saturates network capacity and degrades safety functions. It prioritizes semantically important features across scales for transmission. The target is extending the effective safety horizon of cooperative driving.

entry.title: LLM Safety Alignment in Low-Resource Languages: A Systematic Literature Review

author.name: Valdini Douglace Lemofouet, Blessing Ngozi Uzor, Paula Chikaodinaka Anyanwu, Danielle Blanche Kapsa, Sukairaj Hafiz Imam, P Sam Sahil, Abigail Oppong, Tassallah Abdullahi, Clemencia Siro, Idris Abdulmumin, Seid Muhie Yimam, Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.14626v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved substantial progress in safety alignment, yet their safety guarantees remain significantly weaker in low-r...

entry.title: Take it Personally: The Limits of General SSL Representations for Real-Life PPG Emotion Detection

author.name: Dominika Kunc, Przemys{\l}aw Kazienko, Stanis{\l}aw Saganowski

entry.summary: Tests whether self-supervised PPG encoders pretrained on unconstrained real-life data yield representations useful for subjective emotion detection. The representations transfer very well to objective activity recognition but fail to help on emotion, suggesting general SSL features miss person-specific affective signal.

entry.title: Domain Agnostic Text Redaction from Natural Language Rules using Instruction Tuning

author.name: Aravindhan Arunagiri, Ayaan Khan, Udayaadithya Avadhanam, SaiBarath Sundar

entry.summary: Builds a redaction system where the sensitivity policy is expressed as natural-language rules interpreted by an instruction-tuned model, extending beyond fixed PII patterns to arbitrary domain-specific content. The design also produces human-readable justifications for each redaction to support compliance auditing.

entry.title: Class Imbalance and Batch Effects in LLM-Based Screening for Systematic Reviews

author.name: Gilberto Sussumu Hida, Danilo Monteiro Ribeiro, Clayton Suguio Hida

entry.summary: Studies LLM-based abstract screening for systematic reviews under severe class imbalance, comparing single-item and batched prompting with and without prevalence hints across five reviews. Prevalence metadata did not help, whereas batching changed decision behavior in prevalence-dependent ways, and aggregate metrics often disagreed with item-level analysis.

entry.title: Prompting is not enough: supervised baselines and leakage control for measuring shared decision-making with LLMs in pediatric encounters

author.name: Bernardo Modenesi, Jody Lin, Kimberly Kaphingst, Angela Zhu, Maya Wheeler, Peilu Zhang, Angela Fagerlin

entry.summary: Tests whether zero-shot prompting of a local open model suffices to detect shared decision-making behaviors in recorded pediatric surgical consultations, against a supervised classifier over frozen sentence embeddings under patient-grouped nested evaluation. Supervised methods add value, and leakage control changes the apparent performance picture.

entry.title: Command-Space Counterfactual Explanations for Pareto-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Joanikij Chulev, Hendrik Baier

entry.summary: Provides counterfactual explanations for Pareto Conditioned Networks by searching for the minimal change to the desired-return command that would make the trained policy choose an alternative action in a given state. The authors adapt adversarial attack methods to this black-box command-space search using a return-only PCN variant.

entry.title: FZ-VLM: A Two Stage Florence-Zephyr Vision Language Model Framework for Pulmonary Nodule Characterization and Clinical Decision Making

author.name: Pramit Dutta, Jenita Manokaran, Richa Mittal, Ryan Appleby, Eranga Ukwatta

entry.summary: FZ-VLM is a two-stage vision-language pipeline pairing a Florence-style vision encoder with a Zephyr language model to produce structured characterization of pulmonary nodules, covering location, diameter, margins, and attenuation. It aims to unify tasks that existing AI tools handle in isolation to support radiologist follow-up decisions.

entry.title: CETalk: Continuous Valence-Arousal Control for Audio-Driven 3D Talking Head Generation

author.name: Peng Jia, Li Dai, Zhen Xiao, Xueliang Liu, Jia Li

entry.summary: CETalk generates 3D talking heads conditioned on continuous valence-arousal values instead of discrete emotion labels, predicting FLAME parameters with dynamic emotion modulation and multi-scale temporal modeling. It explicitly addresses the frequency mismatch between fast articulation and slower emotional expression.

entry.title: SAPE: Sandwich Adapters for Parameter Efficiency in Large Language Model Fine-Tuning

author.name: Mohammad Aref Jafari-Raddani, Morteza Mohajjel Kafshdooz

entry.summary: Introduces a parameter-efficient fine-tuning scheme that shares adapter weights in a sandwich pattern reflecting the hierarchical structure of transformer stacks, rather than sharing uniformly or with dynamic masks. The goal is faster convergence and lower parameter counts without extra runtime overhead.

entry.title: Agent Inheritance Protocol: Speculating on Feralized Agents After Principals Die

author.name: Botao Amber Hu, Fangting

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.15403v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: You will die eventually. Your agents may not. An AI agent operating on decentralized blockchain infrastructure has no concept of death; it can only g...

entry.title: Afterlife Delegation Protocol: Speculative Design of Self-Sovereign Agents that Outlive Their Principals

author.name: Botao Amber Hu, Iris Long

entry.summary: A companion speculative design project in which a living person signs an agentic will, and upon verified death a self-sovereign agent spawns on-chain with funds and memories to execute that will indefinitely. The team built a working web platform to elicit how real people would configure such posthumous agents.

entry.title: FloodReasonBench: Benchmarking VLM Reasoning Segmentation for Embodied Flood Response at the Edge

author.name: Rajat Bhattacharjya, Yoomee Jung, Minwoo Kim, Sing-Yao Wu, Eli Bozorgzadeh, Nalini Venkatasubramanian, Nikil Dutt

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.15410v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reasoning segmentation enables vision-language models (VLMs) to translate mission-relevant language requests into pixel-level visual grounding, offer...

entry.title: Amortised Post-Hoc Explanation with Exact Preservation for Dynamic Graph Anomaly Detectors

author.name: Iyad Assaad Nekka, Hamida Seba, Walid Khaled Hidouci, Karima Amrouche

entry.summary: Adds a post-hoc explanation layer to a strong but opaque dynamic-graph anomaly detector, producing both structural attributions over neighboring interactions and temporal attributions over historical snapshots for each flagged edge. The wrapper leaves the trained detector frozen and claims exact preservation of its decisions.

entry.title: When Is Shallow Enough? Adaptive Split Federated Learning with Client-Specific Sufficiency Estimation

author.name: Wenhao Yuan, Chenchen Lin, Wenhao Hu, Jian Chen, Jinfeng Xu, Shujie Li, Edith Cheuk Han Ngai

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.15639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: \textit{Split Federated Learning} (SFL) enables distributed model training by splitting networks between the server and clients. However, under clien...

entry.title: RRFC: Recursive Refinement via Feedback Conditioning for Iterative Image-to-Image Generation

author.name: Kareem Hassani, Chaymaa Abbas, Hadi Al Mubasher, Mariette Awad

entry.summary: Turns single-pass conditional image translators into iterative refiners by feeding the model's previous prediction back as extra input channels alongside the original conditioning. This preserves the backbone architecture while allowing the generator to revise its own output over several passes.

entry.title: CM-MAE: A Physics-Guided Cross-Modal Self-Supervised Learning Framework for Vision-Wireless Applications

author.name: Yubo Zhang, Yiyao Liu

entry.summary: Pretrains a joint representation over synchronized camera frames and wireless beam power measurements using a masked autoencoder with a soft contrastive alignment objective, so that representations transfer across deployment scenarios with different geometry and traffic. It uses only RGB and measured beam vectors, avoiding ray-traced or calibrated depth supervision.

entry.title: RagGAD: Rationale-Aware Conditional Gaussian Mixture Normalizing Flow for Unsupervised Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Junxin Lu, Jing Zhao, Shiliang Sun

entry.summary: Attacks unsupervised graph anomaly detection without relying on the assumption that connected nodes are similar, disentangling stable relational rationales from spurious affinities and modeling normal behavior with a conditional Gaussian mixture normalizing flow. Stable rationales are further split into robust and fragile components.

entry.title: A Tree-Structured Approach for Phishing Template and Attacker Attribution Analysis

author.name: Unai Agirre, Imanol Jerico, Felipe Casta\~no, Andrea Venturi, Francesco Zola

entry.summary: The paper analyzes phishing webpages through tree-structured representations of their underlying DOM structure to detect template reuse and attribute pages to shared phishing kits, rather than classifying each page in isolation. This shifts detection toward identifying coordinated campaigns and attacker infrastructure.

entry.title: Digital Twin Degradation: Detecting Cyber Physical Attacks via Temporal Inconsistencies

author.name: Konstantinos E. Kampourakis, Vasileios Gkioulos, Sokratis Katsikas

entry.summary: This framework detects cyber-physical attacks by monitoring temporal consistency between a physical process and its potentially degraded digital twin, using a predictor trained only on normal dynamics and flagging divergence patterns. It treats digital twin fidelity as untrustworthy in adversarial settings rather than assumed.

entry.title: A Human-LLM Teaming Framework for Privacy Risk Analysis: An Illustration with CBDC-Based Welfare Schemes

author.name: Sourya Joyee De, Abdessamad Imine

entry.summary: The paper proposes a human-LLM teaming workflow for privacy risk analysis of complex sociotechnical systems, illustrated on central bank digital currency welfare schemes where surveillance, discrimination, and stigmatization harms arise across many stakeholders. LLMs assist information gathering, scenario exploration, and synthesis while humans supply contextual judgment.

entry.title: RISE: Roadside Infrastructure Sequence Understanding across 3D Tracking and Structured Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Yanbo Jiang, Haotian Zheng, Jiahao Wang, Hanxiao Ren, Yitao Xu, Yining Xing, Zehong Ke, Hao Cheng, Yiqian Tu, Jinhao Li, Zhiyuan Xuan, Fang Zhang, Jianqiang Wang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.16480v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present RISE (Roadside Infrastructure Sequence Understanding and Evaluation), a framework spanning metric 3D tracking and structured vision-langua...

entry.title: Degradation-Aligned Self-Supervised Learning for State of Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries under Label Sparsity

author.name: Jiaqi Yao, Julia Kowal

entry.summary: This work pretrains a CNN-GRU model on unlabeled lithium-ion battery cycling data using a cycle-order ranking pretext task that aligns representations with degradation direction, then fine-tunes on sparse labels for state-of-health estimation. The aim is robust SOH prediction when labeled capacity measurements are scarce.

entry.title: Quantum Models with Multi-Stage Training for Compositional Concept Generalization

author.name: Mina Abbaszadeh, Matilda Karabina Moore, Mehrnoosh Sadrzadeh, Martha Lewis

entry.summary: Proposes a compositional model of meaning using tensors and variational quantum circuits, trained in stages that first learn object representations from single-object image-caption pairs and then learn frozen-object relational parameters. The goal is systematic recombination of learned primitives in novel multimodal contexts.

entry.title: CrevasseSeg: A Label-Efficient UAV Crevasse Segmentation Framework

author.name: Steven Wallace, William D Harcourt, Richard Hann, Aiden Durrant, Somayajulu Sripada, Georgios Leontidis

entry.summary: CrevasseSeg releases a UAV glacier imagery dataset from Svalbard and benchmarks five self-supervised objectives (BYOL, JSD, Barlow Twins, VICReg, a hybrid) across three segmentation architectures including a DINOv3-initialized backbone. It targets label-efficient crevasse mapping for glaciology and field safety.

entry.title: Multi-Granularity Sentiment Integration for LLM-Based Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Shanshan Lin, Yuesheng Wu, Chao Chen, Yizhe Yang, Zhihao Chen, Zexian Yang, Xiangwen Liao

entry.summary: MGSI encodes audio and visual streams at short, medium, and long temporal granularities before fusing them with an LLM for multimodal sentiment analysis, avoiding the information loss of shallow projection or coarse pooling. Targets better cross-modal alignment of affective cues that evolve at different timescales.

entry.title: FETERS: Few-Shot Early Time-Series Classification via Effective Ratio Selection

author.name: Chen-An Tai, Yujia Wu, Vincent S. Tseng

entry.summary: FETERS handles early time-series classification when labeled data are scarce by selecting a single dataset-level stopping ratio via class-wise leave-one-out evaluation on the support set, rather than learning a per-sample stopping module. Uses a penalty-based reward to balance earliness and accuracy.

entry.title: SoftModel: A Neural Model That Grows Its Own Topology -- Governed Structural Growth for Continual In-Service Learning

author.name: Zhoumin Xie

entry.summary: Proposes a neural system in which topology itself is never frozen, defining an algebra of structural growth operators (width, hierarchy, composition, input interface, cycles, attention heads) each exact at the moment of insertion, governed for stability during continual in-service learning on non-stationary streams. Capacity is meant to follow demand rather than be fixed at design time.

entry.title: TRACE-CASH: Trial-History-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Configuration Exploration in Time-Series CASH

author.name: Yu-Han Huang, Yujia Wu, Vincent S. Tseng

entry.summary: TRACE-CASH applies trial-history-conditioned actor-critic search to combined algorithm selection and hyperparameter optimization for time-series forecasting, where the chosen model determines which hyperparameters are active and chronological validation is required. It combines learned candidate generation with fixed rules for coverage, exploitation, and stall-triggered exploration.

entry.title: Learning Generalizable Reconstruction of High-Dimensional Neural Dynamics

author.name: Anima Kujur, Zahra Monfared

entry.summary: PCA-DMD reconstructs long multichannel local field potential recordings by windowing, projecting into a compact PCA space, learning linear Koopman dynamics there, and reassembling via overlap-add. Reports better distributional fidelity than several DMD variants and strong zero-shot cross-subject generalization at 300k-sample scale.

entry.title: Variational Outlier-Robust Gaussian Process Regression with Generative Modeling

author.name: Arslan Majal, Aamir Hussain Chughtai

entry.summary: Introduces a generative Gaussian process regression model that explicitly represents per-observation contamination and learns it with a variational generalized EM procedure, adaptively downweighting outliers. Reports competitive or better accuracy than robust GPR baselines across contamination settings.

entry.title: Data-Efficient and Interpretable Classification of Circulating Tumor Cell Phenotypes in Microfluidic Devices via Deep Learning

author.name: Serena Su, Yifan Wang, Senwei Liang

entry.summary: Classifies circulating tumor cell phenotypes from their trajectories through label-free microfluidic obstacle courses, where nonlinear fluid-structure interactions make the inverse problem analytically intractable. Focuses on data efficiency and physical interpretability given limited trajectory data.

entry.title: Wolff-Parkinson-White Detection at 471:1 Class Imbalance: A Leakage-Controlled Study of the Data Bottleneck

author.name: Nathael Altman

entry.summary: Studies detection of Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome on 12-lead ECG at roughly 471 to 1 class imbalance by pooling PTB-XL and Chapman-Shaoxing-Ningbo, comparing seven signal representations under a single pre-specified leakage-controlled protocol with a held-out fold touched only once. The main finding is negative: added model diversity and capacity do not raise the performance ceiling, implicating data scarcity as the binding constraint.

entry.title: Deep Analog: Open-Set Film Emulation with Reference-Conditioned 3D LUTs

author.name: Yitong Mu

entry.summary: Tackles open-set film-stock emulation by predicting a 3D color lookup table conditioned on a single reference frame, and shows that the common approach of blending a fixed bank of LUTs is a gated mixture of experts that collapses onto one expert when trained purely for reconstruction. Adding an entropy load-balancing term restores expert utilization and recovers about 1 dB PSNR, while the authors argue a fixed LUT basis remains fundamentally closed-set.

entry.title: PandasCorpus: A Resource of Real-World Pandas Workflows and Usage Patterns

author.name: Syrym Abdikhan, Mazhar Hameed

entry.summary: Introduces a corpus of 139 thousand Jupyter notebooks from roughly 100 thousand GitHub repositories capturing more than four million Pandas API calls, along with an analysis of how real-world data-processing workflows are composed. Intended as a resource for studying data science practice and for training or evaluating code models.

entry.title: Uncertainty Identifies Difficult Samples Across Methods: A Multi-Task Study on a Heterogeneous Skin Lesion Dataset

author.name: Leon Koole, Jiapan Guo, Matias Valdenegro-Toro

entry.summary: Compares five uncertainty quantification methods including MC dropout, DropConnect, Flipout, deep ensembles, and DUQ on a pooled multi-source skin lesion dataset with joint binary malignancy and five-class diagnosis heads, evaluating calibration, uncertainty decomposition, and risk-coverage. Reports that which samples are flagged as hard is largely method-agnostic, with per-sample entropy correlations from 0.54 to 0.91, while calibration quality differs substantially by method.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Adaptation of Medical Vision Foundation Models for High-Frequency Micro-Ultrasound Prostate Segmentation

author.name: Ayusha Abbas, Saram Abbas, Kabita Adhikari

entry.summary: Presents a zero-shot segmentation pipeline for 29 MHz micro-ultrasound prostate imaging using the MedSAM foundation model without any modality-specific training data, targeting a setting where speckle obscures the gland boundary and inter-clinician outlines differ by more than 10 percent in area. Motivated by the cost and poor cross-scanner generalization of supervised segmentation.

entry.title: Developing an Offshore Machine Learning Surface Layer Scheme

author.name: Susan Dettling, Sue Ellen Haupt, Thomas Brummet, Patrick Hawbecker, Branko Kosovi\'c, David John Gagne

entry.summary: Trains neural networks and random forests to replace empirically fit surface-layer flux parameterizations for the offshore environment, using momentum and heat flux observations from an air-sea interaction tower, a research platform, and a shipborne deployment, with vertical differences supplied as gradient inputs. Explores generalization of learned schemes across sites for use in numerical weather prediction.

entry.title: Sufficient Dimesion Reduction via Generalized Stein's Lemma

author.name: Ye Tian

entry.summary: Develops a sufficient dimension reduction estimator for the central subspace based on a generalized Stein identity, targeting multivariate responses where inverse-regression methods suffer slice sparsity and distributional assumptions, forward methods need costly iterative smoothing, and deep approaches need large labeled samples. Avoids matrix inversion and heavy smoothing.

entry.title: Convolution Smoothed Quantile Regression for XGBoost

author.name: Mandy Yao (University of Toronto), Meredith Franklin (University of Toronto)

entry.summary: QXGB adds a convolution-smoothed quantile loss to gradient boosting so that conditional quantiles can be estimated densely enough to construct full predictive cumulative distributions, exceedance probabilities, and tail behavior. Targets applications needing characterization of rare or extreme outcomes rather than point predictions.

entry.title: Prediction Inference of Time Series with Standard ReLU Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Kejin Wu

entry.summary: Develops prediction intervals for time series forecasts made with standard ReLU deep networks, explicitly decomposing predictive uncertainty into future innovation variability and estimation variability arising from finite training data. Introduces a pertinent prediction interval construction intended to capture both sources.

entry.title: A Counterexample to the Tang Zhang Schatten Norm Conjecture and Sharp Positive Results

author.name: Zijian Zeng, Houde Liu, Kurunathan Ratnavelu

entry.summary: Disproves a conjectured formula of Tang and Zhang for the best constant relating the Schatten p-norm of a matrix sum to the norm of the sum of absolute values, using two explicit rank-one two-by-two real matrices at p equal to three halves certified by strict rational inequalities. On the positive side it proves the conjectured sharp bound for rank-at-most-one families when p is at least two, classifies equality cases, and settles the endpoint case.

entry.title: Continuous Quantum Feedback Control via Kraus-Parameterized Belief Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Priyanshi Singh, Krishna Bhatia

entry.summary: Combines a Stiefel-manifold-constrained recurrent encoder that outputs density matrix estimates guaranteed to be positive semidefinite and trace-normalized with a PPO actor that maps these belief states to continuous control actions for a continuously monitored qubit. The physics constraints are embedded structurally rather than enforced by penalty, and the learned policy maintains stable belief fidelity under noisy measurement records.

entry.title: PWLR: Pairwise Witness Local Rejection for Boundary-Aware Out-of-Distribution Detection

author.name: Chengyao Jia, Ruixuan Wang

entry.summary: PWLR improves near-out-of-distribution detection by using a multimodal LLM offline to generate visible local cues that discriminate one in-distribution class from a specific confusing rival, then screening these cue phrases with in-distribution data under a frozen vision-language backbone to retain only reliable verifiers. At inference the method first narrows to globally plausible classes and then applies pairwise local rejection as explicit boundary evidence.

entry.title: CLAIR-Fin: An Adversarial Multi-Agent Framework for Claim-Level Verification and Adaptive Debate in Cross-Modal Financial QA

author.name: Fatema Tuj Johora Faria, Mukaffi Bin Moin, Jubayer Al Mahmud, M. F. Mridha, Md. Alam Hossain

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.13706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing defenses against hallucination in retrieval-augmented and multi-agent pipelines remain partial: evidence is trusted despite modality disagreem...

entry.title: Stable Miscalibration in Large Language Models: A Practical View of High-Confidence Errors

author.name: Akira Okutomi

entry.summary: Studies high-confidence LLM errors that stay stable under small perturbations, combining an output-level confidence audit with a hidden-state sensitivity probe. It reports that self-critical prompting reduces internal state movement and helps identify domains where abstention-aware critique lowers decision loss.

entry.title: VoiceChat-TTS: A Low-Latency Continuous Speech Synthesis Model for Interactive Agents

author.name: Edresson Casanova, Jaehyeon Kim, Mariana Graterol Fuenmayor, Shehzeen Hussain, Viacheslav Klimkov, Valentin Mendelev, Mikyas Desta, Paarth Neekhara, Piotr Zelasko, Chen Chen, Elena Rastorgueva, Ke Hu, Ankita Pasad, Xuesong Yang, Aya Alja'fari, Rajarshi Roy, Rohan Badlani, Jason Roche, Jason Li, Zhehuai Chen

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.13831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spoken dialogue is a natural form of human--computer interaction, yet most speech language models remain limited to turn-based operation and lack rea...

entry.title: Periocular Soft Biometrics: A Survey and Applications to Multimedia Forensics and Disinformation Detection

author.name: Fernando Alonso-Fernandez, Kevin Hernandez-Diaz, Josef Bigun

entry.summary: A survey of demographic attribute estimation from the periocular region, covering datasets, methods from handcrafted features to deep learning, and applications to forensics and detection of manipulated media. It emphasizes settings where the rest of the face is occluded.

entry.title: VideoGAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants on Agentic Video Understanding

author.name: Fan Zhang, Guangming Yao, Jinyang Wu, Hao Wu, Zheng Lian, Xinyu Geng, Jingdong Chen, Yi Yuan, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.14718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video understanding is a fundamental task for evaluating the capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, existing leading models...

entry.title: YOLO26-RD: An End-to-End Road Damage Detection Network With Learnable Contrast Enhancement and Edge-Guided Downsampling

author.name: Sompote Youwai, Pawarotorn Chaipetch, Hathairat Samaikul, Theerayut Yonseng

entry.summary: YOLO26-RD adds a tiny learnable contrast module and a Sobel-gated space-to-depth downsampler to an NMS-free detector for road damage, and its data audit falsifies the assumption that pavement distress is a small-object problem. The audit finds most instances are large by COCO standards and that cracks are extreme aspect-ratio structures, which changes the appropriate architectural choices.

entry.title: Beyond Independence: Learning Correlated Views for Variational Incomplete Multi-View Clustering

author.name: Zheming Xu, Aiyue Tang, Shidi Chen, Xuechao Zou, Congyan Lang, Rogelio A. Mancisidor, Michael Kampffmeyer

entry.summary: Proposes a variational framework for incomplete multi-view clustering that drops the usual conditional independence assumption during posterior aggregation, instead learning cross-view correlation from the covariance structure of posterior estimation errors. This better reflects the structured dependence between views when some views are missing.

entry.title: Beyond Clear Skies: Synthetic Seasonal and Weather Variations for Real-World Drone Detection

author.name: Tamara R. Lenhard, Andreas Weinmann, Tobias Koch

entry.summary: Introduces a synthetic dataset extension adding seasonal and adverse-weather variation to drone detection training data using game-engine rendering with automatic annotations. It studies whether controllable synthetic environmental variation can substitute for the expensive real capture of rare weather conditions.

entry.title: Unlocking Motion in Expressions: Temporal Calibration for Referring Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Yiwen Jiang, Zhengtong Zhu, Ruixin Zhang, Jiaqing Fan

entry.summary: The EMC framework for referring video object segmentation explicitly extracts how much a language expression depends on motion semantics, then calibrates temporal modeling accordingly instead of applying uniform cross-modal temporal fusion. This lets motion information be used adaptively based on what the referring expression actually requires.

entry.title: DRAFE: Domain-Robust Asymmetric Fusion of Heterogeneous Detection Transformers for Cross-City Fine-Grained Traffic Object Detection

author.name: Divine Yao Agbobli, Geoffery Eyram Agorku, Israel Afriyie, Kwadwo Amankwah-Nkyi, Marvin Osei-Kuffour, Richmond Owusu Duah, Bright Seglah, Kelvin Asamoah Terkper, Kwabena Amoako Adjei

entry.summary: DRAFE ensembles two independently trained DETR-family detectors with asymmetric fusion for fine-grained vehicle recognition that transfers across cities. It uses a two-stage pipeline with pseudo-label expansion and human-in-the-loop annotation to curate roughly 6,000 images with 200,000 annotations.

entry.title: Untie Squared ReLU variant

author.name: Amy_

entry.summary: Proposes replacing the squared ReLU in transformer feedforward layers with an untied variant that uses two separate up-projections, applies ReLU to each, and multiplies elementwise, generalizing the squared form which is recovered when the two projections are equal. This is essentially a ReLU-gated linear unit style modification presented with small-scale exploration.

entry.title: A Cognitively Motivated Multidimensional Framework for Evaluating Metaphor Explanations

author.name: Ana Naveriani, Jakob Suchan, Stefano Zoia, Mehul Bhatt, Antonio Lieto, Gian Luca Pozzato

entry.summary: Breaks metaphor explanation quality into six theoretically grounded dimensions and collects over eleven thousand human ratings, showing that quality is genuinely multidimensional and that annotator disagreement is systematic rather than noise. A feasibility study checks whether automatic evaluation can recover some dimensions.

entry.title: CardiacMamba: Fair and Robust RGB-RF Fusion for Remote Heart Rate Estimation via State Space Modeling

author.name: Bo Zhao, Zheng Wu, Yiping Xie, Zitong YU

entry.summary: Fuses facial video with radio-frequency sensing using state-space sequence models to estimate heart rate remotely, with modules for amplifying subtle RF temporal changes, aligning the two modalities, and refining channel spectra. Fairness across skin tones is an explicit evaluation goal on a dedicated dataset.

entry.title: Noesis: Bidirectional Graph-RAG with Adaptive Parallelism and Cross-Knowledge-Base Semantic Discovery

author.name: Nicola Cogotti

entry.summary: Presents a graph retrieval-augmented generation architecture with bidirectional traversal that mimics human reading with decaying memory, adaptive concurrency control for ingestion, and automatic routing across multiple domain knowledge bases. It targets chunking, scaling, and multi-domain precision problems in existing systems.

entry.title: Random Quadratic Form with random forcing: Metastable synchronization by noise

author.name: Anna Shalova

entry.summary: Analyzes a random quadratic form dynamics on the sphere under small Brownian forcing, showing the forcing barely changes the law of the process yet breaks the intrinsic symmetry that otherwise causes only partial synchronization. Characterizes a two-stage metastable route to full synchronization.

entry.title: Multi-Channel Feature Fusion and Monte Carlo Dropout for Uncertainty-Aware Diabetic Retinopathy Grading

author.name: Saksham Kumar

entry.summary: A diabetic retinopathy grading pipeline combines green-channel CLAHE preprocessing, an ordinal EfficientNetV2 regressor, Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty for referral, and Grad-CAM explanations. It reports a quadratic weighted kappa above 91 on the APTOS-2019 test split with a 20 percent referral rate.

entry.title: Large Language Models Show Metacognitive Sensitivity in Medical Reasoning

author.name: Ahmad Nazzal

entry.summary: Introduces a psychophysics-inspired clinical benchmark of 45 synthetic vignettes (135 trials) that varies evidence strength, conflict, and missingness to test whether a medical LLM confidence tracks evidence quality when distinguishing Alzheimer-type impairment from depression-related cognitive impairment. The pilot uses a single small model and reports structured-output validity plus confidence behavior.

entry.title: From Doyle to AGM: A Survey and an Implementation Roadmap for Belief Change

author.name: Yuri Almeida, Arthur Casals

entry.summary: A narrative survey tracing computational belief revision from the 1980 Doyle and London taxonomy through the AGM framework to modern approaches, mapping how each taxonomic category evolved. It sets out a roadmap for implementing belief change in contemporary systems.

entry.title: Task-Driven Three-Layer Distributed Scheduling for Emergency Earth Observation in Large Low-Earth-Orbit Constellations

author.name: Qian Yin, Xinwei Wang, Guohua Wu

entry.summary: Proposes a three-layer distributed scheduling method for inserting urgent Earth-observation tasks into already-executing routine plans across large low-Earth-orbit satellite constellations. It uses a shared geographic grid, temporary satellite clusters formed from inter-satellite links, and onboard dual-plan bidding to limit disruption under intermittent ground contact.

entry.title: Second-Order Policy Effects as State Transitions: A Source-Linked Benchmark for Policy Simulation

author.name: Wesley Shu

entry.summary: Formalizes prediction of second-order policy effects, where a policy changes the institutional environment through adaptation, capture, gaming, burden shifting, and irreversibility, and releases a source-linked benchmark of 96 public policy cases across eight domains and four action classes. Each case carries state variables and source locators for grounded evaluation.

entry.title: Towards Standardized Evaluation in Automated Domain Modeling: Introducing a Benchmark

author.name: Vasiliy Seibert

entry.summary: Assembles existing UML reference model sets into a single benchmark so that automated domain modeling approaches, including LLM-based ones, can be compared consistently from natural-language descriptions. It targets the lack of standardized evaluation in domain-driven design automation.

entry.title: Mental Model Management: An Operator-Based Framework for LLM Memory

author.name: Oliver Kramer

entry.summary: Sketches an operator-based memory framework in which an LLM maintains compact evolving mental models composed of knowledge chunks, with operators for extraction, retrieval, update, reorganization, inconsistency detection and inference. Illustrated conceptually using evolution strategies as a running example.

entry.title: PLeDO: Pain Level Detection for Osteoarthritis from EMR Data

author.name: Yuhao Chen, Jiahao Cai, Nafiz Sadman, Farhana Zulkernine, John Queenan, David Barber

entry.summary: A clinical NLP pilot that classifies osteoarthritis patients into mild versus moderate-to-severe pain using structured electronic medical record fields plus a synonym-based extractor of pain expressions from free-text chart notes. Aims to link documented pain severity to diagnosis and treatment patterns.

entry.title: The Authority Resolution Framework: A Five-Domain Ontology for Governing Who and What Decides, at Scale

author.name: Parviz Shariff

entry.summary: Proposes a five-domain ontology for representing whether an autonomous agent's action is authorized, not merely feasible, binding actor, action, object, context and a justification chain into an authority relation with a calibration coefficient. Intended as governance scaffolding for scaled agent deployment.

entry.title: FeatureHospital: A Skill-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Algorithm Customization in Multi-View Multi-Label Feature Selection

author.name: Junxuan Li, Zhiqi Chen, Yuzhou Liu, Peng Zhang, Huaxiao Liu

entry.summary: FeatureHospital is a skill-driven multi-agent framework that automates the design and customization of multi-view multi-label feature selection algorithms, reducing reliance on expert manual tuning across heterogeneous datasets. It packages modeling perspectives as reusable skills that agents select and compose. The aim is practical adoption of feature selection without expert labor.

entry.title: Cross-Sign Language Transfer Learning Using Domain Adaptation with Multi-scale Temporal Alignment

author.name: Keren Artiaga (Victor), Yang Li (Victor), Ercan Engin Kuruoglu (Victor), Wai Kin (Victor), Chan

entry.summary: The authors apply adversarial domain adaptation with multi-scale temporal alignment to transfer sign language recognition across languages, finding domain adaptation outperforms plain neural transfer learning and that aligning shorter-term temporal features helps most. The motivation is severe resource scarcity across more than one hundred sign languages. Results focus on improving American Sign Language recognition.

entry.title: Understanding AI Anxiety in the Workplace: A Multimethod Investigation Using Fear Acquisition Theory and the Technology Acceptance Model

author.name: Jaroslaw Grobelny, Mateusz Klakus, Kacper Szyma\'nski, Teresa Chirkowska-Smolak

entry.summary: Two studies test whether anxiety about AI-driven job replacement can be induced through vicarious exposure to narratives emphasizing AI control over humans, and whether perceived usefulness and ease of use moderate the reaction, drawing on fear acquisition theory and the technology acceptance model. The finding is that anxiety arises from narrative exposure rather than direct personal experience. It informs how AI discourse shapes workforce attitudes.

entry.title: iFuzz-Meta: An Interpretable Fuzzy Learning Framework Bridging Top-Down and Bottom-Up Knowledge Integration

author.name: Xiaowei Jiang, Daniel Leong, Beining Cao, Nan Zhou, Yingtao Ren, Yu-Cheng Chang, Thomas Do, Chin-Teng Lin

entry.summary: Proposes iFuzz-Meta, a fuzzy rule-based learning framework in which each rule maps to a semantic and spatial prototype in the original feature space, aiming for inherently transparent inference. Meta-learning is used as an analytic lens to study how the interpretable rules reorganize across tasks and domains.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Causal Modelling of Semiconductor Process Dynamics

author.name: Daniel S{\o}rensen, Giorgio Melchiorre, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Sandip Halder, Roel Wuyts, Bappaditya Dey

entry.summary: Applies Liang-Kleeman and Pires information-flow estimators to raw semiconductor equipment log time series to infer causal dependencies among process variables. Preliminary expert review found a mix of known, plausible, novel, and inconsistent inferred relations, with a large inconsistent fraction.

entry.title: A Novel Fourier Feature Network for Solving Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Qihong Yang, Zhijie Su, Yangtao Deng, Qiaolin He

entry.summary: Introduces Fourier Feature Networks, single-hidden-layer networks with sine and cosine features whose output weights are fitted by least squares, as PDE solvers. Unlike extreme learning machines, they reportedly reach high precision without affine input transformations.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Tool for Combating Child Labour: A Real-Time Edge Vision Pipeline for Child Detection and Age Estimation

author.name: Mark Nowak (Conflux Laboratory)

entry.summary: Presents a research prototype edge vision pipeline combining person and face detection, cascaded age estimation, tracking, and re-identification to give child labour monitoring programs a continuous presence-based detection channel. The system produces reviewable per-track evidence rather than automated determinations.

entry.title: GATTA: Graph Active Learning with Test-Time Augmentation

author.name: Zsombor B\'anfi, Andr\'as G\'ezsi, Andr\'as Formanek

entry.summary: GATTA brings test-time augmentation to graph neural networks for active learning, aggregating predictions over multiple augmented graph views to get better uncertainty estimates for sample acquisition. A consistency filter discards augmentations whose predictions look unreliable, addressing the difficulty of label-preserving graph perturbations.

entry.title: Valhalla: A Layered Knowledge-State and Service-Governance Framework for Long-Term Scientific Knowledge Work

author.name: Yuyang Zheng, Nan Li, Wenxia Deng, Lige Yan, Xiang Li, Si Chen

entry.summary: Valhalla proposes a layered knowledge-state and service-governance architecture for long-term scientific agent workflows, replacing flat node-centric knowledge graphs with layered encapsulation and stable interfaces. The goal is knowledge that can be shared, integrated, and reorganized across users rather than tied to one person's organizational habits.

entry.title: Logical Embeddings for Argument Analysis

author.name: Leander Heldring, Santiago Torres

entry.summary: Replaces contextual word embeddings with logic-derived embeddings for argument analysis tasks, paired with a similarity measure grounded in formal logic that induces a valid kernel. The stated advantage is transparency and provable properties that cosine similarity over neural embeddings cannot guarantee.

entry.title: Chameleon: An Adaptive AI-Driven Honeypot Architecture Using Threat-Calibrated Particle Swarm Optimization and Semantic Deception Rapidly-Exploring Random Trees

author.name: Rohit Swami, Tushar Singh, Akash Warde, Sri Muthu

entry.summary: Describes an adaptive honeypot platform that combines a fast BiLSTM threat classifier, a locally hosted language model for deceptive responses, and swarm-optimization-driven behavior variation so that attackers cannot fingerprint a static deception environment. It is offered as an open alternative to expensive commercial deception products.

entry.title: Graph Neural Assisted Actor-Critic for Latency-Efficient Edge Vision System

author.name: Alam Noor, Luis Almeida, Kai Li, Jiyan Wu, Miguel Guti\'errez Gait\'an, Eduardo Tovar

entry.summary: This work combines a graph convolutional network with an advantage actor-critic controller to select pixel-correlated regions of interest for UAV video streaming, using a Lagrangian dual formulation with gradient descent to stabilize constrained optimization. The goal is to cut transmission latency while preserving operator-relevant visual detail.

entry.title: Software Engineering for AI-driven Building Operation

author.name: Philipp Zech, Sascha Hammes, Johannes Weninger, J\"urgen Pannosch, Gernot Steidl

entry.summary: Drawing on two interdisciplinary building-automation projects, this position paper argues that software engineering practices for AI assume digital failure modes, whereas bad control decisions in buildings irreversibly waste energy, harm occupant comfort, or wear equipment. It derives revised SE4AI requirements for physically consequential deployments.

entry.title: Geometry Is Not Robustness: A Trajectory-Level Study of PGD Evaluation

author.name: Dhairysheel Durgule

entry.summary: Empirically examines whether trajectory-level PGD diagnostics such as loss evolution, gradient alignment, and steps-to-failure reliably indicate robustness strength, comparing clean and adversarially trained CNNs on Fashion-MNIST with multi-restart 20-step attacks. The conclusion is that attack-path geometry does not straightforwardly track robustness.

entry.title: Learning Stock Trading Policies via Barycenter-Based Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Arishi Orra, Himanshu Choudhary, Manoj Thakur

entry.summary: BRaG aggregates multiple heterogeneous expert trading strategies via a performance-weighted Wasserstein barycenter into a pseudo-expert, pretrains a policy by adversarial imitation, then refines with RL to stabilize exploration and risk. Applied to stock trading with noisy delayed rewards.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Auxiliary Task Discovery for Stable Reinforcement Learning in Stock Trading

author.name: Arishi Orra, Himanshu Choudhary, Manoj Thakur

entry.summary: Proposes automatically discovering auxiliary prediction tasks, expressed as General Value Functions, to stabilize representation learning for RL-based stock trading instead of hand-designing targets and horizons. Motivated by market non-stationarity making fixed auxiliary designs obsolete.

entry.title: Transfer Learning of Keystroke Dynamics for Cross-Device User Authentication

author.name: Nuwan Kaluarachchi, Sevvandi Kandanaarachchi, Kristen Moore, Arathi Arakala, Conrad Sanderson

entry.summary: Builds a cross-device keystroke-dynamics authentication system using inductive transfer learning to adapt typing-pattern models from one device form factor (phone) to another (tablet) despite distribution drift. Combines adapted and native data for the secondary device.

entry.title: Time-Aware Validation of Machine Learning Fuel Consumption Models: Evidence from 1\,Hz Operational Data, CCGS \textit{Sir Wilfrid Laurier}

author.name: Samarasimha Reddy Chittamuru, Ayhan Akinturk, Allison Kennedy, Joshua Barnes, Matthew Hamilton

entry.summary: Shows that ship fuel-consumption models validated with random train-test splits on 1 Hz operational data suffer temporal leakage and report optimistic accuracy, using time-series and blocked cross-validation on Canadian Coast Guard vessel data to expose the gap. Argues for time-aware validation as the default in maritime ML.

entry.title: Auxiliary uncertainty signals for LLM-assisted systematic review screening: a benchmark across eight Cohen drug-class reviews

author.name: Arya Rahgozar, Pouria Mortezaagha

entry.summary: Proposes pairing an auxiliary BERT plus graph convolutional classifier with an LLM to supply calibrated include/exclude/maybe uncertainty signals during title-abstract screening for systematic reviews, tested across eight drug-class datasets from the Cohen benchmark with five prompt-delivery conditions. The contribution is mainly an empirical study of which way of injecting the auxiliary signal into prompts gives the best benefit-to-cost ratio.

entry.title: NPU Offloading of a Frozen Visual Encoder for Robot Policy Training

author.name: Hyojun Yun, Seungjae Won, Hyungpil Moon

entry.summary: Measures whether offloading the forward pass of a frozen visual encoder in robot policy training from GPU to a low-power INT8 NPU reduces total energy despite added data transfer and longer wall-clock time, using an asynchronous dual-device pipeline with FP32 action expert on GPU. Reports the energy and policy-performance trade-offs of the arrangement.

entry.title: Uncovering Hidden Leptonic Correlations with Flow Matching and Autoencoders

author.name: Haruto Kitagawa, Satsuki Nishimura, Hajime Otsuka

entry.summary: Applies flow matching to generate a broad set of Yukawa matrix and Majorana mass solutions consistent with measured neutrino mass-squared differences and mixing angles in the Type-I seesaw mechanism, then uses an autoencoder to discover latent structure among the solutions. Reports new nonlinear relations involving neutrino masses and CP phases.

entry.title: Maintaining IoT Device Identification under Concept Drift via Budget-Aware Traffic Labeling

author.name: Shayan Azizi, Norihiro Okui, Masataka Nakahara, Ayumu Kubota, Gustavo Batista, Hassan Habibi Gharakaheili

entry.summary: Addresses maintaining IoT device-type classification from passive network traffic as device behavior drifts, arguing that how much traffic to label and which instances to label are separable decisions. Shows that retraining only on drift-detector-selected instances systematically misses parts of the emerging behavior space while uniform sampling wastes budget, and proposes a budget-aware labeling strategy.

entry.title: Coded Hankel Polynomial Chaos: Spectral Identification of Dominant Polynomial-Chaos Modes

author.name: Zhiliang Deng, Xiaomei Yang

entry.summary: Develops a spectral alternative to sparse regression for identifying dominant polynomial-chaos expansion modes, converting coefficients into an exponential sum whose order and nodes are recovered from low-rank Hankel matrices with root-of-unity phase labels. Targets uncertainty quantification for high-dimensional surrogate models.

entry.title: Cross-Disciplinary Taxonomy and Modeling of Misunderstanding Generation, Amplification, and Detection, from Pragmatics to AI Agents

author.name: Babak Abbaschian

entry.summary: A cross-disciplinary synthesis of research on communicative misunderstanding, organizing it into generation, amplification, detection, and repair stages with eleven identified failure modes tied to specific points in a conversation. It argues AI-mediated communication removes the repair cues humans normally rely on.

entry.title: HistReNeRF: Historic Image Relocalisation within Contemporary Neural Radiance Field Reconstructions

author.name: Benjamin T. Hughes, Stuart James

entry.summary: HistReNeRF estimates the 6-DoF camera pose of archival photographs inside a modern neural radiance field reconstruction by matching adapted DINOv2 patch features against rays sampled from the NeRF. The continuous scene representation acts as a queryable interface enabling feature-space domain adaptation across large appearance and layout gaps.

entry.title: Automated Fetal Brain MRI Biometry in Healthy and Pathological Cases

author.name: Ema Masterl, Tina Vipotnik Vesnaver, Nejc \v{S}ubi\v{c}, \v{Z}iga \v{S}piclin

entry.summary: Assembles and validates an automated fetal brain MRI biometry pipeline that localizes 22 landmarks on reconstructed 3D volumes and derives 11 clinically relevant measurements, comparing two landmark localization networks. Evaluation spans 122 acquisitions including pathological cases, using mixed-effects modeling and comparison with normative growth curves.

entry.title: TISC: A Text-Driven Image Semantic Communication System for Faithful Reconstruction

author.name: Feifan Zhang, Yuyang Du, Xiaoyan Liu, Soung Chang Liew

entry.summary: TISC is a text-driven image semantic communication system that converts images to text for extremely low-bandwidth transmission and reconstructs them with diffusion at the receiver, addressing semantic loss during captioning and unfaithful reconstruction. It targets fine-grained attribute and spatial-position preservation across both stages.

entry.title: Bit-Level Triangular Content-Aware Permutation for Fragile Image Watermarking: Zero False Positive Rate, Single-Bit Sensitivity, and Arbitrary Dimension Support

author.name: Zahra Ghoraeian, Mohammad-Reza Sadeghi, Samaneh Mashhadi

entry.summary: A fragile image watermarking scheme replaces hash functions with a bit-plane content-aware permutation that has an avalanche property, aiming for zero false positives, single-bit tamper sensitivity, and support for arbitrary image dimensions. It targets vector quantization and collage attacks that defeat prior methods.

entry.title: Platform Adaptation Under Governance Interventions: Actor Best-Response Modeling and an External Public-Case Benchmark

author.name: Wesley Shu, Peng Wei

entry.summary: Proposes a game-theoretic style model of how platform participants best-respond to governance changes such as ranking tweaks, monetization thresholds and moderation rules, and evaluates it against 72 documented public platform cases. The goal is to predict gaming, moderation burden and downstream stability before interventions ship.

entry.title: MistyPilot: Enabling Social-Robot Control through Multi-Agent LLM Skill Orchestration

author.name: Xiao Wang, Lu Dong, Ifeoma Nwogu, Srirangaraj Setlur, Venu Govindaraju

entry.summary: Builds a multi-agent LLM controller for a commercial social robot that routes natural-language instructions to either a sensor-triggered physical control agent or a stateful social interaction agent, handling skill composition and event binding automatically. It removes much of the manual API plumbing developers currently do.

entry.title: Feasible and Novel Synthetic Population Generation with Tabular and Sequential Travel Attributes

author.name: Farbod Abbasi, Zachary Patterson, Bilal Farooq

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage regularized generative framework for synthesizing travel-demand populations that must combine static socio-demographics with sequential trip chains, explicitly balancing coverage of unobserved but valid combinations against generation of structurally impossible ones. Stage one uses an adversarial tabular generator with added regularization terms.

entry.title: Grounding Without Corrective Control: Truth-Tracking Profiles for Large Language Models

author.name: Brett Reynolds

entry.summary: A philosophical analysis distinguishing grounding from corrective control, arguing that LLM representations can have reference without live routes for detecting and repairing discrepancies. It develops route profiles as a tool for analyzing when a system's outputs genuinely track truth.

entry.title: PCT-Prompt: A Prompt-Guided Transformer Framework for Dense Prediction Tasks in Point Clouds

author.name: Dejun Zhang, Yanzi Bai, Yiqi Wu

entry.summary: PCT-Prompt augments a standard point cloud transformer with a prompt-guided feature branch that injects fine-grained multi-scale geometric priors for dense prediction in complex scenes. The pretrained transformer branch handles global features while the prompt branch supplies the missing local geometric inductive bias.

entry.title: Visible Reasoning and Indirect Prompt-Injection Monitorability Across English, Tamil, and Tanglish

author.name: Madhusudhanan G

entry.summary: A small case study of whether API-visible chain-of-thought helps monitor indirect prompt-injection attacks in one Indic-multilingual model across English, Tamil and code-mixed Tanglish. A pilot suggested reasoning reduced attack success, but a preregistered follow-up reversed the direction, and the author concludes the design cannot separate a real effect from prompt-specific noise.

entry.title: Large Language Model Assisted Operational Monitoring for Battery Energy Storage System Integrated Power Distribution Networks

author.name: Azmeer Akhtar, Md Fazley Rafy, Anurag K. Srivastava

entry.summary: Builds an operator-facing LLM interface that converts natural-language questions about battery storage in distribution networks into validated SQL over approved telemetry views, then checks retrieved measurements against engineering constraints. Aims to make grid telemetry queryable without exposing operators to unconstrained model output.

entry.title: A Responsible Artificial Intelligence Framework for Groundwater Modeling

author.name: Chong Chen, Yulu Zhang, Qingxi Guo, Yihan Liu

entry.summary: Applies six responsible-AI principles to groundwater modeling in a river basin case study, training LSTM and Transformer time-series models and validating them with post-hoc interpretability and related checks. Argues responsible AI practice is especially underdeveloped in hydrology compared to healthcare or finance.

entry.title: CoupVisor: Strategy Optimization by Round and Challenge Decision Support

author.name: Cris Huynh

entry.summary: CoupVisor is a decision-support system for the hidden-information card game Coup that shares one event representation across manual play, replay, simulation, belief tracking and learned policies, and estimates claim truthfulness by combining role priors with card counts. It compares rule-based advisors with learned and heuristic players.

entry.title: UAV Video Deblurring via Motion-Aware Diffusion: A Path to Robust Target Detection

author.name: Zhiqiang Hu, Shouren Huang, Masatoshi Ishikawa

entry.summary: Proposes a diffusion-based video deblurring pipeline for drone footage that adapts latent-space resolution to motion intensity and enforces temporal consistency, aiming to restore downstream target detection accuracy. The contribution is mostly an engineering combination of adaptive latent scaling with a motion-aware diffusion restorer for aerial imagery.

entry.title: ENAF: A Multi-Exit Network with an Adaptive Patch Fusion for Large Image Super Resolution

author.name: Duong M. Nguyen, Tuan Nghia Nguyen, Xuan Truong Nguyen

entry.summary: Builds a dynamic super-resolution network for very large images that uses early exits plus a tiny predictor of reconstruction quality to decide how much computation each patch deserves, replacing hand-crafted difficulty heuristics. An adaptive fusion step recombines patches processed at different depths.

entry.title: Identifying Confusion Trends in Concept-based XAI for Multi-Label Classification

author.name: Haadia Amjad, Ronald Tetzlaff

entry.summary: Evaluates two concept-based explanation methods on multi-label image classification with common backbones trained on the most annotated categories of a standard object dataset, focusing on where concept attributions become confused between co-occurring labels. The study characterizes systematic confusion patterns rather than proposing a new method.

entry.title: A Scalable Pipeline for LLM-Teacher Distillation Labeling: Work-Stealing Job Scheduling and Memory-Aware GPU Concurrency

author.name: Ravi Satya Durga Prasad Yenugula

entry.summary: Describes an engineering pipeline for large-scale distillation labeling with teacher models, combining a work-stealing job scheduler with exactly-once claims and crash tolerance with memory-aware GPU concurrency control. It is designed to be reproducible using only a compare-and-set primitive over a simple embedded database.

entry.title: Decoupling Parcellation from Classification: Systematic Benchmark of Fast Brain Segmentation Methods for Alzheimer's Disease Detection

author.name: Jiadao Zou, Hongyu Guo, Wei Xi

entry.summary: Systematically benchmarks fast deep-learning brain parcellation methods against a clinical baseline by measuring their effect on downstream Alzheimer's classification, across volumetry strategies and four classifier families including foundation models with few-shot prompting. All results are reported with bootstrap confidence intervals.

entry.title: Domain-Specific Text Embedding Models for Entity Resolution

author.name: Khajesh Sapram, Srivardhani Raju, Kishore Konda

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune general text embedding models with triplet objectives on synthetic business and person records containing identity-preserving variations and hard negatives, to make retrieval sensitive to entity identity rather than mere semantic similarity. Margin-based evaluation shows improved separation of matching versus non-matching records after adaptation.

entry.title: Fiber Fingerprints of Hidden Learning-State Dynamics

author.name: Qinyou Wang

entry.summary: Formalizes the idea that two learning systems can be behaviorally indistinguishable now yet respond differently to future training, defining fiber fingerprints as future-learning response laws restricted to present-behavior equivalence classes. Builds a Nerode-style minimal predictive representation and decomposes responses into visible, mode-reuse, and irreducible-new components.

entry.title: On Cross-Validation for Hyperparameter Optimization of Deep Learning Image Classifiers

author.name: Ljubomir Buturovic (East Palo Alto, United States)

entry.summary: Empirically compares fixed holdout, reshuffled holdout, and five-fold cross-validation as the validation signal driving hyperparameter search for deep image classifiers, scoring protocols by the absolute gap between the winning configuration's validation AUROC and its test AUROC. Focuses on small-sample regimes typical of medical imaging with search space, sampler, and test set held identical.

entry.title: STAR-FL: Secure Federated Learning with Spatial-Temporal Analysis and Robust Aggregation

author.name: Nawrin Tabassum, Yanzhao Wu

entry.summary: STAR-FL defends federated vision models against targeted data poisoning by clustering client updates over both space and time to identify and drop suspicious contributions, then damping the learning rate during aggregation to limit the residual influence of poisoned updates. Addresses the twin problems of detection accuracy and post-detection mitigation.

entry.title: An Adaptive Gradient Clipping and Noise Injection Mechanism for Differentially Private Federated Learning

author.name: Wenjing Wei, Alla Jammine, Farid Nait-Abdesselam

entry.summary: Presents an adaptive per-layer gradient clipping and noise calibration mechanism for differentially private federated learning with secure aggregation, where each client sets each layer's clipping threshold from the median of its per-sample gradient norms at every round. Aims to avoid the excessive clipping or excessive noise inherent in a single static global threshold.

entry.title: Identifying parameter couplings and uncertainties of mixed-noise stochastic systems via full-covariance Gaussian mixture network

author.name: Xiaolong Wang, Xiangwen Hao, Jing Feng, Yuanyuan Liu, Yong Xu

entry.summary: PENN-GMD trains a neural network to map partially observed trajectories of stochastic dynamical systems driven by mixed noise to a full-covariance Gaussian mixture over system parameters, using a surjective parameterization that hard-encodes mixture constraints and training by negative log-likelihood. The full covariance structure exposes parameter couplings and multimodal likelihood geometry that point estimates hide.

entry.title: LLMs Don't Pay for the Jump

author.name: Paras Balani, Subhrakanta Panda

entry.summary: A short position piece rebutting the claim that LLMs cannot perform creative abductive leaps for lack of embodied simulation, using Planck's quantization of energy as a counterexample driven by mathematical inconsistency rather than sensorimotor grounding. It is argument rather than experiment.

entry.title: Depth-Dominant Skeleton Detection for Natural Scenes

author.name: Chengkun Rao, Yixuan Deng, Min Li, Yangjun Ou, Ye Li, Ziwei Luo, Zhaojing Wang, Junwei Tang, Bangchao Wang, Xiaoyun Yan

entry.summary: DDSkel inverts the usual modality hierarchy for natural scene skeleton detection, making depth the dominant input and RGB auxiliary, on the grounds that depth is insensitive to color and texture clutter while giving clean contours. The paper claims first exploration of this depth-dominant paradigm for skeleton extraction.

entry.title: Incision trajectory tracing for electrosurgical navigation by CNN-based knife contacting frames extraction method

author.name: Yu Chun Wang, Kaixu Chen, Naoto Ienaga, Yoshihiro Kuroda

entry.summary: This study uses a CNN on thermal images to detect when an electrosurgical knife or ultrasonic cutter is actually contacting tissue, then extracts those contact frames to reconstruct incision trajectories for surgical navigation. The trajectories are intended to update preoperative 3D models during surgery.

entry.title: AccretionLink: On-Device Auditing of Exposure-Control Attacks on Attribute Inference

author.name: Faruk Alpay, Taylan Alpay

entry.summary: Studies an attack in which an adversary does not alter content but merely reorders or selects which authentic public posts a model sees, in order to strengthen inference of a private attribute, and proposes time-uniform e-process auditing for detecting it. Effects reported on synthetic profiles and a PAN15 test set are very small in magnitude.

entry.title: What 27 AI Safety Generalists Are Building This Summer

author.name: agucova

entry.summary: A roundup of projects from 27 participants in the first cohort of a Berkeley-based residency for AI safety generalists, including workshops for mid-career professionals entering the field, talent directories, university group support, and tooling for model welfare and model spec research. It is primarily a field-building status report.

entry.title: An Agentic Framework Using Rules and LLMs for Embedding and Annotating Descriptive Document Layouts: A Plant Science Use Case

author.name: Nicolas Turenne, Youcef Sklab, Eric Chenin, Jean-Daniel Zucker

entry.summary: Presents an agentic pipeline combining rules and LLMs to embed and annotate descriptive document layouts, applied to plant science literature for improved retrieval over structured botanical descriptions. It integrates layout analysis, dense and sparse retrieval, and multi-agent reasoning.

entry.title: Accuracy and Reliability of Large Language Models in Cosmetic Chemistry and Skin Health: A Benchmarking Study

author.name: Amelia Liu

entry.summary: Benchmarks 14 LLMs, with web search disabled, on cosmetic chemistry and skin health questions covering ingredient properties and consumer scenarios. Performance is generally weak, especially on quantitative reasoning and chemical structure identification, even though general skincare answers appear reasonable.

entry.title: Demand-Driven Vertiport Siting and Discrete-Event Fleet Simulation for On-Demand Urban Air Mobility Network Design

author.name: Hossein Z. Saghazadeh, Yonas Ayalew, Reza Ahmari, Parham Kebria, Abdollah Homaifar

entry.summary: Presents a demand-driven pipeline for urban air mobility network design that clusters estimated trip endpoints into candidate vertiport sites, screens networks under range and spacing constraints, and evaluates them with a discrete-event simulation of dispatch, deadheading, and battery swaps. A Los Angeles case study assesses door-to-door travel-time feasibility.

entry.title: Validation-Frontier Representation Selection under Constrained Observation

author.name: Wesley Shu

entry.summary: Studies how to choose a state representation when observations are incomplete, costly, or degraded, proposing a selector that trades balanced accuracy against feature cost, overfit gap, and validation-to-test instability. It is evaluated on three standard tabular datasets across five observation regimes.

entry.title: Constitutive Priors for Machine Intelligence: A Legitimacy Theory of the Artificial Physical World

author.name: Jiang Jiang (Persagy Science and Technology Co., Beijing, China), Yifu Sun (Persagy Science and Technology Co., Beijing, China), Qi Shen (Persagy Science and Technology Co., Beijing, China)

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that physical-world AI can escape its data cold-start problem by exploiting the fact that buildings and infrastructure ship with design archives that constitute their instances. It proposes a four-world ontology and a legitimacy criterion for when such documents may serve as priors.

entry.title: Baseline-Relative Counterfactual Refinement for Bit-Aware Visual Token Communication

author.name: Jia Guo, Xiaohan Zhao, Changwang Liu, Shuqing He, Chenyang Zhang, Bingchuan Zhao, Jinqi Zhu

entry.summary: GCR-C adds a rollout-style counterfactual correction layer to generative visual-token communication, replacing a baseline token-selection action only when a matched full-budget continuation shows a positive reconstruction gain under the same packet budget. It aims to fix the mismatch between local token-importance heuristics and end reconstruction quality. Application is bandwidth-constrained semantic communication.

entry.title: Drive, Pack, Fly: The Travelling Thief Problem with Drone

author.name: Kabir Murjani, Abhay Sobhanan

entry.summary: The paper introduces a routing variant in which a ground vehicle slows as its payload grows while an onboard drone retrieves outlying items, jointly optimizing item selection, routing, and flight synchronization to maximize profit net of time-based rental cost. A mixed-integer program solves small instances exactly and heuristics handle larger ones. It extends the travelling thief problem with drone logistics.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Generative Fuzzy System: Fuzzy Inference Guided Large Model Interactive Question Answering Framework

author.name: Hailong Yang, Jianqi Wang, Guanjin Wang, Zhaohong Deng

entry.summary: This framework uses fuzzy inference to guide large multimodal models in question answering, aiming to counter modality bias from differing feature distributions and to represent uncertainty when questions require knowledge from several domains. Fuzzy rules provide interpretable intermediate structure over deep semantic reasoning. It targets robustness in multimodal question answering.

entry.title: Fractional Optimizers Meet Fractal Activation Functions: An Empirical Study of Multi-Scale Optimization in Neural Network

author.name: Sebastian Raubitzek, Georg Goldenits, Sebastian Schrittwieser, Philip K\"onig, Kevin Mallinger

entry.summary: This empirical study examines whether fractional-derivative optimizers and fractal, self-similar activation functions interact usefully, evaluating optimizer families on synthetic benchmark surfaces with and without multi-scale perturbations and then in feedforward networks across ten classification datasets. The framing is multi-scale optimization matched to multi-scale nonlinearity. Results compare against conventional activations and optimizers.

entry.title: FedImp: Enhancing Federated Learning Convergence with Impurity-Based Weighting

author.name: Hai Anh Tran, Cuong Ta, Truong X. Tran

entry.summary: FedImp weights client contributions in federated averaging by the informational impurity of each client's local data distribution, aiming to speed convergence under non-IID conditions. Experiments on EMNIST and CIFAR-10 report substantial reductions in communication rounds.

entry.title: Does the Heart Show Your Pain? Tackling the X-ITE Pain Challenge with Self-Supervised ECG Representation Learning

author.name: Dominika Kunc, Przemys{\l}aw Kazienko, Stanis{\l}aw Saganowski

entry.summary: Evaluates self-supervised representation learning on ECG, plus multimodal pretraining with chest accelerometry, for classifying low versus medium pain on the X-ITE dataset. Results are modest overall and highlight large inter-subject variability in physiological pain signatures.

entry.title: Offline Ambient-Controlled Latent Diffusion: Architecture, Telemetry, and On-Device Evaluation

author.name: Lech Kalinowski, Artur Morys-Magiera, Piotr Mi{\l}kowski

entry.summary: Presents an Android app running latent diffusion fully on-device, conditioned on the ambient light sensor rather than text, with each generated artifact bound to its sensor reading, runtime path, and seed. The contribution is the auditability and telemetry workflow rather than a new generative method.

entry.title: Handover Analysis for Vehicular Communication with Explainability on the Fly

author.name: Ali Fuat Sahin, Semiha Tedik Ba\c{s}aran, Tufan Kumbasar

entry.summary: Applies inherently interpretable functional ANOVA models to handover detection in vehicular networks, using two real operator datasets, and compares against an LSTM with post-hoc SHAP explanations. The claim is that on-the-fly interpretability can match black-box accuracy while giving operators trustworthy real-time reasons.

entry.title: DualMiT-Net: Local-Global Transformer-Convolutional Fusion for Breast Mass Segmentation in Mammographic Regions of Interest

author.name: Alibek Kamiluly, Milana Muratova, Yash Patel, Fan Li

entry.summary: DualMiT-Net segments breast masses in mammographic regions of interest using a local Mix Transformer branch for mass detail and a global EfficientNet branch for surrounding tissue context, fused through a spatially gated decoder. The design targets low-contrast, irregular masses whose boundaries blend into breast tissue.

entry.title: LAPF: LLM-Agent-Based Path Finder Using the UAVScenes Dataset

author.name: Yousef Emami, Mohammadhossein Homaei, Hao Zhou, Miguel Guti\'errez Gait\'an, Atefeh Hajijamali Arani, Rui Zhang

entry.summary: LAPF wraps an LLM agent with memory, planning, and tool interaction around UAV path finding using the UAVScenes dataset, aiming for adaptability that predefined optimization or task-specific RL policies lack. The framework targets dynamic outdoor missions with uncertain conditions.

entry.title: Quantifying the Gap Between Laboratory Battery Test Patterns and Field Duty Profiles

author.name: Chunyang Zhao, Chresten Tr{\ae}holt

entry.summary: Quantifies the mismatch between laboratory battery test protocols and real field duty profiles across six data sources using usage frequency, intensity, C-rate, and a duty-structure index. Finds lab protocols are far more aggressive and structured than field traces, questioning degradation models trained on lab data.

entry.title: One Residual with Three Reuses: A Wristband Front End for Gesture Sensing

author.name: Sam Rifaki

entry.summary: Design study of an always-on wristband sensing front end that shares a single on-chip residual generator across classifier wake-up gating, radar-versus-IMU routing, and Kalman filter measurement reweighting, fitting in about 14 KB of program memory at 110K MACs per frame. Targets coin-cell power budgets for gesture and motor-symptom monitoring.

entry.title: An Analytical-Prior Framework for Data-Efficient Prediction of Sound-Reduction Frequencies in Rectangular Side-Branch Helmholtz Resonators

author.name: Jiaming Li

entry.summary: Uses a cheap analytical acoustic model as a prior for predicting sound-reduction frequencies of side-branch Helmholtz resonators under scarce finite-element data, either learning only the analytical-to-simulation discrepancy or distilling the analytical mapping into a self-contained predictor. Improves data efficiency for engineering surrogates.

entry.title: 6G Native AI and Channel Foundation Models

author.name: Shugong Xu, Jun Jiang, Yuan Gao

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that so-called native AI in 6G should be co-designed as an intrinsic part of the wireless system rather than bolted on, and that task-specific supervised models cannot serve as the technical basis because of labeled-data dependence and poor generalization across propagation environments. Advocates channel foundation models as the alternative substrate.

entry.title: Phase-Aware CNN for Real-Time 5G/6G Channel Estimation with Hardware-in-the-loop Validation

author.name: Javad Zolfaghari-Bengar, Rakibul Rony, Elisa Gomez-de-Lope, Alejandro Villena-Rodriguez, Abhinav Mahadevan, Nicolas Kourtellis

entry.summary: Presents a phase-aware convolutional network for pilot-based 5G/6G channel estimation that reconstructs both magnitude and phase across the subcarrier grid, explicitly handling the wrap-around discontinuity that degrades naive deep estimators.
