entry.summary: Proposes an amortized neural video representation that produces compact video tokens in one feed-forward pass and reconstructs continuous spatio-temporal queries with a shared coordinate-conditioned decoder. This avoids the per-video optimization or per-video weight generation that limits scalability of implicit video representations.

entry.title: SDO: Subspace Deconflicting Operator for Multi-Adapter Composition

author.name: Zhongsheng Wang, Zhedong Lin, Qian Liu, Xinyu Zhang, Jiamou Liu

entry.summary: Analyzes why composing independently trained diffusion adapters causes identity mixing and attribute leakage in multi-character generation, attributing it to overlapping dominant subspaces in shared layers. The proposed operator extracts compact subspace signatures from low-rank updates, measures pairwise conflict via output-subspace overlap, and deconflicts the updates before joint deployment.

entry.title: Benchmarking data-driven material models on the classic Treloar dataset

author.name: Hagen Holthusen, Moritz Flaschel, Denisa Martonov\'a, Ellen Kuhl

entry.summary: Benchmarks several machine-learning constitutive modeling frameworks for hyperelasticity against the classic Treloar rubber dataset, comparing fit quality, compute cost, hyperparameter sensitivity, and implementation effort. It provides a like-for-like comparison across neural-network and discovery-based approaches to material law learning. Useful housekeeping for a fast-growing scientific ML subfield.

entry.title: Polaris : Multi Agentic System for Conversational Enterprise Analytics

author.name: Varuni H K, Soham Sarkar, Jay Kumar, Goutham Krishnan, Tanvi Johari, Avinash Bharadwaj, Santosh Hegde

entry.summary: Polaris is a supervisor-led multi-agent system for conversational enterprise analytics that frames agent-task assignment as adaptive bipartite matching, coordinating querying, visualization, and reasoning agents with recovery and re-optimization. It targets the gap between organizations having data and getting usable insight from it. The contribution is an orchestration layer plus a ReAct-style reasoning pattern.

entry.title: Federated Prompt Learning: A Unified Framework, Empirical Analysis, and Future Directions

author.name: Qinglin Yang, Chen Qiu, Hongyuan Zhang, Pengdeng Li, Yuan Liu, Zhihong Tian

entry.summary: This survey consolidates federated prompt learning, covering motivations, taxonomies, and empirical comparisons of methods that adapt large models across decentralized clients without sharing raw data. It frames prompt-level federation as a communication-efficient alternative to federated fine-tuning. The value is orientation for researchers entering the area.

entry.title: Meteorology-driven Causal Nowcasting of Fugitive Landfill Emissions Enables Proactive Public Health Response

author.name: Timothy C. Pearce, David J. T. Smith, Alec Dobney, Alessia Freddo

entry.summary: Builds a machine learning nowcasting framework for hydrogen sulphide episodes at a monitored landfill whose internal memory structure is matched to empirically identified meteorological timescales, splitting fast wind transport from slower weather evolution. The aim is to shift public-health response from retrospective investigation to proactive warning.

entry.title: GBU-Palm: A Multimodal Video Dataset and Benchmark for Palm Presentation Attack Detection

author.name: Yingjie Ma, Zitong Yu, Wei Jia, Ajay Kumar, Linlin Shen

entry.summary: Releases a large multimodal video dataset for palm-based presentation attack detection with over 21k videos, 105 subjects, six capture environments, and synchronized RGB and near-infrared samples, plus leakage-controlled evaluation protocols. Benchmarks show substantial degradation when generalizing to unseen environments.

entry.title: High-dimensional nonparametric changepoint detection via low-rank degree-two density projection

author.name: Guoqing Zhang, Zhaixin Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a nonparametric high-dimensional changepoint detection method that encodes all degree-at-most-two density information in a symmetric feature matrix, turning density estimation into matrix mean estimation and scanning low-rank truncated matrix CUSUMs. Provides nonasymptotic guarantees exploiting low rank of the projected jump rather than coordinate sparsity.

entry.title: Connected Subspace Clustering: Hardness, a Scalable Heuristic, and an Application to Sea Level Geodesy

author.name: Johanna Hillebrand, Jan H\"ockendorff, J\"urgen Kusche, Kelin Luo, Heiko R\"oglin, Melanie Schmidt, Christian Sohler, Bernd Uebbing

entry.summary: Formalizes clustering under a connectivity constraint where each subspace cluster must be contiguous in a given graph, establishes hardness, and provides a scalable heuristic. Applied to partitioning sea-surface measurements into physically coherent regions for principal component analysis in geodesy.

entry.title: Trajectory Dynamics in Self-Supervised Learning Latent Space for Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Tom\'as Andrade Weber

entry.summary: Tests whether synthetic speech violates the temporal trajectory structure that physiological constraints impose on genuine speech, by training a causal LSTM next-frame predictor on bona fide audio only in a self-supervised latent space. A second supervised stage classifies from frozen LSTM internals, and a pooling baseline on identical features isolates the contribution of temporal modeling.

entry.title: Non-Shattering at and Above the Dynamical Temperature in the Spherical Pure p-Spin Model

author.name: Taegyun Kim

entry.summary: Proves that shattering, a landscape property linked to sampling hardness, does not occur in spherical pure p-spin glasses for certain overlap ranges at and above the dynamical temperature, using deterministic band-counting and a general sign law. For p equal to three the results rule out shattering at every fixed overlap in the studied regime.

entry.title: CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing

author.name: Qinye Zhou, Jun Zheng, Yongchao Du, Yuan Wang, Zhengrui Chen, Zuan Gao, Taihang Hu, Chao Lin, Yefeng Shen, Xingjian Wang, Zhao Wang, Zhengtao Wu, Xiaoli Xu, Zhengze Xu, Hao Yan, Denghui Yang, Yuhang Yu, Huayu Zhang, Mingzhou Zhang, Mengting Chen

entry.summary: A benchmark for real-world image editing spanning multi-image edits, reasoning-heavy instructions and deployment-style scenarios, arguing existing benchmarks are too simple to separate modern editing models. Provides three core evaluation suites with human-verified content.

entry.title: Reducing ANN-SNN Conversion Error via Residual Membrane Potential Alignment

author.name: Zirui Chen, Zihan Huang, Tong Bu, Jianhao Ding, Yiting Dong, Zhaofei Yu

entry.summary: Analyzes residual membrane potential statistics to explain why converting trained artificial networks into spiking networks loses accuracy at short timestep budgets, then proposes an alignment scheme to reduce this conversion error. Targets low-latency, energy-efficient neuromorphic inference.

entry.title: TeachMateGPT: A Multi-Agent Knowledge-Grounded Framework for Pedagogical Assessment Generation from Science Curriculum Materials

author.name: Fatema Tuj Johora Faria, Mukaffi Bin Moin, M. F. Mridha, Jubayer Al Mahmud

entry.summary: TeachMateGPT generates curriculum-grounded science assessment items using a hierarchical knowledge base that segments documents along syllabus structure and links them at multiple granularities, replacing flat token-window chunking, plus safeguards against weak evidence. It targets low-resource, board-exam-structured curricula that generic RAG systems serve poorly. The contribution is an applied multi-agent education system.

entry.title: Does ISO-Grounded NFR Specification Improve LLM Code Generation? A Comparison of Rich and Structured Interventions against a Natural-Language Baseline

author.name: Jo\`ao Pedro Monteiro Pereira, Vinicius Cardoso Garcia

entry.summary: This study asks whether grounding non-functional requirements in the ISO/IEC 25010 quality model, either as rich prose or structured JSON, improves LLM-generated code compared with terse one-line requirement phrasing, using HumanEval-style benchmarks and paired non-parametric statistics. Enriched specifications improved static quality proxies such as readability and reduced some smells. It provides evidence on prompt specification design for code quality rather than correctness.

entry.title: Rewrite Once, Validate Anywhere: Producing OWL-Aware SHACL Constraints (Extended Version)

author.name: Anouk Oudshoorn, Piotr Gorczyca, D\"orthe Arndt

entry.summary: This work internalizes OWL ontology axioms directly into SHACL shape constraints via a rewriting for a restricted fragment of OWL EL, so a standard validator produces reasoning-aware results without a separate inference step. It removes an error-prone and inefficient two-technology pipeline for validating RDF graphs. The contribution is formal, with correctness results for the rewriting.

entry.title: Resource-Adaptive Primal-Dual Learning for One-Warehouse Multi-Store Systems with Censored Demand

author.name: Jiameng Lyu

entry.summary: Develops a learning framework for one-warehouse multi-store inventory allocation with censored demand in which the target allocations and dual variables are re-indexed as remaining resource per period evolves, instead of fixing a target from the initial resource rate. Uses censored sales for gradient estimation along a primal-dual resolving path.

entry.title: What to Preserve, Where to Adapt: A Depth-Wise Analysis of Forgetting in Continual Gynecological Image Segmentation

author.name: Amal Saqib, Tausifa Jan Saleem, Numan Saeed, Mohammad Yaqub

entry.summary: Analyzes catastrophic forgetting layer by layer in continual gynecological image segmentation across heterogeneous modalities, anatomies and annotation protocols. The study identifies which encoder and decoder regions should be frozen versus adapted to balance retention and plasticity.

entry.title: XSA-MAD: Cross-modal Semantic Alignment for Morphing Attack Detection

author.name: Jie Jin, Mahiro Tokumasu, Yu Makino, Masakatsu Nishigaki, Tetsushi Ohki

entry.summary: Improves generalization of single-image morphing attack detection to unseen generators by decomposing morphing artifacts into four interpretable attributes covering identity, geometry, texture and consistency, encoding them as structured text, and progressively aligning a CLIP image encoder to that space. The result is a semantic representation intended to be generation-invariant.

entry.title: Does DiffusionGemma do latent reasoning?

author.name: Jan Bauer

entry.summary: Interpretability study of a diffusion-based text generation model from Google DeepMind, released in June 2026, testing whether its many denoising steps hide reasoning in continuous vectors that no one can read. The authors find that earlier reported performance loss from truncating the distribution is largely a sampling artifact, that even top-one projection usually preserves performance, and that the rare cases where the full vector matters appear to encode interpretable superposition; standard tools such as probes, steering and logit-lens variants transfer reasonably well.

entry.title: Content Depth Matters in Short-Video Recommendation: Rethinking the Attention Economy

author.name: Liwei Deng, Jing Jiang, Zhiwei Li, Yang Wang, Guodong Long

entry.summary: The paper introduces a Content Depth Score to quantify how much a short video is likely to stimulate higher-order cognitive engagement, then argues that engagement-maximizing recommenders systematically favor shallow content. It positions depth as a measurable objective that can be traded against attention-economy metrics. This is a societal-impact contribution to recommender objective design rather than a modeling advance.

entry.title: A Generalized Parallelogram Rule for Proportional Analogies on Riemannian Manifolds

author.name: Pierre-Alexandre Murena, Marcelo Hartmann

entry.summary: Generalizes the vector-space parallelogram rule for proportional analogies to Riemannian manifolds, defining an analogy relation valid on spheres, shape spaces, and manifolds of probability distributions. It extends a classic formalism used in word-embedding analogies to curved geometries. Primarily a theoretical contribution to analogical reasoning and geometric representation learning.

entry.title: RecipeNet: A Hierarchical Transformer for Recipe Data

author.name: Pin-Yen Huang, Sachin Chhabra, Prasanth Sai Gouripeddi, Abhinav Kumar, Baoxin Li

entry.summary: Introduces a hierarchical transformer for procedural recipe-style data, encoding heterogeneous fields within each step and dependencies across ordered steps rather than flattening everything into a fixed tabular schema. Reports consistent gains over standard tabular models on recipe datasets relevant to materials synthesis and manufacturing.

entry.title: Learning-to-Transition for Large-scale and High-Order MIMO Detection

author.name: Yubo Zhang, Yiyao Liu, Xiaodong Wang

entry.summary: Reformulates high-order MIMO signal detection as a learned stochastic sequence of full-vector transitions, using a channel-conditioned transformer that updates both an embedding and a sampling policy with blockwise autoregressive factorization. Includes a curriculum from residual minimization toward bit-error-rate objectives and soft-output generation for decoding.

entry.title: Hard Cases, Bad Labels: Testing Error Exposure and Error Location in Uncertainty Sampling Under Bounded Label Noise

author.name: John Myron Uy

entry.summary: Tests whether uncertainty-based active learning underperforms because it collects more mislabeled examples or because errors in hard regions are disproportionately damaging, using paired seeds across noise regimes and annotation budgets on tabular datasets. Uses exposure-matched noise controls to separate the two mechanisms.

entry.title: Dynamic Multi-Depot Vehicle Routing with Online Requests: Event-Driven Transformer--DRL and Rolling-Horizon Benchmarking

author.name: Faezeh Ardali, Gerald M. Knapp

entry.summary: Builds an event-driven learning framework for dynamic multi-depot vehicle routing with requests revealed over time, training masked MLP and transformer policies via behavior cloning and PPO with feasibility masking and commitment constraints on already-planned route prefixes. Benchmarks learned policies against insertion heuristics and time-limited rolling-horizon optimization.

entry.title: Sequence prediction under a lying oracle

author.name: Puspabeethi Samanta, Nikhil Karamchandani, Jayakrishnan Nair

entry.summary: Studies sequential probabilistic prediction over a finite alphabet where the loss reflects the cost of resolving outcomes through comparative queries to an oracle that may lie, giving algorithms and logarithmic regret-style bounds in both stochastic and adversarial settings. Connects prediction complexity to noisy comparison query models.

entry.title: CORAL: Curriculum-Optimized Reward Adaptation for LiDAR-Based Goal-Directed Urban Driving

author.name: Anisa Saleem, Duksu Kim

entry.summary: Presents a five-stage curriculum plus stage-aware reward weighting for LiDAR-based goal-directed urban driving trained with PPO in a simulator, shifting emphasis from mission progress toward route following, safety, smoothness and rule compliance as tasks harden. The policy is a multi-stream actor-critic network.

entry.title: BM25-Augmented Many-Shot Translation for Low-Resource North-Eastern Indian Languages

author.name: Aashish Dhawan, Christopher Driggers-Ellis, Dzmitry Kasinets, Christan Grant, Daisy Zhe Wang

entry.summary: A shared-task system that translates between English and eleven North-Eastern Indian languages by retrieving similar parallel examples with BM25 and prompting an existing Gemini flash model with many in-context examples, with no fine-tuning. A grid search tunes retrieval and exemplar counts across all 22 directions.

entry.title: Rethinking Auxiliary Modalities in Multimodal Zero-shot Anomaly Detection: From Semantic Fusion to Conditional Modulation

author.name: Peng Wu, Xin Ge, Yujia Sun, Guansong Pang

entry.summary: Argues that fusing depth or other auxiliary modalities directly into the shared semantic space of a vision-language anomaly detector corrupts the text-aligned anomaly semantics, and instead proposes a plug-and-play conditional modulation scheme. Aims for modality-agnostic zero-shot industrial anomaly detection without bespoke architectures.

entry.title: FIRM: Fine-Grained Intra-Token Representation of Masks for Remote Sensing Reasoning Segmentation

author.name: Weidong Tang, Kaiyu Li, Yikai Wang, Yanan Wu, Haotian Gan, Shihong Wang, Xiangyong Cao

entry.summary: Points out that a single binary mask label per visual token discards sub-token spatial detail, which hurts multimodal LLM reasoning segmentation on remote sensing imagery with thin structures and small adjacent targets. Predicts a sub-cell pattern code inside each token to recover fine boundaries.

entry.title: RankT2I: A Submodular Framework for Discovering Interpretable and Diverse Semantics in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Ritika Allada, Pinar Yanardag

entry.summary: A training-free, model-agnostic framework that automatically discovers which semantic edits a text-to-image model can actually perform in a given visual domain, by having a vision-language model propose candidates and then selecting a diverse, interpretable subset via submodular optimization. Removes trial-and-error prompt search for editing.

entry.title: MagnifiQ: Patch-aware Text Guided Progressive Upscaling for High-Resolution Image Restoration

author.name: Mahesh Reddy, Yashesh Savani, Antoine Mercier, Hong Cai, Fatih Porikli, Guillaume Berger

entry.summary: Restores and upscales images to 4K by progressively refining across resolutions and replacing the self-attention layers of a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model with convolutions whose cost scales linearly with pixels. Avoids the repeated-texture artifacts and quadratic cost of direct high-resolution diffusion.

entry.title: BICPO-VLA: Behavior-Identified Continuation Preference Optimization for Smooth Asynchronous Vision-Language-Action Control

author.name: Ming Shang, Yuchen Huang, Jiaoyang Chen, Haoyuan Hu, Han Yu, Liping Song, Luyun Feng, Shuo Bao, Wei Dong, Xinzhou Wang, Fuchun Sun

entry.summary: Targets the gap between when a new command is issued and when a robot actually hands control to the new action chunk, decomposing action chunks into coarse scaffold and residual coefficients so generation is faster and transitions are smoother. Adds an instruction-aware history encoder to disambiguate intended behavior.

entry.title: OccPlanner: Goal-Aware Occupancy-Conditioned Diffusion Planner for Pixel-Goal Navigation

author.name: Binling Huang, Nianjin Ye, Xi Yang, Liang Hu, Zhou Huang, Shuang Wei, Longrui Yang, Yanchi Chen, Lanpeng Jia

entry.summary: A diffusion planner for navigating to a goal specified as a pixel in the camera view, grounding that pixel into metric space by conditioning on learned local 3D occupancy. Also introduces a pipeline that converts monocular navigation videos into robot-centric occupancy labels for scalable supervision.

entry.title: Three thoughts on civilisational handoff

author.name: Cleo Nardo

entry.summary: Three speculative arguments about what happens when humans delegate civilizationally significant decisions to AI systems, including the counterintuitive claim that handoff might slow progress because aligned successors would be more afraid of the pace than their human predecessors were. Considers handoff by companies, governments and humanity broadly.

entry.title: Decoding the sequence determinants of locus-specific DNA methylation across human tissues

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A journal article on learning which DNA sequence features determine methylation at specific genomic locations across human tissues. Only the title was available in the provided data, so the modeling approach and results cannot be assessed.

entry.title: CMCNet: Aligning Ultrasound Image Embeddings with Textual TI-RADS Representations for Fine-Grained Thyroid Classification

author.name: Bingxin Yu, Xueli Wang, Jerry Zhou, Wenyan Wang, Li Wen, Lan Huang, Xin Feng, Fengfeng Zhou, Kewei Li

entry.summary: CMCNet aligns thyroid ultrasound image embeddings with textual representations of the clinical TI-RADS feature categories to support fine-grained five-level risk classification rather than binary malignancy prediction, and releases a 600-nodule dataset with paired transverse and longitudinal views, bounding boxes, and complete feature labels. It follows the clinical decision process explicitly. The annotated dataset is a notable contribution.

entry.title: S2Dialog: Multimodal Dialogue Retrieval with Semantic and Acoustic-Style Modeling

author.name: Xueqi Wang, Zhigang Wang, Runqing Zhang, Zhenqi Jia, Junfeng Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for retrieving whole dialogues that match a target both in textual semantics and acoustic conversational style, rather than matching single utterances or one modality. Retrieved dialogue exemplars are meant to support emotion recognition, spoken dialogue systems and conversational speech synthesis.

entry.title: Face Re-morphing: Differential Morphing Attack Detection via Feature-Space Similarity Changes

author.name: Jie Jin, Masakatsu Nishigaki, Tetsushi Ohki

entry.summary: Detects face morphing attacks differentially by applying a further morphing operation to the suspect document image and measuring how feature-space cosine similarities shift relative to a trusted live capture. The change in similarity, rather than a static difference, serves as the detection score.

entry.title: SemPlan: Benchmarking Structured Semantic Planning for LLM-Based Queries over Enterprise Data

author.name: Bruno Santos Teixeira

entry.summary: Introduces a deterministic bilingual synthetic benchmark of 1,800 cases comparing four architectures for natural-language querying of enterprise data: direct SQL generation, a bounded tool agent, structured semantic-request generation with deterministic planning, and a clarification-based stateful variant. It measures answer correctness alongside invalid queries, policy failures, cost, and nondeterminism.

entry.title: Joint Optimization of Memory and Computing Frequency for Energy-Efficient DNN Inference

author.name: Yunchu Han, Zhaojun Nan, Sheng Zhou, Zhisheng Niu

entry.summary: Argues that memory frequency, not just compute frequency, materially affects on-device DNN inference latency and energy, and jointly optimizes both together with communication resources to minimize total device energy. The formulation is grounded in a measured inference-time model across multiple mobile devices.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Production Scheduling in an Industry-Based Coating Scenario Using the Digital Model Playground

author.name: Arne Kr\"oger, Ralf Buscherm\"ohle, Wilhelm Hasselbring, Henrik Wilbers

entry.summary: Applies standard RL scheduling agents to an industry-inspired coating process with sequence-dependent setup times, machine breakdowns, and variable utilization, using an open-source discrete-event simulation framework. The point is to test whether RL scheduling results survive contact with realistic manufacturing complexity rather than toy benchmarks. It contributes an open simulation environment as well as results.

entry.title: Grounding Without Corrective Control: Truth-Tracking Profiles for Large Language Models

author.name: Brett Reynolds

entry.summary: A philosophy-of-AI paper distinguishing grounding from corrective control, arguing that an output is answerable only when live independent routes can detect and repair discrepancies, and introducing route profiles as a way to analyze truth-tracking in language model deployments. It treats text-only systems as the hard case for representational success. The framework offers vocabulary for reasoning about when model outputs can be trusted as tracking truth.

entry.title: Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation

author.name: Zhelun Wu

entry.summary: This paper argues that multi-source LLM pipelines should split evidence interpretation from decision aggregation, proposing a four-field evidence tuple of hypothesis, reliability bucket, rationale, and provenance as the interface between the two halves. It identifies count-scale drift, where thresholding a sum of unnormalized weights behaves as posterior thresholding at an uncontrolled operating point. The framing is useful for designing auditable evidence-combining systems.

entry.title: Optimal Power Allocation and AI Receiver Design for Superimposed DMRS and Data Transmission

author.name: Sha Hu, Zhongwang Fu

entry.summary: This paper derives an analytical model of the interaction between channel-estimation and detection errors for superimposed reference-symbol MIMO OFDM transmission, uses it to optimize pilot power allocation and patterns, and then builds a Transformer-encoder receiver performing iterative estimation and detection. It combines classical communication theory with a learned receiver. The audience is wireless physical-layer research.

entry.title: CipherSight: Robust Website Fingerprinting via Record-Resource Semantic Supervision under Distribution Shifts

author.name: Runhan Song, Qiqi Liu, Chuanzhou Pan, Zhenquan Ding, Youquan Xian, Chongru Fan, Lei Cui, Wei Wang, Zhiyu Hao

entry.summary: CipherSight performs HTTPS website fingerprinting from TLS record structure and resource-level semantics instead of raw TCP packet sequences, aiming for representations that survive temporal and geographic distribution shift and open-world settings with unseen sites. The hierarchical design targets a known generalization failure of prior fingerprinting models. It is a privacy-adjacent traffic analysis contribution.

entry.title: Content Based Video Narration of Gameplay with Vision Language Models

author.name: Mathew Varghese

entry.summary: This system generates spoken esports-style commentary for arbitrary gameplay recordings using a general-purpose vision-language model plus text to speech, with no engine telemetry or task-specific training. Key tricks are packing nine sampled frames into a single 3x3 mosaic so an image-native model can infer motion cheaply, and replaying recent narrations as assistant history for continuity. It is a lightweight demonstration of temporal reasoning workarounds for image-native models.

entry.title: Fixed-Budget Gaussian Volume Encoding with Structure-Aware Allocation

author.name: Michael R. Martin, Joseph Insley, Victor A. Mateevitsi, Silvio Rizzi, Kwan-Liu Ma

entry.summary: This paper encodes scientific scalar volume data as anisotropic Gaussian primitives under a fixed storage budget, allocating primitives analytically from local field structure and then refining them against the field without densification or pruning, so both storage and refinement time are controllable in situ. Truncation-aware evaluation substantially cuts encoding time. It addresses simulation output that outpaces storage and transfer capacity.

entry.title: AlignFace: Human-Aligned Face Similarity Metric with Interpretable Concept Relations

author.name: Ying Huang, Wencan Zhang, Brian Y. Lim

entry.summary: Proposes a face-similarity metric intended to track human perception more faithfully by grounding it in cognitive findings about face processing and exposing interpretable concept relations, rather than treating perception as a black box. It also targets population-level variation instead of assuming a single universal observer, which matters for evaluating face editing and privacy-protection systems.

entry.title: Acoustic UAV Detection in Battlefield Scenarios: Handling Noise, Domain Shift, and Weak Labels

author.name: Vadym Vilhurin, Volodymyr Sydorskyi, Andrii Shevtsov

entry.summary: Presents an acoustic drone-detection pipeline hardened for battlefield conditions using per-channel energy normalization, attention pooling, and domain-aware training with auxiliary classes and multi-microphone data. Targets very low signal-to-noise ratios, heterogeneous sensor hardware, and weak labels.

entry.title: From Style Replication to Style Exploration: Enabling Art Style Exploration with Analyze-Experiment-Resituate Framework

author.name: Wen-Fan Wang, TsaiHsuan Lin, Chi-Lan Yang, An-Ru Cheng, Bing-Yu Chen

entry.summary: Derives a three-part framework from interviews with professional digital artists to support exploring new visual styles with generative tools rather than replicating existing ones, covering reference interpretation, stylistic experimentation, and reflection on reception. Positions current tools as biased toward high-fidelity imitation.

entry.title: Robust XGBoosting for Regression

author.name: Iris Arag\'on Mladosich, Christophe Croux

entry.summary: Studies how sensitive gradient-boosted trees are to outliers and high-leverage points and replaces the usual squared or Huber loss with robust regression estimators, finding a two-step M then S style procedure gives the best robustness-accuracy tradeoff. Practical guidance for tabular regression on contaminated data.

entry.title: Variation Brownian Kernel Ladders

author.name: Mahdi Mohammadigohari

entry.summary: Develops a function-space framework in which recursively composed Brownian reproducing-kernel atoms are combined by signed-measure variation, and proves regularity, compactness, and strict growth of expressive capacity with depth under a non-degeneracy condition. Aims to make claims about the benefit of depth depend on an explicit complexity measure.

entry.title: Fashion Outfit Generation via Unified Sequential Composition Models

author.name: Kaicheng Pang, Xingxing Zou, Ruohan Xu, Waikeung Wong

entry.summary: Formalizes fashion outfit assembly as constrained ensemble generation modeled as a deterministic finite-horizon MDP, learns set-level compatibility and latent composition intent jointly, and searches the huge item space with a latent-expansion Monte Carlo tree search. Addresses the non-monotonic nature of aesthetic compatibility.

entry.title: Polar Code Based Federated Learning: Convergence Analysis and Resource Allocation

author.name: Han Xiao, Wei Kang, Nan Liu

entry.summary: Designs a federated learning communication scheme that exploits the unequal error protection property of polar codes to give stronger channel protection to the more significant bits of quantized model updates. Includes convergence analysis and resource allocation under finite blocklengths.

entry.title: Learning Unsteady Aneurysm Hemodynamics with Physics-Informed DeepONets

author.name: Oscar L. Cruz-Gonzalez, Val\'erie Deplano, Badih Ghattas

entry.summary: Develops a modified multi-input multi-output physics-informed DeepONet with an aggregated injection strategy to predict unsteady blood flow, wall shear stress and pressure fields in idealized abdominal aortic aneurysm geometries. The aim is to complement computational fluid dynamics with faster patient-specific hemodynamic assessment.

entry.title: Fast Implicit Neural Light Field Representation via Geometric Decomposition and Multi-Resolution Low-Rank Features

author.name: Yao Guo, Ligen Shi, Shuchen Sun, Jun Qiu, Chang Liu

entry.summary: Speeds up implicit neural light field reconstruction by decomposing the 4D ray space into horizontal disparity, spatial texture and other planes and representing them with multi-resolution low-rank features. The decomposition exploits spatial-angular redundancy and structured disparity to shorten optimization time while preserving cross-view consistency.

entry.title: Learning to Forecast Crop Growth from Earth Observation Data

author.name: Dominik Senti, Mehmet Ozgur Turkoglu, Michele Volpi, Helge Aasen

entry.summary: Uses Sentinel-2 satellite time series plus weather variables to forecast future leaf area index trajectories for winter wheat at national scale across Switzerland, with over 20 million pixel-level series. Handles the sparse, cloud-gapped supervision inherent to optical remote sensing.

entry.title: UMPIRE-Net: Unrolled Magnitude-Phase Regularization Network for Accelerated MRI

author.name: Mahdi Saberi, Toygan Kili\c{c}, Mehmet Ak\c{c}akaya

entry.summary: An unrolled physics-driven MRI reconstruction network that regularizes image magnitude and phase separately instead of jointly regularizing the complex image, which matters for partial Fourier acquisitions where recovering omitted k-space depends on phase. Improves reconstruction where phase modeling is critical.

entry.title: FlatLab: A Unified Methodology Framework and Simulation-Based Benchmark for Robotic Manipulation of Flat Objects

author.name: Xingyu Zhu, Wenshuo Han, Zhouyu Wang, Yuran Wang, Ruihai Wu, Hao Dong, Fan Tang, Hechang Chen, Hyung Jin Chang, Yixing Gao

entry.summary: A framework and simulation benchmark for manipulating flat, hard-to-grasp objects, splitting the problem into a strategy generator that predicts an approach from point clouds and an execution module built from reusable action primitives. Uses contrastive learning to make strategy representations object-invariant.

entry.title: A Temporal Barrier Framework for Collision Avoidance in Multi-Agent Autonomous Aerial Vehicles

author.name: Benedikt Barthel Sorensen, Mitchell Black, Erfaun Noorani, Themistoklis Sapsis

entry.summary: Defines a risk measure capturing how fast any nearby aircraft could reach a given agent if it acted adversarially, then builds a control barrier function directly in that time domain rather than in distance or velocity. Produces anticipatory but non-conservative collision avoidance for aircraft teams.

entry.title: Why AI systems are most useful as designers of new scientific tools

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature commentary arguing that the highest-leverage role for AI systems in science is designing new instruments, assays and computational tools rather than directly producing discoveries or writing papers. The framing is relevant to the ongoing debate about autonomous AI scientists and where lab investment in agentic research systems should be directed.

entry.title: Implementing Computational Law in Wolfram Language for the Governance of Artificial Intelligence

author.name: James K. Wiles

entry.summary: Implements a reified input-output deontic logic (the formalism behind a well-known legal knowledge base) in a symbolic computing language, covering obligations, permissions, constitutive norms, and temporal operators, and argues governance requires checking compliance rather than inspecting reasoning. It then tests whether an older GPT-4 generation model can translate English legal statements into the formalism and documents failure modes including hallucinated functions, dropped temporal scope, and code that runs while silently encoding the wrong norm.

entry.title: Designing Sustainable Federated Learning as a Service using Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Keya Patel, Sajib Mistry, Sheik Fattah, Deepak Kanneganti, Aneesh Krishna, Mufti Mahmud, Monowar Bhuyan

entry.summary: Proposes a carbon-constrained neural architecture search framework for federated-learning-as-a-service, transforming client sustainability profiles into a feasible architecture region before training and estimating per-client carbon feasibility under dynamic grid conditions. The goal is to keep heterogeneous clients participating under hard carbon budgets. It links sustainability constraints directly to architecture selection.

entry.title: Context Aware AI Assistant and AR Interface for Lunar Extravehicular Activity (EVA) Procedural Guidance

author.name: Rodrigo Gallardo, Qilmeg Doudatcz, Ganit Goldstein, Ilkyaz Sarimehmetoglu, Sergio Mutis, Alexander Htet Kyaw, Anita Lin, Clara Emmerling, Berfin Ataman, Skylar Tibbits

entry.summary: GAIN-AI grounds a language model in EVA procedure documents, live telemetry, and error-handling protocols encoded as structured JSON, then surfaces only minimal heads-up guidance for astronauts during simulated lunar spacewalks. The design principle is timing and attention management rather than raw information access. It is an applied human-AI interaction study in a high-stakes procedural domain.

entry.title: HiCo-GS: Hierarchical Context Aggregation and Geometric Consistency for Octree Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Wei Zhang, Shengkai Yu, Shiqiang Gong, Qi Zhang, Qiang Li, Qi Wang

entry.summary: Improves octree-based Gaussian splatting for city-scale novel view synthesis by letting anchor features at different levels of detail exchange information, which the authors argue fixes color drift and over-smoothing caused by level-wise isolation. Adds a geometric consistency component for higher-fidelity large-scene reconstruction.

entry.title: Deep Vision in Smart Manufacturing: MODERN Framework for Intelligent Quality Monitoring and Diagnosis

author.name: Yicheng Kang, Yuling Jiao, Xin Geng, Mahesh Nagarajan

entry.summary: Presents a deep learning framework for industrial quality monitoring that combines an inception-residual network with a statistical control chart on defect likelihood, plus a transfer-learning fault region estimator for localizing defective areas. It targets sensor-rich smart manufacturing lines.

entry.title: A Calibrated Test of Internal Action Maps: State Signals Without Global Affine Closure

author.name: Dekun Yang

entry.summary: Tests whether hidden-state directions that are decodable or causally usable also support reusable, composable action maps, using an evidence lattice of gates covering composition, inverses, decoding, and commutativity. Results on a synthetic affine group carrier and on a small post-trained Qwen model suggest state signals exist without global affine closure.

entry.title: Simulation-Driven Vehicular Traffic Data Augmentation: Extending Sensor Coverage Through Virtual Sensing

author.name: Davide Andrea Guastella, Eladio Montero Porras, Evangelos Pournaras, Gianluca Bontempi

entry.summary: Proposes generating augmented traffic datasets by replacing physical sensors with virtual sensors placed at surrogate road-network locations chosen via a graph-search heuristic that preserves flow continuity and traffic similarity. The goal is to let models generalize to unmonitored locations and survive sensor infrastructure changes without retraining. It targets a real cost and privacy constraint in urban mobility ML.

entry.title: A Hybrid LLM-Based Framework for Automated Security Annotation Generation in Business Process Models

author.name: Md Kamrul Islam, Tiphaine Henry, Mattia Salnitri, Julius K\"opke, Sami Souihi

entry.summary: Combines LLM-based semantic extraction with schema-constrained mapping, rule-based normalization, and deterministic validation to auto-generate security annotations for BPMN process models from natural-language requirements documents. Aims to replace an expert-intensive and error-prone manual modeling step.

entry.title: Style or Signature? Artist-Disjoint Evaluation of Style Classification in Frozen Vision Embeddings

author.name: Rory Ashton

entry.summary: Shows that reported accuracy of painting style classification from frozen CLIP-style embeddings partly reflects artist recognition rather than movement understanding, because standard random splits let works by the same painter appear on both sides. Under an artist-disjoint holdout on a balanced set of 320 paintings, nearest-neighbor style accuracy drops from 0.87 to 0.77.

entry.title: When Lexical Change Misleads: Rethinking Dynamic Topic Model Evaluation with Traditional and LLM-Based Metrics

author.name: Charu Karakkaparambil James

entry.summary: Compares traditional temporal coherence metrics with LLM-based semantic similarity for evaluating dynamic topic models, using 120 topics across three corpora, three human annotators and strata by degree of lexical change. Traditional coherence correlates erratically with human judgment while LLM semantic similarity aligns more strongly for one model family.

entry.title: Leading-Silence Augmentation and Multi-Stage Synthetic Supervision for the Second MLC-SLM Challenge

author.name: Kexin Shi, Renhe Sun, Yuge Huang, Ximeng Wang, Jiayi Zhou, Jian Liu, Malu Zhang

entry.summary: A challenge system report for multilingual conversational speech: for diarization and recognition it fine-tunes a large ASR model with random leading-silence cropping, timestamp correction and exponential moving average training, and for understanding it synthesizes question-answer pairs to fine-tune a large omni-modal model. Neither task provides oracle boundaries or, for the second task, any training QA data.

entry.title: Beyond Control Points: Arcsecond Relative-Motion Estimation of Vision Measurement Platforms With Incomplete or Absent Control Fields

author.name: Meng Lian, Jian Wang, Shuixin Pan, Haibo Liu, Yueqiang Zhang, Yulan Guo

entry.summary: Presents a differential framework that estimates inter-frame camera platform motion for long-range deformation monitoring directly from image displacements and known 3D points, avoiding the double pose-error propagation of absolute pose differencing. It degrades gracefully with zero, one or two control points and needs no nonlinear optimization or pose initialization.

entry.title: Secret-Stego Dissimilarity as a Design Axis: Invertible Coverless Image Steganography with Diffusion Models

author.name: Hongxin Xu, Jianping Mei, Can Wang, Defang Chen

entry.summary: InvCISD is an invertible diffusion framework for coverless image steganography that explicitly makes visual dissimilarity between the secret and the synthesized stego image a design objective, rather than only optimizing recovery fidelity. Prior diffusion-based methods leave structural and semantic resemblance that leaks information. The work adds a security axis to the evaluation of generative steganography.

entry.title: Data-driven techniques for translational neuroscience and personalized neuro-health

author.name: Vishal Subedi, Shashipraba N. K. Rajakaruna, Pratyusha Sarkar, Subhankar Chattoraj, Anjali Khasa, Siddhartha Nandy, Hamza Farooq, Animikh Biswas, Sanjay Chaudhuri, Asim K. Dey, Karuna Joshi, Christophe Lenglet, Ansu Chatterjee

entry.summary: This review surveys data-driven methods for early detection of neurodegenerative disease from neuroimaging, organized around four methodological pillars and aimed at individual-level, mechanistically grounded models of brain health. It emphasizes convergence toward clinically actionable personalized prediction. It is a domain review rather than a methods contribution.

entry.title: LP-NAS: Linear Programming-based Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Abhishek Shukla, Ankur Sinha, Faiz Hamid

entry.summary: Casts the architecture update in differentiable NAS as a linear program built from validation-loss gradients and training-loss Hessian information, giving a mathematical-programming view of the search step. Claims applicability across a wide range of continuous search spaces.

entry.title: SCVIB: Editable State-Conditioned Visual Instance Binding forMulti-Turn Personalized Localization

author.name: Xiongtai Yang, Ziyan He, Tao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a multi-turn visual grounding setting where several user-defined instances are introduced across turns and state events determine which is the final target, along with a 1,500-episode benchmark. Shows direct inference reaches only about 60 percent joint accuracy and proposes a transition-tree grounding method to close the gap.

entry.title: TRIAGE: Risk-Controlled Pseudo-Label Admission for Annotation-Efficient Semi-Supervised Retinal OCT Classification

author.name: Md Ashraful Hossen Akash, Shyla Afroge, Abdullah Al Mamun, Md. Kishor Morol, Tze Hui Liew

entry.summary: A semi-supervised retinal OCT classifier that admits pseudo-labels through a patient-level conformal risk controller with an asymmetric cost matrix, so false negatives on sight-threatening disease are penalized more than false positives. Targets annotation-efficient clinical deployment.

entry.title: Graph-MambaNav: Spatial-Temporal Graph Mamba Leveraging Object-Relation Knowledge for Object-Goal Navigation

author.name: Leyuan Sun, Genxin Chen, Linwei Ye, Yan Zhang, Xi Kan, Yanfei Sun

entry.summary: Applies a state-space graph model to object-goal navigation, arguing that ordering nodes by target relevance, rather than permutation-invariant attention, is what enables effective long-range spatial reasoning. Encodes object-relation knowledge in a spatial-temporal graph for embodied search.

entry.title: Communication in modular robotic motor control: Bilateral controllers under realistic constraints

author.name: Jingwen Li, Levin Kuhlmann, Jason Friedman, Gideon Kowadlo

entry.summary: Tests whether brain-inspired modular controllers with a delayed communication channel between two hemispheric modules outperform monolithic controllers for musculoskeletal arm control under signal-dependent noise and energy costs. Trained end-to-end in a differentiable two-arm simulator.

entry.title: PILOT: Privileged Imitation Learning for End-to-End Motion Planning of Autonomous UAVs under Partial Observability

author.name: Qingrui Zhang, Feng Xue, Xiang Zhou, Chenghao Yu

entry.summary: Distills an expensive optimal control expert with privileged information into a vision-based drone motion planner, regularized by a dual objective covering safety and dynamic feasibility, with a temporal convolutional module fusing depth history and odometry. Targets flight in cluttered environments under partial observability.

entry.title: Study Update: Does post-training quantization change welfare-relevant indicators in open-weight language models?

author.name: ashesfall

entry.summary: A progress update and preregistration amendment for a study testing whether post-training quantization of open-weight language models shifts welfare-relevant behavioral indicators toward more distressed or less stable states. Early calibration work on the development model and control model forced procedural changes before the main experiment.

entry.title: Case for Funding AI Safety in Japan

author.name: mmKALLL

entry.summary: A funding analysis of the Japanese AI safety ecosystem based on roughly 120 hours reviewing organizational finances and grant applications, estimating a gap of about 2.1 million dollars and substantially lower researcher costs than in the United States. Argues that dozens of researchers could be productively hired if funding existed.

entry.title: Depth-Aware Sensitivity Analysis of Mixture-of-Experts Models via Magnitude-Based Expert Masking

author.name: Pradeep Kumar Sharma, Shantanu Godbole, Hritvik Shrivastava

entry.summary: An empirical layer-wise sensitivity study of a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model (an existing Qwen3.6 35B A3B checkpoint with 256 experts per layer and top-8 routing), using magnitude-based expert masking on a cross-lingual code translation benchmark. The main finding is that sensitivity to expert removal is strongly depth-dependent, with early layers far more fragile than later ones.

entry.title: Ontology-Grounded Project Memory for Coding Agents

author.name: James Adam

entry.summary: Introduces MOOSEDev, which gives coding agents ontology-grounded project memory by storing architectural decisions, constraints, and rationales in a knowledge graph with lifecycle status, provenance, and supersession links, exposed through a Model Context Protocol interface. It is compared against a production vector-memory tool.

entry.title: Nanbeige4.2-3B on Apple Silicon: Fixing Deployment Bugs and Decreasing Looped Transformer Memory Overhead

author.name: John T. Halloran

entry.summary: A single-author engineering report on getting a 3B-parameter looped-transformer agentic model to run on Apple Silicon, documenting five checkpoint/library bugs that block out-of-the-box inference and showing that layer reuse roughly doubles peak attention memory. The author proposes a chunked-prefill scheme to make agentic workloads fit on consumer hardware. It matters as a practical reminder that parameter-efficient depth recycling trades parameters for memory at inference time.

entry.title: The Architect: Interactive Visualization of Deep Learning Mathematics Directly in Microsoft Excel

author.name: Mohammad Imrul Jubair, Tom Yeh

entry.summary: The Architect generates Excel workbooks that expose the full forward pass, backward pass, and parameter updates of a user-specified neural network as live, editable spreadsheet formulas. Learners can perturb inputs, weights, or hyperparameters and watch arithmetic propagate through the recalculation engine. It is an education and demystification tool rather than a research advance.

entry.title: Hybrid Quantum-inspired Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Privacy-Aware Federated Biosignal Learning

author.name: Chun-Hua Lin, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen, Yu-Chao Hsu, Kuo-Chung Peng, Jiun-Cheng Jiang, Chi-Sheng Chen, Tai-Yue Li, Nan-Yow Chen, En-Jui Kuo, Hsi-Sheng Goan

entry.summary: This work evaluates a hybrid quantum-inspired Kolmogorov-Arnold network for federated ECG arrhythmia classification, targeting communication efficiency and robustness under small client datasets, label imbalance, and non-IID distributions. Raw biosignals remain on hospitals and devices. The contribution is an empirical architecture comparison in a privacy-constrained clinical setting.

entry.title: BGA: A noise-immune neural distillation framework for malicious signature extraction in high-entropy encrypted flows

author.name: Sheng Hong, Yixuan Huang, Weiwei Jiang, Junyuan Zhang, Jiacheng Wang, Ruijian Jiao

entry.summary: BGA extracts malicious signatures from high-entropy encrypted TLS 1.3 industrial traffic by using variance analysis to separate discriminative control-plane features from cryptographic noise, a Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty to synthesize rare attack samples, and a bidirectional recurrent plus attention backbone for detection. Recall on rare state-command-injection attacks reportedly improved substantially. It is applied intrusion detection for industrial systems.

entry.title: Mind the Long Tail: Understanding the Difficulty of Delay Detection in Business Processes

author.name: Keyvan Amiri Elyasi, Lukas Kirchdorfer, Heiner Stuckenschmidt

entry.summary: Investigates why detecting delayed business-process cases is hard by moving beyond aggregate error metrics to examine model performance across the delay distribution, especially the operationally critical long tail. Frames intrinsic task difficulty as a distinct issue from architecture choice in predictive process monitoring.

entry.title: Designing Compact Neural Architectures via Neuron Gating and Mixed Activation

author.name: Abhishek Shukla, Ankur Sinha, Faiz Hamid

entry.summary: Formulates architecture search as bilevel optimization and introduces continuous relaxations of neuron-level gating and activation-function choice so compact networks can be found across MLPs, CNNs, RNNs, and transformers. Targets the discreteness and cost that make conventional NAS expensive.

entry.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning solution for pickup and delivery routing problems with time window and capacity constraints

author.name: Andrew Soroka, Alex Meshcheryakov, Sergey Gerasimov

entry.summary: Applies a modified deep reinforcement learning routing model to pickup-and-delivery problems with joint capacity and time-window constraints, reporting fast near-optimal solutions on small and medium instances. Extends learned routing to a constraint combination the authors say had not been handled before with this approach.

entry.title: Revisiting Energy-based Tabular Anomaly Detection: Energy and Reconstruction are Complementary

author.name: Junichiro Niimi

entry.summary: Revisits explicit energy-based models for tabular anomaly detection using a deep Boltzmann machine, arguing its mean-field energy score is complementary to reconstruction-based scores rather than redundant. Evaluated on two tabular benchmarks spanning marketing and network intrusion data.

entry.title: Continual Evolution Strategies in Control Tasks

author.name: Nicola Pitzalis, Eleni Nisioti, Antonio Carta, Davide Bacciu, Andrea Cossu

entry.summary: A short empirical study finding that evolution strategies suffer severe catastrophic forgetting on sequential MuJoCo locomotion tasks, that replay largely restores retention and can enable positive transfer, and that larger replay budgets reduce plasticity.

entry.title: PPOM: Marginalizing Patch-Grid Phase for CLIP-Based Generalizable Vision-Language Prompt Tuning

author.name: Liang Wang, Haoyang Li, Chao Wang, Guodong Long, Jing Jiang, Yan Peng

entry.summary: Observes that CLIP predictions shift depending on how an image aligns with the frozen vision transformer patch grid, then introduces a training-free inference operator that averages over paired opposite pixel shifts to marginalize this nuisance phase variable. Improves generalization of prompt-tuned vision-language models at no training cost.

entry.title: Machine learning of artistic fingerprints in jazz

author.name: Peter M. C. Harrison

entry.summary: A Nature Machine Intelligence News and Views piece by Peter Harrison discussing work by Cheston and colleagues that trains a classifier to identify twenty well-known jazz pianists from raw audio with reported accuracy up to 94 percent. Beyond the classification result, the analysis decomposes which musical dimensions such as melody, harmony, rhythm and dynamics carry performer-specific signal, giving a quantitative handle on the notion of individual artistic style.

entry.title: Stable Miscalibration in Large Language Models: A Practical View of High-Confidence Errors

author.name: Akira Okutomi

entry.summary: Studies whether confident wrong answers from language models are fragile or locally stable, combining an output-level confidence audit with an internal hidden-state sensitivity probe. It reports that self-critical prompting reduces internal state movement and that some high-confidence errors persist stably under small perturbations.

entry.title: LLMs Don't Pay for the Jump

author.name: Paras Balani, Subhrakanta Panda

entry.summary: This is a short position piece in an ongoing arXiv debate about whether LLMs can perform genuine abductive leaps, arguing via the Planck blackbody example that a major conceptual jump can be driven by mathematical inconsistency rather than embodied simulation. It is commentary on other position papers rather than new empirical or theoretical results. Its value is mostly framing for discussions of creativity and scientific discovery in models.

entry.title: Decoding the Past: An Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Sex Attribution in Prehistoric Hand Stencils

author.name: Karel Becerra, Boris Mederos, Dean Snow, Ram\'on A. Mollineda

entry.summary: Applies an uncertainty-aware deep learning pipeline to infer the biological sex of creators of Upper Paleolithic hand stencils, explicitly propagating uncertainty from image degradation, contour extraction, and population mismatch. Positions the modeling of uncertainty as essential given the absence of ground truth.

entry.title: Smart routes: a system for development and comparison of algorithms for solving vehicle routing problems with realistic constraints

author.name: Andrew Soroka, German Mikhelson, Alexander Mescheryakov, Sergey Gerasimov

entry.summary: Presents a system for developing and comparing algorithms on capacitated vehicle routing with time windows, benchmarking an exact solver against classical heuristics, an industrial routing framework, and a deep learning policy. Reports that at moderate instance sizes learned and heuristic solutions approach exact quality at much lower runtime.

entry.title: Adaptive Protection for Evolutionary Feature Construction in Symbolic Regression with Application to Credit Classification

author.name: Hengzhe Zhang, Qi Chen, Bing Xue, Lean Yu, Wolfgang Banzhaf, Mengjie Zhang

entry.summary: Adds an adaptive protection mechanism to evolutionary feature construction for symbolic regression so that highly important constructed features are shielded from disruptive genetic operators while less important ones remain free to change. Applied to credit classification, where interpretable engineered features are valuable.

entry.title: Adjacency-Based Spectral Proxy Control of Mobile Communication Agents

author.name: Mariana del Castillo, Federico Larroca

entry.summary: Studies online repositioning of controllable relay agents to keep a mobile network connected, replacing the standard algebraic-connectivity controller that needs slow distributed Fiedler vector estimation. The authors decompose the Fiedler gradient controller and derive an adjacency-based spectral proxy suitable for real-time distributed control.

entry.title: E-S2Feat:Semantic-Guided Spiking Local Feature Detection and Description for Event Cameras

author.name: Yang Yi, Juntao Hua, Jinpu Zhang, Liangwei Fan, Hui Shen, Dewen Hu

entry.summary: A spiking neural network pipeline for detecting and describing local features in event-camera streams, using module-specific spiking activations and semantic guidance to keep fine structure while staying energy efficient. Targets deployment on power-constrained platforms such as drones.

entry.title: CoDS: Robust Collaborative Perception via Expert-driven Detection and BEV Segmentation

author.name: Jinlong Wang, Yuang Jia, Junhong Lin, Nannan Li, Wei Gao

entry.summary: A multi-agent collaborative perception framework that jointly trains detection and bird-eye-view segmentation and quantifies per-region fusion feature quality with a reliability map, so pose errors and communication delays degrade performance less. Targets vehicle-to-vehicle perception robustness.

entry.title: PISA: A Pseudo-Individual Source-Domain Feature Adaptation Framework for Test-Time Open-Vocabulary Object Detection

author.name: Ziyan He, Xiongtai Yang, Tao Wang

entry.summary: A source-free test-time adaptation method for open-vocabulary object detection that synthesizes pseudo source-domain dense features rather than relying on confidence rescoring or pseudo-labels, which degrade when initial predictions are poor. Designed as a drop-in for open-vocabulary detectors under domain shift.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Polar Low Segmentation in Sentinel-1 SAR Imagery

author.name: Andrea Federici, Jakob Grahn, Giacomo Boracchi, Filippo Maria Bianchi

entry.summary: Generates pixel-level segmentation masks for polar low cyclones in radar satellite imagery using only image-level labels, via an adversarial erasing scheme with soft targets and region constraints. Addresses a domain where expert masks are unavailable and boundaries are inherently ambiguous.

entry.title: Knowledge-Data-Dual-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Vehicle Control in Mixed Traffic

author.name: Jie Fang, Wei Zheng, Mengyun Xu, Eui-Jin Kim

entry.summary: Combines a conditional generative model that synthesizes rare interaction scenarios with reinforcement learning for autonomous driving in mixed human and autonomous traffic, addressing long-tail safety events and the instability of hybrid discrete-continuous action spaces. Uses knowledge priors alongside data-driven learning.

entry.title: Demonstration of Space Robot Teleoperation over a Lossy and Delayed Network using ATMOS

author.name: Inkyu Jang, Gregorio Marchesini, Nicola De Carli, Byeongjun Kim, Sunwoo Hwang, Dabin Kim, Elias Krantz, Youngkyoung Kong, Frank J. Jiang, Annika Wong, Pedro Roque, Prasetyo W. L. Sanjaya, Nicola Bastianello, Mani H. Dhullipalla, Karl H. Johansson, Hyungbo Shim, Dimos V. Dimarogonas, H. Jin Kim

entry.summary: Hardware demonstration of teleoperating a planar spacecraft-analog robot through a lossy, variably delayed link, combining state prediction with trajectory tracking to complete a docking maneuver. Validates control architectures for ground-operated orbital servicing.

entry.title: Control-Informed Constraint Adaptation in Minimum-Time Trajectory Planning for Autonomous Racing

author.name: Ann-Kathrin Schwehn, Alexander Langmann, Mattia Piccinini, Johannes Betz

entry.summary: An online racing trajectory planner that measures its own systematic tracking errors during a run and adaptively relaxes or tightens spatial track constraints, reclaiming margin normally sacrificed to conservative assumptions about perfect tracking. Remains time-optimal while accounting for controller execution error.

entry.title: Cross-Disciplinary Taxonomy and Modeling of Misunderstanding Generation, Amplification, and Detection, from Pragmatics to AI Agents

author.name: Babak Abbaschian

entry.summary: Consolidates work from nine research fields into a taxonomy of how misunderstanding is generated, amplified, detected, or left unrepaired, and identifies eleven specific failure modes tied to points in a communicative process. It aims to inform detection and repair in AI-mediated and agent-to-agent communication.

entry.title: Towards Efficient Multimodal and Multilingual Opinion Extraction for STI: A QLoRA-Based Fine-Tuning Approach

author.name: Sheng Hong, Xuanqi Wang, Jiacheng Wang, Yuwei Wang

entry.summary: Fine-tunes video-language models with QLoRA on about 2,200 curated multilingual multimodal samples to extract core opinions for science and technology intelligence, using visual evidence as an anchor for textual judgment. It targets structured-output reliability that off-the-shelf models lack in zero-shot multilingual settings. Primarily an applied fine-tuning pipeline for an information-analysis use case.

entry.title: Voxel-based 3D Facies Segmentation from Seismic Data: A Comparative Study

author.name: Duc-Thanh Pham, Minh-Tan Pham, Anh Nguyen, Van Nguyen

entry.summary: This paper provides a reproducible comparative benchmark for voxel-based 3D seismic facies segmentation, arguing that the common practice of slicing 3D volumes into 2D inline and crossline images introduces cross-slice discontinuities and discards structural continuity. Multiple architectures are compared under a consistent 3D protocol. The contribution is a domain benchmark rather than new architecture.

entry.title: Owner3D: Ownership-Guided Style Writing for Training-Free Localized 3D Stylization

author.name: Suchang Tao, Kaifeng Shi, Zhiyan Liu, Zhuoyuan Jiang, Yuqi Ouyang

entry.summary: Training-free localized stylization for large 3D reconstruction models that writes reference style only into triplane regions owned by the target part, avoiding style bleeding onto neighboring surfaces. Produces a single stylized triplane without extra optimization.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Skeleton-Based Action Anticipation

author.name: Hongsong Wang, Pengbo Yan, Yang Zhang, Qiuxia Lai

entry.summary: Defines and benchmarks a new task: anticipating in-progress human actions from partial skeleton sequences when the action class was never seen during training. Combines the difficulty of early prediction with zero-shot generalization for robotics-relevant intent prediction.

entry.title: IRGNN: Efficient Invariant Radar Graph Neural Network for Radar Point Cloud Object Detection

author.name: Xiao Guo, Wanke Xia, Lili Yang, Caicong Wu

entry.summary: Converts sparse automotive radar returns into graphs with translation- and rotation-invariant edge features and runs a graph neural network for 3D detection, motivated by radar robustness in bad weather where lidar degrades. Emphasizes efficiency alongside accuracy.

entry.title: An Interactive, Automated 4D-STEM data acquisition and analysis routine for Scanning Electron Nanobeam Diffraction and Ptychography experiments

author.name: Mohsen Danaie, Max England, Yiming Xu, Ruomu Zhang, Ed Darnbrough, Josh Willem De Boer, Frederick Allars, Zaeem Najeeb, Aakash Varambhia, Jinseok Ryu, Benjamin Bradnick, Damien McGrouther, Manfred E. Schuster, Christopher S. Allen

entry.summary: Describes an automated acquisition and analysis routine for four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy, exposing microscope functions through a programming interface to remove operator bias and enable high-throughput statistical studies. Represents lab automation for materials characterization.

entry.title: Proxy-Validated LLM UX Micro-Simulations: An Artifact-First Protocol for Early-Stage Decision Support

author.name: Alexandre Cristov\~ao Maiorano

entry.summary: This paper proposes an LLM-driven pipeline that simulates user experience feedback from personas, tasks, and UI screenshots for teams that cannot run real usability studies, and validates the simulated friction themes against proxy corpora such as app reviews and support tweets using Jaccard-style alignment metrics. The contribution is mainly a lightweight validation protocol for synthetic user research. It is a pragmatic tool paper for early-stage product decisions.

entry.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Spatially Independent Multispectral Land Classification

author.name: Katherine L. Bauer, Teemu Harkonen, Simo Sarkka, Arturo Sanchez-Azofeifa

entry.summary: Benchmarks Kolmogorov-Arnold networks against random forests and multilayer perceptrons for pixel-wise land cover classification from Landsat imagery, training in one Canadian city and testing on an independent city across five land classes. The setup deliberately isolates spectral rather than spatial information.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Qwen3-27B for C-to-Rust Code Translation: A Three-Stage Curriculum of Pretraining, Debugging-Aware SFT, and Task-Specific SFT

author.name: Pu Zhao, Changdi Yang, Yixiao Chen, Yi Gao, Yifan Cao, Haochen Zeng, Yanzhi Wang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.13681v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Translating C code into safe, idiomatic Rust is a longstanding software-engineering goal because it can eliminate entire classes of memory-safety vul...

entry.title: Musical Mirrors: The LLM as Sounding Board in Songwriting

author.name: Xiao Xiao

entry.summary: This first-person case study documents eight months of songwriting in which a language model acted as an interpretive sounding board for human-generated material rather than a generator followed by human curation, analyzed through a sociological theory of resonance. The author argues sounding-board behavior had to be actively cultivated through sustained calibration. It offers a qualitative alternative framing of creative human-AI collaboration.

entry.title: Structure-Guided Spatiotemporal Attention Graph Neural Network for Traffic Flow Prediction

author.name: Xuanmian He, Can Li, Wanjing Ma

entry.summary: Proposes a spatiotemporal graph attention network for traffic flow forecasting that builds interpretability into the architecture rather than relying on post-hoc explanations, aiming to expose the structural mechanisms behind predictions. Motivation is deployment trust in safety-critical urban traffic management.

entry.title: Ensuring Safe Physical AI in Urban Mobility via Hazard-Informed Synthesized Envelopes

author.name: Alexei Odinokov, Rostislav Yavorskiy

entry.summary: Sketches a framework that carries results of systematic hazard analysis into runtime safety envelopes for urban robots, spanning symbolic, spatial, and dynamic world-model layers instead of scattering safety checks across software modules. Positions the representation as an interface to physical-AI runtime enforcement.

entry.title: Optimal Scheduling of Road Maintenance Jobs Considering Impact on Traffic Flows

author.name: Charitha Nandepu, Lohitha Kalepu, Gabriele Ciavarella, SangWoo Park

entry.summary: Trains data-driven surrogates that approximate equilibrium traffic assignment flows directly from origin-destination demand so that road maintenance scheduling can be optimized without repeatedly solving expensive equilibrium problems. Demonstrated on real traffic data from the Newark area.

entry.title: Robust Dual-Model Collaborative Random Vector Functional Link Network

author.name: A. Quadir, A. Rahaman, Mushir Akhtar, M. Tanveer

entry.summary: Replaces the least-squares objective in random vector functional link networks with a kernel risk-sensitive mean p-power criterion so the model downweights corrupted labels, outliers, and imbalanced data while keeping fast randomized-feature training. Presented with a dual-model collaborative variant.

entry.title: Recent Advances in Deep Learning-Based Drug-Target Binding Affinity Prediction

author.name: Jafin Khan, Md Hossain Shuvo

entry.summary: Reviews recent deep learning approaches to drug-target binding affinity prediction, comparing architectures and molecular representation strategies and analyzing seven commonly used benchmark datasets and their evaluation metrics. Aims to surface limitations and research gaps in the current literature.

entry.title: TRUE-Colon: Exposing a Consistent Transfer Asymmetry in Real-Time Polyp Detection

author.name: Sebastian Doerrich, Andreas Franz Schwab, Francesco Di Salvo, Shyam Nandan Rai, Hanh Huyen My Nguyen, Christian Ledig

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.13711v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computer-aided detection (CADe) systems for colonoscopy promise to reduce clinical miss rates, yet reliable real-world deployment remains elusive. Th...

entry.title: Architecture and Affordances of PLAUD: Performative Latents and Unsupervised DDSP

author.name: B{\l}a\.zej Kotowski, Frederic Font

entry.summary: Describes the architecture and interaction design of a neural synthesizer plugin for live electronic music that combines a variational differentiable-DSP model, latent smoothing, adversarial and spectral losses, and optional transformer prior, plus deliberate circuit-bending style interventions. The paper pairs the technical description with an affordance analysis of performative use.

entry.title: A Survey of Large Models in Sports

author.name: Yichen Xu, Jianzhe Ma, Chuhan Wang, Zhonghao Cao, Liangyu Chen, Wenxuan Wang, Qin Jin

entry.summary: A survey of large language and multimodal models applied to sports, covering tasks and applications for different participant groups, available datasets and benchmarks, and open challenges. It aims to consolidate a scattered application area.

entry.title: ProFocus: Interpreting Affective Experience in Artistic Images with Progressive Visual Focusing

author.name: Zhiyan Zhang, Zicheng Yan, Jianqi Chen, Peipei Song, Shanshan Wang, Xun Yang

entry.summary: Presents a framework for predicting the emotions that artworks evoke by progressively focusing visual attention in stages modeled on a hierarchical theory of aesthetic appreciation, rather than relying on generic CLIP embeddings. Targets affective computing on visual art, where metaphor and abstraction defeat standard features.

entry.title: SSP: An Event-Matched Syn2Sim2Phy Cross-Domain Evaluation Framework for Autonomous Driving VLA Models

author.name: Haojie Feng, Peizhi Zhang, Xinrui Zhang, Zhuoren Li, Junpeng Huang, Xiurong Wang, Dongxiao Yin, Yuxiang Zhang, Junfan Zhu, Lu Xiong

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.14024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models for autonomous driving jointly produce scene interpretation, language-based reasoning, and driving trajectories. Ex...

entry.title: InstructVVT: Instruction-Driven Video Virtual Try-On without Auxiliary Spatial Priors

author.name: Dingbao Shao, Song Wu, Xinyu Chen, Qian Wang, Jiahang Li, Kuai Jiang, Jiang Lin, Yuhang Liu, Ziyu Chen, Duo Li, Jiaxin Hu, Shengrong Gu, Ziheng Tang, Rongrong Liu, Yanlun Peng, Liang Li, Junlan Feng, Lujia Jin, Ting Zhang, Jian Yang, Zili Yi

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.14070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video virtual try-on is a highly constrained editing task requiring the precise replacement of a target person's clothing while strictly preserving the...

entry.title: VLM- and LLM-Driven Multi-Agent System for PET Image Denoising

author.name: Boxiao Yu, Savas Ozdemir, Yang Xing, Fumio Hashimoto, Jiong Wu, Yizhou Chen, Axel Rominger, Ruogu Fang, Kuangyu Shi, Tinsu Pan, Kuang Gong

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.13791v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) imaging suffers from limited spatial resolution and low signal-to-noise ratio, which can compromise quantitative a...

entry.title: A Subjective Study on a New Sharpness Informed Class of Metrics

author.name: Uditangshu Aurangabadkar, Vibhoothi Vibhoothi, Darren Ramsook, Anil Kokaram

entry.summary: Runs a human subjective study on deblurring models trained with and without losses that explicitly target sharpness, releases a dataset with graded sharpness levels and opinion scores, and proposes image quality metrics that penalize over-sharpening. The sharpness-informed variant correlates better with human judgment than standard peak signal-to-noise ratio variants.

entry.title: MMUSV-Sim: A Perception-Oriented Simulation and Data-Generation Platform for Multi-USV Cooperative Perception

author.name: Ziao Li, Jianxiong Ye, Biao Tang, Leping Zhang, Kun Zuo, Siyu Huang, Chenqiang Gao

entry.summary: A game-engine-based maritime simulator that generates synchronized multi-sensor data for teams of unmanned surface vehicles across islands, open sea and port settings with configurable weather and waves. Supplies shared annotations for cooperative perception research where real multi-vessel data is scarce.

entry.title: Ontology-Grounded World Models for Failure Diagnosis and Closed-Loop Repair in Physical AI Systems

author.name: Kailin Wang, Haoxiang Jie, Yaoyuan Yan, Jiacheng Zhou, Zhiyou Heng

entry.summary: Layers a symbolic ontology over a learned world model so that robot failures are recorded as specific unmet task predicates with labeled correction routes and verified acceptance results, rather than opaque quality scores. Aims at closed-loop diagnosis and repair for physical AI systems.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Tube-Based Safety-Certificate for Autonomous Navigation of Articulated Vehicles

author.name: Mohd. Faizuddin Faruqui, Ratnangshu Das, Ravi Kumar L, Pushpak Jagtap

entry.summary: Presents a spatiotemporal tube planning method that certifies that every trailer in an articulated truck stays inside the road corridor throughout a maneuver, using linked-body kinematics and sway constraints. Targets narrow-route autonomous navigation for freight vehicles and towed automated guided vehicles.

entry.title: Separating Spatial and Clinical Risk with Node-Splitting SVM Survival Trees

author.name: Drew Lazar, Aye Aye Maung

entry.summary: A two-stage nonparametric survival method that first fits a clinical tree to patient covariates, then fits a second tree to the residual cumulative hazards over geographic coordinates, so spatial risk is separated from clinically explainable variation. Produces piecewise-constant, interpretable spatial risk maps.

entry.title: Shift Aware Transfer Learning with Adaptive Dual-Encoder Fusion for PM Forecasting in Data-Limited Environments

author.name: Shahab Band, Hamed Mohammadi

entry.summary: This work forecasts short-horizon PM2.5 concentrations in data-scarce regions using a dual-encoder transfer framework that fuses a source encoder pretrained on US monitoring stations with target-specific representation learning, explicitly guarding against negative transfer under distribution shift. It is validated on two years of hourly data from 77 Taiwanese stations. The contribution is applied environmental forecasting rather than core ML.

entry.title: Interactive Analysis of Global Explanations using Aggregated Class Activation Maps for Network Data

author.name: Igor Cherepanov, David Sessler, Alex Ulmer, Felix Wagner, Throsten May, J\"orn Kohlhammer

entry.summary: This work provides a visual analytics system that aggregates class activation maps to give global explanations for deep classifiers of encrypted network traffic, helping analysts spot divergent sub-patterns inside a single predicted class and extract descriptive rules for firewall and intrusion detection use. It is applied explainable AI for security operations. The novelty lies in the interactive aggregation workflow rather than new explanation theory.

entry.title: Probabilistic indirect models for undrained shear strength: addressing significant data missing and variability with advanced imputation and machine learning techniques

author.name: Haibin Xiong, Shaoheng Dai, Peng Lan, Xuzhen He, Chenxi Tong, Sheng Zhang, Daichao Sheng

entry.summary: Develops probabilistic models for predicting undrained soil shear strength from index and cone-penetration measurements on a large global clay database, comparing three imputation strategies for heavily missing data and validating them through a probabilistic gradient boosting model. Delivers uncertainty-aware predictions for geotechnical design.

entry.title: SAFE: Scene-Aware Feature Modulation for Color Constancy with Learned Color Space in Pure-Color Scenes

author.name: Yuan-Kang Lee, Kuan-Lin Chen, Chih-Heng Chang, Jian-Jiun Ding

entry.summary: Proposes a scene-aware feature modulation network plus a learned, scene-dependent chromaticity space to fix illumination estimation when nearly all pixels in a photo share one hue, a failure case where standard color constancy cues collapse. Reports consistent gains on pure-color scenes over prior baselines.

entry.title: Label-Free Deep-Tissue Peripheral Nerve Detection with a Handheld Multimodal OCT Probe and NerveDetNet

author.name: Yihan Wang, Ruilin You, Shaobai Li, Jiabin Chen, Bofan Song, Anh D. Le, Rongguang Liang

entry.summary: Combines a handheld probe integrating swept-source optical coherence tomography with white light and autofluorescence imaging, plus a learned detector, to find peripheral nerves buried under intact tissue and estimate their depth without contrast agents. Aimed at intraoperative guidance to avoid nerve injury.

entry.title: THRIVE: Therapeutic Humanoid Robot In Virtual Environment

author.name: Jin Xu, Yu-Ping Chen, Ayanna Howard

entry.summary: An at-home pediatric rehabilitation platform combining virtual reality upper-limb games, camera-based motion tracking and a socially interactive robot therapist that coaches during play. Designed to increase adherence to task-specific practice for children with motor impairments.

entry.title: Extending Occam's inversion with lasso fusion, overcomplete dictionaries, and isotropic total variation regularisation

author.name: Anandaroop Ray

entry.summary: Modernizes a classical geophysical inversion algorithm by importing tools from statistics and imaging, notably orientation-invariant total variation, fused lasso and overcomplete dictionaries, correcting a distinction often glossed over in geophysics. Yields sharper but still noise-consistent subsurface models.

entry.title: Source-Agnostic Image Translation Based on Latent Aware Adaptive Masking

author.name: Tomislav Dobri\v{c}ki, Byung-Woo Hong

entry.summary: Refines an editing mask during reverse diffusion by thresholding the statistics of a pretrained model prediction discrepancy at each noise level, so the edited region adapts to model confidence rather than a fixed cutoff. Demonstrated on face and animal face translation datasets.
