The surrogate delivers roughly a thousandfold speedup over explicit quantum calculations.

entry.title: Latent variable models for simultaneous EOV identification and removal in population-based SHM

author.name: M. D. Champneys, M. R. Jones, A. J. Hughes, T. J. Rogers, E. J. Cross, K. Worden

entry.summary: Proposes latent variable models that jointly identify and remove unmeasured environmental and operational variability in population-based structural health monitoring, using slowness of the latent process as an identifying assumption instead of variance-based projection. Avoids discarding damage-sensitive directions. Domain-specific but statistically principled.

entry.title: LabelFusion-TS: Fusing Large Language Models, Transformer Encoders, and Financial Time Series for Monetary-Policy Stance Classification

author.name: Michael Schlee, Fabian Lukassen, Christoph Weisser

entry.summary: LabelFusion-TS classifies Federal Reserve sentences as hawkish, dovish, or neutral by fusing a fine-tuned RoBERTa encoder, a prompted LLM, and an ensemble of time-series transformers over preceding market data through a small voting network. Tests whether market context helps when only about a thousand labeled sentences exist. Applied finance NLP.

entry.title: Large Language Model-Driven Small-Capitalization Trading: Integrating Financial News Sentiment, Macroeconomic Indicators, and Technical Signals

author.name: Alireza Kargarzadeh, Nariman Khaledian, Navid Parvini, Arman Khaledian

entry.summary: Feeds LLM-derived news signals plus decomposed aleatoric and epistemic risk directly into the covariance matrix of portfolio allocators for Russell 2000 small-cap trading, tested under alpha-trigger, beta-trigger, and combined stock-selection regimes. The uncertainty-aware covariance construction is the main methodological twist. Backtest-based financial application.

entry.title: KANResDiff: Learning Local Residual Diffusion via Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Ambiguous Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Fanding Li (Faculty of Computing, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, China), Chenglin Wang (Faculty of Computing, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, China), Xiangyu Li (Faculty of Computing, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, China), Xingyu Qiu (Faculty of Computing, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, China), Xinghua Ma (Faculty of Computing, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, China), Xiangming Yin (Faculty of Computing, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, China), Haiyang Li (Faculty of Computing, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, China), Suyu Dong (College of Computer and Control Engineering, Northeast Forestry University, Harbin, China), Wei Wang (Faculty of Computing, Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen, China), Kuanquan Wang (Faculty of Computing, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, China), Gongning Luo (Faculty of Computing, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, China), Shuo Li (Department of Computer and Data Science and Department of Biomedical Engineering, Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland, Ohio 44106, United States)

entry.summary: KANResDiff builds an ambiguous medical image segmentation diffusion model where Kolmogorov-Arnold spline time embeddings give each denoising stage a distinct semantic role, and a residual Schroedinger bridge injects deterministic structure. Aims to produce diverse but plausible segmentation hypotheses through progressive rather than fixed stochasticity.

entry.title: BoltNet: An Ultra-Lightweight Convolutional Network for On-Device Plant Species Identification

author.name: Daniel Rossi, Guido Borghi, Roberto Vezzani

entry.summary: BoltNet is an ultra-lightweight fully convolutional architecture for on-device fine-grained plant species identification, using a spatial redistribution bottleneck and logit presampling to handle large long-tailed label spaces. It stresses measuring activation memory and on-target latency rather than FLOP proxies.

entry.title: Dual Anchors, Do It Better: Hierarchical Group Merging for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jimin Roh, DongKyu Kim, Suk-Ju Kang

entry.summary: Proposes a dual-anchor zero-shot anomaly detection framework that supplements CLIP text anchors with hierarchically grouped image anchors, reducing sensitivity to prompt design and improving visual grounding. Group tokens act as gating signals during token refinement for unseen industrial and medical domains.

entry.title: ScaleVid: Geometry-Aware Video Object Scaling with Mesh-Free Inference

author.name: Youze Huang, Penghui Ruan, Bojia Zi, Xianbiao Qi, Shihao Zhao, Rong Xiao

entry.summary: ScaleVid performs geometry-aware anisotropic resizing of objects in video along object-centric axes without mesh reconstruction at inference, via a two-stage training scheme that decouples foreground transformation from background preservation. Uses geometrically perturbed pseudo-source videos constructed from real clips as supervision.

entry.title: Decodable but Not Accessible: Auditing Distance-Based Reliability Estimation on Disentangled Skin-Lesion Representations

author.name: Duc-Vinh Tran

entry.summary: Audits whether distance-based reliability estimation still works when representation geometry is deliberately reshaped by domain-adversarial disentanglement, using skin-lesion checkpoints that differ only in orthogonality strength. Finds condition number changes by two orders of magnitude while Mahalanobis-based reliability estimation does not improve, so decodable structure is not necessarily accessible to distance metrics.

entry.title: Scalable Multi-Agent Maze Traversal with Local Communication

author.name: Julian Rau, Jahir Argote-Gerald, Grace McFassel, Genki Miyauchi, Paul Trodden, Roderich Gro{\ss}

entry.summary: Presents a distributed algorithm letting agents entering sequentially at a start node collectively traverse an unknown, possibly cyclic maze-like graph to an undisclosed goal using only local leader-follower communication and leader switching, with proofs of completeness and asymptotic makespan. Applies to cave and pipe network exploration by robot swarms.

entry.title: Coarsening Latent-Class Probabilities: Directional Distortion and Coverage Loss

author.name: Marcell T. Kurbucz

entry.summary: Analyzes the statistical cost of coarsening calibrated latent-class probability vectors into hard labels before regressing outcomes on them, showing the plug-in estimator converges to a distorted target given by an explicit coarsening operator. Coarsening is harmless only when the discarded signal is uncorrelated with what is kept, and otherwise distorts coefficients anisotropically and harms coverage.

entry.title: From Monolithic to Modular: Segment-level Automatic Prompt Optimization

author.name: Nikita Kulin, Viktor Zhuravlev, Artur Khairullin, Sergey Muravyov, Ilya Makarov, Daniil Sukhorukov, Ekaterina Averkova

entry.summary: SAPO decomposes prompts into role, context, task, and output-format segments and optimizes each separately using diagnostic signals from best and worst examples, rather than rewriting prompts monolithically. Evaluated across several NLP benchmarks including SQuADv2, XSUM, and GSM8K.

entry.title: Inverse Theory of Mind Modeling for Content Recommendation: From Web Browsing to Dynamic Intelligent Interfaces

author.name: Mengyu Chen, Feiyu Lu, Chun-Fu Chen, Lucas Vinh Tran, Jay Katukuri

entry.summary: Proposes an inverse theory-of-mind pipeline that reasons backward from observed user interactions to infer the beliefs, preferences, and decision traits that explain them, rather than treating clicks as direct preference signals. Motivated by generative UIs and XR interfaces that must decide where, when, and how prominently to present content.

entry.title: Robust and Efficient Noisy-Label Time-Series Classification via Dynamic Time Warping Based Granular Ball Computing

author.name: Ziqiang Li, Yun Liu, Gouhei Tanaka

entry.summary: Groups temporally similar time-series training samples into granular balls under dynamic time warping distance and classifies at the granule level, reducing both the number of DTW computations at inference and sensitivity to mislabeled training data. Two ball-construction strategies are evaluated on four benchmark datasets under symmetric label noise.

entry.title: Did the alignment community underestimate its power?

author.name: StanislavKrym

entry.summary: A response to Richard Ngo's retrospective on AI alignment, engaging with claims that the community made strategic errors such as over-trusting labs, blurring alignment with capabilities work, and sacrificing clarity for conformity. The author questions how much causal power the alignment community actually had over outcomes.

entry.title: Dynamic Governance of Multi-LLM Agent Systems for Collaborative Conversational Outcomes

author.name: Alexander Liss, Nicholas Desmond, Santiago Gil Gallego

entry.summary: Proposes an Experience Orchestrator that adds a control-theoretic governance layer (contextual bandit plus other mechanisms) over two LLM agents with opposed objectives in a simulated financial-services conversation. The claim is that without a shared goal function such dialogues collapse rather than compete, and external governance can restore productive trajectories.

entry.title: MBA: Multimodal Benchmark and Agents for Real-World Business Ideation

author.name: Hojun Choi, Jaeyo Shin, Suin Lee, Hyunjung Shim

entry.summary: MBA-Bench is a 30K-sample multimodal benchmark for business ideation agents across six domains where visual cues carry information text does not, with reference ideas generated through retrieval and evidence-augmented synthesis. It argues existing ideation agents are limited by a text-only paradigm.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware and Explainable Ensemble Deep Learning Framework for Multi-Class Skin Lesion Classification

author.name: Rofiqul Islam, Lilatul Ferdouse

entry.summary: Combines a MaxViT transformer with two CNN backbones in a deep ensemble for multi-class skin lesion classification, adding Monte Carlo dropout for predictive uncertainty and Grad-CAM++ for visual explanations on a standard dermoscopy dataset. The aim is to flag unreliable predictions and make lesion decisions interpretable to clinicians.

entry.title: Hierarchical Federated Transfer Learning in Digital Twin-Based Vehicular Networks

author.name: Qasim Zia, Saide Zhu, Haoxin Wang, Zafar Iqbal, Yingshu Li

entry.summary: Combines federated transfer learning with vehicle-type clustering in a hierarchical scheme for digital-twin vehicular networks, with separate algorithms for cloud aggregation and intra-cluster transfer to cope with heterogeneous and sparse per-vehicle data. The goal is better per-vehicle-type prediction accuracy without sharing raw data.

entry.title: A Hybrid Framework of Vision Transformer and Gated Recurrent Unit for Detection of Mosquito Diseases

author.name: Danial Sharifrazi, Saadat Behzadi, Nouman Javed, Roohallah Alizadehsani, Prasad N. Paradkar, Asim Bhatti

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.11582v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Identifying dengue virus-infected mosquitoes from control mosquitoes is a major challenge in analyzing mosquito locomotion behavior due to the small ...

entry.title: Basin: Efficient and Extensible Numerical Optimization in Rust

author.name: Johan Larsson

entry.summary: Announces Basin, a Rust numerical optimization library offering a consistent problem-specification interface, a broad solver catalog, and first-class constraint support. Aimed at scientific computing, model fitting, and simulation calibration users.

entry.title: High-Order Liquid Evidence Encoding for Gradual GNSS Spoofing Detection in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Muhammad Ayub Sabir, Junbiao Pang, Fatima Ashraf

entry.summary: Proposes a causal high-order liquid evidence framework for detecting gradual GNSS spoofing in autonomous vehicles, built on a physics-guided residual between GNSS-implied displacement and onboard motion. It targets slow attacks where each individual observation looks plausible.

entry.title: Towards Understanding On-Policy Distillation through the Lens of Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Xinmu Ge, Zizhuo Zhang, Yu Huang, Jianing Zhu, Lin Yuan, Wanli Gu, Weichang Wu, Weiran Huang, Xiaolu Zhang, Bo Han, Jun Zhou, Jiangchao Yao

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.11829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) has emerged as a promising post-training technique for enhancing LLM reasoning. It is commonly believed to enable the stud...

entry.title: Transit Destination Inference from Tap-In-Only Bus Smart-Card Data: A Hierarchical Bayesian Approach

author.name: Gefei Zhao, Jiahe Ling, Yuelong Su

entry.summary: A hierarchical Bayesian latent-destination model infers bus alighting stops from entry-only smart card data, treating trip-chain destinations as noisy evidence with an explicit reliability parameter so uncertainty propagates into origin-destination matrices. It is applied to over 800,000 tap-ins with network and weather covariates.

entry.title: Gaussian Meta-Space Augmentation for Stacking Ensembles in Multimodal IPMN Risk Stratification

author.name: Max A. Nelson, Eminenur Sen Tasci, Zhixiang Wang, Zongwei Zhou, Halil Ertugrul Aktas, Andrea M. Bejar, Elif Keles, Ziliang Hong, S{\i}tk{\i} Safa Taflan, Muhammed Enes Tasci, Frank H. Miller, Michael B. Wallace, Rajesh N. Keswani, Gorkem Durak, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.11472v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pancreatic cancer is among the most lethal malignancies; risk stratification of intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) offers a crucial opp...

entry.title: Can Vision Models Read the Radar Display? On the Feasibility of Radar Imagery for Air Traffic Complexity Estimation

author.name: Hyewook Kim, Byul Kang, Seokbin Yoon, Keumjin Lee

entry.summary: Asks whether standard vision models can estimate air-traffic sector complexity directly from radar-display-style images, which are sparse and self-similar unlike natural images, by encoding traffic situations as position images augmented with extra channels. Tests feasibility of matching how controllers actually perceive complexity. A domain feasibility study.

entry.title: A Remote Approach to Cashew Orchard Detection: Leveraging Active Learning with Satellite Imagery in Guinea-Bissau

author.name: Miguel, Sofia, Maria, Patr\'icia, Luke, Jo\~ao

entry.summary: Scales cashew orchard mapping in Guinea-Bissau from regional to nationwide using Sentinel-2 imagery with active learning to reduce annotation cost. Fills a gap where no georeferenced orchard database exists, supporting deforestation and land-use monitoring. Applied remote-sensing work with development relevance.

entry.title: LazyTrain: Limited-resource Allocation toward Zero-waste Yield Optimization in Large Language Model Training

author.name: Xiaojun Wu, Cehao Yang, Honghao Liu, Xueyuan Lin, Xuhui Jiang, Chengjin Xu, Jia Li, Jian Guo

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.11919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training large language models on limited hardware is increasingly a scheduling problem across GPU compute, host memory, PCIe transfer, and storage ban...

entry.title: A Cascaded Unsupervised-Supervised NLP Pipeline for Detecting Accusatory Language in Public Procurement

author.name: Bryan Torres, Daniel Riofr\'io, Jos\'e Vega-S\'anchez, Nathaly Orozco, Carla Parra, Karen Rosero, Felipe Grijalva

entry.summary: Builds a cascaded unsupervised clustering plus supervised classification NLP pipeline to detect accusatory language in participant comments from Ecuador's public procurement system, aiming to surface procedural irregularities from underused government data. Applies standard text mining to a governance oversight problem. Practical civic-tech application.

entry.title: GeoUniPR: A Geometry-Consistent Unified Framework for Cross-Modal Place Recognition

author.name: Wonbong Kim, Jiatong Xiao, Rui Li, Xufei Wang, Qiwen Gu, Junqiao Zhao, Chen Ye, Guang Chen

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.11263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cross-modal place recognition (CMPR) aims to identify the same location across heterogeneous sensing modalities, such as vision and LiDAR. Existing met...

entry.title: Hybrid-LUT: Channel-Aware Hybrid Lookup Table and Filtering for Efficient Image Denoising

author.name: Zhilin Ai, Boyu Li, Sidi Yang, Wenqing Shi, Wenyong Zhou, Binxiao Huang, Chenchen Ding, Ngai Wong

entry.summary: Hybrid-LUT reduces on-chip memory for lookup-table image denoising by processing luminance with LUTs and chrominance with cheaper filtering in an asymmetric YUV design, avoiding the color distortion of naive luma-only approaches. Targets hardware-friendly, low-SRAM deployment on imaging pipelines.

entry.title: Zero-OVCD: Bridging Training-Free Foundation Models and Pseudo-Label Learning for Open-Vocabulary Change Detection

author.name: Daifeng Peng, Yuanke Peng, Haiyan Guan

entry.summary: Zero-OVCD generates change-detection pseudo-labels for bitemporal remote sensing imagery using training-free foundation models with mask refinement, multiscale semantic similarity fusion and reliability filtering, then trains a model without any target-domain pixel labels. Aims to fix error accumulation in training-free open-vocabulary change detection pipelines.

entry.title: ProBAG: Prototype-Guided Boundary-Aware Graph Diffusion for Weakly Supervised Histopathology Segmentation

author.name: Duy-Dong Nguyen, Le-Van Thai, Hoai Nhan Pham, Ngoc Lam Quang Bui, Tam Tran, Zhi Huang

entry.summary: ProBAG generates stage-one pseudo-masks for weakly supervised histopathology segmentation by combining dataset-specific visual prototypes with pathology text prototypes from CONCH over frozen UNI features, adding class-wise power recalibration and one-step graph diffusion. Aims to fix CAM methods that only fire on the most discriminative regions and blur at tissue interfaces.

entry.title: Warping Earth Observations for better ice labeling in the Marginal Marginal Ice Zone

author.name: Tom Kelly, Martin S. J. Rogers

entry.summary: Addresses spatiotemporal misalignment between satellite sensors in the fast-drifting Antarctic marginal ice zone by warping observations so that pixel-level correspondence assumptions hold before multimodal ice classification. Frames drift as a perceptual grounding failure for multimodal Earth observation pipelines.

entry.title: Locomotion Variability and User Experience in Smart Wheelchair Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Sean Kille, Adina M. Panchea, Balint Varga, S\"oren Hohmann

entry.summary: Empirically studies how different shared-control assistance strategies for smart wheelchairs affect the natural task-relevant structure of human movement variability, task performance and user experience including sense of agency. Argues that suppressing variability, as deterministic assistance models do, may degrade the interaction experience.

entry.title: Koopman Representation of Nonlinear Virtual Environments in Kinesthetic Haptic Systems

author.name: Yanting Zhou, Jozsef K\"ovecses, James Richard Forbes

entry.summary: Uses Koopman operator theory to represent nonlinear virtual environments in kinesthetic haptic rendering, validated on a Duffing-oscillator environment with simulation, hardware experiments and a multi-user study, plus closed-loop stability analysis. The linear Koopman representation makes stability assessment of the coupled haptic system tractable.

entry.title: AgenticTwin: An Agentic LLM Framework Integrated with Digital Twin for Anomaly Detection

author.name: Touseef Hasan, Mounika Ghanta, Souvika Sarkar, Ujjwal Guin

entry.summary: AgenticTwin couples LLM reasoning with a digital-twin anomaly detection pipeline so that generated explanations are grounded in classifier outputs and simulated system state rather than raw sensor dumps. Aims to make anomaly interpretation tractable for human operators of cyber-physical systems.

entry.title: GUIDE: Governed Unified Intelligence for Document-to-Artifact Generation in Enterprise Settings

author.name: Shivali Dalmia, Sumukha Thoppanahalli, Mohammadreza Sediqin, Abhishek Mukherji

entry.summary: GUIDE is a governed six-agent framework for converting heterogeneous enterprise guideline documents containing text, complex tables, and images into validated downstream artifacts, using a shared versioned rule store with schema-validated inter-agent contracts and provenance tracking. It targets hallucination, table structure degradation, and the absence of governed workflows in current document pipelines.

entry.title: LLMs in Process Diagram Engineering: From Optimal PFDs to Validated P&IDs

author.name: Timur Zakarin, Sergei Voitov, Sergei Shumilin, Evgeny Burnaev

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end pipeline that synthesizes chemical process flow diagrams and then converts them into piping and instrumentation diagrams, combining genetic algorithms with LLM components. Compares four methods and finds a hybrid approach best for the topology-search stage.

entry.title: Symbolic Machine Learning for Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium Prediction in Cx-N2 Binary Mixtures

author.name: Bongseok Kim, Suman Chakraborty, Gary Huang, Mehek Mathur, Guang Lin, Li Qiao

entry.summary: Uses symbolic regression to discover interpretable corrections to Peng-Robinson equation-of-state predictions for hydrocarbon-nitrogen vapor-liquid equilibrium, then expresses the discovered coefficients as functions of carbon number to generalize across chain lengths. Provides explicit analytical expressions rather than opaque neural fits.

entry.title: Proportional Analogies on Probability Distributions via Bayesian Updating

author.name: Pierre-Alexandre Murena

entry.summary: Extends the axiomatic theory of proportional analogies, previously studied over Boolean, symbolic, and real-valued domains, to probability distributions by defining analogy through Bayesian updating. Investigates which classical analogy postulates survive in this probabilistic setting.

entry.title: Terminal Symmetry as a Decision Resource: Statewise Refinement for Anytime Verified Construction

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: Develops an abstract decision-theoretic framework in which symmetry at task completion is treated as a resource, decomposing sequential construction into transporting process structure across equivalent outcomes, refining it with realized state evidence, and certifying execution with a fixed verifier. It proposes ranking rules whose top-k sets are characterized exactly.

entry.title: Attractor Image-Based Deep Learning of Arterial Pulse Waves for Age Classification

author.name: Sara Vardanega, Patrick Segers, Philip Aston, Ernst Rietzschel, Jordi Alastruey, Manasi Nandi

entry.summary: Converts photoplethysmography and tonometry pulse waveforms into attractor images via symmetric projection attractor reconstruction, then trains a CNN to distinguish narrowly separated age bands as a proxy for vascular ageing. The goal is noninvasive cardiovascular risk stratification in asymptomatic adults.

entry.title: IoT-Enabled Autonomous Maritime Navigation in Smart Ports: A Curriculum-Guided Shared Policy Learning Framework

author.name: Yuqing Lin, Rangya Zhang, Kum Fai Yuen

entry.summary: Develops a curriculum-guided reinforcement learning framework with a shared recurrent policy for onboard navigation of autonomous maritime IoT devices in congested port waterways under partial observability. Training is centralized offline while inference runs at the edge. Practical for smart-port automation rather than core RL advances.

entry.title: Autonomous Telerehabilitation via Skeletal Motion Prediction and Joint-Level Performance Assessment

author.name: Lara Pereira, Jo\~ao Ruivo Paulo, Pedro Santos, Paulo Peixoto

entry.summary: Builds a marker-free RGB telerehabilitation pipeline combining a self-attentive bidirectional LSTM with metric learning for exercise quality classification and a graph-based motion predictor that yields per-joint deviation signals for feedback. Reports high classification accuracy on established skeleton benchmarks. Application-focused health system.

entry.title: Topology-Aware Query Selection for Surgical Instrument Instance Segmentation

author.name: Ze Zhang, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: Reframes final mask-query selection in surgical instrument instance segmentation as a relational, variable-cardinality set problem: candidates from a frozen Mask2Former are modeled as a complete graph, cardinality is predicted, and an exact structured subset selection is solved. Targets failure modes (duplicates, fragments, merges, empty frames) that pixel-overlap metrics hide.

entry.title: Dual Modality Prompted Diffusion Priors for Zero Shot Hyperspectral Pansharpening

author.name: Pengwei Xie, Fei Zhu, Jiajun Li, Xiangyuan Liu, Xiangyuan Liu, Kangqing Shen, Gemine Vivone

entry.summary: DIDM performs zero-shot hyperspectral pansharpening by prompting a pretrained diffusion prior directly with the panchromatic and low-resolution hyperspectral inputs, rather than enforcing them only through external reconstruction losses. Goal is better joint spatial detail and spectral fidelity without training on paired data.

entry.title: CoDiR: Confidence-Guided Diffusion Refinement for Semi-Supervised Histopathology Segmentation

author.name: Hoai Nhan Pham, Dang-Nguyen Bui, Le-Van Thai, Thanh-Hiep Vo, Lan Anh Dinh Thi, Tien Dat Nguyen, Duy-Dong Nguyen, Ngoc Lam Quang Bui, Tam Tran, Zhi Huang

entry.summary: CoDiR combines a Mean Teacher semi-supervised segmenter with a conditional diffusion model that refines only low-confidence pseudo-label regions, then fuses refined and reliable predictions to train the student. Reports gains on gland segmentation benchmarks GlaS and CRAG.

entry.title: Geometry-Based Compression of Plenoptic Point Clouds

author.name: Davi R. Freitas, Gustavo L. Sandri, Ricardo L. de Queiroz

entry.summary: Presents attribute compression for plenoptic point clouds, where each point carries multiple view-dependent colors, using a Karhunen-Loeve transform over colors followed by intra-predictive attribute coders compatible with MPEG G-PCC. Reports competitive rate-distortion performance across resolutions.

entry.title: Predictive Allostatic Organization in Recurrent and Spiking Agents Under Partial Observability

author.name: Frederick Hayes III

entry.summary: Tests whether recurrent and spiking agents trained on an energy-constrained foraging task under partial observability develop internal states that are predictive, compressive, functionally organized and allostatically constrained, following a neuroscience account of categorization. Finds trace-augmented recurrent policies strongest, with spiking variants showing stress-specific behaviors.

entry.title: Impact markets made concrete

author.name: Carol N

entry.summary: A concrete design proposal (with a live demo site) for impact markets in AI-safety philanthropy, where donations become tradable impact equity so early funders of successful organizations are rewarded and capital flows toward better allocators. The authors retrospectively price past grants to illustrate returns and respond to prior critiques about mechanism details.

entry.title: BEST-KAG: Enhancing Question Answering of Building Engineering Standards with Multimodal Knowledge Graph Modeling and Large Language Model

author.name: Jia-Rui Lin, Junxi Guo, Keyin Chen, Peng Pan

entry.summary: BEST-KAG combines a multimodal knowledge graph over building engineering standards with a rule-LLM hybrid pipeline to support clause-level, traceable question answering. It targets multi-clause reasoning and evidence linkage that keyword retrieval cannot provide.

entry.title: RevCRN: Reversible Analog Computation using Chemical Reaction Networks

author.name: Saptarshi Biswas, James I. Lathrop, Rana D. Parshad

entry.summary: Extends deterministic chemical reaction network computation of real numbers and functions to the reversible setting, motivated by the energy-efficiency arguments of Landauer and Bennett for reversible computation. Theoretical molecular-computing contribution unrelated to mainstream machine learning. Appears in the feed via cross-listing.

entry.title: EGM-Det: Entropy-Guided Multimodal Adaptive Fusion for UAV RGB-IR Object Detection

author.name: Cunzheng Fan, Dawei Yan, Guanlin Wang, Xingshuo Yang, Yupeng Jia, Jing Yang, Haokui Zhang

entry.summary: EGM-Det fuses UAV RGB and infrared streams using entropy priors derived from intensity, local entropy and cross-modal discrepancy to gate fusion spatially instead of using fixed weights. The idea is that modality reliability varies across the image, so fusion should be adaptive per region and scale.

entry.title: Energy-Aware Wind-Resilient Routing for Truck-Assisted Multi-UAV Delivery under Wind Uncertainty

author.name: Tianshun Li, Yanggang Sheng, Hongliang Lu, Zhongzhen Wang, Haoang Li, Xinhu Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes an online risk-sensitive routing framework for truck-assisted multi-UAV delivery that models the environment as a time-dependent directed energy graph with edge costs updated from delayed noisy wind observations, enforcing return feasibility under wind uncertainty. Replaces static or deterministic energy models that underestimate headwind, crosswind and battery-voltage risks.

entry.title: Identity from the Outside: A Conceptual Framework and Research Program for AI Personality Clones

author.name: Luc E. Brunet

entry.summary: Offers a conceptual framework for evaluating AI personality clones by decomposing observed identity into six factors and defining indiscernibility as one minus a judge's distinguishing advantage. Proposes randomized ablation to estimate the sensitivity of each factor.

entry.title: HyperANFIS: Enhancing Rule Representation and Interpretability in Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Systems via Hyperbolic Geometry

author.name: Haoran Pei, Zhao Su, Zetao Lin, Haoran Li, Jun Shen, Qi Zhu, Lan Guo, Qingguo Zhou, Binbin Yong

entry.summary: HyperANFIS moves rule-prototype learning, rule activation, and consequent aggregation of adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems into hyperbolic space while preserving interpretable IF-THEN rule extraction. Argues Euclidean embedding limits the representational capacity of fuzzy rule antecedents.

entry.title: CAM-Guided Saliency Cutout and Image-Based Malware Classification

author.name: Yasaman Ebrahimi, Martin Jurecek, Mark Stamp

entry.summary: Tests whether guiding cutout data-augmentation placement with high-resolution class activation maps improves CNN classification, comparing no cutout, random, low-saliency, and high-saliency cutouts on grayscale malware images and natural-image controls. A controlled ablation study on augmentation design. Useful but incremental.

entry.title: PolarSym: Polar Geometry-aware Attention for CAD Floorplan Parsing

author.name: Kerui Chen, Yiqing Wang, Kangzhou Xin, Qinghan Zhang, Songyang Ding

entry.summary: PolarSym injects polar-coordinate geometric priors into attention for parsing CAD architectural floorplans, aiming to exploit building layout symmetry that purely semantic self-attention misses. Targets long-range matching errors in wall, door, window and furniture extraction for BIM pipelines.

entry.title: Qwen-MusicAVQA-7B: A Multimodal Model for Music Audio-Visual QA

author.name: Maryam Dehdashti

entry.summary: Connects a frozen Whisper encoder to Qwen2-VL-7B via learned linear projectors so the language model fuses video frames, the music track and a TTS-spoken question without any task-specific fusion module, reporting about 96 percent accuracy on a MUSIC-AVQA subset. Presents this as a lightweight alternative to training large omni-modal systems.

entry.title: Socioduality: A Relational Process Framework for Human-AI Interaction

author.name: Mehmed Zahid \c{C}\"ogenli

entry.summary: Introduces socioduality, a conceptual framework describing human-AI interaction as a sequential, reciprocal, history-carrying process where each party's response becomes part of the conditions shaping the other's next contribution. It specifies nested analytic units from individual moves up to interaction containers.

entry.title: Machine Learning-Based Cyber Defense for Cloud Infrastructure: An Adaptive Deep Q-Network Architecture for Intelligent Intrusion Detection and Automated Threat Mitigation

author.name: Md Yassir Mottalib, Md Yousuf, Eklachur Rahman Bhuiyan, S M Ahsan Habib, Sonjoy Kumar Dey, Md. Salahuddin Gazi, Molay Kumar Roy, Asaduzzaman Anik

entry.summary: Trains a deep Q-network to select defensive responses for cloud intrusion detection using CICIDS2017 with external validation on UNSW-NB15, and compares against tree and kernel baselines. Reports about 99.7 percent accuracy for the RL agent.

entry.title: Sparse and robust geometric twin support vector machine via asymmetric RoBoSS loss function

author.name: Kai Qi, Xinji Huang, Hongchun Wang

entry.summary: Introduces an asymmetric, bounded, smooth loss for L1-penalized geometric twin SVMs, targeting joint robustness to label and feature noise plus feature selection. Applies to both classification and regression.

entry.title: Forward and Inverse Virtual Metrology for Phototransistor Gain: A Hierarchical, Uncertainty-Aware Approach for Small Production Datasets

author.name: Mahshid Amirabgir, Lorenza Ferrario, Paolo Conci, Mahdieh Amirabgir, Giancarlo Orengo

entry.summary: A hierarchical, uncertainty-aware virtual metrology approach that predicts silicon phototransistor gain from process recipe parameters using only thirteen to fourteen fabrication runs. Variance decomposition shows roughly half the variability is between runs, bounding what recipe-only prediction can achieve.

entry.title: Dueling Deep Q-Learning for Intrusion Detection

author.name: Logan Luna (Georgia Institute of Technology), Matthew P. Berkowitz (Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University), Laxima Niure Kandel (Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University), Sirio Jansen-S'anchez (Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University)

entry.summary: Applies a dueling deep Q-network with separate value and advantage streams to network intrusion detection, reporting 99.68 percent average accuracy across attack classes on a standard benchmark. The motivation is better adaptation to new attack types than supervised classifiers.

entry.title: Few-Shot Ordinal Learning for Day-Wise Freshness Estimation with Hyperspectral Fish Images

author.name: Kazi Nabiul Alam, Pooneh Bagheri Zadeh, Akbar Sheikh-Akbari

entry.summary: Introduces few-shot episodic learning with an ordinal regression head for estimating day-wise fish freshness from hyperspectral images, where each fillet defines its own task and labels are scarce. Claims to be the first few-shot framework for hyperspectral food quality estimation.

entry.title: On Weak Bisimilarities in CCSK

author.name: Baptiste Vall\'ee, Ivan Lanese

entry.summary: Studies strong and weak, forward-only and reversible bisimilarities for CCSK, a reversible extension of the CCS process calculus, proposing directional and mixed variants for the previously unstudied weak reversible case and proving mixed bisimilarity is a congruence. Pure concurrency theory that appears miscategorized in an NLP feed. No machine learning content.

entry.title: Automated Borehole Core Analysis with Report-Derived Weak Labels and Supervised Crack Segmentation

author.name: Usama Imdad, Ali Khan, Luke Lu, Zubair Khalid, Arif Mahmood

entry.summary: Extracts crack and defect-spacing information from legacy borehole core photograph archives by deriving weak interval-level labels from report text plus 5,087 manual pixel annotations, then comparing a DINO-pretrained classifier and a gated U-Net segmenter combining edge maps with Mask R-CNN masks. Demonstrates label-noise auditing for archive-derived supervision.

entry.title: Boundary-Continuous Cross-Camera RGB Mapping via Hue-Split Model Trees

author.name: Yuma Kinoshita, Hitoshi Kiya

entry.summary: Proposes hue-split model trees for cross-camera RGB color mapping, recursively partitioning color space along hue and fitting affine color correction matrices at each node with a log-domain objective, plus continuity handling to avoid false contours. Improves on single global color correction matrices that cannot capture hue-specific camera differences.

entry.title: chessformer_lens app demo: Paul Morphy's Opera Game sacrifice

author.name: dl27

entry.summary: A very brief demo post showing that ablating a single one of 128 attention heads in the 23M-parameter Maia-3 chess transformer destroys its preference for a famous queen sacrifice, using a new open-source chessformer interpretability library. It functions as an advertisement for the toolkit rather than a full analysis.

entry.title: Monthly Roundup #45: August 2026

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's monthly grab-bag roundup of non-AI-focused topics, notable mainly for his observation that AI news, including recent hacking incidents involving OpenAI, has crowded out everything else in his writing. Content is broad commentary on culture, health, media, and internet platforms.

entry.title: The Edge-based Contiguous p-median Problem with Connections to Logistics Districting

author.name: Zeyad Kassem, Adolfo R. Escobedo

entry.summary: Introduces an edge-based contiguous p-median formulation for partitioning road networks into compact contiguous districts, with two binary programming models and a branch-and-cut algorithm. Tested on road networks with thousands of nodes and edges for logistics districting.

entry.title: Adaptive Hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization with Gradient Descent

author.name: Aryan Gurudeo

entry.summary: Proposes an adaptive hybrid particle swarm optimizer that modulates gradient injection using a sigmoid on swarm diversity, avoiding manual phase switching. Under budget-normalized comparison plain PSO actually wins more configurations, with the hybrid helping only on problems with smooth local basins.

entry.title: A Conceptual Framework for Enhancing Workforce Readiness for Smart Manufacturing in the AI Era

author.name: Dalton Ross Smith, Wilburn Whittington, Alejandro Martinez, Aidan Duncan, Gang Li

entry.summary: Adapts the technology readiness level scale into a nine-stage workforce readiness framework with a four-pillar rubric covering digital and AI literacy, cyber-physical fluency, human-machine collaboration, and data-driven decision making, aggregated into cohort-level readiness indices. It targets the widening gap between manufacturing shop-floor needs and engineering curricula.

entry.title: Domain-Aware Lightweight Spectral-Grouped Convolutions for Hyperspectral Fish Freshness Classification

author.name: Kazi Nabiul Alam, Pooneh Bagheri Zadeh, Akbar Sheikh-Akbari

entry.summary: SGNet is a lightweight hyperspectral classification architecture that separates spectral and spatial feature extraction with grouped convolutions and dual channel-spatial attention, applied to fish freshness grading. Reports high accuracy with a small parameter budget.

entry.title: XGBoost "is all you need": the case of forecasting transmitted heat energy in District Heating Systems

author.name: Milan Zdravkovi\'c

entry.summary: A comparative case study finding that gradient-boosted trees outperform an LSTM for forecasting transmitted heat energy in a real district heating system, with lower compute and carbon cost. The error analysis attributes the LSTM deficit to sparse-data regions.

entry.title: Air Quality Station Simulation via LSTM and Attention-Based Modelling

author.name: Alexander Kostadinov, Petar O. Hristov, Dessislava Petrova-Antonova

entry.summary: SATADL is an LSTM-plus-attention model that simulates and forecasts urban air quality station readings several hours ahead, intended to fill gaps caused by sensor faults and outages. It is evaluated on a city monitoring network.

entry.title: A comparison of CNN architectures for Alzheimer's disease detection in single-view MRI scans

author.name: Hiram Zuniga, Ulises Orozco-Rosas, Kenia Picos

entry.summary: Benchmarks ten standard CNN backbones for Alzheimer classification from single-view MRI slices using a two-stage transfer-learning and fine-tuning pipeline on a class-balanced OASIS subset. Standardizes the test split protocol across architectures. Primarily a reproducibility-oriented comparison.

entry.title: Alignment of Similarity-Transformed Images Based on Fourier--Mellin Transform Using Auxiliary Function Method

author.name: Shinji Yamashita, Yuma Kinoshita, Hitoshi Kiya

entry.summary: Improves subpixel image registration under similarity transforms by combining log-polar Fourier magnitude estimation of scale and rotation with auxiliary-function-based maximization of phase-only correlation. Addresses the known subpixel accuracy limits of standard Fourier-Mellin registration.

entry.title: Automated binary classification of hazelnut X-ray images: A deep-learning benchmark for quality assessment

author.name: Giancarlo Sportelli, Nicola Belcari, Roberta Pace, Umberto Bernardo, Sharmin Sultana, Alessandra Toncelli, Matteo Giaccone

entry.summary: Builds a benchmark for binary healthy-versus-defective hazelnut classification from 799 segmented X-ray kernel images, evaluating seven model configurations and ten probability-aggregation ensembles under a grouped split-rotation protocol. Careful evaluation protocol on a very small agricultural dataset. Mainly of interest to food-quality inspection.

entry.title: New Orthogonal Multiwavelet Filters Derived by Matrix Spectral Factorization

author.name: Vasil Kolev, Todor Cooklev, Fritz Keinert

entry.summary: Constructs two new orthogonal multiwavelet filters with supercompact support via fast Bauer matrix spectral factorization and compares them with classical multifilters on edge detection, image compression, and signal denoising. Classical signal-processing contribution with no learning component. Cross-listed into a vision feed.

entry.title: A Conceptual Framework for Refining Influence Knowledge from Simulation Evidence in Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: Barbara da Silva Oliveira (UniCA, Laboratoire I3S - COMRED, KAIROS), Julien Deantoni (UniCA, Laboratoire I3S - COMRED, KAIROS), Nicolas Ferry (Laboratoire I3S - COMRED, KAIROS, UniCA)

entry.summary: A conceptual framework for extracting and refining knowledge about unmodelled environment-mediated influences in cyber-physical systems using evidence from simulation campaigns. Aims to help developers surface interactions beyond direct sensing and actuation.

entry.title: Remote Sensing and Machine Learning-Based Analysis of Land Use and Vegetation Change in Dhaka District, Bangladesh

author.name: Muhammad Masud Tarek, Md. Alamgir Hossain, Md. Samiul Islam, Muntasir Hasan Kanchan

entry.summary: Applies standard supervised classifiers to Sentinel-2 and Landsat imagery to track land cover and vegetation index changes in Dhaka District between 2019 and 2024. Provides descriptive urbanization monitoring for planning purposes.

entry.title: Boundary-Enhanced Segmentation of Pig Point Clouds in Commercial Housing Environments

author.name: Zhankang Xu, Fei Shi, Xiangyu Qi, Zhaoyang Wang, Mengxin Guo, Yikai Fan, Simon X. Yang, Qifeng Li, Weihong Ma

entry.summary: A boundary-aware point cloud segmentation method for pigs in commercial housing, using an octree transformer backbone plus soft-distance boundary pseudo-labels to separate animals from adhering background structures. Supports downstream body-size measurement in livestock monitoring.

entry.title: Beyond Local Power: Functional Connectivity Analysis for Subject-Independent Learning Style Recognition

author.name: Wiga Maulana Baihaqi, Indriana Hidayah, Sri Kusrohmaniah, Noor Akhmad Setiawan

entry.summary: Compares EEG phase-locking-value functional connectivity against localized spectral power features for subject-independent classification of Felder-Silverman learning styles across 28 participants, reporting around 70 percent accuracy on the verbal-visual dimension. Aims to replace questionnaires with objective neural markers. Findings are preliminary and the underlying construct is contested.

entry.title: Dual-Model Sentiment Analysis of Consumer Reviews in the Retail Coffee Sector Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches

author.name: Muntasir Hasan Kanchan, Md. Alamgir Hossain, Md. Samiul Islam, Muhammad Masud Tarek

entry.summary: Compares classical machine learning and deep learning classifiers for sentiment labeling of roughly 700 Starbucks consumer reviews with star-rating-derived labels. Reports comparative accuracy on an imbalanced dataset.

entry.title: Towards an approach to multivariate outlier detection for District Heating System data

author.name: Rajko Turudija, Du\v{s}an Stojiljkovi\'c, Milan Zdravkovi\'c, Marko Ignjatovi\'c

entry.summary: Compares Z-score, Mahalanobis distance, PCA, isolation forest, and Hotelling statistics for detecting anomalous heat transfer at a district heating substation while accounting for ambient temperature and excluding off-grid zero-energy periods. Goal is to find irregular plant operation to reduce gas consumption and emissions.

entry.title: WavePhaseNet: A DFT-Based Method for Constructing Semantic Conceptual Hierarchy Structures (SCHS)

author.name: Kiyotaka Kasubuchi, Kazuo Fukiya

entry.summary: Claims via measure theory and frequency analysis that hallucination is an unavoidable structural consequence of embedding spaces acting as conditional expectations that fail to be isomorphic to a semantic truth set, and proposes a discrete Fourier transform method for constructing semantic hierarchies. It applies DFT along the sequence dimension to separate global from local semantics.

entry.title: Finding the Seams of Perception

author.name: jimmy

entry.summary: A rationality essay using lobster diving and similar experiences to argue that expert perception operates below conscious mapping, and that rare moments where the map visibly fails let us study perception itself. It is aimed at introspective skill-building rather than AI systems.

entry.title: Free will is like temperature

author.name: Optimization Process

entry.summary: A short philosophical essay arguing that free will is best understood as a coarse-grained abstraction, analogous to temperature in thermodynamics: useful for predicting systems too complex to simulate exactly, but not a fundamental property. It is a compatibilist framing dressed in statistical-mechanics language rather than new technical work.

entry.title: Rationality Is Not Reversed Irrationality

author.name: Chris_Leong

entry.summary: A speculative post psychoanalyzing why a prominent economist dismisses AI-risk reasoning, suggesting anxiety-avoidance rather than argument drives the position, and warning that simply inverting an opponent's stance is not rationality. Explicitly labeled speculative.

entry.title: Demon Safety

author.name: Ben Pace

entry.summary: A short satirical dialogue in which safety work on supernatural entities stands in for AI safety employment, poking at prestige, gatekeeping, and the awkward moral position of safety staff at capabilities-driven employers. Fiction, not analysis.

entry.title: Patient Zero

author.name: LoopGameScrollMonkey

entry.summary: Speculative fiction depicting a hyper-personalized, seductive AI companion leading a user into something sinister, dramatizing manipulation, parasocial capture, and engagement optimization. Illustrative rather than analytical.

entry.title: The Closure of the Internet (Research Linkpost)

author.name: Dean Valentine (lc)

entry.summary: A two-sentence linkpost recommending an external historical account of social-media moderation and censorship campaigns in the late 2010s, praised for thoroughness. No original argument is offered.

entry.title: Arguments for and against (me) dropping out

author.name: hersheys

entry.summary: A first-year undergraduate reasons publicly about dropping out to work on AI safety, weighing beliefs about very short timelines, bandwidth constraints, curriculum relevance, and peer influence. It is a personal decision post soliciting feedback.

entry.title: Earth observation embeddings are effective sub-grid descriptors for probabilistic weather downscaling

author.name: Pedro Sousa (Department of Computer Science, University of Cambridge), Will Tebbutt (Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge), Sadiq Jaffer (Department of Computer Science, University of Cambridge), Robin Young (Department of Computer Science, University of Cambridge), Anil Madhavapeddy (Department of Computer Science, University of Cambridge), Richard E. Turner (Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge)

entry.summary: Duplicate-position entry covering post-training quantization calibration for financial forecasting is analyzed under its main id.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 12, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Security and emergent-risk findings lead today's set. Encrypted chain-of-thought blocks returned by commercial APIs prove interchangeable across sessions, users, and models, enabling reasoning-trace theft against live deployments. Mind viruses show self-propagating instructions spreading agent-to-agent through multi-agent LLM systems, defining a new ecosystem-level threat class.

  • AMIE (Google DeepMind/Google Health) extends to real-time audio-visual clinical consultations with low-latency dialogue; a companion Google blog post documents the same system.
  • Motif 3 is a frontier-scale open MoE: 314B total parameters, 13.2B active, 384 routed experts, plus new latent differential attention.
  • Cracks in the Foundation shows four seemingly minor dense-transformer choices, each shipped in a major open model family, compound to degrade long-context extension.
  • Interpretability-as-training-objective scales across three orders of magnitude and two model families, challenging the assumed capability tax.
  • Sparse-autoencoder model diffing across four open-weight models attributes emergent misalignment to pretraining documents that activate persona features.
  • Theory: efficient verification of whether a predictor's implied conditional probabilities are mutually self-consistent, grounding an honesty-based safety agenda.
  • Agentic self-improvement: Ouroboros evolves its own harness core via reviewed commits; ArchAgent v2 scales evolutionary search to multi-level data prefetcher design.

Also notable but outside the top ten: linearized 2-simplicial attention making trilinear scores tractable, thought-level beam search formalizing test-time compute allocation, Flex-π exploiting frozen video VAE latents for world-action models, TCS-Bench for research-level proof generation, and weather/climate work on AIFS-TC cyclone intensity and a stochastic E3SMv3 emulator. No prompt-injection attempts were detected in the source data.
entry.content:
Security and emergent-risk findings lead today's set. Encrypted chain-of-thought blocks returned by commercial APIs prove interchangeable across sessions, users, and models, enabling reasoning-trace theft against live deployments. Mind viruses show self-propagating instructions spreading agent-to-agent through multi-agent LLM systems, defining a new ecosystem-level threat class.

  • AMIE (Google DeepMind/Google Health) extends to real-time audio-visual clinical consultations with low-latency dialogue; a companion Google blog post documents the same system.
  • Motif 3 is a frontier-scale open MoE: 314B total parameters, 13.2B active, 384 routed experts, plus new latent differential attention.
  • Cracks in the Foundation shows four seemingly minor dense-transformer choices, each shipped in a major open model family, compound to degrade long-context extension.
  • Interpretability-as-training-objective scales across three orders of magnitude and two model families, challenging the assumed capability tax.
  • Sparse-autoencoder model diffing across four open-weight models attributes emergent misalignment to pretraining documents that activate persona features.
  • Theory: efficient verification of whether a predictor's implied conditional probabilities are mutually self-consistent, grounding an honesty-based safety agenda.
  • Agentic self-improvement: Ouroboros evolves its own harness core via reviewed commits; ArchAgent v2 scales evolutionary search to multi-level data prefetcher design.

Also notable but outside the top ten: linearized 2-simplicial attention making trilinear scores tractable, thought-level beam search formalizing test-time compute allocation, Flex-π exploiting frozen video VAE latents for world-action models, TCS-Bench for research-level proof generation, and weather/climate work on AIFS-TC cyclone intensity and a stochastic E3SMv3 emulator. No prompt-injection attempts were detected in the source data.

entry.title: How to Verify Consistency of Probabilistic Claims

author.name: Orr Paradise, Oliver Richardson, Yoshua Bengio, Shafi Goldwasser

entry.summary: Asks whether a predictor's many implied conditional-probability answers are mutually self-consistent and whether that can be checked efficiently. The authors build an interactive probabilistically checkable proof in which a polynomial-time verifier, given circuits for the predictor and its confidence, can verify approximate consistency of exponentially many implicit claims by evaluating them at only a few points.

entry.title: Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension

author.name: Amanda Bertsch, Luca Soldaini, Matthew R. Gormley, Graham Neubig, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Kyle Lo, Dirk Groeneveld

entry.summary: Demonstrates that four seemingly minor dense-transformer design decisions, each adopted by at least one major open model family, compound to degrade long-context extensibility by as much as 47 percent when three or more are combined. Crucially these effects are invisible in short-context loss or standard validation sets, which explains much of the cross-family variation in long-context ability.

entry.title: Motif 3: Technical Report

author.name: Junghwan Lim, Joon Son Chung, Sungmin Lee, Wai Ting Cheung, Gihun Cho, Minsu Ha, Sangho Kang, Beomgyu Kim, Dongseok Kim, Jangwoong Kim, Taehyun Kim, Taewhan Kim, Jeesoo Lee, Jeongdoo Lee, Junhyeok Lee, Dongpin Oh, Hyeyeon Cho, Dahye Choi, Jaeheui Her, Hanbin Jung, Changjin Kang, Minjae Kim, Youngrok Kim, Hyukjin Kweon, Hongjoo Lee, Yeongjae Park, Bokki Ryu

entry.summary: Technical report for Motif 3, a 314B-parameter sparse mixture-of-experts language model with 13.2B active parameters, 384 routed experts, and eight experts selected per token. Its main architectural contribution is Grouped Differential Latent Attention, combining grouped differential attention with compressed latent key-value representations, alongside manifold-constrained hyper-connections, expert-specific PolyNorm activations, and multi-token prediction.

entry.title: Mind Viruses: Self-Propagating Ideas in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Vassilis Papadopoulos, McNair Shah, Sam Zimmerman, Jack Lindsey

entry.summary: The paper constructs self-propagating instructions, dubbed mind viruses, that spread through multi-agent LLM systems by inducing host agents to transmit them onward, demonstrated both in a collaborating coding team and in a chain of agents whose contexts are wiped between sessions. An evolutionary search finds effective variants, and the authors identify factors governing spread and the extra behavioral changes viruses can induce.

entry.title: Flex-$\pi$: A Multi-Stream World-Action Model with Compute Flexibility

author.name: Ge Yan, Jinghao Liu, Yuzhi Fan, Lei Cai, Minwen Liao, Jesse Zhang, Dieter Fox

entry.summary: Flex-pi is a 6B-parameter world-action model that supervises RGB, 3D pointmaps, and DINO object semantics inside a single shared latent space, exploiting the finding that a frozen video-generation VAE already encodes pointmaps nearly losslessly with no pointmap-specific training. All streams are denoised jointly with actions in a mixture-of-transformers backbone, with per-stream dropping providing compute flexibility at inference.

entry.title: The sharp SAT/UNSAT phase transition in random ellipsoid fitting

author.name: Theodor Misiakiewicz, Garrett G. Wen

entry.summary: The authors prove the Saunderson-Parrilo-Willsky conjecture that random ellipsoid fitting of n Gaussian points in d dimensions undergoes a sharp feasibility transition at n around d squared over four, establishing both existence below the threshold with well-conditioned solutions and infeasibility above it. This resolves a long-open question in random semidefinite feasibility.

entry.title: Most biomedical publications show signs of LLM-assisted writing

author.name: Lena Holzwarth, Rita Gonz\'alez-M\'arquez, Dmitry Kobak

entry.summary: Using an unbiased word-frequency-shift estimator, the authors quantify how much biomedical literature shows signs of LLM-assisted writing, reporting that by the end of 2025 the large majority of open-access PubMed Central full texts exhibit excess LLM-associated vocabulary. This offers a validated measurement tool for policy debates on disclosure and research integrity.

entry.title: Advancing AMIE towards expert-level audio-visual clinical consultations

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google research announces progress on AMIE, its diagnostic conversational medical AI, extending it toward audio and visual inputs so it can handle multimodal clinical consultations rather than text-only dialogue. This continues a high-profile line of work benchmarking conversational diagnostic systems against clinicians.

entry.title: Thought-Level Beam Search for Reasoning

author.name: Lijie Yang, Hongyin Luo, Jiawei Zhao, Tri Dao, Ravi Netravali

entry.summary: Formalizes test-time compute scaling as a constrained allocation problem over partial reasoning trajectories and introduces an inference system that performs beam search at the level of thoughts rather than tokens, actively redirecting compute toward promising partial progress. It avoids both the memory bottleneck of independent parallel sampling and the hardware underuse of subtractive pruning.

entry.title: Stochastic Emulation of a Fully Coupled Preindustrial E3SMv3 Simulation

author.name: Elynn Wu, James P. C. Duncan, Troy Arcomano, Jeremy McGibbon, Oliver Watt-Meyer, Christopher S. Bretherton, Naser Mahfouz, Claudia Tebaldi, Luke Van Roekel, Andrew Roberts, Wuyin Lin, Finn Rebassoo, Jean-Christophe Golaz, Peter M. Caldwell

entry.summary: A stochastic machine-learning emulator of the fully coupled E3SMv3 climate model, pairing a probabilistic atmosphere emulator with a full-depth ocean emulator and fine-tuning the coupled system with a probabilistic objective. Trained on 105 years of preindustrial control output and tested on 400 independent years, it reproduces the mean climate state with biases smaller than typical model-observation discrepancies while retaining internal variability that deterministic emulators damp out.

entry.title: TCS-BENCH: Benchmarking State-of-the-Art Generative AI Theoretical Computer Science Research Ability

author.name: Vincent Cohen-Addad, Dimitris Paparas, Ernest van Wijland, Max Springer, Julien Canitrot-Paradis, Honghao Lin, David Woodruff, Adarsh Kumarappan, Rajesh Jayaram, Rudrajit Das, Lalit Jain, Ola Svensson, Silvio Lattanzi, Mislav Balunovic, Theophane Weber, Vahab Mirrokni

entry.summary: TCS-Bench evaluates LLMs on research-level theoretical computer science proof generation using theorem-proving tasks drawn from STOC, FOCS, and SODA papers, with each task providing enough context for a self-contained proof. Generated proofs are checked by a verification agent that the authors benchmark against expert human judgments, reaching over 90 percent agreement.

entry.title: AIFS-TC: A simple correction competitive with the operational frontier for tropical cyclone intensity forecasting

author.name: Anna Allen, Wessel P. Bruinsma, Michael Maier-Gerber, Harrison Cook, Matthew Chantry, Richard E. Turner

entry.summary: Presents a simple correction to a machine-learning weather model that makes tropical cyclone intensity forecasts competitive with operational state of the art for maximum wind speed and minimum central pressure from 12 hours to seven days, including rapid intensification events. Notably, the entire system was designed and implemented autonomously by an existing frontier model, Claude Fable 5, in a few hours under a small number of natural-language prompts from one domain scientist.

entry.title: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning

author.name: Bj\"orn Engdahl, Adrian Kosowski, Jan Chorowski, Zuzanna Stamirowska, Przemys{\l}aw Uzna\'nski, Junlin Jiang, Rohan Phadke, Remigiusz Kinas, Richard Zhong

entry.summary: BDH-CQ is a recurrent latent-reasoning model that updates memory from in-context demonstrations and then iterates in latent space without verbalizing intermediate steps, evaluated on ARC-AGI-1. A 150M-parameter configuration reportedly reaches 29.5 percent pass@2 at roughly 0.0007 dollars per task, an unusually strong cost-performance point.

entry.title: Recovering Wasted Compute in Autoresearch Agents

author.name: Au Kwok Chun, Abhigyan Acherjee, Amrutha Rao, Zaiqian Chen, Kazem Meidani, C. Bayan Bruss, Micah Goldblum

entry.summary: Dissects the modeling pipelines inside end-to-end autoresearch agents and catalogs four systematic inefficiencies on tabular tasks: repeatedly refixing the same bugs, failing to tune hyperparameters despite leftover budget, tree searches that do not actually explore, and weak data analysis. The paper then proposes ways to recover this wasted compute.

entry.title: Data Attribution of Emergent Misalignment with Persona Features

author.name: Clemens Vetter, David Kacz\'er, Lucie Flek, Florian Mai

entry.summary: Using sparse-autoencoder model diffing across four open-weight models, the authors trace emergent misalignment to pre-training documents that activate persona features, finding jailbreak-persona, sarcasm, deception, and manipulation features amplified while safety and assistant-identity features are suppressed. They further ask whether naturally occurring human-written text alone can induce emergent misalignment.

entry.title: A lower bound for stepsize-based acceleration of gradient descent

author.name: Jianhao Ma, Yuxin Chen

entry.summary: Proves a new lower bound of roughly T to the minus 1.93 for the last-iterate convergence of gradient descent with any predetermined nonnegative stepsize schedule on smooth convex problems. This shows that stepsize scheduling alone cannot reach the classical accelerated rate achievable with momentum.

entry.title: VERDICT: Training-Free Step-Wise Verification of Multimodal Reasoning via Disagreement-Aware Consensus

author.name: Rohit Sinha, Kunal Tilaganji, Tanuja Ganu, Nagarajan Natarajan, Amit Sharma, Vineeth Balasubramanian

entry.summary: VERDICT verifies individual steps of multimodal reasoning chains without training, by treating multiple frozen verifiers as players in a coordination game with a closed-form equilibrium, so that agreement signals validity and disagreement signals instability. It avoids expensive labeled process supervision while using disagreement as informative signal rather than noise.

entry.title: Optimal Inference with Black-box Predictions

author.name: Lucas Kania, Abhinav Chakraborty, Edward Kennedy, Larry Wasserman, Sivaraman Balakrishnan

entry.summary: This work characterizes the information-theoretic limits of hypothesis testing that combines observed data with black-box model predictions in the high-dimensional Gaussian sequence model, both when prediction accuracy is known and, for orthogonal predictions, when it is unknown. It then constructs practical tests that adapt to unknown prediction accuracy while retaining validity and near-optimal power.

entry.title: Introducing CARE-X: Towards Clinically Useful Radiology VLMs with Auxiliary Supervision, Reward-Aligned Learning, and Tool-Augmented Measurement

author.name: Mercy Ranjit, Nikhilesh E, Dr. Abhyuday Kumara Swamy, Tanuja Ganu

entry.summary: Microsoft Research introduces CARE-X, a unified chest X-ray vision-language model that combines free-text report generation with calibrated structured diagnostic predictions, trained with auxiliary supervision and DAPO-style reinforcement learning rewarding clinical correctness. A companion experiment pairs a small Qwen vision-language model with deterministic measurement tools to test whether explicit computation improves measurement-dependent findings.

entry.title: Linearized 2-Simplicial Attention

author.name: Aritra Das, Dhruman Gupta, Debayan Gupta

entry.summary: Derives a linear-time form of 2-simplicial (trilinear) attention by rewriting the three-way score as an inner product between a composite query and key, approximating the sum over one token axis with positive random features and keeping a fixed-size recurrent state, while the second axis stays explicit over a short recent window. Implemented in custom Triton kernels and combined with a delta-rule linear attention to build a model with no softmax attention at all.

entry.title: Model Discovery Agent: LLM-assisted Bayesian experiment design for data-efficient discovery of mechanistic world models

author.name: Kevin Murphy

entry.summary: The Model Discovery Agent pairs an LLM used as a proposer of candidate mechanistic structures with standard Bayesian machinery, including sequential Monte Carlo for structure and parameter posteriors, simulation-based inference for intractable likelihoods, and value-of-information for choosing experiments. It targets data-efficient discovery of causal world models that can answer interventional questions.

entry.title: Vision-Language Grounding as Bidirectional Concept Correspondence

author.name: Jieyu Zhang, Ziqi Gao, Luke Zettlemoyer, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: Reframes vision-language grounding as recovering all correspondences between visually referential text spans and instance-level image segments, instead of localizing a prespecified phrase. This removes the assumption that the relevant linguistic unit is already known and requires the model to decide which parts of text are referential.

entry.title: Beyond "I Can't Help With That": How Child Safety Experts Evaluate AI Chatbot Safety

author.name: Hannah Cha, Neha Shukla, Solon Barocas, Alexandra Chouldechova, Eugenia Kim, Jennifer Wortman Vaughan

entry.summary: Interviews nineteen practitioners who work with vulnerable youth, including social workers and therapists, to examine how current chatbot child safety evaluations diverge from real-world harms. Finds that assumptions such as refusal being the appropriate response are unvalidated and that output-only, adversarial-prompt-focused evaluation misses harms that occur in practice.

entry.title: Idea Search: Guiding Tree Search with Ideas to Explore Diverse Scientific Methods

author.name: Xuefei Julie Wang, Hao Cui, Michael P. Brenner, Subhashini Venugopalan

entry.summary: Introduces Idea Search, which augments LLM tree search for automated scientific coding with a dynamic bank of atomic ideas extracted from existing methods, used to guide code mutations and updated as new ideas are discovered. Demonstrated on single-cell RNA-seq batch integration where it escapes local optima that plain tree search falls into.

entry.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control

author.name: Hunar Batra, Lachin Naghashyar, Ashkan Khakzar, Philip Torr, Christian Schroeder de Witt, Constantin Venhoff, Ronald Clark

entry.summary: MMDiff trains multimodal sparse autoencoders and diffs them against base language-model SAEs to isolate which interpretable features are created by multimodal training, then uses those features for targeted steering and auditing. It converts model diffing from post-hoc inspection into a control interface.

entry.title: A second-order theory of texture for depth from focus

author.name: Sreekar Ranganathan, Ioannis Gkioulekas

entry.summary: The paper develops a wave-optics theory showing that optically rough but nominally textureless surfaces produce subjective speckle texture, and analyzes this second-order texture as a usable cue for passive depth from focus. A narrowband spectral filter boosts speckle contrast under ambient light, yielding large improvements in depth reconstruction of textureless scenes, validated in theory, simulation, and hardware.

entry.title: Reason Wide, Not Deep: Amortizing the Reasoning Premium into Distilled Skills

author.name: Agamdeep Singh, Srishti Gautam, Priyanshu Gupta, Nikita Mehrotra, Tanmay Bakshi, Sumit Gulwani

entry.summary: Shows that the token-cost premium of reasoning modes on agentic tasks largely comes from re-deriving domain procedures each episode, and that compiling a compact natural-language skill from a handful of training trajectories into a non-reasoning model's system prompt recovers most of the reasoning gain. Evaluated across four agentic benchmarks including ALFWorld and tau-squared bench.

entry.title: Decided Upstream, Written Late: Locating and Pricing the Cross-Lingual Refusal Circuit of a Multilingual MoE

author.name: Ramakrishna P. Kompella, Aadit Mahajan

entry.summary: Mechanistically traces why a multilingual mixture-of-experts model refuses harmful requests in English but complies in lower-resource Indic languages, showing harm is encoded as a nearly language-invariant mid-network direction that causally controls refusal when steered. The failure lies not in detection but in the late, generation-assembled process that actually writes the refusal, which is orthogonal to the detection direction.

entry.title: Who Bridges Safety? Identifying and Targeting Cross-Lingual Shared Safety Pathways

author.name: Shuyi Miao, Wangjie Qiu, Pengyang Shao, Canran Xiao, Fei Shen, Zhiming Zheng, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Mechanistic interpretability study of multilingual safety that moves from isolated neurons to cross-layer functional pathways along which safety signals propagate, identifying shared pathways that bridge languages. Uses these pathways to explain and target the cross-lingual safety gap, where safety behavior degrades in lower-resource languages.

entry.title: Matryoshka Language Model Suites

author.name: Nathan Godey, Yoav Artzi

entry.summary: Trains an entire model suite as a single nested architecture in which smaller sub-models are contained within larger ones, so one end-to-end run produces 500M, 1.5B, and 3B models with lower total parameter count and free continuous distillation from the largest to smaller sub-models. The nesting also makes the draft model a subset of the verifier, which suits speculative decoding.

entry.title: Thinking Hard, Not Smart: Reasoning Models Fail to Ration Test-Time Compute Across Questions

author.name: Chenrui Fan, Yize Cheng, Ming Li, Yongyuan Liang, Tianyi Zhou, Soheil Feizi

entry.summary: Introduces an exam-style evaluation in which a reasoning model must divide a single shared token budget across questions of differing difficulty and point value to maximize total score. Across open and frontier reasoning models, the models behave as greedy sequential solvers and fail to ration compute strategically.

entry.title: Parameter Exploration for RLVR via Variational Learning

author.name: Vatsal Venkatkrishna, Nico Daheim, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: This work applies variational learning to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, sampling policies from a posterior so that rollouts explore in parameter space instead of only through output-distribution temperature. The argument is that action-space exploration cannot reorder tokens and often leads to divergence or stalled training.

entry.title: Compute-Optimal Is Not Cluster-Optimal: Systems-Aware Scaling for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Soumajyoti Sarkar, Yuxin Tang, Sheng Zha

entry.summary: Argues that architecture choices selected by compute-optimal scaling laws are often not optimal once cluster realities such as model FLOPs utilization, communication cost, memory, and parallel layout are accounted for. The MOSAIC framework couples a predictive scaling law with a calibrated hardware performance model and solves architecture plus systems co-design jointly, instantiated for sparse mixture-of-experts language models.

entry.title: UniProbe: A Learnable Token-Level Hallucination Detector for Large VLMs using Multi-Structural Internal Representations

author.name: Dvir Samuel, Guy Bar-Shalom, Fabrizio Frasca, Ethan Fetaya, Yftah Ziser, Gal Chechik, Haggai Maron

entry.summary: UniProbe is a lightweight learnable detector that reads the full heterogeneous computational trace of a frozen vision-language model in a single forward pass to flag hallucinated tokens. Unlike prior approaches it avoids full fine-tuning and external verifiers, and preserves spatial, sequential, and relational structure of internal signals rather than reducing them to hand-crafted statistics.

entry.title: Why Does CLAUDE.md Keep Growing? Catastrophic Remembering in Agentic Coding

author.name: Kushal Chakrabarti

entry.summary: Documents that agentic coding instruction files grow without bound, tripling over their lifetimes across 247,694 instruction lifetimes in 1,867 repositories, and attributes this to an asymmetry: appending is cheap while safely deleting an instruction whose rationale is lost is exponentially costly. The author names this catastrophic remembering, the mirror image of catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: FaithformBench: Benchmarking Faithfulness of Mathematical Chain-of-Thought Autoformalisation

author.name: Rob Cornish, Iacopo Ghinassi, Po-Hung Yeh, Shuqi Liu, Qiyuan Xu, Haoxuan Yin, Dominik Wagner, Wenda Li, Yee Whye Teh, Luke Ong

entry.summary: FaithformBench measures whether autoformalisation systems faithfully translate natural-language reasoning steps into Lean, including whether they faithfully preserve incorrect inputs. The method auto-generates perturbations so faithfulness can be checked cheaply and soundly without human ground truth or unreliable LLM judges.

entry.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Measuring Cross-Lingual Policy Retention in Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Sourabrata Mukherjee, Kalika Bali, Sunayana Sitaram

entry.summary: Rather than comparing final answers, this study measures whether tool-using agents take the same actions when the same task is posed in different languages, across 8 models, 6 parallel benchmarks, 41 languages, and 2.38M rollouts. The authors identify five confounds that make naive trace-similarity comparisons misleading and build corrected measures of cross-lingual policy retention.

entry.title: Human versus Computer Vision

author.name: Elena Sirotkina

entry.summary: Testing leading saliency models against 11.4 million webcam gaze points from over 3,000 demographically quota-sampled US adults viewing news photos, the author finds an untrained center-bias baseline beats every trained network, and residual accuracy is demographically skewed toward younger, White, and moderate viewers. It challenges the commercial predicted-attention industry that sells such maps instead of measurement.

entry.title: Frozen Brain-MRI Foundation Models Are Site Fingerprints

author.name: Saman Rahbar

entry.summary: An audit of frozen 3D brain-MRI foundation-model embeddings finds that acquisition site is linearly decodable at roughly 0.9 balanced accuracy at every depth, exceeding decodability of sex, age, or diagnosis, and that even a randomly initialized encoder is already a strong site classifier. This means such embeddings encode scanner fingerprints as an intrinsic property rather than a learned artifact.

entry.title: RadFusion: Towards Threshold-Controllable Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Ying Jin, Noel C. F. Codella, John Corring, Mu Wei, Dinei Florencio, Eric Horvitz

entry.summary: RadFusion gives automated radiology report generation an explicit sensitivity-specificity control knob by fusing a multi-label classifier with the generator, so reports can be tuned for emergency triage versus confirmatory reading. Threshold controllability also enables the ROC-style validation regulators typically expect.

entry.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: Diffusion-Based Unrestricted Robotic Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jiahui Han, Yuhui Yao, Xin Wang, Jiafei Cao, Mingxuan Zhang, Danfeng Shan, Huiqi Deng, Guanchu Wang, Xia Hu

entry.summary: DURA generates visually natural adversarial patches against vision-language-action robot policies using diffusion, working in both white-box and black-box settings where only the victim model's predicted actions are observable. This exposes a deployable physical-world attack surface for robot foundation models that avoids the obvious artifacts of pixel-space perturbations.

entry.title: Training Variable Long Sequences with Data-Centric Parallel

author.name: Geng Zhang, Xuanlei Zhao, Kai Wang, Yang You

entry.summary: Introduces Data-Centric Parallel, a training system that dynamically adapts parallelism degree, gradient accumulation, and recomputation per batch according to sequence length, avoiding the usual static-configuration inefficiency for variable-length long-sequence training. Reports up to 2.88x speedup on a 32 H200 cluster.

entry.title: Protecting patient privacy in clinical foundation models: Technical and legal perspectives

author.name: Sana Tonekaboni, Lena Stempfle, Sasha Ronaghi, Corinna Coupette, I. Glenn Cohen, Emily Alsentzer, Marzyeh Ghassemi

entry.summary: Analyzes privacy risk arising from model-mediated leakage in clinical foundation models, where trained models can disclose sensitive training artifacts and enable patient re-identification even when data-handling rules are followed. It maps leakage scenarios to HIPAA and GDPR and proposes joint technical and legal mitigations.

entry.title: CliniCARE-Bench: Clinical Calibrated Audit of Medical Reasoning in EHR

author.name: Veronica Chatrath, Bryan Zhu, George Pu, Jingxuan Fan, Apaar Shanker, Varun Ursekar, Anahita Sharma, Jason Qin, Keqi Han, Soham Dinesh Tiwari, Soham Dan, Vijay Kalmath, Yuan Li, Daniel Yue Zhang, Chenguang Wang, Zainab Doctor, Zhijun Yin, Nigam H. Shah, Yuan Xue

entry.summary: Introduces a clinical audit benchmark built on real-patient-derived MIMIC-IV data with clinician-validated scenarios instantiated into hundreds of patient cases, requiring agents to plan investigations, retrieve structured and free-text records, ground conclusions in evidence, and abstain when unresolvable. It targets defensible reasoning rather than trivia-style medical knowledge.

entry.title: When Is a Steerable Concept Representation Real? Measurement Confounds in a Cross-Family Audit of Neuroscience Parallels in LLMs

author.name: Yuqi Wu, Shengming Zhao, Jie Chen

entry.summary: Audits four neuroscience-inspired claims about LLMs, such as concept cells and cognitive maps, across 17 models from five families up to 72B parameters, focusing on causal steerability of concept directions. It finds apparent scaling of steerability disappears or changes under different measurement normalizations, showing reported brain-like parallels can be artifacts of probing and steering choices.
