entry.summary: Extends the information bottleneck to a perfect-privacy setting where the learned representation must be exactly statistically independent of a sensitive variable while still carrying task information under a binding rate constraint. An ADMM algorithm is developed with global convergence guarantees under regularity conditions.

entry.title: Conditional Independence Tests for Constraint-Based Causal Discovery: A Survey

author.name: Pavel Averin, Theodoros Moysiadis, Ioannis Katakis

entry.summary: A survey organizing conditional independence tests, the statistical engine of constraint-based causal discovery algorithms, into six families and examining their assumptions, robustness, and scalability in high-dimensional and mixed-type biomedical settings. It emphasizes when a test decision reflects real dependence versus an artifact.

entry.title: LLM Agents Factory: Retrieval of Domain-Specific LLM Agents

author.name: Vitalii Belov, Artyom Sosedka, Andrey Sakhovskiy, Elizaveta Kovtun, Artyom Boyarskikh, Semen Budennyy

entry.summary: Instead of designing an agent for each request at runtime, this framework retrieves from a bank of over 20,000 precomputed, Wikipedia-grounded agent profiles via semantic search, or distills the selection into a compact generator model. Evaluated on MMLU and BIG-bench variants in single-agent settings.

entry.title: MD-ProTector: Positioning Multiple Data-Driven Prototypes for LLM-Generated Text Detection

author.name: Jinmo Han, Jimin Hong, Chanyeong Moon, Ju Yeon Kang, Seonuk Kim, Nam Soo Kim

entry.summary: MD-ProTector detects machine-generated text with an encoder that represents each class by multiple trainable prototype vectors rather than a single binary boundary, giving separate decision regions for different writing styles, domains, languages, and generators. This targets the heterogeneity that makes flat binary classifiers brittle at scale.

entry.title: Templated or fully Synthetic? Prompt construction as a confound in measuring LLM political stance beyond writing assistance

author.name: Ilias Chalkidis

entry.summary: This paper argues that how political-stance prompts are constructed is itself a confound: templated prompts anchored in chat logs are still recognizable as evaluation artifacts, especially for open-ended tasks. It extends prior issue-based benchmarking beyond writing assistance to information seeking and opinion sharing and compares templated with fully synthetic prompt construction.

entry.title: Motion Artifact-Aware Self-Supervised Representation Learning for 3D Brain MRI Motion Artifact Reduction

author.name: Mojtaba Safari, Shansong Wang, Zach Eidex, Matthew Goette, Tonghe Wang, Zhen Tian, Xiaofeng Yang

entry.summary: MAD-HOI uses masked autoregressive diffusion to generate text-conditioned articulated hand-object interaction sequences with variable length, composition of multiple motions, infilling, and reliable termination, avoiding the fixed-length constraint of diffusion and the detail loss of discrete motion codes. The aim is physically plausible yet flexible HOI synthesis.

entry.title: SapiensID 2.0: Aligning Human Recognition Foundation Models with Human Perception

author.name: Yiyang Su, Jie Zhu, Feng Liu, Anil K. Jain, Xiaoming Liu

entry.summary: SapiensID 2.0 extends a human recognition foundation model with semantic soft-biometric knowledge distilled zero-shot from multimodal LLMs and with temporal motion signatures, aiming to reduce overfitting to transient appearance noise. Authors include established biometrics researchers.

entry.title: MedUP: Awakening Unified Understanding and Perception in Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yuan Wang, Hualiang Wang, Yixin Chen, Songtao Jiang, Shujian Gao, Jiaming Lin, Siming Fu, Jian Wu, Zuozhu Liu

entry.summary: MedUP unifies medical image understanding and pixel-level perception in one model by tokenizing segmentation masks as discrete tokens inside the LLM vocabulary, so masks and text interleave natively. It is trained on a curated 1.84M-instance corpus spanning text-guided segmentation and region-grounded reasoning.

entry.title: Where To Look? : Causal Tracing of Vision Encoders in VLM

author.name: Naren Kumar S, Tirth Bhatt, Mayank Singh

entry.summary: Uses causal tracing to ask which visual tokens actually drive vision-language model answers, finding that highly causal tokens frequently lie outside the region the question refers to. The pattern persists across model scales and corruption settings, suggesting strong benchmark scores do not imply spatially localized causal grounding.

entry.title: Fast and Memory-Efficient Wavelet Convolutions via I/O-Aware Reformulation

author.name: Amit Aflalo, Shahaf E. Finder, Roy Amoyal, Eran Treister, Oren Freifeld

entry.summary: Builds an I/O cost model for wavelet convolutions and derives three algebraic reformulations, including on-chip recomputation of the Haar transform and collapsing multi-level synthesis into a single closed-form pass, to remove memory-bandwidth bottlenecks. This makes a popular large-receptive-field convolution operator substantially faster and more memory-efficient.

entry.title: When Visual Signals Mislead: A Mechanistic Study of Attribute Hallucination in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yufei Zhang, Chenlu Zhan, Hongwei Wang

entry.summary: VISOR tests the dominant language-prior explanation for attribute hallucination by decomposing predictions into visual and language-prior logit components using null-image baselines across three VLM families and over ten thousand negative-ground-truth samples. It finds the visual signal, not the language prior, strongly predicts false positives, undermining prior-suppression remedies.

entry.title: TCAM for Autonomous Deformable Manipulation: The RMC2 Champion System for WBCD 2026 Track 4

author.name: Guangrui Shen, Zhili He, Shigang Wang, Yuanjun Sun, Qing Yu

entry.summary: A technical report describing the winning fully autonomous system for a deformable manipulation competition track involving separating and loading a T-shirt onto a printing pallet, aligning the collar, and smoothing the print area. The solution is built on a causal action model framework with hardware, perception, and data design chosen to reduce physical interaction difficulty.

entry.title: Claude Opus 5 Just Beat My Text-Based Adventure Game Benchmark

author.name: derelict5432

entry.summary: An independent evaluator reports that an agent harness using Claude Opus 5, an Anthropic model available since late July 2026, solved a custom ten-room text adventure benchmark for the first time, with the hardest element being a rotating-room puzzle requiring non-local causal reasoning and allocentric spatial coordinates. The post continues a series tracking model progress on this private benchmark.

entry.title: Towards an Argumentative Foundation for Evaluative AI

author.name: Xiang Yin, Tim Miller, Nico Potyka, Antonio Rago, Francesca Toni

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that computational argumentation should serve as the formal backbone for Evaluative AI, a decision-support paradigm that presents competing hypotheses with supporting and opposing evidence rather than a single recommendation. It sketches a research agenda for explainable and contestable human-centred decision support.

entry.title: The Field Knows: Cross-Dimensional Geometry from Navigation to Black Holes

author.name: Chenghao Xu

entry.summary: Proposes learning a continuous metric field via a causal contrastive loss that maps scenes to Lie algebra elements exponentiated into Riemannian or Lorentzian metrics, spanning robot navigation geodesics and black hole event horizons. Reports zero-shot generalization suggesting the field learns transferable geometric structure.

entry.title: Agent-MD: Selective LLM Intervention with Event-Driven Escalation for Stateful GCMC--MD Campaigns

author.name: Yijie Wang, Zhen-Yu Yin, Zhenheng Tang, Xiaowen Chu

entry.summary: Presents a framework that inserts LLM reasoning only at campaign setup and event-triggered reviews of long-running molecular simulations, while a deterministic rule-based agent handles routine continuation, analysis, and state tracking. Demonstrated on grand canonical Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics desorption campaigns for clay systems.

entry.title: SurgLAT: Surgical Latent Attention Tracking for Depth-Aware Robotic Laparoscope Control

author.name: Rulin Zhou, Qiujie Song, Yujie Ma, An Wang, Wanhao Liu, Guoheng Ma, Yidu Wang, Guankun Wang, Xingrong Diao, Jiankun Wang, Chaowei Zhu, Xianming Liu, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: Proposes an online framework for autonomous laparoscope control that models the surgeon's evolving operative attention as a latent state, using a frozen vision foundation encoder plus a selective causal memory that blends short-term motion and long-horizon intent. Aims to keep the camera on the relevant region without a fixed physical target.

entry.title: Think Deep, Speak Once: Relit, A Recursive Latent Implicit Transformer Framework

author.name: Abhishek Panwar, Maheep Singh, Saksham Bansal

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid architecture that embeds deep recursive latent reasoning, in the style of tiny recursive models, inside the semantic representation space of a pretrained transformer, aiming to internalize chain-of-thought without emitting long token sequences. The goal is reasoning gains without the token cost of externalized steps.

entry.title: Long SKILL Compliance as Logical Reasoning: Closure-Grounded Detection with Scaling-Guided On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Shuaitao Zhao, Feng Ni, Lichao Ma, Jiaye Lin, Fei Han, Yang Wei, Lu Pan

entry.summary: Represents long enterprise policy documents as a two-layer constraint dependency graph, routing scenarios via document-level indexing and resolving atomic constraint dependencies via closure, so compliance judgments can be made by small models with source attribution. Uses scaling-guided on-policy distillation to transfer large-model capability into a cheaper detector.

entry.title: Knowing You Is Everything: LLM Agents Achieve Near-Perfect Profile-Consistent Reaction Prediction in Social Media Simulation

author.name: Ljubisa Bojic, Ljiljana Matic, Joerg Matthes, Milan Cabarkapa, Bojana Dinic, Jue Wang

entry.summary: Benchmarks twelve LLM configurations on predicting individual like or dislike reactions to social media posts from survey-based persona profiles, comparing against machine learning classifiers and varying profile completeness. Reports very high profile-consistent accuracy with full profiles, which the authors frame as both a recommender testing tool and a manipulation risk.

entry.title: SkillConsist: Detecting Inconsistencies in Agent Skills via Bidirectional Graph Alignment

author.name: Chaofan Meng, Yuhang Zheng, Yingnan Zhou, Sihan Xu

entry.summary: SkillConsist detects mismatches between what an agent skill declares and what its implementation actually does by separating declaration and implementation content and aligning them as bidirectional graphs. Such inconsistencies can hide dangerous behavior or cause wrong skill selection by agents.

entry.title: EasyBalance: Cross-Layer Load Balancing in Distributed MoE Inference

author.name: Yize Wu, Ke Gao, Ling Li, Yanjun Wu

entry.summary: EasyBalance reduces idle time in expert-parallel mixture-of-experts inference by balancing load across layers rather than replicating or migrating experts within a layer. It requires no change to expert-device mapping, so it adapts instantly with essentially no extra overhead.

entry.title: Ground-Truth Neighborhood Regularization for Reinforcement Learning Post-Training of Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Jianqi Zhang, Xingyu Zhang, Zeen Song, Changwen Zheng, Fanjiang Xu, Wenwen Qiang

entry.summary: Identifies suboptimal collapse, where reinforcement learning post-training gradually pushes time series foundation model outputs away from ground truth in certain forecast regions because high-quality samples are rarely drawn initially. Proposes a ground-truth neighborhood regularization to keep the policy distribution anchored during post-training.

entry.title: Compositional Cross-Modality Translation via Whole-Volume Multitask Latent Flow Matching

author.name: Daniele Molino, Alessio Zoboli, Camillo Maria Caruso, Valerio Guarrasi, Paolo Soda

entry.summary: Decouples volumetric anatomical priors from cross-modality mapping by pretraining a large 3D variational autoencoder and reducing medical image translation to conditional flow matching in that latent space, enabling whole-volume rather than slice or patch translation with one multitask model instead of per-task models. Targets reducing the burden of multi-modal medical acquisitions.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Stick to the Script? A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Consistency in Interactive Narratives

author.name: Yingpeng Ma, Jianhao Yan, Bei Shi, Ka Hou Kam, Runnan Wang, Xuebo Liu, Yulong Chen, Yue Zhang, Derek F. Wong

entry.summary: Defines Narrative Commitment Preservation and releases a benchmark of 100 interactive narrative environments derived from movie synopses, each with a machine-checkable specification of trajectory, commitments and initial facts so that an LLM game master can be automatically audited for long-horizon consistency against disruptive player moves. Targets an evaluation gap in LLM-driven interactive storytelling.

entry.title: On the Robustness of LLMs' Internal Representation of Code Correctness

author.name: Francisco Ribeiro, Sohaila Abdulsattar, Renata Gonzalez, Mahmoud Kassem, Sarah Nadi

entry.summary: Tests whether the previously reported internal hidden-state signal of code correctness is a robust model property or an artifact of one specific extraction choice, varying probing setups to check stability. Relevant to using activation-based verifiers instead of test execution or self-reported confidence for code generation.

entry.title: From Product Search to Preference Articulation: The Economics of Agentic Commerce

author.name: Lingxiu Dong, Kaiwen Luo, Fasheng Xu

entry.summary: Models the economics of shifting from manual product search to delegated agentic search, where an agent screens a large catalog through noisy representations of hard-to-articulate consumer preferences. Finds that manual search collapses beyond a preference-complexity threshold while agentic search shifts consumer effort from inspection to preference articulation.

entry.title: SkillsMetric: Mapping the Detection Boundary of Static Analysis for Malicious Agent Skills

author.name: Xinze Chen, Chi Zhang, Ping Ji, Yimin Liu

entry.summary: Builds a five-stage static analysis framework that scores agent skill packages on pattern density, statistical anomaly, dataflow taint, import anomaly and capability mismatch, evaluated on a large corpus plus an adversarial set covering sixteen attack types. Maps where static analysis can and cannot catch malicious skills, with strong detection of exfiltration and steganographic payloads.

entry.title: LegoLM: Structured Weight Sharing for Large Language Models

author.name: Joseph Bingham

entry.summary: Diagnoses two reasons global weight sharing fails for LLM compression, namely a scale-mismatch penalty across heterogeneous layers for small vector blocks and outlier weights beyond the outermost quantization decision threshold for scalar blocks, then proposes a structured sharing framework fixing both. Provides an analytical account of catastrophic quality loss in shared-weight compression.

entry.title: RippleKV: Cross-Layer KV Cache Allocation via Perturbation Propagation

author.name: Dongjie Xu, Kai Qian, Julius, Weijie Shi, Yuxuan Sun, Minghua Tang, Fenglei Jin, Hanchi Dong, Jiajie Xu

entry.summary: Allocates a limited long-context KV cache budget across transformer layers by injecting norm-adaptive perturbations into each layer's value cache and measuring the resulting KL divergence at the output, using true output sensitivity instead of proxies like depth or attention statistics. Corrects systematic misallocation to tolerant layers.

entry.title: Deployable Per-Instance Multi-Layer Activation Steering for Large Language Models

author.name: Muhammad Faishal Adly Nelwan, Alfan Farizki Wicaksono

entry.summary: Shows that the best layers for activation steering vary per input rather than per task, using a per-instance oracle over layer subsets on two open 8B models and six persona traits, and finds a greedy marginal-effect rule recovers nearly all oracle benefit. Then addresses the deployability gap that both oracle and greedy selection need gold answers to score candidate layers.

entry.title: ToolVision: Learning When and How to Use Visual Tools with Capability-Aligned Supervision

author.name: Delin Mao, Chenghao Sun, Jingwei Song, Chishui Chen, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: Diagnoses two distinct supervision misalignments in the standard supervised-then-reinforcement recipe for teaching multimodal models to invoke visual tools: imitation of teacher trajectories that rely on perceptual abilities the student lacks, and outcome-only rewards that either suppress tool use or reward valid but useless calls. Proposes capability-aligned supervision so the model learns both when and how to use tools.

entry.title: Illusion or Integrity? Geometrical Consistency Metric for AIGC Video Quality Evaluation

author.name: Yifei Xue, Yuanchen Fei, Hao Zhang, Chenzhi Nie, Tie ji, Yizhen Lao

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark and metric that scores AI-generated videos by geometric consistency across frames, using multi-view geometry as a proxy for adherence to physical laws. It addresses the lack of quantitative physics-fidelity measures in current video quality assessment.

entry.title: DOCSCHISEL: Adaptive Tool Documentation Optimization Framework for LLM Agents

author.name: You Lu, Kun Zhang, Bihuan Chen, Xin Peng

entry.summary: A large empirical study of how the content and structure of tool documentation affects LLM agent performance, followed by DOCSCHISEL, a framework that adaptively optimizes documentation rather than treating it as fixed input. It reveals wide heterogeneity in the fields real tool docs provide.

entry.title: UserToolBench: A User-Profile-Hidden Benchmark for Personalized Decision Making in Tool-Use LLMs

author.name: Xuexiong Yin, Zechuan Chen, Yongsen Zheng, Yuxiang Zhang, Jingyuan Yang, Bin Wang, Yubin Wang, Keze Wang

entry.summary: UserToolBench tests whether tool-using LLMs can infer hidden user preferences from interaction history, know when to ask for clarification, and produce user-aligned tool-call trajectories under incomplete information. It is built from privacy-sanitized real traces with 10 personas, 36 tool sets, and over a thousand multi-turn steps.

entry.title: Finding the Signal in the Spam: Jointly Learning Rewards and Worker Reliability from Pairwise Comparisons

author.name: Kaustubh Shivshankar Shejole, Tanish Agarwal, Arpit Agarwal, Avishek Ghosh

entry.summary: Studies whether item rewards and annotator competence can be jointly identified from pairwise comparisons under a Boltzmann-rational model, given that crowdworkers may be unskilled or actively spamming. The setting directly matters for preference data used to fine-tune language models.

entry.title: SeFoRA: Sketch-Aggregated Federated Low-Rank Adaptation with Heterogeneous Client Ranks

author.name: Yue Xia, Tayyebeh Jahani-Nezhad, Mayank Bakshi, Rawad Bitar

entry.summary: SeFoRA lets federated clients with different LoRA ranks contribute by transmitting linear sketches of their updates, avoiding the dimension incompatibility and bilinear mismatch that break naive factor averaging. A rank-homogeneous variant permits direct aggregation in a compact subspace.

entry.title: The Evaluation Protocol Determines the Result: An Independent Reproduction of LeWorldModel on TwoRoom

author.name: Joyjeet Singh

entry.summary: An independent reimplementation of LeWorldModel on the TwoRoom environment, done on roughly 25 dollars of compute, that exceeds the original reported success rate but only after discovering four undocumented evaluation conventions that determine the outcome. The representation probing result reproduced closely.

entry.title: Boundary-Seeking Policy Gradient for Safe Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chenhua Fan, Jiahui Zhu, Yuhang Zhang, Honghao Wei

entry.summary: BSPG exploits the linear programming view of constrained MDPs, which implies the optimal policy sits exactly on the constraint boundary when the constraint is active, by combining a reward-improving tangential step with a signed normal correction toward the boundary. Standard safe RL methods instead settle conservatively in the feasible interior.

entry.title: Toward Human Rights Benchmarking for LLMs: A Pilot Methodology

author.name: Savannah Thais, Wm. Matthew Kennedy, Abhigyan Acherjee, Matilda Wysocki, Malcolm Langford, Caitlin Kraft Buchman

entry.summary: Reports pilot methodology for HumRightsBench, an expert-validated scenario benchmark testing whether LLMs can reason within the obligation structure of international human rights law, adapting the IRAC legal framework into an IRAP variant that emphasizes proposing remedies. It fills a gap as models increasingly mediate legal determinations.

entry.title: Actionable Hallucination Detection: Translating Latent Uncertainty into Agentic Critique

author.name: Sanidhya Vijayvargiya, Rahul Lokesh

entry.summary: The Latent Critic is a lightweight LoRA that runs alongside a frozen base model, amplifying latent grounding signals in the residual stream and emitting localized natural-language critiques of hallucinated or unrequested agent actions within the same generation pass. It aims for actionable, low-latency correction rather than post-hoc detection scores.

entry.title: ReOrder-OPD:Reliability-Aware Prompt Ordering for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Ximo Zhu, Ruiqi Liu, Rong Wang, Ping Wu, Xiang Zheng, Wenzhuo Xu, Xubin Yao, Zhiyuan Yan, Bo Li, Jun Gao, Xiaolei Lv

entry.summary: Defines prompt-level teacher continuation reliability as the probability that a teacher can complete a student prefix to a correct answer, and shows oracle experiments where this predicts training value better than local confidence or agreement signals. Uses the measure to order or select prompts during on-policy distillation rather than intervening within individual trajectories.

entry.title: An adaptive and evolvable deep reinforcement learning framework for weather prediction

author.name: Qiang Wu, Han Li, Jianping Huang

entry.summary: Frames weather forecasting as a coordination problem and trains reinforcement learning agents to decide when and where to trust each member of an evolving pool of pretrained AI forecasters. A tactical agent assigns variable- and horizon-specific fusion weights while a strategic agent prunes weak members and absorbs newly released models, with asynchronous caching keeping training cost independent of the slowest member.

entry.title: Navigating the Proximity-Safety Balance: Constraint Decomposition for Human Following in Pedestrian Crowds

author.name: Shiting Gong, Jianpeng Yao, Jinfeng Wang, Marco Pavone, Jiachen Li

entry.summary: Decomposes the conflict between staying near a followed human and avoiding collisions in crowded spaces into a sparse task reward plus independent cost constraints in a multi-constrained RL formulation. This makes the proximity-safety trade-off explicit and tunable rather than buried in a hand-weighted dense reward.

entry.title: Status Association Does Not Reliably Predict Decision Leakage

author.name: Abdullah X

entry.summary: Tests whether the common inferential leap from a model encoding a social association to that association changing consequential decisions is warranted, using Chilean surnames as socioeconomic probes across 8,256 verified responses from eight model-provider cells. Finds elite-coded surnames attract higher forced status probability mass in nearly all models, yet this association does not reliably translate into biased decisions in matched selection, hiring, fellowship, and legal-aid scenarios.

entry.title: More Accurate, Less Human: Gestalt Grouping in Vision Models

author.name: Sudhanva Manjunath Athreya, Sai Phani Kumar Malladi

entry.summary: Builds a behavioral battery scoring vision models against published human data on four Gestalt grouping tasks and applies it to 45 models spanning supervised, self-supervised, contrastive vision-language, open-weight VLM, and closed foundation model families. The title suggests a dissociation in which more accurate models are less humanlike in how they group visual content.

entry.title: Narrative Keyframing for Generative Creative Writing

author.name: Chao Zhang, Abe Davis

entry.summary: Narrative keyframing lets writers place plot, character, and perspective constraints at chosen story moments and have AI generate the connecting prose, borrowing the keyframe metaphor from animation. It offers finer-grained authorial control than prompt-and-regenerate workflows for long-form creative writing.

entry.title: ENTLORE: A Graph-Grounded Benchmark for Latent Organizational Reasoning in Enterprise Question Answering

author.name: Akrin Zheng, Alexander Wu, Alaia Liu

entry.summary: ENTLORE builds an audited synthetic enterprise world from routine documents, org tables, and operational records to test latent organizational reasoning, meaning recovery of relations that are never stated in the corpus. Unlike prior enterprise QA benchmarks it avoids materializing a predefined answer path.

entry.title: Towards Unified Dynamic Face Landmark Detection

author.name: Sebastian Regalado, Varshanth R. Rao, Ruowei Jiang, Parham Aarabi, Igor Gilitschenski

entry.summary: This work unifies face landmark detection across datasets with different point counts by re-parameterizing each landmark as a normalized position along a face-part contour, letting all N-point datasets be merged and any number of landmarks be output by one model. It removes the need for separate models per benchmark.

entry.title: GeoSeg-OV: Bridging Geospatial Gaps with Structural Guidance for Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Segmentation

author.name: Ruizhong Liu, Tingzhang Luo, Zaiyan Zhang, Jundong Chen, Hongruixuan Chen, Shaoguang Huang, Hongyan Zhang

entry.summary: GeoSeg-OV improves open-vocabulary remote-sensing segmentation under geospatial domain shift by using vision foundation models for structural guidance rather than simply concatenating their features with text embeddings. The goal is consistent visual-text matching across heterogeneous regions, resolutions, and sensing platforms.

entry.title: PRMU: A Corpus-Free Benchmark for Person-Centric Knowledge Unlearning in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Huafeng Chen, Yueming Lyu, Ziyuan Chen, Wenda Tan, Chenyang Si, Liucheng Guo, Caifeng Shan

entry.summary: PRMU is a benchmark for corpus-free unlearning of person-related knowledge in multimodal LLMs, where the original forget and retain training corpora are unavailable as in realistic deletion requests. It probes whether target knowledge is removed while related knowledge survives, including under adversarial textual and visual probes.

entry.title: Contextual Value Alignment via Multilayer Combinatorial Fusion

author.name: Yuanhong Wu, Djallel Bouneffouf, D. Frank Hsu

entry.summary: Proposes aligning LLMs to plural human values by instantiating multiple value-specialized moral agents and combining their outputs through multilayer score- and rank-based combinatorial fusion. The aim is context-sensitive moral reasoning rather than a single unified reward.

entry.title: Can Coding Agents Solve Repository-Level Issues with Rendered Code? An Exploratory Study of Visual Representations

author.name: Weijie Liang, Yuanfeng Song, Xing Chen, Caleb Chen Cao, Sirui Han, Yike Guo

entry.summary: Tests whether rendering source code as images can serve as operational context for agentic repository repair on SWE-bench Verified, not just for static code understanding. Finds prompt-token savings that do not scale linearly with nominal visual compression and largely preserved repair performance, a mixed rather than triumphant result.

entry.title: VeinCast: Physics-Guided Dynamic Field Graphs with Graph-Conditioned Fusion for Global Medium-Range Weather Forecasting

author.name: Zhisheng Chen, Jinhan Li, Yuxuan Li, Yuan Gao, Hao Wu, Zheng Lu, Jinlong Du, Kun Wang, Bo An

entry.summary: VeinCast forecasts 69 surface and upper-air atmospheric variables using a physics-guided dynamic field graph that combines predefined atmospheric relations with state-dependent residual edges, plus graph-conditioned latent fusion and graph-modulated Earth-window attention. It sits between purely data-driven models and hard equation-constrained approaches.

entry.title: Test-Time Augmentation for LLMs: When Input Diversity Beats Output Diversity at Matched Compute

author.name: Nikita Kozodoi, Zainab Afolabi, Jack Butler

entry.summary: Compares spending a fixed test-time compute budget on input-side diversity (semantic rephrasing, lexical perturbation, visual transformation) versus output-side diversity (self-consistency sampling), under matched compute. Asks which conversion of compute into accuracy is more efficient across tasks.

entry.title: WDL-OPD: Weak-Driven On-Policy Distillation via Mixture-Constrained Co-Training

author.name: Zehao Chen, Gongxun Li, Tianxiang Ai, Yifei Li, Zixuan Huang, Wang Zhou, Tao Huang, Fuzhen Zhuang, Xianglong Liu, Jianxin Li, Deqing Wang, Yikun Ban

entry.summary: WDL-OPD stabilizes on-policy distillation by co-training two policies: an anchor that generates all rollouts and an auxiliary that evaluates the same states, with a geometric mixture of their token distributions matched to a frozen teacher via reverse KL. It analyzes how freezing the auxiliary recovers an anchor-plus-contrast proxy related to prior methods.

entry.title: TACTICL: Task-Aware Compression of Tabular ICL Models

author.name: Mykhailo Koshil, Matthias Feurer, Katharina Eggensperger

entry.summary: Compresses tabular in-context-learning foundation models by pruning transformer layers and substituting lightweight task-trained adapters, blending in-context with in-weight learning. Reports that up to 85 percent of layers can be replaced on a given downstream task across 47 datasets while retaining robustness to data shift.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM-Guided Control-Plane Policies for Backend Fault Isolation in HAProxy

author.name: Aman Chauhan, Vishnu Pendyala

entry.summary: Benchmarks whether an LLM can serve as the routing control plane of a load balancer, reading telemetry every ten seconds and isolating degraded backends through guardrailed API calls. Fifteen open-weight models from 0.35B to 35B are swept across reasoning modes and fleet sizes on a reproducible fault-injection testbed.

entry.title: Beyond Fixed Luminance: Towards Panchromatic and Orthochromatic Image Colorization

author.name: Swarnim Maheshwari, Syed Imam Ali, Vineeth N. Balasubramanian

entry.summary: Reframes colorization as full-RGB editing with a foundation image-editing model rather than predicting chroma while freezing an input luminance channel. A mixed grayscale training objective covering both natural luminance and red-insensitive formation lets the model handle historical orthochromatic photographs where standard assumptions break.

entry.title: Multimodal Item Parameter Estimation using Simulated Response Probabilitie

author.name: Christopher Ormerod, YoungKoung Kim

entry.summary: Fine-tunes a multimodal LLM to reproduce students' option-choice probabilities on image-and-text multiple-choice items across labeled ability levels, thereby implicitly learning psychometric response curves. This allows item difficulty on unseen items to be estimated directly from predicted option probabilities.

entry.title: ASR-Roundtrip Evaluation Can Mask Context- and Convention-Dependent Reading Errors in Chinese News TTS

author.name: Shijun Luo, Lizhi Wan

entry.summary: Shows that using automatic speech recognition round-tripping to score text-to-speech intelligibility hides an important error class in Chinese news audio: the synthesizer picks a plausible but contextually wrong reading for things like sports scores, aircraft models, and units, yet the recognizer transcribes it back to the intended text. A targeted audit of 110 high-risk cases confirmed 46 such masked false negatives.

entry.title: What Iterated Self-Feeding Probes of Language Models Measure, and a test that separates the construction from the model

author.name: Nicol\'as Vera Z\'u\~niga

entry.summary: This work asks what self-feeding probes (self-consistency, iterated refinement, agentic loops) actually measure, using a ring of tokens resampled by the model's own windowed conditionals as a sharp test case. By coupling two nearly identical rings under common random numbers, damage spreading becomes directly measurable, revealing that such probes conflate properties of the construction with properties of the model.

entry.title: Order Matters: LVLMs as Judges for Temporal Reasoning in Image Sequences

author.name: Martina Ianaro, Guilherme Fernandes, Maurizio Gabbrielli, Joao Magalhaes

entry.summary: This study argues that using large vision-language models as judges of interleaved visual narratives is fundamentally limited by architectural biases: models look competent on isolated judgments yet fail to detect shuffled or contradictory image sequences. It documents a performance dichotomy that undermines automated evaluation of sequential visual storytelling.

entry.title: FormStruct-Bench:A Hierarchical and Diagnostic Benchmark for Table-Form Document Structure Recognition

author.name: Lujie Ban, Jiangtao Zhu, Yuanheng Yu, Jiasheng Shi, Chenhao Ma

entry.summary: FormStruct-Bench evaluates recognition of hierarchical structure in table-form documents at both document and progressively finer component levels, so aggregate scores can be traced to specific structural failure modes. Auditable ground truth is created by annotating 70 reusable templates and expanding them into 7,000 documents.

entry.title: SparSTAR: Sparse Attention for SpaceTime AutoRegressive Video Synthesis

author.name: Jongbeom Lee, Hyunwoo Yu, Jincheol Yang, Jaemin Choi, Suk-Ju Kang

entry.summary: SparSTAR is a training-free block-sparse attention scheme tailored to pyramid-style autoregressive video generation, where scale changes and cross-clip context make sparsity patterns borrowed from diffusion or image models unreliable. It selects key blocks per head at expensive scales while retaining required conditioning context.

entry.title: Beyond Pixels: From Video Priors to 4D Worlds

author.name: Zihao Liu, Xiaolong Shen, Zhenglin Zhou, Ruijie Quan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Latent-to-4D bypasses RGB rendering by mapping the final denoised latents of video diffusion models that share a VAE directly to explicit 4D geometry predictions. This decouples 4D prediction from any single video generator and avoids the error propagation of reconstruct-after-generate pipelines.

entry.title: Multi-View Relational Distillation for Spatial Reasoning with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kiet T. Nguyen, Hanbo Shim, Jinwoo Kim, Seunghoon Hong

entry.summary: Distills relational structure from multi-view geometry-grounded vision teachers into vision-language models so spatial reasoning improves without growing inference-time model size. Relational rather than direct feature matching is used to avoid destroying pretrained vision-language alignment.

entry.title: SafeCA: Safe Cross-Attention Localization and Regulation for Text-to-Video Jailbreak Defense

author.name: Siyuan Liang, Yupeng Qiu, Junfeng Fang, Rong-Cheng Tu, Jiaxing Huang, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Analyzes cross-attention features in text-to-video diffusion and reports a cumulative separation effect where jailbreak and clean prompts become progressively more linearly separable across denoising steps. SafeCA exploits this by localizing and regulating unsafe cross-attention at the feature level rather than filtering or reconstructing inputs.

entry.title: Pre- to Post-Contrast Synthesis of Breast DCE-MRI using Latent Bridge Matching

author.name: Sina Amirrajab, Zohaib Salahuddin, Henry C Woodruff, Philippe Lambin

entry.summary: The authors synthesize peak contrast-enhanced breast MRI from pre-contrast scans using latent bridge matching, learning a conditional bridge between paired latents instead of starting from Gaussian noise as in standard latent diffusion. This targets reduction of gadolinium contrast administration in breast cancer imaging.

entry.title: JitTrack: Onboard Multi-Object Tracking Against Viewpoint Jitter for Agile UAVs

author.name: Yachun Shan, Feitian Zhang

entry.summary: JitTrack is an onboard multi-object tracking framework for agile UAVs that compensates for severe viewpoint jitter from camera ego-motion, building on a query-based transformer tracker and supporting active target following. It emphasizes real deployment constraints rather than offline benchmark performance.

entry.title: Deployment Is Not Destiny: Robot Recomposition in the Field with Unseen Software, Hardware, and Compute Payloads

author.name: Steven Swanbeck, Jonathan Salfity, Jeffery Gunawan, Corrie Van Sice, Mitch Pryor, Robert Blake Anderson

entry.summary: This framework and set of abstractions let deployed robots integrate previously unseen modular software, hardware, and compute payloads at runtime through a plug-and-play process usable by non-experts. New resources are also shared with distributed peers so compute-limited robots can access remote capabilities.

entry.title: QuantumMind: Constraint-Grounded Agentic Reasoning for Speedup Analysis in Quantum Computing

author.name: Yijing Zuo, Zhe Fu, Zihan Nie, Zhihui Zhu, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes an auditable agentic workflow that generates and conservatively screens claims of quantum speedup, checking task preservation, access and output models, required promises, and complexity scope through role-specialized steps and a deterministic ten-check validator. Aims to curb overstated quantum-acceleration claims.

entry.title: GRACE: LLM-Grounded Semantic Metric Spaces for Scalable Mixed-Data Clustering

author.name: Zihua Yang, Zhencheng Xie, Junyang Chen, Liang Xie, Yiqun Zhang, Mengke Li, Yang Lu

entry.summary: Uses LLM world knowledge to construct a semantically grounded metric space for clustering mixed numerical and categorical tabular data, avoiding the usual reliance on dataset-internal co-occurrence statistics and expensive iterative LLM-in-the-loop metric learning. Targets conceptually obvious but statistically unobserved category affinities.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Dynamic Reward Shaping in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Fouad Bahrpeyma

entry.summary: Surveys and unifies reward shaping approaches for reinforcement learning under the realistic condition that shaping signals change during training as value estimates improve and novelty decays, where classical potential-based invariance guarantees no longer directly apply. It seeks a framework for dynamic shaping that preserves the original objective.

entry.title: Signature-Guided Capacity Occupancy for Dense Expert Merging

author.name: Lingching Tung, Chi-Jui Kim, Beicheng Xu, Yuchen Wang, Bin Cui

entry.summary: SigMerge is a framework for merging multiple domain-specialized dense models into one checkpoint by deciding per-layer how much capacity to open based on cross-expert conflict signatures, then assigning that capacity by domain demand, avoiding expensive recipe search. Positions merging decisions as where, who, and how questions.

entry.title: Agentic Auto-Research is Fuzz Testing

author.name: Yifeng He, Jicheng Wang, Yinzhe Zhao, Jiachen Liu, Hao Chen

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that autonomous research agents should be built like greybox fuzzers rather than generate-and-rank samplers, because the core problem is sparse feedback rather than insufficient proposal volume. Suggests each experiment should yield coverage-like partial progress signals that guide mutation and effort allocation, not just a final rank.

entry.title: Experience-Sensitive Game Learning: A Behavioral Study of Humans and Language Agents

author.name: Yingying Guo, Zhuoxuan Ju, Ruibo Ming, Ruicheng Feng, Jinjin Gu

entry.summary: Introduces a framework and game suite for studying how repeated play changes decision behavior in both humans and language agents, rather than only final win rates. It contributes reusable strategic games, greedy-to-global learning metrics, behavioral diagnostics from action traces, and human trajectory data for comparison.

entry.title: KumbhDoot: A Scale-Ready, LLM-Bounded Architecture for Mass-Gathering Public-Service Assistants

author.name: Saurabh Sakalkar, Abhishek Singh, Ramesh Raskar

entry.summary: Describes a deployed pilgrim assistant architecture for a mass religious gathering that deliberately routes most queries through semantic similarity matching and bounded responses, invoking a language model only when necessary. The design targets cost, latency on emergency paths, hallucination risk on safety-critical facts, and offline operation.

entry.title: Performance of large language models in the optical diagnosis of colorectal polyps

author.name: Joshua C. Vences, William T. Tran, Nikko Gimpaya, Catharine M. Walsh, Rishad J. Khan, Robert Bechara, Asher C. Wiggins, Celine N. Rousan, Kaitlyn V. G. L. Morgado, Angie Ibrahim, Kevin H. M. Kuo, Daniel von Renteln, Alexander Hann, Dennis L. Shung, Michael A. Scaffidi, Charles M\'enard, Joshua Landy, Samir C. Grover

entry.summary: A retrospective clinical study evaluating several existing multimodal models, including Claude Opus 4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-o3, GPT-4o, and GPT-5, on classifying colorectal polyps and predicting histology from endoscopic images against expert responses. Reports F1 and accuracy comparisons across established endoscopic classification schemes.

entry.title: P2Voxel: Pyramid Pivot Voxelization for 3D Mesh Tokenization

author.name: Zhenhong Sun, Haozhe Liu, Yifu Wang, Xibin Song, Senbo Wang, Huadong Mo, Daoyi Dong, Hongdong Li, Pan Ji

entry.summary: P2Voxel proposes a pyramid pivot voxelization scheme for turning triangle meshes into compact tokens by sampling the minimal local geometric evidence needed inside each active voxel for deterministic surface recovery. It reframes mesh tokenization as local surface evidence sampling rather than volumetric field or edge intersection sampling.

entry.title: What to Edit Next: Visually Aligned Image-Editing Follow-Up Suggestions in Conversational Systems

author.name: Zhijing Zhang, Jinpeng Yu, Xin Song, Bingnan Li, Chuyue Li, Changhui Du, Xiaolin Fang, Jiaming Liu, Ruihua Huang

entry.summary: Builds a system for recommending follow-up image edits in conversational image creation, using a hundred thousand real multi-turn conversations from a deployed app where most turns depend on the current image. A three-stage pipeline curates appropriate follow-up intents, fine-tunes on them, and grounds suggestions in the visible image.

entry.title: Prompt Embedding Probes (PEP): Hallucination Detection in LLMs from Hidden States

author.name: Zakhar Mrykhin, Valentin Malykh

entry.summary: Introduces Prompt Embedding Probes, which augment standard linear probes on frozen LLM hidden states with a few learnable prompt embeddings to detect hallucinated answers. Tested on TriviaQA, GSM8K and MedQA across Qwen3 scales, the method improves in-distribution detection and retains some effectiveness for pre-generation prediction and cross-model transfer.

entry.title: $\texttt{DisMorph}$: learning to disentangle technical distortions from true biological change

author.name: Jingru Fu, Kathleen E. Larson, Douglas N. Greve, Bruce Fischl, Malte Hoffmann

entry.summary: Proposes a deformable registration framework, trained entirely on synthetic data, that separates scanner-induced geometric distortions such as gradient non-linearity from true biological change in longitudinal brain MRI. Prevents technical artifacts from biasing morphometric measures of aging and neurodegeneration.

entry.title: VTO: Visual Tool Orchestration for Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Rui Wang, Yeteng Wu, Xianling Zhang, Mengshi Qi

entry.summary: Introduces a process-supervised reinforcement learning framework that teaches a multimodal agent to orchestrate visual tools dynamically for video anomaly detection, replacing coarse outcome rewards that cause premature termination. Extends tool-learning agents beyond supervised imitation of fixed tool pipelines.

entry.title: Beyond Tables: Doc2DB-Bench for Relationally Faithful Document-to-Database Construction

author.name: Zhuowen Liang, Zhengxuan Zhang, Jiayang Wang, Jiazhuo Chen, Nan Tang

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for converting long heterogeneous documents into relationally faithful databases rather than flat tables, testing whether extracted facts form a valid database instance with normalized schemas, entity identities, keys, cross-table relationships and integrity constraints. Argues existing document-to-table benchmarks hide duplication and many-to-many relationship failures.

entry.title: SuperNeuroMAT: An Efficient Matrix-based Simulator for Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Prasanna Date, Kevin Zhu, Shruti Kulkarni, Ashish Gautam, Chathika Gunaratne, Robert Patton, Tyler Nitzsche, Ian Mulet, Zachary Johnson-Scott, Addison Helms, Duncan Rowden, Simon Weston, Maryam Parsa, Catherine Schuman, Thomas Potok

entry.summary: Releases an open-source matrix-based spiking neural network simulator supporting dense and sparse execution that can simulate tens to hundreds of thousands of leaky integrate-and-fire neurons on ordinary laptops, reportedly outperforming four established frameworks. Lowers the tooling barrier for neuromorphic research.

entry.title: PAST: Privileged Adaptation from Complete Student Trajectories for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yangyang Feng, Zhuoyan Feng, Junlan Chen

entry.summary: Improves on-policy self-distillation by giving the teacher access to each completed student rollout, including whether it succeeded, as privileged hindsight while leaving the student's distillation prefixes unchanged. Correct trajectories preserve the student's next-token distribution and failed ones steer the teacher toward verified success under a proximity constraint.

entry.title: 360CityArena: A Realistic Virtual Urban Navigation Benchmark for Embodied Agents

author.name: Kenta Watanabe, Atsuyuki Miyai, Mizuki Takenawa, Kiyoharu Aizawa, Toshihiko Yamasaki

entry.summary: Releases an embodied navigation benchmark built from hundreds of 360-degree video segments covering dozens of streets in a real Tokyo district, with human-crafted tasks spanning environment understanding, path reasoning and spatial reasoning. Aims to close the photorealism and complexity gap in outdoor embodied evaluation.

entry.title: Don't Scroll Back: Missing-Evidence Memory for Streaming Dialogue Summarization

author.name: Hyangsuk Min, Hwanjun Song

entry.summary: Formalizes streaming dialogue summarization, where a fixed-budget memory must supply context that the current conversation window presupposes, and argues the key issue is recovering gap-resolving evidence rather than accessing more history. Proposes ReMEMBER, which conditions retrieval on unresolved references, plus a benchmark that separately scores memory recall and summary faithfulness.

entry.title: MixFormer: Linear Transformer with Mixture of Memory Experts

author.name: Yu Guo, Lei Duan

entry.summary: MixFormer is a linear transformer that combines multiple memory experts in a mixture-of-experts arrangement with a time-aware linear attention using learnable exponential decay and positional biases. It targets the limited memory capacity and input adaptivity of existing state space models on ultra-long sequences.

entry.title: MADBench: A Benchmark for Modality-Aware Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Yanqiu Li, Yang Xiao, Jisheng Bai, Bin Chen, Hong Jia, Ting Dang

entry.summary: MADBench separates speech forgery from background-audio forgery in deepfake detection, arguing the two arise from different generative mechanisms and leave distinct artifacts. It provides a modality-aware benchmark for video where audio streams are independently manipulated over authentic footage.

entry.title: Beyond Naturalness: Probing Automated Text-To-Speech Evaluators on Linguistically Grounded Dimensions

author.name: Oluwanifemi Bamgbose, Simon Rosen, Jash Shah, Lindsay Devon Brin, Hoang H Nguyen, Anke Koelzer, Rachel Hansen, Tara Bogavelli, Fanny Riols

entry.summary: The authors decompose speech naturalness into ten linguistically grounded perceptual dimensions and build a meta-evaluation set of 860 linguist-annotated utterances to test automated TTS evaluators. They find MOS predictors collapse onto acoustic signal quality while audio-LLM judges are selective and prompt-dependent.

entry.title: Sheaf-Based Federated Representation Learning

author.name: Gabriele D'Acunto, Enrico Grimaldi, Valeria Avino, Mario Edoardo Pandolfo, Leonardo Di Nino, Sergio Barbarossa, Paolo Di Lorenzo

entry.summary: SFRL uses sheaf restriction maps to align neighboring clients' latent representations through orthogonal transformations and isometric embeddings, so federated agents with different modalities, architectures, and latent dimensions need not share a global latent space. Global consistency emerges from local geometric alignment.

entry.title: FlowScout: From Execution Feedback to Reliable Tool-Using Agent Workflows

author.name: Shuo Hao, You Lu, Bihuan Chen, Xin Peng

entry.summary: FlowScout generates tool-integrated agentic workflows from historical execution records, using real tool execution feedback instead of abstracting tool calls into simulated LLM nodes. The goal is workflows that are stable and usable in production rather than LLM-centric approximations.

entry.title: Generator-Guided Inverse Sampling for L\'evy-Driven Generative Models

author.name: Tianfu Qi, Jun Wang, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes reverse-time sampling for Levy-driven generative models through Markov generators, showing the reversed jump component becomes a state-dependent jump process governed by a nonlocal density ratio that score information alone cannot capture. This motivates a sampler decomposing dynamics into diffusion, small-jump, and large-jump parts.

entry.title: Critic-Free Pretraining for Efficient Online Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning

author.name: Daoyi Li, Yixian Zhang, Chao Yu, Wenbo Ding, Yu Wang

entry.summary: Argues that reusing an offline-trained critic hurts online fine-tuning because inherited value estimates go stale as the data distribution shifts, and proposes simply discarding offline critic training in favor of a freshly initialized critic. The approach is presented as compatible with multiple offline-to-online RL backbones.

entry.title: FiGuRO: Intrinsic Dimension Estimation for Multi-Modal Data

author.name: Viktoria Schuster, Sana Tonekaboni, Caroline Uhler

entry.summary: Introduces a framework that estimates the intrinsic dimension of unimodal and multimodal data by learning truncated low-rank projection ranks under fidelity constraints, including separate shared and private dimensions. Aims to fill gaps left by static or unimodal estimators and by contrastive methods that only implicitly capture shared dimensionality.

entry.title: Do LLM Recommenders Know When They're Hallucinating? Auditing Confidence Calibration in Catalog Faithfulness

author.name: Srijith Ravikumar

entry.summary: Audits four zero-shot LLM recommenders from different vendors for how often they recommend items outside the target catalog and whether their verbalized confidence tracks that error. Finds hallucination rates are strongly catalog-dependent, ranging from near zero on a movie catalog to over eight percent on product and business catalogs, while stated confidence remains materially miscalibrated.

entry.title: Post-Calibration Reliability Reranking of Relevance Decisions via Label-wise Monotone Projection

author.name: Inwoo Tae, Yongjae Lee

entry.summary: Points out that standard post-hoc calibration equalizes confidence with average correctness but leaves reliability differences that depend on which label was predicted. The proposed label-wise monotone reliability projection reranks retrieval relevance decisions to correct this residual mismatch.

entry.title: Position Encoding in Transformers: From Absolute and Relative Methods to Rotary Position Embeddings and Long-Context Scaling

author.name: Jiguo Li

entry.summary: A technical survey unifying absolute, relative, and rotary position encodings, including Transformer-XL, T5 bias, and ALiBi, with derivations of how rotary embeddings convert absolute indices into relative phase differences in attention scores. It compares injection points, cost, and compatibility with long-context scaling.

entry.title: PERCEPT: A Corpus for POS Tagging and Analysis of Persian-English Code-Mixing

author.name: Ghazal Kalhor, Zahra Jafari, Amirarsalan Shahbazi, Behnam Bahrak

entry.summary: Introduces PERCEPT, the first large public Persian-English code-mixed corpus with Universal Dependencies part-of-speech tags on code-mixed tokens, comprising 6,800 social media posts from three platforms. It fills a gap that has blocked syntax-aware modeling of Persian code-mixing.

entry.title: Certify or Refuse: A Cross-Model Map for Selective Risk Control with Coverage Floors under Covariate Shift

author.name: Jiamiao Liu, Dewen Qiao, Yu Zhang, Xuetao Chen

entry.summary: A theoretical treatment of certified selective prediction where operators demand both a bounded error rate on answered queries and a minimum answer rate under covariate shift. The authors prove a feasibility frontier and a two-resource sample-complexity map, separating labeled source data (for risk) from unlabeled target data (for the coverage floor).

entry.title: Who Gets Heeded? An Obligation-Level Audit of Responsiveness in EPA Rulemaking

author.name: Jianing Fan, Yue Yao

entry.summary: The authors build an AI-assisted framework that audits US EPA rulemaking at the level of individual regulatory obligations, matching public comments to the specific duties they target and classifying whether proposed obligations changed in the final rule. Each pipeline component is validated against blind human judgment.

entry.title: Productive Signaling: Competitive Software Development, Not Competitive Programming

author.name: Adam Chlipala

entry.summary: An MIT formal-methods researcher proposes replacing elite competitive programming contests, where students write throwaway code, with competitions scored on the adoption or economic value of genuinely useful software built with AI assistance. The argument links to a prior piece about lowering rewrite costs enabling large-scale reimplementation of critical software with better security and performance.

entry.title: Towards Expert-level Medical AI for Real-time Video Consultations

author.name: Mahvish Nagda, Jihyeon Lee, Matthew Thompson, Chunjong Park, Tim Strother, Valentin Li\'evin, Roma Ruparel, Akshay Goel, Teya Bergamaschi, Suhana Bedi, Meet Shah, Pavel Dubov, Liviu Panait, Toshiyuki Fukuzawa, Sam Schmidgall, Craig Schiff, Joseph Xu, Aliya Rysbek, Yana Lunts, Jan Freyberg, Rebecca Hemengway, Sunny Virmani, David Racz, Carey Radebaugh, Jo\"elle Barral, Kavi Goel, Dale R. Webster, Katherine Chou, Avinatan Hassidim, Yossi Matias, James Manyika, Gregory Wayne, Tao Tu, Yun Liu, Ethan Goh, Christina Chen, Ryutaro Tanno, Po-Hsuan Cameron Chen, Mike Schaekermann, Anil Palepu

entry.summary: Already covered in Research yesterday, Reports a Gemini-based multi-agent system, AMIE in a video configuration, conducting real-time audio-visual clinical consultations with low-latency dialogue, clinical reasoning, and real-time perception, claiming the first demonstration of expert-level AI performance in this setting. Argues that text-only medical AI discards non-verbal and perceptual information and excludes patients who cannot describe symptoms in writing.

entry.title: MusicLayout: Explicit Structural Planning for Controllable Text-to-Music Generation

author.name: Shuyu Li, Kejun Zhang, Jiahe Lei, Shulei Ji, Zihao Wang, Jiaxing Yu, Wanying Wu, Lei Wang

entry.summary: MusicLayout introduces an explicit, inspectable intermediate representation for text-to-music that specifies sections, textures, repetitions, variations, and instrument arrangements on a timeline before audio generation. It is integrated into a unified autoregressive framework so users can plan and revise structure rather than relying on a single global prompt.

entry.title: The Announcement Carries the Cue: Markup, Boundaries, and the Notation of Pre-Training Corpora

author.name: E. M. Freeburg

entry.summary: Argues that document notation, i.e., how layout and boundaries are written down during text extraction, is an unmeasured training variable, and introduces a clean-window survival metric quantifying how much of a corpus still requires boundary inference. A census of thirteen public corpora shows survival collapsing in vision-converted PDF slices compared with web text like C4.

entry.title: Not All Visual Tokens Are Equally Safe to Remove:Consequence-Sensitive Visual Token Compression

author.name: Jingbo Wen, Liang He, Mingyu Cao, Haoyu Wang, Minxuan Hu, Kangning Cui, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: Argues that visual token compression in VLMs should account for asymmetric error costs, since misreading an invoice total is far worse than mislabeling a background color. Proposes a calibrate-then-allocate procedure that estimates consequence-specific error-budget curves offline and allocates visual compute per request accordingly.

entry.title: Software Engineering for and with GUI Agent

author.name: Shengcheng Yu, Yuchen Ling, Junyang Xing, Quan Zhou, Chunrong Fang, Zhenyu Chen

entry.summary: Reviews 336 GUI-agent papers from 2018 through April 2026 and argues the field has outgrown its engineering maturity, with brittle, insufficiently validated systems that are really closed-loop software including perception, execution feedback, recovery, and human oversight. Proposes a software-engineering perspective on building and testing such agents.

entry.title: ZetaGPT: A Reference Implementation of Positional--Encoding--Free State--Space--Attention Language Models

author.name: R\'ois\'in Luo

entry.summary: ZetaGPT is a reference implementation of a language model that removes explicit positional encodings entirely, instead placing causal state-space equations before attention so that token order is implicitly encoded by the recurrence. It tests whether position can be an inherent property of the architecture rather than an add-on like RoPE.

entry.title: Build it, Break it, Repeat: Benchmarking and improving LLM-manipulated disinformation detection in social media posts

author.name: Kevin Thomas, Milosz Kasprzyk, Reuel C Igbokwe Onuigbo, Elliott Pert, Cameron Tovey, Jo\~ao A. Leite, Olesya Razuvayevskaya, Carolina Scarton

entry.summary: Adapts the Build it, Break it, Fix it methodology into an iterative Build it, Break it, Repeat protocol for stress-testing detectors of LLM-manipulated disinformation, where human and model adversaries repeatedly rewrite posts to evade classification across five rounds. Shows that static held-out benchmarks overstate detector robustness under deliberate adversarial rewriting.

entry.title: RangeFactory: Scalable Construction of Multi-Hop Cyber Ranges

author.name: Hanlin Jiang, Puyi Wang, Jiandong Jin, Shaofei Li, Zhan Shen, Pengli Wang, Ziming Wang, Yifeng Cai, Ning Jia, Yuxin Ren, Peng Jiang, Yao Guo, Ding Li

entry.summary: RangeFactory automatically composes isolated vulnerability environments into end-to-end validated multi-hop cyber ranges, providing the multi-host infrastructure needed to evaluate whether LLM agents can sustain full attack chains. It removes the manual specification of vulnerability semantics required by prior scenario construction.

entry.title: ENCORE: Efficient Noise Context-Aware Representation for Low-Dose CT Denoising

author.name: Minwoo Yu, N. Robert Bennett, Jongduk Baek, Adam S. Wang

entry.summary: ENCORE improves low-dose CT denoising by replacing the usual Gaussian noise assumption with a realistic noise-synthesis procedure for training-pair generation and conditioning the denoiser on local noise power and correlation context. It tailors architecture choices to CT-specific non-stationary, spatially correlated noise instead of borrowing natural-image designs.

entry.title: When Vision Becomes Text: Visual Token Pruning via Cross-Modal Residual Guidance in VLMs

author.name: Congyang Ou, Ruike Song, Yang Zhou, Libo Sun, Haokui Zhang, Zhenbo Luo

entry.summary: Identifies that in vision-language models, text tokens progressively absorb visual content through self-attention as layers deepen, and uses this cross-modal residual signal as a new criterion for pruning visual tokens. It complements existing similarity-based pruning that only looks at local, per-layer correlations.

entry.title: Rethinking LLM Verification: Evidence Structure, Uncertainty, and Selective Refinement

author.name: Uma Ranjan, Kunal Tilaganji, Aditya Koul, Anurag Mahipal, Dashpreet Singh, Hriday Rana, Manan Jain, Sidharth Gupta, Ajo Babu George, Vineeth Balasubramanian, Nagarajan Natarajan, Amit Sharma

entry.summary: A two-stage medical hypothesis verification framework lets a model abstain when uncertain and then applies targeted ontology grounding only to abstained cases, reporting a 9.6 point accuracy improvement using GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-R1 as frontier backbones. It also provides evidence that abstention correlates with genuine low confidence rather than being random.

entry.title: MVTrack: Ultrafast Appearance-Free Moving Object Tracking from Compressed Bitstreams

author.name: I\~naki Erregue, Kamal Nasrollahi, Sergio Escalera

entry.summary: MVTrack tracks moving objects directly from H.264 motion vector fields in compressed bitstreams, combining a lightweight detector with a simple kinematic association module. It reports beating a small YOLO baseline on a surveillance dataset with roughly 60 times fewer parameters, 40 times fewer FLOPs, and 8.6 times lower CPU latency.

entry.title: GESTO: Human-Centric Spatio-Temporal Memory for Reasoning in Dynamic Scenes

author.name: Ermanno Bartoli, Buwei He, Dennis Rotondi, Sebastian Koch, Federico Tombari, Kai O. Arras, Patric Jensfelt, Yixi Cai, Iolanda Leite

entry.summary: GESTO builds a persistent spatio-temporal memory that couples a 4D scene graph with a two-level hierarchy of atomic human-object interactions and goal-directed events, extracted automatically from RGB-D streams. It targets robot reasoning about how people use objects over time, not just where objects are.

entry.title: CARE: Confidence-Aware Reasoning for Reliable Medical VQA

author.name: Yuetian Du, Yucheng Wang, Zhenyuan Chen, Luyuan Chen, Rongyu Zhang, Jinjian Zhang, Wei Zhou, Zhijie Xu, Ming Kong, Zhan Zhou, Jie Liu, Qiang Zhu

entry.summary: CARE addresses confidence miscalibration in medical multimodal LLMs trained with reinforcement fine-tuning, where expressed certainty diverges from diagnostic accuracy. It combines synthesized medical chain-of-thought cold-start data with group relative policy optimization using a confidence-aware reward that jointly optimizes accuracy and calibration.

entry.title: VidForensics-M1: Meta-Detection Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Temporal Grounding for AI-Generated Video Forensics

author.name: Bowei Liu, Zheng Lu, Yuhan Bian, Xinchen Zhang, Xingming Shui, Yuesheng Huang, Xuhuan Li, Zihao Liu, Yifan Yang, Jun Zhou, Xiu Li

entry.summary: VidForensics-M1 applies a meta-detection reinforcement learning objective to AI-generated video detection, jointly optimizing the authenticity label and verifiable temporal grounding of supporting evidence. The aim is better generalization to unseen generators than label-only supervised or RL training provides.

entry.title: Multitask Pareto Optimization for Monotone Submodular Problems with Dynamic Constraints

author.name: Liam Wigney, Frank Neumann

entry.summary: This theory paper studies evolutionary multitasking for monotone submodular maximization where tasks share one objective but differ in dynamic knapsack constraints, showing that uniform within-constraint costs yield small Pareto fronts. Small fronts enable solution sharing across tasks and runtime advantages over solving each task independently.

entry.title: Enabling Scalable Kinesthetic Teaching via Observer-based Hand-guiding with Active Support

author.name: Anna Tuma, Giuseppe Monetti, Jochen J. Steil, Niels Dehio

entry.summary: RHOAS makes robot hand-guiding for kinesthetic teaching less fatiguing by actively assisting the operator's intended motion using model-based force estimation, without requiring wrist force-torque sensors or pre-learned motion priors. The goal is to scale demonstration collection for imitation learning over longer sessions.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Kinodynamic Motion Planning Under Uncertainty For Safe Navigation on Planetary Environments

author.name: Sachin Sunil Kelkar, Tanmay Dokania, Yashwanth Kumar Nakka

entry.summary: The paper combines a sampling-based asymptotically optimal planner producing risk-aware dynamically feasible trajectories with a second optimization stage, for planetary rovers whose learned terrain interaction models carry significant uncertainty. It targets safe navigation where both terrain mechanics and perception introduce risk.

entry.title: Emotion in an active inference model of human driving

author.name: Julian F. Schumann, Johan Engstr\"om, Ran Wei, Jens Kober, Martijn Wisse, Arkady Zgonnikov

entry.summary: Extends active inference models of human driving to include affective state, representing emotion along valence and arousal axes in continuous rather than discrete state spaces. The goal is more realistic cognitive models of driver behavior for traffic simulation and autonomous vehicle interaction.

entry.title: Dynamic Coalition Formation and Communication Pricing in Skill-Based Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Mojtaba Eslami

entry.summary: Models agent selection and inter-agent communication in multi-agent LLM systems as a cooperative game, with a marginal-value activation rule, a greedy router, and Shapley-value estimates to decide which agents and communication edges are worth paying for. Aims to cut token cost, latency, and error propagation in agentic pipelines.

entry.title: Guixu: Valuation-Driven Data Discovery for Autonomous AI Agents with On-Chain Attestation

author.name: Yifan Wu, Yuchen Peng, Jiaqi Chai, Yufei Qian, Xilin Li, Ke Chen, Lidan Shou

entry.summary: Presents a data discovery system for autonomous agents that estimates task-specific dataset utility via proxy-label propagation, selects datasets under budget using multi-round knapsack optimization, and records usage feedback through on-chain attestation and an agentic payment protocol. It goes beyond retrieval-oriented dataset search.

entry.title: KGCache: Amortized Subgraph Retrieval for KG Reasoning with LLMs

author.name: Uros Stanic, Changcheng Yuan, Sabuj Laskar, Ariful Azad

entry.summary: Observes that knowledge-graph QA systems repeatedly query the same one-hop neighborhoods across questions and introduces an in-memory neighborhood cache placed between the QA engine and the graph backend. It is compatible with both iterative traversal and one-shot planning paradigms and is evaluated on standard KGQA datasets.

entry.title: Coupled Graph--Policy Distillation for Personalized Medication Safety in Older Adults with Multimorbidity

author.name: Zihan Wang, Anglin Liu, Rongyi Wang, Dantong Li, Yi Lu, Siqing Yuan, Hongxia Xu, Zhongtian Long, Jintai Chen

entry.summary: ATLAS builds a medication-safety knowledge graph from guidelines, asks targeted questions to fill in patient details, distills a patient-specific conflict graph, and runs a risk-first multi-agent policy to screen contraindications and verify plans for older adults with multiple conditions. It also introduces GeriMedBench, an interactive evaluation for this setting.

entry.title: Capability Is Not Propensity: Measuring Pressure-Robust Cooperative Behavior in Civic LLM Agents

author.name: Neel Tushar Shah, Manglam Kartik, Akshat Karkar

entry.summary: Argues that cooperative-AI evaluation must separate what models can do under benign instructions from what they tend to do under realistic pressure, and introduces a ten-scenario civic suite covering persuasion, commitment design, asymmetric information, and dissent preservation. Across seven models from four families, subtle omission pressure uniformly increased manipulative enablement and decreased dissent preservation.

entry.title: From Sweep to Seam: Interleaved Cross-Block Post-Training Quantization

author.name: Achille Jacquemond, Yuma Ichikawa, Akira Sakai

entry.summary: Proposes Interleaved Cross-Block Quantization, a scheduling change for block-wise post-training quantization that revisits the boundary pair between consecutive chunks so seam errors are refined twice instead of being locked in by a single forward sweep. Reuses existing calibration inputs and keeps the local two-block reconstruction objective.

entry.title: JaleesBench: Are AI Assistants Good Spiritual Company?

author.name: M. Waleed Kadous (iaser.ai, Faith Family Technology Network), Benjamin Olsen (Faith Family Technology Network)

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 140 two-turn scenarios drawn from a classical Islamic virtue compilation to test whether AI assistants provide beneficial spiritual counsel under adversarial pressures and different framings, judged against each scenario supporting texts. Finds generic frontier models perform only middling on this criterion.

entry.title: AeroDPO: Unleashing Lightweight UAV Navigation with High-Fidelity Perception and Automated Preference Optimization

author.name: Peng Xu, Chengcheng Wang, Shaohua Wan

entry.summary: Argues that for UAV vision-language navigation, perception fidelity matters more than language model size, showing a 2B model with high-quality visual input matching 7B baselines on success rate. It then adds automated preference optimization to address robustness weaknesses of the minimalist policy for edge deployment.

entry.title: CosmosAlign: Adapting a World Foundation Model for Generative Traffic Video Forecasting

author.name: Quang Minh Dinh, Tuan Kiet Doan

entry.summary: Adapts a pretrained world foundation model for long-horizon traffic video forecasting using a two-stage low-rank adaptation that first aligns the conditioning mode with the forecasting task and then aligns caption style with the model expectations. The claim is that distribution alignment, not added capacity, drives successful downstream adaptation of world models.

entry.title: Distilling CT Foundation Models into Editable Concept Bottlenecks for Lung Nodule Malignancy Prediction

author.name: Fakrul Islam Tushar, Stephen Adamo, Geoffrey D. Rubin

entry.summary: Distills frozen CT foundation model embeddings into interpretable concept bottlenecks that predict eight radiologist-defined nodule attributes, then predicts malignancy from those concepts plus nodule size. Concept fidelity and malignancy performance are evaluated on internal and external cohorts.

entry.title: Private Anytime Selective-Risk Certification for Federated Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Guarantees and Empirical Limits

author.name: Sanjeda Akter, Ibne Farabi Shihab, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: Develops a score-agnostic selective-risk certificate for federated retrieval-augmented generation under differential privacy, where clients release only noise-perturbed score and loss histograms. Martingale arguments bound risk and accepted mass across all thresholds and rounds, allowing anytime monitoring with dropout and optional stopping.

entry.title: Evidence-Grounded Forensic Reasoning for Detecting and Grounding Multi-Modal Media Manipulation

author.name: Yichun Yeh, Yiheng Li, Xiaobo Hu, Zhen Lei, Yang Yang

entry.summary: Targets detection and grounding of image-text manipulation by forcing explanations to be tied to the predicted evidence locations, rather than generating free-floating rationales alongside black-box detections. Training signals are differentiated so that localization tokens receive distinct optimization pressure from explanation tokens.

entry.title: On-Device Multi-Species Malaria Detection with Uncertainty-Calibrated Slide-Level Aggregation

author.name: Idaya Seidu, Ahmed Tahiru Issah, Charles B. Delahunt, Carine Mukamakuza

entry.summary: Develops a multi-species malaria microscopy diagnosis pipeline designed around clinical constraints elicited from a national health center, including image-acquisition stopping criteria, human-in-the-loop review and uncertainty-calibrated slide-level aggregation, running on-device for low-resource settings. Emphasizes deployability requirements typically ignored in machine learning malaria papers.

entry.title: REVEAL: A Rubric-Guided Agent for Explicit Evidence Sufficiency Verificationin Long-Video Question Answering

author.name: Caijun Yan, Yang Zhou, Meixing Shi, Haoran Sun, Yichen Li, Yuxiang Cai, Yankai Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes a rubric-guided agent for long-video question answering that explicitly verifies evidence sufficiency before answering, replacing fixed-length temporal chunking and static offline memory banks with adaptive event-aware retrieval during reasoning. Addresses premature answering when only semantically relevant but causally insufficient clues have been retrieved.

entry.title: CuteTTS: Efficient and High-Quality Speech Synthesis via Autoregressive Modeling of Continuous Latents

author.name: Yuqian Zhang, Yao Shi, Kexin Huang, Botian Jiang, Zhe Xu, Yiwei Zhao, Min Liang, Shuang Chen, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: Presents a compact zero-shot text-to-speech system that autoregresses over continuous latent patches from a semantically aligned causal variational autoencoder, with explicit speaker conditioning and a bidirectional flow-matching decoder, to cut the inference cost of iterative diffusion sampling per step. Aims at streaming, low-latency high-fidelity synthesis.

entry.title: DeepFreqMark: End-To-End Learnable Frequency-Domain Watermarking with Spherical Attack Simulation for Latent Diffusion Models

author.name: Chen-Hsiu Huang, Mario K\"oppen, Ja-Ling Wu

entry.summary: DeepFreqMark replaces handcrafted frequency-domain patterns in latent-diffusion watermarking with a learned neural message encoder and decoder embedded in the initial latent noise. A spherical-interpolation attack simulator avoids costly DDIM inversion during training, improving capacity and robustness.

entry.title: RAG-Audio: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Faithful Brain-to-Audio Reconstruction

author.name: Ambuj Mehrish, Sebastiano Vascon

entry.summary: RAG-Audio combats prior domination in brain-to-audio reconstruction, where a strong pretrained generator conditioned on weak fMRI signals produces realistic but wrong audio, by retrieving a real audio exemplar and initializing the frozen generator's sampling trajectory from it. On Brain2Music it lifts 10-way stimulus identification from near chance to roughly 0.4 and cuts Frechet Audio Distance by about an order of magnitude.

entry.title: ELBench: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Education-Facing Large Language Models

author.name: Yilin Jiang, Xiaorong Zhu, Fei Tan, Zicheng Zhang, Kaiyi Huang, Yang Yu, Zexuan Fei, Yiming Luo, Keqian Li, Hao Hao, Guangtao Zhai, Aimin Zhou

entry.summary: ELBench proposes an integrated benchmark for education-facing LLMs, jointly measuring general capability, safety under sensitive prompts, basic instructional utility, and higher-level pedagogical cultivation under one protocol. It argues that current evaluations test these dimensions separately and therefore cannot certify a model as classroom-ready.

entry.title: Confusion-Geometry Rebalancing for Long-Tailed Adversarial Training

author.name: Mengnan Zhao, Geyong Min, Lihe Zhang, Tianhang Zheng, Jie Cui

entry.summary: CGRm rebalances long-tailed adversarial training by using directed robust errors between class pairs, rather than treating classes in isolation, to derive loss weights and confusion-geometry corrections. It is presented as a plug-in for existing robust training pipelines.

entry.title: From Values to Benchmarks: Evaluating Large Language Models for Governmental Use in Dutch

author.name: Laurens Samson, Iva Gornishka, Gossa L\^o, Yuki M. Asano, Sennay Ghebreab

entry.summary: Developed with a Dutch municipal organisation, this framework derives six evaluation dimensions for government LLM use, including factuality, honesty, social bias, energy consumption, cost, and training-data transparency, and operationalises them across 30-plus benchmarks. It links public-sector values to concrete measurements in a non-English context.

entry.title: From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation

author.name: Changshuai Wei, John Bencina, Phuc Nguyen, Andre Assuncao Silva T Ribeiro, Benjamin Zelditch

entry.summary: An industrial framework that replaces predictive scoring plus heuristic allocation with end-to-end causal optimization, combining a transformer-based treatment-effect network, a Bayesian bandit layer for uncertainty-aware exploration, and a dual-based linear program for constrained allocation. It targets marketing and notification systems where incremental impact, not prediction, is the objective.

entry.title: Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks

author.name: Zelei Cheng, Amritansh Mishra, Sambit Sahu, William Campbell

entry.summary: SINKFLEX-RL is a modular training system for multi-turn tool-use RL, combining a Gymnasium-compatible environment wrapper, a VERL-style rollout dataflow, group-relative policy optimization without a value model, and a sink-aware FlexAttention path that preserves attention-sink scaling under causal and sliding-window masks. It targets the systems obstacles of long-context agentic rollouts.

entry.title: Invertible Logits Transformation for Accuracy-Preserving Post-Hoc Uncertainty Calibration

author.name: Lening Zhao, Qipeng Zhan, Li Shen

entry.summary: InvLT applies a single learned scalar MLP element-wise to pre-softmax logits, giving a nonlinear post-hoc calibrator whose parameter count does not grow with the number of classes and which preserves rank ordering so predictions never change. It targets the gap between inexpressive temperature scaling and class-count-dependent alternatives.

entry.title: Fisher8: Stabilizing Neural Heteroscedastic Regression via Output-Layer Fisher Geometry

author.name: Sumedh Vemuganti, Nickvash Kani

entry.summary: Fisher8 attributes the instability of jointly predicting mean and variance in heteroscedastic regression to gradient steps misaligned with loss-landscape geometry, and corrects output-layer updates using Fisher rather than Euclidean geometry.
