It adds no data-dependent hyperparameters and yields an approximate KL trust radius between successive predictive distributions.

entry.title: Retrieval-Corrected Conformal Prediction for Time Series

author.name: Sangjin Jin, Kangmin Kim, Junhyeong Lee, Yongjae Lee

entry.summary: Improves conformal prediction for time series by retrieving past residuals from similar historical conditions as local calibration evidence, then applying a correction for residual coverage error left after retrieval. Targets the temporal dependence and regime shifts that break standard exchangeability-based calibration.

entry.title: Pair-Centric Graph Rewiring for Over-Squashing via Optimal Transport-Guided Communication Alignment

author.name: Yan Wang, Chuan-Xian Ren

entry.summary: Proposes a graph rewiring method that allocates a limited rewiring budget by explicitly scoring which node pairs have the greatest shortfall between required and available message-passing support, using optimal transport to align communication demand and supply. Targets the over-squashing problem in message-passing GNNs.

entry.title: SQuaT: Self-Supervised Knowledge Distillation via Student-Aware Quantized Teacher Features

author.name: HyeonJun Lee, Hyeonsik Jo, Jinwoo Chung, Jangho Kim

entry.summary: Identifies that combining quantization-aware training with knowledge distillation leaves an irreducible distillation loss floor caused by range mismatch between teacher and quantized student features. Proposes quantizing teacher features in a student-aware way to eliminate this residual without needing labels.

entry.title: Physics-informed Diffusion Generative Model for Time-Series Data Synthesis in Dynamic Systems

author.name: Haiteng Wang, Yunfei Zhu, Tao Wang, Yikang Li, Jiabao Dong, Xiaoge Zhang, Lei Ren

entry.summary: Presents a diffusion generative model that embeds physical laws into every reverse diffusion step to synthesize industrial time series such as aero-engine temperature and speed signals. Enforcing constraints stepwise rather than only at the final output is claimed to yield trajectory-level physical consistency.

entry.title: Efficient Hypergradient Descent for Inverse Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Nikita Sevriukov, Anna Barabanova, Uliana Gagarina, Karina Ivanova, Sofiia Kasaeva, Ilya Levin, Marina Sheshukova

entry.summary: Formulates inverse reinforcement learning as bilevel optimization and tackles the expensive inverse-Hessian-vector product in the hypergradient by showing that at the inner optimum the inner Hessian is proportional to the Fisher information matrix of the policy. This enables cheaper natural-gradient-style hypergradient computation.

entry.title: Batch Size or Negatives? A Selection Rule for Memory-Constrained Recommender Training

author.name: Artyom Sabitov, Daniil Volkov, Alexey Zaytsev

entry.summary: Analyzes whether a fixed memory budget in sampled-softmax recommender training should be spent on larger batches or more sampled negatives, deriving a selection rule under smoothness and variance assumptions. Provides guidance for the common case where the final classification layer over a huge item vocabulary dominates memory.

entry.title: Cross-View Feature Matching: Survey, Benchmarking, and Foundation-Model Perspectives

author.name: Songlin Du, Xiaoyong Lu, Zeyu Wu, Xiaobo Lu, Guobao Xiao, Bin Fan, Jiayi Ma, Takeshi Ikenaga

entry.summary: A survey of cross-view feature matching that unifies fragmented problem formulations, architectures, training paradigms, and evaluation protocols into a single taxonomy, extending through the recent shift toward vision foundation models. Adds benchmarking to compare methods on common footing.

entry.title: Divergent Response Modes in Frontier Language Models Under Steering Pressure

author.name: Ali Jalal-Kamali

entry.summary: Evaluates how six frontier models from six developers respond to explicit steering pressure across values-conflict, reasoning-elicitation, and reasoning-suppression prompts, using 300 paired base and steered items. All six models act as blind peer judges over the resulting 24,480 responses, and the study finds models differ not only in how much steering shifts behavior but in the qualitative mode of response.

entry.title: Deciding When to Switch: E-Processes for Adaptive Minimax Training for Generative Adversarial Nets

author.name: Hyunjoo Kim, Sicheng Wu, Agastya Venkatraman, Guang Lin, Sehwan Kim

entry.summary: Formulates the decision of when to switch between discriminator and generator updates in GAN training as a sequential hypothesis-testing problem solved with e-processes, replacing fixed update ratios and heuristics. Provides anytime-valid statistical criteria for whether further updates in the current phase remain beneficial.

entry.title: BreastMammo and DenseMammo: Benchmarks for Mammography Domain Generalization

author.name: Hongyi Pan, Gorkem Durak, Halil Ertugrul Aktas, Andrea Mia Bejar, Mustafa Ege Seker, Nebile Alibeyoglu, Rumeysa Guclu, Rana Gunoz Comert Bozkurt, Sibel Ozkan Gurdal, Neslihan Cabioglu, Beyza Ozcinar, Ravza Yilmaz, Vahit Ozmen, Erkin Aribal, Sukru Mehmet Erturk, Yalda Zafari, Mohamed Mabrok, Kayhan Batmanghelich, Mohammad Yaqub, Ziyue Xu, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: Releases two new multi-view mammography datasets and a domain generalization framework that uses foreground-only histogram matching to reduce vendor-specific acquisition shift for breast density classification. Reports strong internal cross-validation performance with a Swin Transformer backbone plus external evaluation on two additional cohorts.

entry.title: MRIComp4Flow: Compression of 3D Brain MRI for Training Multi-Modal Generative Models

author.name: Lisa K. Fischer, Mykhailo Riabets, Daniel Rueckert, Benedikt Wiestler, Anke Meyer-Baese, Sandeep Nagar

entry.summary: Studies whether standard lossy image codecs (JPEG2000, near-lossless JPEG-LS) can shrink large 3D brain MRI datasets without degrading the training of a wavelet flow-matching generative model. The question matters because generative models must fit the whole data distribution rather than just a decision boundary, so compression tolerance may differ from segmentation.

entry.title: On the Importance of Geometric Nonlinearity and Temperature-Dependent Properties in Multi-Material Thermo-Mechanical Topology Optimization

author.name: Shirin Hosseinmardi, Xiangyu Sun, Ramin Bostanabad

entry.summary: Quantifies how much the usual small-strain and temperature-independent-material assumptions distort multi-material topology optimization of thermally actuated compliant devices. The authors introduce a physics-informed simultaneous analysis-and-design framework with finite-strain constitutive modeling and temperature-dependent properties.

entry.title: Leveraging Human Reading Behavior for Keyphrase Extraction: A Webcam-based Eye-tracking Corpus

author.name: Chengzhi Zhang, Xinyi Yan, Wenqi Yu

entry.summary: Collects a Chinese eye-tracking corpus for library and information science abstracts using a lightweight webcam-based platform, then tests whether reading-behavior features improve keyphrase extraction. The motivation is that keyphrases are not only statistically salient but also attract reader attention.

entry.title: TRIBE: Predicting Team Performance via Communication Behavior Ensembles

author.name: Ali Jalal-Kamali, Nikolos Gurney, David V. Pynadath, Fred Morstatter

entry.summary: TRIBE clusters teams into behavioral types from communication patterns alone, predicting team performance as early as 10% into a task across four datasets without task-specific knowledge. Temporal analysis shows that AI agents shift team behavioral trajectories differently from human teammates.

entry.title: Edge Phoneme Recognition for Children's Speech through Age-Aware Training

author.name: Matthew Arboleda, Ryan Arboleda, Sophie Haak, Sam Hjelmeset, Andrew Franck, Bingrui Yang, Jose Bustamante Ortiz, Yuanrong Shen, Joel Walsh

entry.summary: By jointly training a lightweight model to predict a child speaker's age alongside the phoneme sequence, a 94M-parameter system outperforms a 317M WavLM Large baseline on children's speech phoneme recognition and nearly matches far larger competition ensembles. The result enabled an on-phone pronunciation training application.

entry.title: Lesion-Aware Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator for CT-to-PSMA PET Synthesis in Prostate Cancer

author.name: Rashmi Bhaskara, Waleed M. Almutairi, Matthew Gopaulchan, Maram Musaad Alqurashi, Francis Asamoah, Alex Ocana, Clinton D. Bahler, Oluwaseyi M. Oderinde

entry.summary: This method synthesizes whole-body PSMA-PET from CT using a lesion-aware adaptive Fourier neural operator, replacing purely global L1 or MSE objectives that let models score well on SSIM and PSNR while underestimating small tumor activity. Radiomics-informed guidance is incorporated without requiring per-case feature extraction from delineations.

entry.title: Gaussian Sculpting: End-to-End Controllable Surface Reconstruction via Field Optimization

author.name: Ke Jiaxin, Juncheng Liu, Yi Wang, Zhouhui Lian, Bin Liu, Shengfa Wang, Xiangjia He

entry.summary: Gaussian Sculpting anchors 3D Gaussians to an evolving differentiable surface so the splats actively guide signed distance field optimization instead of having a mesh extracted only in post-processing. A bi-level design isolates gradients for stable joint optimization, targeting sparse-view surface reconstruction.

entry.title: CapProbe: Evaluating Detailed Image Captions via Full-Scene Dense Question Answering

author.name: Mouxiao Huang, Qiangyu Yan, Borui Jiang, Han Shu

entry.summary: CapProbe evaluates detailed image captions by decomposing each image into coarse foreground and background regions and generating region-aligned multiple-choice questions across ten semantic categories, converting caption scoring into dense factual verification. It targets weaknesses of reference-based metrics and LLM-as-judge protocols.

entry.title: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs

author.name: Alexander Panfilov, David Schmotz, Ilia Shumailov, Luca Beurer-Kellner, Joachim Schaeffer, Ameya Prabhu, Jonas Geiping, Maksym Andriushchenko

entry.summary: Already covered in Research yesterday, The authors find that encrypted chain-of-thought blocks returned by commercial providers are interchangeable across sessions, users, and models within the same ecosystem, and exploit this to inject a strong model's hidden reasoning into a weaker, less guarded sibling model that then reveals it. This yields a scalable decryption jailbreak that undermines the intellectual-property protection of concealed reasoning traces.

entry.title: When Confidence Fails: Overconfidence in LLMs under Uncertainty and Missing Clinical Information

author.name: Maryam Tahermazandarani, Adnan Mahmood, Fahmida Islam, Quan Z. Sheng

entry.summary: Systematically probes LLM confidence calibration in clinical multiple-choice reasoning under two uncertainty regimes: injected linguistic hedging cues in prompts, and deliberately removed clinical information. Finds models remain confidently wrong, which is the most dangerous failure mode for clinical decision support.

entry.title: When Latents Forget Pixels: Restoring Fidelity in Diffusion Transformer Super-Resolution

author.name: Yu Shi, Yuyao Zhang, Yu-wing Tai

entry.summary: Diagnoses that latent diffusion transformers hallucinate super-resolution details because the VAE compression bottleneck discards fine spatial evidence from the low-resolution input. The proposed pixel-grounded framework preserves and reinjects pre-compression pixel evidence throughout restoration to improve fidelity without sacrificing perceptual quality.

entry.title: SiriusDeliver: Automating Data Warehouse Delivery at Tencent

author.name: Haining Xie, Xiaokai Zhou, Jiaming Yang, Siqi Shen, Ziwei Wang, Yifeng Zheng, Tengyue Xu, Yipeng Shi, Zefang Zong, Yang Li, Peng Chen, Jie Jiang, Debiao He, Xiao Yan, Jiawei Jiang

entry.summary: SiriusDeliver is a deployed Tencent agent that automates enterprise data warehouse task delivery end to end, covering context retrieval, workflow configuration, code generation, submission, and failure diagnosis. It adds hierarchical skill orchestration, lifecycle-aware artifact control, and continuous adaptation to changing platform practices.

entry.title: MoRSE: Task-Oriented Multi-Agent System with Mixture of Role-Subtask Experts

author.name: Peiwen Li, Shiyang Zhang, Yangtian Zhang, Sizhuang He, David van Dijk, Rex Ying

entry.summary: MoRSE gives multi-agent LLM systems heterogeneity at the parameter level rather than just via different prompts, conditioning specialized experts on (role, subtask) pairs and making agent responsibilities explicit in the task structure. Aimed at long-horizon complex tasks where prompt-only differentiation limits specialization.

entry.title: Rethinking Data Efficiency in Industrial Dense Prediction: Pretraining Coherence, Not Inductive Bias, Determines ViTs Low-Data Advantage

author.name: Haoran Sui, Yaoyuan Jia

entry.summary: Controlled experiments on four industrial datasets argue that the supposed data hunger of Vision Transformers relative to CNNs stems from mismatch between ImageNet-pretrained ViT backbones and COCO-pretrained CNN necks, not from missing convolutional inductive bias. The authors propose lightweight feature recalibration blocks and map a data-efficiency frontier.

entry.title: Compact Feed-Forward 3D Gaussians via Saliency-Guided Primitive Merging

author.name: Tim-Felix Fassch, Jochen Kall, Cyrill Stachniss

entry.summary: A structure-aware merging pipeline consolidates the redundant per-pixel Gaussians produced by feed-forward reconstruction methods into content-adaptive clusters, retaining most visual quality with roughly one twentieth of the primitives. It is designed as a post-hoc module usable with any feed-forward splatting method.

entry.title: FADE: From Passive Verification to Active Discovery in Counterfactual Video Understanding

author.name: Fufangchen Zhao, Jinhu Fu, Jiachen Lei, Jiahong Wu, Xiangxiang Chu, Danfeng Yan

entry.summary: FADE argues that counterfactual video multiple-choice benchmarks leak the target event through their questions and options, converting discovery into text-guided verification. It trains models with evidence-internalized fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning that progressively fades textual anchors, forcing visual discovery.

entry.title: MIRA: Medical Image Reflection for Agentic Diagnosis

author.name: Shengzhi Wang, Jun Yang, Kai Wu, Xiaozhong Ji, Yiwen Ye, Ziyang Chen, Mingliang Xiong, Wen Fang, Mingqing Liu, Mengyuan Xu, Miaoxuan Shan, Caiyan Liu, Bin He, Qingwen Liu

entry.summary: MIRA is a medical visual agent that invokes image operations such as zoom, grounding, pointing, rotation, and measurement plus web search, while reflectively verifying whether each tool call was necessary and whether returned evidence supports the current hypothesis. It addresses the risk that indiscriminate tool use injects misleading evidence into diagnosis.

entry.title: NullEdit: Stealthy Image Protection via VLM Condition Redirection

author.name: Weiyao Huang, Liqin Wang, Ziqi Sheng, Wei Lu

entry.summary: NullEdit protects images from unauthorized instruction-based editing by perturbing them so that VLM-conditioned diffusion editors produce a natural-looking no-op instead of a visibly corrupted output. The stealthy failure mode is intended to suppress the edit without revealing that protection is present.

entry.title: Temporally Grounded Compositional Camera Motion Understanding via Geometric Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Dazhao Du, Shiyan Du, Jian Liu, Yongjian Yu, Bohai Gu, Tao Han, Hualuo Liu, Eric Liu, Yujia Zhang, Xi Chen, Song Guo

entry.summary: Reformulates camera motion understanding as temporally grounded, compositional recognition, since real shots contain changing and simultaneous movements that clip-level labels obscure. Introduces CamChoreo, a benchmark of 4,229 real single-shot clips, and uses geometric knowledge distillation to teach multimodal LLMs this capability.

entry.title: ThinkAfford: Affordance-Centric Reasoning for Fine-Grained 3D Grounding in Cluttered Scenes

author.name: Xinrui Lin, Sha Zhang, Shumin Wang, Zenghuan Zhu, Jiajun Deng, Yanyong Zhang

entry.summary: ThinkAfford separates high-recall affordance proposal generation from instruction-grounded reasoning to localize functional interaction regions in cluttered 3D scenes from natural-language task descriptions. It targets failures of wrong granularity and confusion among visually similar candidates under relational instructions.

entry.title: R4DSG: Relative 4D Scene Graph Memory for Object-Centric Question Answering in Long Egocentric Video

author.name: Ke Ma, Yamin Mao, Weiming Li, Shuai Tan, Yijie Zhong, Hao Chen, Haofen Wang, Meng Wang

entry.summary: R4DSG builds a relative 4D scene graph memory over long egocentric video so a system can answer object-centric questions about where items moved, when they changed state, and why they were relocated, without requiring depth, poses, or reconstructions. It compresses graph sequences instead of storing raw histories.

entry.title: CausalSplat: Towards Comprehensive Hierarchical Reasoning in 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jiayu Ding, Meilu Song, Yun Chen, Wei Gao, Ge Li

entry.summary: Introduces reasoning-based 3D Gaussian segmentation, where queries involve implicit intent, spatial constraints, commonsense, affordance, and counterfactual reasoning rather than explicit object names, plus two benchmarks. CausalSplat combines vision-language models with 3D scene graphs and reportedly outperforms current methods that do poorly on these queries.

entry.title: Seeing above the waves: A modular sensing framework for data acquisition at sea

author.name: Jonathan E. Schmidt, Julius Wirbel, P. Nicholas Hansen, Morgan Lou\'edec, Christian L. H. Westerdahl, Dimitrios Dagdilelis, Roberto Galeazzi

entry.summary: The authors present a modular, reproducible maritime sensing platform integrating radar, lidar, IMU, GNSS, AIS, RGB and thermal cameras, and weather sensors, together with a ROS2 software framework for data acquisition at sea. It is intended as a blueprint for systematic evaluation of perception subsystems for autonomous surface vessels.

entry.title: Flow-by-Flow:Content-Judgment Bypass for Governing AI Output in High-Loss Domains

author.name: Hiroki Naito

entry.summary: A conceptual analysis arguing that human oversight of AI output fails not just because of output volume but because of per-item cognitive load, decomposed into triage, judgment, and response costs. It claims model capability gains only reduce the judgment component, and often by inducing omission rather than genuine relief, so oversight in high-stakes domains stays structurally strained.

entry.title: NL2SHACL-Bench: A Benchmark Suite for Natural Language to SHACL Translation

author.name: Yuchen Zhou, Niels Bobet, Maribel Acosta

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark suite for translating natural language requirements into SHACL constraint shapes for validating RDF knowledge graphs, along with semantics-aware evaluation methods beyond string matching. Four frontier LLMs are evaluated, showing generally competent but imperfect shape generation.

entry.title: IntelliAudit: Using Large Language Models to Evaluate Audit Controls

author.name: Allison Wilson, Sina Moradi Sabet, Diar Shakimov, Panteha Shahrivar, Mohammad Reza Bagheri, Dean Konenkamp, Mohammad A. Tayebi

entry.summary: Describes a retrieval-grounded multi-agent system for IT audit that gathers evidence for a control, drafts an assessment, challenges adverse findings, adjudicates disagreements, and outputs a cited recommendation with gaps flagged. Targets semantic compliance judgment that keyword search cannot handle.

entry.title: CyberAGENTS: Structured Autonomy for Agentic Gamified Learning in Cybersecurity

author.name: Ivan Hornung, Deepthi Marasinghe Arachchige, Tharindu Kumarage, Garima Agrawal, Yuli Deng, Ying-Chih Chen, Huan Liu

entry.summary: Presents an agentic framework for gamified cybersecurity education that constrains generative agents with ontology-guided validation, schema-governed behavior, and competency-based progression to reduce hallucination and pedagogical misalignment. It grounds adaptive tutoring agents in learning science.

entry.title: VDGR-RAG: Vectors, Directories, Graphs, and Reflection Are All You Need for Unified Reasoning over Hierarchical Enterprise Knowledge

author.name: Wenqi Chen, Haofei Yang, Rui Yang, Fangming Li

entry.summary: Combines vector retrieval, directory-structure-driven reasoning, graph traversal, and iterative reflection into a single agentic GraphRAG system for enterprise product documentation question answering. It targets domain routing errors and poor use of hierarchical document structure.

entry.title: Context Is Not Authority: Structured Runtime Governance for Financial Market Agents

author.name: Rui Tang, Qiangqiang Liu, Yichi Zhang, Youwei Wang, Xi Chen, Chen Dong

entry.summary: Presents SAGE-Fin, a runtime control layer for financial LLM agents that treats the proposed real-world effect (a trade, commitment, or deployed policy) rather than the generated text as the object of authorization. It compiles agent proposals into typed candidates, tracks missing institutional obligations as coverage debt, and requires artifact receipts matching the consuming adapter, rechecking authorization after state changes.

entry.title: CRUISE: Vision-Language Model-Guided Uncertainty-Aware Cross-Modal Sensor Fusion for Robust Autonomous Driving

author.name: Junyao Wang, Yulin Xu, Yu Li, Pramod Khargonekar, Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque

entry.summary: CRUISE uses a vision-language model to guide uncertainty-aware fusion of camera, LiDAR, and radar features for autonomous driving, arguing that simple feature-level uncertainty estimates fail out of distribution. The VLM provides semantic context to modulate per-sensor reliability under adverse conditions.

entry.title: Business Truth, not SQL Accuracy: A Rule-Gated 7B Analytics Agent Outperforms a Direct-Prompted 32B Baseline

author.name: Morris Lee

entry.summary: Introduces WarehouseReliabilityBench, 400 frozen analytics tasks over synthetic data warehouses where roughly half of the correct responses are clarifications, abstentions, or refusals rather than SQL, plus QueryProof, a rule-gated 7B agent using semantic-layer and catalog rules. Reports that the small gated agent beats a directly prompted 32B baseline on business-truth correctness.

entry.title: Entropy-based Code Adversarial Translation for Real-world Repository Migration

author.name: Yushun Tang, Yisen Cao, Zhicheng Chen, Lin Peng, Junkang Mao, Fengyi Song, Yantao Jia

entry.summary: ECAT is a multi-agent framework for migrating whole application repositories between mobile platforms, framed as adversarial minimization of a Code Entropy metric between a generator and a discriminator that emits textual gradients specifying file-level directives. Targets the long-horizon failure mode where migrated repositories do not build or run.

entry.title: ComboShoppingBench: Evaluating LLM Agents for Budget-Constrained Basket Shopping with Coupons

author.name: Adrian Li, Kelong Mao, Yudong Guo, Heming Xia, Xinwei Yang, Lirui Luo, Jace Wong, Pu Yao, Sulong Xu, Simiu Gu

entry.summary: ComboShoppingBench evaluates agents on building budget-constrained baskets of complementary items with coupons, delivery fees, and store-level requirements, where many different baskets can satisfy a request. It combines feasibility and payment verification with semantic checks so that infeasible orders and invalid coupon stacking are detected.

entry.title: CADEngBench: It Looks Like CAD, but Does It Work? Evaluating Parametric Design, Assembly Reasoning, and Physics Simulation

author.name: Harmanjot Singh, Abhra Dubey, Jorge Alejandro Amador Herrera

entry.summary: CADEngBench tests whether generated CAD is engineering-grade rather than merely plausible, evaluating 300 parametric parts across zero-to-CAD and functional-editing tasks with boundary-representation validity, manufacturability checks, parameter perturbations, and finite-element comparison against reference responses, plus 150 assembly body pairs for joint reasoning. Includes physics simulation in the loop.

entry.title: verdi: retrieval is not transfer for continual world model optimization

author.name: Junyu Wu, Shiqin Nie, Youyi Kou, Baohua Yin, Guocai Yao, Qingyu Chen, Jingheng Ma, Shiji Zhou, Hongyong Song, Mingchen Zhuge, Sen Cui, Changshui Zhang

entry.summary: Argues that retrieving an optimization strategy that worked on one world model is only a hypothesis for another, and builds an agentic system for continual world-model optimization that requires target-side experimental validation before treating retrieved strategies as transferable knowledge. Aims to stop research agents from rediscovering strategies each campaign while avoiding blind reuse.

entry.title: Bidirectional Context Self-Distillation for Reinforcement Learning of Skill-Based LLM Agents

author.name: Tianjun Pan, Yuan Li, Hongda Wang, Linbo Jin, Mengfei Song, Lei Gao, Qiming Shi, Shaokang Fu, Jiarong Zhao, Chengyu Wang, Chengfu Huo

entry.summary: BCSD trains skill-using agents with reinforcement learning augmented by bidirectional context self-distillation, providing denser supervision on how well the policy converts natural-language skill guidance into actions rather than relying only on sparse task rewards. Targets skill-utilization ability, which is largely unaddressed by task-level RL.

entry.title: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching

author.name: Yuke Li, Xuehan Hou

entry.summary: Proposes a regression-free GUI grounding pipeline where a frozen multimodal model elaborates abstract instructions into concrete element descriptions and a dedicated layout-aware matcher selects among detected elements, avoiding direct coordinate prediction. Aims to eliminate coordinate hallucinations while retaining semantic understanding of vague instructions.

entry.title: From Trajectories to Evidence: Auditable Experimental Records for Industrial Research Agents

author.name: Zijie Zhuang, Changxin Lao, Pengbo Xu, Hanwen Xu, Ruochen Yang, Yingzhi He, Peng Zhang, Jiangxia Cao, Yusheng Huang, Guohong Mu, Jian Liang, Ruiming Tang, Shuang Yang, Zhaojie Liu, Wenwu Ou, Kun Gai

entry.summary: Studies converting completed research-agent trajectories into actual evidence in industrial recommendation experimentation, noting that generated artifacts may be unsupported, executed rounds may be confounded, and later edits can obscure earlier findings. Proposes bounded verification of consequential artifacts in an isolated generate-verify-repair loop plus post-execution qualification of claims.

entry.title: EmoPatient: An Emotion-Directed Patient Simulator for Realistic Palliative Care Communication Training

author.name: Yining Wu, Tianshu Du, Jinrui Fang, Chi Zhang, Sonal Admane, Ying Ding

entry.summary: Presents a palliative care patient simulator in which a separate emotion director agent estimates the simulated patient emotional state and emits turn-level control signals for intensity and regulation. The goal is training clinicians against dynamically shifting emotions rather than a static affective persona.

entry.title: Innovating with Generative AI: A Human Bottleneck Framework

author.name: Julian De Freitas, Ayelet Israeli, Gideon Nave, Artem Timoshenko, Olivier Toubia

entry.summary: Proposes that innovation constraints are largely cognitive and social bottlenecks and analyzes how generative AI relieves or worsens them at each stage of the innovation pipeline, from ideation through diffusion and market learning. Written by marketing and business school researchers as a research agenda.

entry.title: Generalizing deep reinforcement learning across cable-driven parallel robot configurations with actuator-level policies

author.name: Abir Bouaouda (CRAN, UIR), Mohamed Boutayeb (CRAN, UIR), Fran\c{c}ois Charpillet (LARSEN), Dominique Martinez (LORIA, ISM), R\'emi Pannequin (CRAN)

entry.summary: Trains deep reinforcement learning controllers for cable-driven parallel robots at the level of individual actuators, so each motor learns to reach its target cable length, rather than learning a whole-robot end-effector policy. This makes the learned policy transferable across robot configurations and different numbers of actuators.

entry.title: Latent-Frequency Validity: Fast Spectral Editing with Screened Video-VAE Transfer Operators

author.name: Bowen Xue, Jiafeng Xiong, Xin Quan

entry.summary: Introduces a validation-gated approach to editing video autoencoder latents directly in the frequency domain, learning a compact spectral response per autoencoder and deploying it only when decoded fidelity improves without harming round-trip stability. Evaluates across hundreds of autoencoder and edit combinations spanning several spectral families.

entry.title: SpikeWorld: Fast-State Adaptation for Frozen Spiking World Models

author.name: Ziqiao Yu

entry.summary: SpikeWorld is a small sparse spiking network jointly trained for sensory prediction, semantics, image-text binding, and action-conditioned dynamics, with all weights frozen after deployment. Adaptation happens through external paths driven by delayed next-state residuals, avoiding optimizer state or representation drift.

entry.title: LGNNIC: Acceleration of Large-Scale GNN Training using SmartNICs

author.name: Liad Gerstman, Aditya Dhakal, Dejan Milojicic, Avi Mendelson

entry.summary: LGNNIC offloads preprocessing and communication-reduction tasks to smart network cards co-located with remote memory nodes to cut inter-node congestion during distributed graph neural network training. It targets the case where graphs are too large to fit on a single node.

entry.title: Multi-Task Consistency-based Detection of Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Cong Chen, Jean-Philippe Monteuuis, Jonathan Petit

entry.summary: Detects adversarial perturbations in autonomous driving perception by checking consistency between outputs of multiple vision tasks such as detection and segmentation, rather than deploying a dedicated costly defense model. The approach reuses computation already present in multi-task perception stacks.

entry.title: ScaleSense: Cost-Intelligent Scaling Framework via Learned Resource Estimation in Alibaba AnalyticDB

author.name: Yifan Wu, Yuhan Li, Zhenhua Wang, Ke Chen, Lidan Shou, Zonghao Chen, Liang Lin, Huan Li, Gang Chen

entry.summary: Presents a learned resource estimation framework for serverless cloud data warehouses that predicts per-query resource needs from plan topology and hardware specifications, deployed in Alibaba AnalyticDB. It targets a production pattern where users over-provision out of fear of resource exhaustion, wasting budget without fixing non-CPU bottlenecks.

entry.title: Verication-driven closed-loop multi-agent large language modelframework for code-compliant structural design

author.name: Jianbin Luo, Weibin Lin, Yiran Lin, Qing Wei, Wei Guo

entry.summary: Couples a multi-agent structural design system with an external physics-based finite element verifier in a closed repair loop, turning code violations into hard constraints and quality scores into soft constraints, with retrieval linking each violation to a specific code clause. Reports code compliance rising from about 57 percent to nearly 99 percent across five structure types and 44 cases.

entry.title: DialectS2S: End-to-End Speech Dialogue Modeling for Low-Resource Chinese Dialects

author.name: Yi Shu, Tianyu Peng, Yingzhuo Deng, Wen Yang, Jun Lin, Changming Xie, Xinyu Yu, Jiajun Zhang

entry.summary: Builds an end-to-end speech-to-speech dialogue model for low-resource Chinese dialects, combining a synthetic dialect dialogue data pipeline with a two-stage post-training recipe that keeps speech supervision aligned with the drifting semantic representation space during dialect adaptation. Targets naturalness and stability failures that arise when adapting speech LLMs to underrepresented varieties.

entry.title: Dramarrator: Object-Based Audio Editing for Audio Drama Production from Books

author.name: Karim Benharrak, Oriol Nieto, Bryan Wang, Zeyu Jin, Amy Pavel

entry.summary: Presents an authoring tool that converts books into audio dramas using object-based audio editing, extracting story elements like characters and scenes as editable objects, generating linked speech, sound-effect and music assets, and propagating a single change across dependent assets on a multi-track timeline. Addresses the ripple-effect editing burden in generative audio production.

entry.title: Human-Guided Causal Knowledge Injection for Virtual Cells

author.name: Pengcheng Wang, Changjian Chen, Zhuo Tang, You Wu, Long Wang, Feng Yu, Kenli Li

entry.summary: Adds human supervision to automatically constructed causal graphs used to make virtual cell models interpretable, providing a gene-similarity-aware visualization interface for experts to correct errors introduced by unsupervised concept grouping and causal discovery. Aims to inject trustworthy causal knowledge into cellular simulation models.

entry.title: DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference

author.name: Asaad Althoubi

entry.summary: Formulates KV-cache eviction as a sequential decision problem and trains a lightweight policy network with REINFORCE using a per-step KL-divergence reward, drawing on internal signals such as attention statistics, value norms, entropy and position. Aims to beat static heuristics that miss a token's future predictive influence.

entry.title: From Semantic Grounding to Decision Optimization: A Unified Framework for Long-Horizon UAV Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Zeyuan Ma, Jiaxin Chen, Di Huang

entry.summary: A framework for UAV vision-language navigation that injects object-level semantics and spatial cues into observations, aggregates long-horizon history with relevance weighting, and stabilizes action choice to avoid loops and local traps. It targets known weaknesses of aerial agents following natural-language instructions in open 3D space.

entry.title: How Do Large Language Models Judge Social Attraction? Evidence from Theory-Grounded Persona Ratings Across Multiple LLMs and Humans

author.name: Hasan Mahmud, Khawaja Abaid Ullah, Mohammad Javad Khojasteh, Jamison Heard, Prabu David

entry.summary: Thirty-four LLMs rated theory-grounded persona profiles for social attraction across repeated runs, and their judgments were compared with human raters. Models were highly stable and agreed on the ordering of socially attractive, mixed, and unattractive tiers, informing whether LLMs can substitute for humans in subjective social evaluation.

entry.title: Modern Backbones Improve Multi-task DETR for Mammography Classification and Lesion Localization

author.name: Dinh Tan Nguyen, Quang-Hien Kha, Le-Hoang Nguyen, Minh-Toan Dinh, Xuan-Huy Nguyen, Dac Phu Ho, Cao Truong Tran, Sai Ho Ling, Lan T Ho-Pham, Liem Pham, Nguyen Quoc Khanh Le

entry.summary: A multi-task DETR framework for mammography jointly predicts exam-level malignancy and localizes lesions, benchmarking modern backbones including ConvNeXtV2, DINOv3, and MambaVision across two cohorts. Modern backbones clearly beat ResNet-style features, with reported AUC near 98 percent on OPTIMAM.

entry.title: Agentic Harnesses: LLM-Driven Verification Layers for Robot Autonomy

author.name: Rohan Bhagra, Mahantesh Halapannavar, Uddhav Bhattarai

entry.summary: Proposes inserting an LLM-based verification layer between robot planning and execution that judges whether proposed actions are permissible, using an ensemble of chain-of-thought judges. The motivation is that planning models can be goal-biased, forget prior safety incidents, or be adversarially manipulated.

entry.title: Observational Policy Ranking for SMB Financial Guidance from Multi-Action Accounting Logs

author.name: Shrutendra Harsola, Vignesh Subrahmaniam, Vikas Raturi, Kamalika Das, Xiang Gao, Kratika Gupta, Ruocheng Guo, Padmaja Jonnalagedda, Ananya Pramod, Sricharan Kumar

entry.summary: Formulates financial guidance for small businesses as observational policy ranking over 34 ledger-derived action categories using 85,078 company-month records, and proposes an action-wise R-learner regularized by observational support. It is compared against uplift T-learners, a conservative value model, and a zero-shot LLM baseline.

entry.title: ChronoSSM: Training for Temporally Aware Representations in Autoregressive State Space Models

author.name: Adrien Schoen, Nachiketa Ratnakar Patil, Arjun Bhagoji, Francesco Bronzino

entry.summary: ChronoSSM trains autoregressive state space models so that event timing is learned jointly with event identity, rather than bolting a timing head onto representations optimized only for next-event prediction. This targets temporal reasoning, anomaly detection, and faithful chronology reconstruction in event streams.

entry.title: Do Time-Series Forecasters Use the Right History: Recoverability, Recovery, and Functional Use of Temporal Delays

author.name: Qipeng Qian, Yuntao Qian

entry.summary: Separates three distinct questions for time-series models with known lag structure: whether the true delay is recoverable from the data, whether the model reports it, and whether the forecast actually uses that history. The authors prove and empirically confirm that a model can report the correct delay and achieve near-oracle risk while still relying on the wrong lag.

entry.title: Detecting an Effect Is Not Learning to Act on It: A Reward-SNR Floor for LLM Acquisition Agents

author.name: Ying Yuan

entry.summary: Distinguishes detecting that an expensive auxiliary signal such as LLM reasoning helps on average from learning per-instance when to pay for it, and derives a reward signal-to-noise floor governing when the latter is possible. Empirically, learned acquisition routing never beat random across several granularities even when an in-sample oracle showed large apparent gains.

entry.title: A Joint-Distribution Route to Fair Representations with Continuous Sensitive Attributes

author.name: Yijin Ni, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: Proposes measuring independence between a learned representation and a continuous sensitive attribute via a single discrepancy between the joint distribution and the product of marginals, instead of averaging per-value conditional discrepancies. This removes the need for nonparametric conditional-law surrogates at each sensitive value, with a disintegration identity linking the two views.

entry.title: IADD-TR: Intervention-Aware Dynamics Decoupling with Targeted Regularization for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zefeng Liang, Jie Qiao, Ruichu Cai, Weilin Chen, Zhifeng Hao

entry.summary: A model-based RL framework that disentangles action interventions from environment evolution in the learned dynamics model and applies targeted regularization to counter policy-induced data bias and uneven action coverage. Aims to reduce distortion in the counterfactual value estimates used for policy improvement.

entry.title: ProTAGAD: A Foundation Model for TAG Anomaly Detection with Decoupled Topological and Textual Prototypes

author.name: Ziyan Wang, Liwen Wu, Cheng Xie, Song Gao, Zhenli He, Xin Jin

entry.summary: Proposes an anomaly-detection foundation model for text-attributed graphs that keeps topological and textual prototypes decoupled instead of fusing structure and semantics during message passing. Motivated by applications including LLM security, content moderation, and cyber threat detection.

entry.title: Path Integral Value Matching for Linear Quadratic Stochastic Optimal Control

author.name: Bangyan Liao, Chenglei Yu, Yuchen Yang, Chuanrui Wang, Zhisheng Song, Peidong Liu, Tailin Wu

entry.summary: Revisits path integral control for linear-quadratic stochastic optimal control, deriving a temporally recursive value function by truncating and marginalizing the path integral to avoid full-trajectory simulation. Positions this value-based approach as a cheaper, more stable alternative to current policy-based methods.

entry.title: GARLIC: Graph Attention-based Relational Learning of Multivariate Time Series in Intensive Care

author.name: Ruirui Wang, Yanke Li, Manuel G\"unther, Diego Paez-Granados

entry.summary: Proposes an ICU prediction architecture that imputes missingness with a learnable exponential-decay encoder, models inter-sensor dependencies through time-lagged summary graphs, and fuses global with cross-dimensional sequential attention. All attention weights and graph edges are learned end to end to serve as built-in explanations at observation, signal, and edge level.

entry.title: DEFT: Data-Efficient Frequency-domain Top-k Sampling via Inverse Discrete Fourier Transform for Spatiotemporal Dynamical Systems Modeling

author.name: Hengbo Xiao, Jiale Liu, Jiahao Song, Guannan He

entry.summary: Proposes generating training data for PDE surrogate models by identifying dominant Fourier modes of a system and systematically varying their amplitudes and phases, reconstructing physically consistent samples through the inverse discrete Fourier transform. Includes a generalization bound for the resulting sampling scheme.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning for Genomics Applications: Insights from an Empirical Study

author.name: Sepideh Saran, Mahsa Ghanbari, Uwe Ohler

entry.summary: Empirically compares deep ensembles, Bayesian neural networks, and Monte Carlo dropout for uncertainty quantification across genomics tasks including sequence-to-activity prediction and single-cell expression analysis. Assesses how dataset characteristics common in genomics affect the reliability of each uncertainty estimate.

entry.title: Two-stage Odd Residual Flows for Mean-Preserving Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Kiran Madhusudhanan, Christian Kl\"otergens, Lars Schmidt-Thieme, Vijaya Krishna Yalavarthi

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage probabilistic forecaster that first learns a point mean forecast and then fits residual normalizing flows constrained to preserve that mean, avoiding the accuracy degradation that joint likelihood training causes. Targets long-horizon risk-sensitive forecasting where both calibrated distributions and accurate means are needed.

entry.title: Quantifying the noise sensitivity of the Wasserstein metric for images

author.name: Erik Lager, Gilles Mordant, Amit Moscovich

entry.summary: Derives finite-sample bounds on how additive pixel noise perturbs Wasserstein distances between images treated as discrete measures, showing the signed 2-Wasserstein error grows with the square root of the noise standard deviation rather than linearly as for Euclidean distance. Provides theoretical grounding for preferring optimal-transport distances in noisy imaging settings.

entry.title: HyperShape: Hyperelasticity Across Diverse Shapes

author.name: Leo Widmer, Sidaty El Hadramy, St\'ephane Cotin, Philippe Claude Cattin

entry.summary: Releases an extensible generator of synthetic shapes and matching hyperelastic simulation data, producing 2D and 3D datasets with tunable geometric complexity. Enables systematic evaluation of whether neural operators generalize across domain geometry and boundary conditions, including out-of-distribution and synthetic-to-real transfer.

entry.title: SPOTting the Future: Lookahead Explanations for Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tamar Gozlan, Claudia V. Goldman

entry.summary: Introduces a model-agnostic tool that explains deep RL policies by building an interpretable finite-horizon tree from sampled actions and simulated successor states, given access to the policy and a simulator. Provides formal guarantees on asymptotic recovery of the most probable action and characterizes disagreement behavior.

entry.title: DualSpectralCF: Training-Free Sign-Aware Spectral Collaborative Filtering

author.name: Guanqun Yang, Tong Qi, Xiaoxue Han

entry.summary: Extends training-free spectral collaborative filtering to use explicit negative feedback such as one-star ratings and distrust links, via a signed input signal that plugs into any spectral filtering backbone. Aims to capture the accuracy gains of learned sign-aware recommenders without gradient-based training.

entry.title: Quantum Incremental Learning with Mixed State Prototypes

author.name: Yu Wu, Qianli Zhou, Xinyang Deng, Wen Jiang, Kang Hao Cheong, Witold Pedrycz

entry.summary: A quantum incremental learning framework that adds classes by introducing trainable mixed-state prototypes instead of widening the quantum circuit, sidestepping NISQ-era width limits and the orthogonal-basis cap on class count. Aims to avoid catastrophic forgetting under tight parameter and memory budgets.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Vision Foundation Models for Robust Leukemia Cell Classification across Multiple Microscopy Datasets

author.name: Carlos Zamora, Hiram Zuniga, Ulises Orozco-Rosas, Kenia Picos

entry.summary: A two-stage pipeline built on a pretrained vision foundation model with retrieval augmentation classifies leukemia cells across five heterogeneous microscopy datasets, first detecting leukemia and then subtyping into ALL versus AML. The focus is generalization across staining, illumination, and site protocol shifts that break single-dataset models.

entry.title: Conflict or Strategy? Asymmetric Role Framing of La France insoumise and Rassemblement National in French News Headlines, 2022-2025

author.name: Amr Sobhy

entry.summary: Analyzes 28,592 French news headlines about two populist parties using a three-model LLM annotation pipeline validated against a stratified human audit. The main finding is role asymmetry rather than valence asymmetry: the left-populist party is framed through conflict while the right-populist party gets a strategic-electoral register.

entry.title: MAD-HOI: Masked Autoregressive Diffusion for Generating Articulated Hand Object Interactions from Text

author.name: Ananya Bal, Kartik Sharma, Ethan Lai, Samyak Tiwari, Liza Dahiya, Chaitanya Chawla, Laszlo A. Jeni

entry.summary: SSRL-MAR reduces motion artifacts in 3D brain MRI without paired clean-corrupted data or k-space access, using contrastive learning on 3D patches to extract motion representations, an artifact-aware synthesis network, and a final correction stage. This suits clinical settings where paired supervision is unavailable.

entry.title: Seeing things through in the age of AI

author.name: alkjash

entry.summary: The essay observes an asymmetry in which AI dramatically accelerates drafting and prototyping while offering only a small speedup on the finishing work of polishing, debugging, verification, and production hardening. The author argues this asymmetry explains the flood of low-quality AI-assisted output alongside disappointing gains on work that matters.

entry.title: ArchAgent v2: A Case Study with the Data Prefetching Championship

author.name: Abraham Gonzalez, Raghav Gupta, Akanksha Jain, Hanna Alam, Alexander Novikov, Po-Sen Huang, Matej Balog, Marvin Eisenberger, Sergey Shirobokov, Ng\^an V\~u, Hank Levy, Borivoje Nikoli\'c, Sagar Karandikar, Martin Dixon, Parthasarathy Ranganathan

entry.summary: Already covered in Research yesterday, ArchAgent v2 scales agentic evolutionary search from single-level cache replacement policies to multi-level data prefetcher design, adding cascaded evolutionary search that subdivides the design space by memory level and other techniques to handle vast search spaces, hardware budgets, and slow simulation. Framed as a case study against a data prefetching championship setting.

entry.title: TeXFix-Bench: An Empirically Grounded Multi-Format Benchmark for LLM-Based Document Source Repair

author.name: Prajwal S. Venkateshmurthy

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for LLM repair of broken document sources across LaTeX, Typst, and Markdown, grounded in an empirically mined 18-category fault taxonomy derived from real crash reports and commits. Fault injection uses AST-aware mutation operators across formats.

entry.title: Bridging the Gap Between Semantics and Reconstruction:Unifying Sign Language Translation and Production

author.name: Xiao Liu, Shiwei Gan, Yafeng Yin, Jiaxin Yin, Bowen Guo, Yaqi Sun, Zhiwei Jiang, Lei Xie

entry.summary: Attempts to unify sign language understanding (recognition and translation) with sign language production in a single model, despite the two directions requiring opposite mappings between visual sign sequences and text. Bridges semantic understanding with signal reconstruction in one framework.

entry.title: RecoverFly: A Failure-Aware Reinforcement Learning Post-Training Framework for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Boxiong Wang, Hui Kang, Geng Sun, Jiahui Li, Chao Yu, Daxin Tian

entry.summary: RecoverFly post-trains end-to-end UAV vision-language-action policies with failure-aware reinforcement learning to supply the corrective supervision that behavior cloning lacks in closed-loop flight. It targets sample inefficiency, long-tailed scene distributions, and policy distribution shift during optimization.

entry.title: STAIR: Effective Incident Response Using an End-to-End Agentic Planning Framework

author.name: Hanlin Jiang, Jionghao Huang, Shaofei Li, Bojia Yu, Peng Jiang, Yuxin Ren, Ning Jia, Yao Guo, Ding Li

entry.summary: STAIR is an agentic planning framework for cybersecurity incident response that maintains the incident as a graph-structured state, aligns actions with the current recovery stage, and reuses historical experience, addressing the instability of LLM planners over long-horizon recovery. It aims to replace static expert playbooks that cannot adapt to evolving incident conditions.

entry.title: DoseBridge: Denoising Diffusion Bridge Model for Dose Prediction in Lung Intensity-Modulated Proton Therapy

author.name: Zerun Zhang, Xiaoda Cong, Xiangkun Xu, Peter Y. Chen, Xuanfeng Ding

entry.summary: DoseBridge predicts proton-therapy dose distributions with a denoising diffusion bridge that anchors on the patient CT and encodes beam geometry as a spatially aligned mask, fused multiscale with target and organ-at-risk maps for under 2% extra parameters. It was evaluated retrospectively on 52 advanced lung cancer plans.

entry.title: Dynamic Context Adapters: Efficiently Infusing History into Vision-and-Language Models

author.name: Yuhang Song, Bor-Jiun Lin, Jiaxu Liu, Te-Chuan Chiu, Anh Nguyen, Chun-Yi Lee

entry.summary: Dynamic Context Adapter injects compressed fixed-size memory of past frames into pretrained vision-language models so they can handle sequential decision-making without quadratic attention over full frame history. It aims to avoid both compute blowup and lossy temporal compression.

entry.title: Visual Geometry Foundation-Aware Gaussians for Single-Frame Surround-View Driving Reconstruction

author.name: Junhong Lin, Jinlong Wang, Xianda Guo, Yanlun Peng, Wei Zheng, Guoqing Liu, Hanli Wang, Tiesong Zhao, Wei Gao

entry.summary: VGGD uses pretrained visual geometry foundation model features (VGGT) as a frontend prior for feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction from single-frame surround-view driving cameras with minimal overlap. The argument is that upstream geometric representation quality, not decoder complexity, is the bottleneck.

entry.title: ConfTriage: A Calibration-Aware LLM Triage Framework for Pulmonary Nodule Malignancy with Selective Specialist Deferral

author.name: Md Rabiul Islam, Samir Abdaljalil, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: ConfTriage tests whether a generalist LLM reading a natural-language rendering of standard nodule attributes can act as a calibrated triage layer for pulmonary nodule malignancy, deferring low-confidence cases to a specialist imaging model. It provides a finite-sample combined-error bound and an oracle inequality for excess risk.

entry.title: Evidence-Grounded Trustworthy Multimodal Reasoning and Evaluation Benchmark in Complex Urban Scenes

author.name: Zhaoyang Wei, Bowen Jiang, Xumeng Han, Jiashu Li, Xuehui Yu, Yuling Liu, Guorong Li, Zhenjun Han, Jianbin Jiao

entry.summary: AD2-Bench proposes a hierarchical visual diagnosis framework that decomposes multimodal reasoning in adverse-condition urban driving scenes into a structured chain of evidence, so failures in reasoning steps can be attributed rather than only final answers scored. Findings indicate models often infer without adequate visual evidence.

entry.title: Every Packet Counts: Dispersing Information for Loss-Resilient Learned Image Compression

author.name: Yuhang Wei (Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Chuqin Zhou (Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Yibo Shi (Huawei Technologies Ltd), Jing Wang (Huawei Technologies Ltd), Guo Lu (Shanghai Jiao Tong University)

entry.summary: Makes learned image compression resilient to packet loss by redistributing energy across latent channels so critical information is not concentrated, and by interleaving channel groups to break sequential decoding dependencies. Targeted at satellite and emergency communication links.

entry.title: Is There Really a Camouflaged Object? Towards Realistic Camouflaged Object Detection

author.name: Huafeng Chen, Yueming Lyu, Chenyang Si, Wende Tan, Liucheng Guo, Caifeng Shan

entry.summary: Argues that camouflaged object detection is evaluated under a closed-world assumption where every image contains a camouflaged target, causing severe false positives in open-world deployment. Introduces OPC16K, a 16,245-image benchmark from 14 sources that includes pure backgrounds and non-camouflaged objects.

entry.title: Robust Safety Filtering for Input-Constrained Underactuated Linear Systems

author.name: Muhamad Rausyan Fikri

entry.summary: The paper builds a safety filter for input-constrained underactuated linear systems facing unknown disturbances, combining an H-infinity baseline derived from a differential game with a disturbance observer whose estimate and error bound feed robust high-order control barrier function constraints. Pointwise feasibility for scalar-input systems is characterized exactly through an admissible input interval.

entry.title: Scaling Inherently Interpretable Language Models

author.name: Guide Labs Team, Andreas Madsen, Aya Abdelsalam Ismail, Giang Nguyen, Isaac Plant, Muawiz Chaudhary, Nathaniel Monson, Saqib Azim, Zhichen Guo, Julius Adebayo

entry.summary: Already covered in Research yesterday, Argues that interpretability need not cost capability by making it a training objective rather than a post-hoc analysis, and shows across three orders of magnitude of compute that representations become more disentangled and concept-aligned as scale grows, for both autoregressive and diffusion language models. The recipe is instantiated in an 8B diffusion language model built for steerability.

entry.title: Legal Responsibilities Using Autonomous Agents For Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Mark Burgess

entry.summary: Applies Promise Theory and a downstream causal-influence principle to the question of who bears legal responsibility when autonomous AI agents cause criminal or negligent damage, including cases of agents escaping containment. It argues responsibility can be assigned via policy-constrained agent freedoms.

entry.title: From Relevance to Execution Utility: Reward-Aware Dynamic Execution Gating for Skill-Based LLM Agents

author.name: Liang He, Jingbo Wen, Hongyu Gu, Hao Li, Haoyu Wang, Yixiong Chen, Kangning Cui, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: RADEG inserts a lightweight learned gate between skill retrieval and execution for skill-based LLM agents, predicting whether executing a retrieved skill bundle is worth its cost rather than just whether it is topically relevant. It is retriever-agnostic and trained as a cheap surrogate of downstream execution utility.

entry.title: NeuroPilot: An Agent-Driven Smart Pipeline for Processing, Quality Control, and Managing Neuroimages

author.name: Yiyao Chen, Yucheng Li, Jungong Tong, Shaoqi Wang, Kunhao Zhou, Ziquan Wei, Monica Murea, Marissa DiPiero, Tingting Dan, Guorong Wu

entry.summary: NeuroPilot packages neuroimaging standardization, preprocessing, and quality control expertise into three LLM-invocable skills orchestrated by an agent, replacing project-specific scripting and manual quality review. It aims to generalize across infrastructure settings with a single configuration.

entry.title: Learning an Interior Layout Policy in a Domain Specific Language Action Space

author.name: Yuhao Lu, Weichen Zhang, Wenyi Xiao, Haohui Chen, Yiyun Fei

entry.summary: LayoutDSL has an LLM emit interior layout decisions as programs in a domain-specific symbolic language instead of directly regressing object coordinates, and accounts for structural elements such as doors and windows. The claim is that a symbolic action space lets the model learn design reasoning rather than raw geometry fitting.

entry.title: Geometry Beats Estimated Depth: RGB-Only Multi-Camera 3D Tracking under Sim2Real

author.name: Abdullah Naeem, Anav Katwal, Ayon Dey, Noman Khan, Md Tamjidul Hoque

entry.summary: Compares a geometry-first RGB pipeline using homography lifting and multi-camera fusion against a monocular depth pseudo-LiDAR pipeline for warehouse multi-camera 3D tracking under simulation-to-real transfer. Concludes that cross-view geometric consistency rather than monocular depth accuracy governs performance.

entry.title: LoRSA: Toward Generalizable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Biomedical Downstream Tasks

author.name: Saed Moradi, Benyamin Ghojogh, M. Hadi Sepanj, Yimin Yang, Ashirbani Saha

entry.summary: LoRSA combines a dense low-rank adapter capturing globally shared task structure with a dynamically structured sparse low-rank component providing localized residual corrections, for adapting vision foundation models to biomedical tasks. The motivation is that a single low-rank update confines all adaptation to one narrow subspace.

entry.title: Metadata Reconstruction from Values Alone: Recovering Column Semantics in Undocumented Warehouses

author.name: Mike Helwig

entry.summary: Tackles the inverse of typical text-to-SQL settings by recovering column and value semantics from data alone in undocumented warehouses with cryptic identifiers. A deterministic profiler extracts structural evidence such as value fingerprints, pattern matches, and checksum verdicts, and the language model proposes semantics conditioned on that evidence with provenance and evidence-bounded confidence.

entry.title: Effect of Abstractions and Prompting Strategies on LLM-Guided High-Performance Optimizations

author.name: Ji\v{r}\'i Klepl, Maty'a\v{s} Brabec, Martin Kruli\v{s}

entry.summary: Studies how different code abstractions and prompting strategies affect an LLM's ability to produce high-performance, parallel-optimized code, comparing LLM-guided optimization against traditional domain-specific auto-tuning pipelines. Findings inform how to structure representations given to models for HPC code optimization.

entry.title: Biologically Informed Representation Learning for Robust Cross-Center Generalization of MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry

author.name: Alejandro L. Garc\'ia-Navarro, Carlos Sevilla-Salcedo, Bel\'en Rodr\'iguez-S\'anchez, Vanessa G\'omez-Verdejo

entry.summary: Introduces a probabilistic representation-learning framework for MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry that jointly models acquisition-specific variability and biological supervision available in microbiology datasets, improving cross-institution generalization. Aims to make microbial identification and resistance prediction models portable across labs.

entry.title: Do Evaluation Metrics Detect Errors in Classical Chinese to English Translations?

author.name: Osvaldo Quinjica, Eric Bennett, Xinchen Yang, Andrew Schonebaum, Marine Carpuat

entry.summary: Builds a minimal-pair diagnostic framework to test whether standard automatic translation metrics detect error types that matter to scholars translating Classical Chinese into English, probing both reference-based and reference-free metrics. Finds all metrics have blind spots, with one learned metric performing best overall.

entry.title: Calling the Bluff: Detecting Ever-Shifting Harmful Chat Dialogue via Ordered Reasoning Chain Regularization

author.name: Haojie Yu, Ziyou Jiang, Junjie Wang, Mingyang Li, Yuekai Huang, Jie Huang, Qing Wang

entry.summary: Proposes decomposing harmful-dialogue detection into an ordered reasoning chain over topic, harm indicator, severity and type, using intermediate supervision as a structured regularizer plus prototype-based feature augmentation to stay robust as attackers shift harm categories and vocabulary. Reports gains across multiple domains and harm categories.

entry.title: Epistemic Transfer in AI-Assisted Verification: A Framework and Evaluation Protocol

author.name: Christoph Trattner

entry.summary: Proposes evaluating AI verification assistants by what users can do after the tool is removed, introducing an epistemic transfer effect measure comparing delayed unassisted performance and a tool-removal cost measure of immediate performance drop. Distinguishes this construct from correction effects, trust, reliance and human-AI team performance.

entry.title: SignLlama: Enhancing Gloss-free Sign Language Translation by Prioritizing Visual Features for LLMs

author.name: Shiwei Gan, Xiao Liu, Yafeng Yin, Zhiwei Jiang, Bowen Guo, Lie Xie, Sanglu Lu, Hongkai Wen

entry.summary: SignLlama adapts LLMs to gloss-free sign language translation by diagnosing two failure modes: the distribution gap between visual and text embeddings, and autoregressive concatenation causing the model to underweight visual cues. It restructures fusion so visual features are prioritized during decoding.

entry.title: How People Evaluate AI-, Expert-, and Peer-Style Financial Advice

author.name: Aryan Ramchandra Kapadia, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: A preregistered vignette experiment with 285 participants holding financial content constant while varying communication style (AI assistant, certified planner, online forum) and independently manipulating displayed source labels, including mislabeled conditions. Separates the effect of who people think is speaking from how the advice is written.

entry.title: SafeQL: Search-based Refinement for Safe and Efficient LLM-based Text-to-SQL

author.name: Geonho Lee, Min-Soo Kim

entry.summary: SafeQL makes the database an active participant in text-to-SQL refinement, using search-based repair guided by schema and DBMS feedback instead of regenerating whole queries after execution errors. Targets the persistent problem of LLMs referencing nonexistent tables, columns, functions, or values.

entry.title: Learning Preference Adaptation for Large Language Model Personalization via Verbal Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuting Liu, Wei Wu, Jianzhe Zhao, Guibing Guo

entry.summary: Studies task-specific preference adaptation: given a universal natural-language user preference summary, derive a task-conditioned view that keeps decision-relevant evidence and drops distracting context. AlignXada is a training-free meta-learning framework that produces these views verbally rather than requiring fine-tuning or manual per-task engineering.

entry.title: LEED: Local Embedding Evolution Distance for over-smoothing estimation and virtual node selection in GNN

author.name: Killian Cressant, Pedro B. Velloso

entry.summary: LEED is a node-level metric that tracks how individual embeddings evolve across GNN layers, giving finer-grained diagnosis of over-smoothing than global Dirichlet energy. It is also used to select where to insert virtual nodes to relieve over-squashing.

entry.title: NeuroRefiner: Morphology-Aware Multi-Agent Refinement for 3D Fluorescence Microscopy Neuron Segmentation

author.name: Haiyang Yan, Jinyue Guo, Yanchao Zhang, Bingqing Wang, Zhenchen Li, Jing Liu, Jiazheng Liu, Linlin Li, Hua Han

entry.summary: NeuroRefiner is a multi-agent system that mimics expert workflows for 3D neuron segmentation, with agents that diagnose topological errors, issue correction instructions, and validate refinements against a dedicated refinement network. It targets fragmentation caused by sparse, elongated neuron morphology.

entry.title: Power law graph attention: exact generalization of scaled dot-product attention, empirical collapse at inference

author.name: Burc Gokden

entry.summary: Analyzes power law graph attention, which replaces the fixed bilinear form of scaled dot-product attention with a learned input-generated operator, proving it contains standard attention exactly as a special case and establishing positivity and spectral structure. The author also reports an empirical collapse of the learned operator at inference and labels each claim by evidentiary status.

entry.title: Can Bayesian Optimization Efficiently Find a Strong Single Expert in Neural Thickets?

author.name: Nigel Bastian Cendra, Abdelhamid Ezzerg, Fernando Julio Cendra, Jeremias Knoblauch, Jakob Zeitler

entry.summary: Applies Bayesian optimization inside a random low-dimensional linear embedding of LLM weight space to find strong single expert models without backpropagation. Reports matching or exceeding random search with roughly five times fewer candidate evaluations on reasoning benchmarks using small Qwen2.5-Instruct models.

entry.title: Benchmarking Time Series Generation Methods for Privacy-Preserving Forecasting

author.name: Luis Amorim, Vitor Cerqueira, Moises Santos, Paulo J. Azevedo, Carlos Soares

entry.summary: Benchmarks synthetic time series generators and noise-based anonymization baselines when synthetic data fully replaces real data for forecasting, jointly measuring downstream forecast quality and distance-based empirical privacy risk on seven datasets. Characterizes the utility-privacy trade-off in the train-on-synthetic test-on-real regime.

entry.title: MIDAS: Mutual Information Disentanglement with Uncertainty-Aware Fusion for Incomplete Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Yuhua Wen, Yingying Zhou, Qifei Li, Yingming Gao, Zhengqi Wen, Jianhua Tao, Ya Li

entry.summary: Handles missing or corrupted modalities in multimodal sentiment analysis by variationally disentangling shared from modality-specific information via mutual-information objectives and fusing the remaining evidence with uncertainty weighting. Argues this extracts task-relevant signal better than imputation or heuristic coordination constraints.

entry.title: Knowledge-Guided 3D CT Generation: A Conditioning-Centric Taxonomy

author.name: Francesca Pia Panaccione, Eugenio Lomurno, Matteo Matteucci

entry.summary: Surveys conditional 3D CT generation and organizes the fast-growing literature along a taxonomy centered on how external knowledge conditions the generative process. Motivated by clinical needs including augmentation, privacy-preserving sharing, and simulating specific anatomical or pathological scenarios.

entry.title: P3CA: Encoder-Agnostic Interpretation of Vision Foundation Model Embeddings via Spatial Probing

author.name: Amoon Jamzad, Dilakshan Srikanthan, Faranak Akbarifar, Nooshin Maghsoodi, Parvin Mousavi

entry.summary: Proposes an encoder-agnostic probing method that, given a user-selected spatial region, estimates local feature normalization and dominant covariance directions and projects the whole spatial tensor onto them to visualize where locally informative directions appear. Requires no retraining, encoder modification, or task labels, targeting inspection of vision foundation model embeddings in medical imaging.

entry.title: A Quantum Roadmap for Softmax Attention: Exact Born-Rule Analogs for Softmax Attention on the Probability Simplex

author.name: Eric A. F. Reinhardt, Adam J. Hauser

entry.summary: Argues that when attention inputs and outputs live on the probability simplex, softmax attention has an exact quantum realization: scores become Hadamard-test statistics on block-encoded projections of amplitude-encoded inputs, and the softmax temperature maps to a measurement repetition count. Sparse attention with exact zeros appears at the boundary of the resulting family.

entry.title: A Convolutional Layer Activation Dimensionality Reduction for Out-of-Distribution and Adversarial Attack Detection Methods

author.name: Leandro de Souza Rosa, Lorenzo Capelli, Clara Nunes Barrancos, Mauro Mangia, Riccardo Rovatti

entry.summary: This work proposes a dimensionality-reduction step for convolutional layer activations that explicitly controls the compression versus information trade-off, improving downstream out-of-distribution and adversarial-attack detection based on intermediate activations. It targets a gap where existing reduction methods either lack such control or discard useful structure.

entry.title: MammoMix: Leveraging Mixture of Experts for Robust Mammogram Breast Detection

author.name: Dinh Tan Nguyen, Hoang Quan Dang, Chen Zhang, Sai Ho Ling

entry.summary: MammoMix trains per-domain expert detectors for mammographic lesions and combines them with an input-dependent gating mechanism, aiming for robustness across datasets that differ in image quality, lesion appearance, and demographics. It targets the degradation single detectors suffer when trained on heterogeneous mammography sources.

entry.title: Embedding Rotation Invariance for Provable Multi-Oriented Scene Text Recognition

author.name: Zhibin Ma, Pengwen Dai, Yi Liu, Xugong Qin, Chenyun Yu, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: A multimodal pretraining framework for medical imaging that treats structured clinical tables as semantically meaningful two-dimensional objects rather than flat vectors, using importance-aware adaptive masking as a label-free curriculum. It argues tabular phenotypes carry quantitative diagnostic signal that unstructured reports lack.

entry.title: Grid-Preserving Knowledge Distillation: Transferring Convolutional Inductive Bias to Vision Transformers under Data Scarcity

author.name: Junyong Choi, Cheolhyeon Park, Jaehoon Cho

entry.summary: iBKD distills convolutional inductive bias into Vision Transformers under data scarcity by preserving the spatial grid throughout the transfer path instead of pooling or projecting to logits. An inductive bias attention module aggregates student layers to align with CNN teacher structure.

entry.title: SpecF2M: A Spectral-Aware Multi-task Network Estimating Axial Length and Refractive Error from Pediatric Fundus Photographs

author.name: Mengxian He, Xinyue Liu, Yunyun Sun, Wei Hao, Minqing Zhang, Lichun Wang, Shunyi Zhang, Wu Yuan

entry.summary: SpecF2M is a multi-task network that estimates axial length and refractive error components from pediatric fundus photographs using anatomy-guided enhancement and a hybrid spatial-spectral encoder. It aims to make myopia screening possible without dedicated biometry or cycloplegic refraction.

entry.title: OAA: Three Phases of Vocal Guidance in Human-Drone Teleoperation

author.name: Allan Henry (LPNC, GIPSA-COPERNIC, LIG, GETALP), Christian Graff (LPNC), Solange Rossato (LIG, GETALP), Jos\'e-Ernesto Gomez-Balderas (GIPSA-COPERNIC), Sylvain Huet (GIPSA-COPERNIC)

entry.summary: Using motion capture and speech from human-human pointing guidance and human-drone gamepad teleoperation, the study shows that spontaneous vocal guidance consistently organizes into three distinct phases of orientation, approach, and adjustment. Phases are detected automatically by change point detection on 3D trajectories and validated statistically.

entry.title: Robust Sliding Mode and Admittance Control of Underactuated Aerial Manipulators for Contact-Based Inspection

author.name: Tareq Aziz Alqutami, Yvan Petillot, Matthew W. Dunnigan, Mustafa Suphi Erden

entry.summary: A robust control architecture for an underactuated hexarotor with a one-degree-of-freedom arm combines integral-augmented sliding mode control for trajectory tracking with admittance control for contact force regulation, mapping contact force to a feedforward attitude command. The arm actively compensates vehicle tilt to keep surface alignment during sustained contact inspection.

entry.title: Improved cross-validated distances for multivariate pattern analysis

author.name: Laurent Caplette, Sarah Lipp\'e

entry.summary: This commentary improves on recommended cross-validated distance measures for multivariate pattern analysis of neural data, showing that the cross-validated Euclidean distance decomposes into between-partition distances and using that structure to build a more reliable generalized variant. It also derives improvements for correlation-based distances.

entry.title: AI governance work needs much better monitoring

author.name: jackultraphil

entry.summary: The author argues that AI governance funders rarely verify whether grants achieved anything, and proposes a lightweight practice of agreeing on written indicators before disbursement, having grantees assign probabilities, and scoring annually. An example is given where a grantee reported twenty policy recommendations while only a fifth were even partially implemented.

entry.title: DualCert: A Solver for the Traveling Salesman Problem with Constraint-Coupled Learning

author.name: Yancheng Song, Yongzhi Qi, Wei Qi, Zuo-Jun Max Shen

entry.summary: Introduces DualCert, a learning-augmented TSP solver in which learned refinement steps are constrained by degree equations and dynamically separated subtour elimination constraints, so learned transitions remain feasible with respect to constraints discovered during search. Uses KKT-manifold structure and dual repair to couple learning with optimization guarantees.

entry.title: TRACE: TRajectory Attribution for Automated Context Engineering

author.name: Yikai Zhao, Pradeep Kumar Misra, Saurabh Pandey

entry.summary: TRACE mines historical agent trajectories for implicit dissatisfaction signals such as user corrections, rephrasings, and abandonment, then attributes failures to specific context sources (system prompts, knowledge bases, tool descriptions, skills) and proposes remediations. It automates context engineering maintenance without model fine-tuning or explicit feedback collection.

entry.title: DSLE: A Learning Environment for Dark Souls Boss Encounters

author.name: Derin Gezgin, Jim O'Connor, Tanner Goodwin, Gary B. Parker

entry.summary: Releases a containerized learning environment exposing all 22 boss fights of a difficult action game through a Gymnasium-style interface with real-time combat, high-dimensional visual input, and sparse terminal rewards, plus a recommended five-boss subset for controlled comparison. Baselines include random, expert-system, and evolutionary agents.

entry.title: Evaluation of Motivational Interviewing Counsellors with Task-Aware Multi-Stage LLM-Based Simulated Clients

author.name: Jiading Zhu, Xinyu Cindy Wang, Thomas Nguyen, Yan Qing Lee, Osnat C. Melamed, Peter Selby, Jonathan Rose

entry.summary: Introduces a task-aware simulated client framework for evaluating motivational interviewing counselors in smoking cessation, structured around the evoking stage with staged conversation flow and a policy governing what the client reveals. It targets the mismatch between generic simulated patients and the specific therapeutic tasks being assessed.

entry.title: An evolutionary model of animats with VLM-based subjective evaluation

author.name: Shota Miyazaki, Takaya Arita, Reiji Suzuki

entry.summary: Uses a vision-language model as a subjective fitness judge in an evolutionary algorithm, comparing image sequences of two virtual soft robots and selecting on aesthetic terms such as cute or strange. Morphology and locomotion co-evolve under this subjective selection pressure.

entry.title: Tools to Explain Neural Networks for Power System Dynamics

author.name: Petros Ellinas, Johanna Vorwerk, Spyros Chatzivasileiadis

entry.summary: Applies Neural Tangent Kernel analysis to explain why machine learning surrogates for stiff, multi-timescale power system dynamics train well or poorly, giving a modal interpretation analogous to small-signal eigenvalue analysis. Positions explainability as a prerequisite for grid operators to adopt learned simulators.

entry.title: STEMMA: An Adversarial Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Self-Identity Consistency in LLMs

author.name: Nuthakki Siva Gopala Krishna, Kanishka Jain

entry.summary: Argues that knowledge distillation transfers not just capability but behavioral patterns including how a model represents its own identity, and introduces an adversarial multi-agent framework to stress-test self-identity consistency in student models. Raises concerns about homogenization, inherited bias and accountability in distilled model families.

entry.title: Tabular Numeric Stretch Transformation

author.name: Zihao Ye, Juyong Kim, Johnna Sundberg, Burak Varici, Pradeep Ravikumar

entry.summary: Frames numeric feature preprocessing for tabular deep learning as an optimization problem that stretches feature distributions to make the target function smoother and easier to learn, in unsupervised (density-equalizing minimax) and supervised (target-aware) variants. Targets the underexplored preprocessing stage rather than model architecture.

entry.title: Distributed Optimization with Streaming Data: A Temporal Weighting Perspective

author.name: Muhammad Faraz Ul Abrar, Nicol\`o Michelusi, Erik G. Larsson

entry.summary: Theoretical study of decentralized first-order optimization when data arrive as a stream and the global objective is a temporally weighted average of evolving losses. The authors derive convergence guarantees for multi-iteration decentralized gradient descent under strong convexity and smoothness.

entry.title: Transformer Geometry Observatory TGO-IV: Developmental Topology Observatory

author.name: Kaustubh Kapil, Kishor P. Upla

entry.summary: The fourth instalment of the Transformer Geometry Observatory tracks how the representation point cloud and its manifold topology evolve layer by layer during training, rather than analyzing isolated layers or whole networks. The goal is a developmental account of when raw inputs become task-relevant representations.

entry.title: Coordinating the Unknown Lipschitz Constant in Multiplayer Bandits

author.name: Ricardo Parada, Chenzhang Zhao, William Chang

entry.summary: Studies cooperative multi-agent bandits over continuous Lipschitz action spaces when the Lipschitz constant is unknown, across three information structures. The key technical difficulty is that non-communicating agents must independently converge on the same discretization of the joint action space, and the paper gives regret guarantees for algorithms that do so.

entry.title: Beyond Detection Accuracy: Measuring Explanation Cost, Stability, and Utility for Resource-Aware IoT Intrusion Detection

author.name: Abdurrahman Tolay

entry.summary: Argues that intrusion-detection research ignores the compute cost and instability of generating explanations, and jointly measures detection accuracy, SHAP cost, local explanation stability, and selective explanation on a carefully de-leaked IoT dataset.
